Love the cinnamon flavor of this gum and it actually lasts longer than most gums.  I LOVE the fact that it doesn't upset my stomach and make me bloated like regular sugarless gums.  I am just reordering my 2nd tub.

column9: Taste doesn't last long, but the benefits outweigh that
column10: I've been researching an alternative to other sugar free gums and came across this brand. Xylitol has many health benefits and is all natural, so I decided to try it. Taste was great- strong, cinnamon flavor (think Big Red). The taste did not last, but it did linger in a pleasant way (cinnamon oil). No weird after taste whatsoever. Choosing this over Glee!
Very good flavor at a good price!  It does loose it's flavor pretty quickly. You won't be disappointed with this product and it's  way better for you than gum that's laden with aspartame.

I love cinnamon flavored gum so I was excited about this being a natural sugar free version.  It has great flavor but the flavor only lasts about 5 minutes and then it tastes like I'm just chewing a piece of wax. Also, the pieces are kind of small so I chew two pieces at a time in order to feel like I'm chewing a substantial enough piece of gum.  Probably won't buy this again.

I am trying to avoid aspartame in my diet, but most sugar-free gum contains it. This gum uses only Xylitol as the sweetener.  It is very strong at first (I purchased cinnamon flavor), but the flavor subsides quickly.  If you keep it in your mouth though, you begin to taste it again.  Maybe the initial strength deadens the taste buds temporarily. One upside is that it isn't nearly as sticky or soft as other gums, so it doesn't make a mess trying to throw it away.  Make sure you keep it away from pets, because Xylitol is toxic for dogs.
I'm no gum chewing expert but I can't seem to get the flavor to last for more than a few seconds.

column9: Healthy Chewing Gum with Good Flavor
column10: Since I was a kid, I have loved chewing sugarless gum. I have read that it is a good habit, as it helps clean your teeth after meals and prevent cavities, and may even help prevent acid reflux. Chewing cinnamon gum has even been shown to boost mental performance in a study. However, I became concerned about the possible heath risks from artificial sweeteners like potassium acesulfame used in the gum available at local stores, so I was chewing less often. I decided to try this Xlear Spry cinnamon gum, sweetened with Xylitol. According to Wikipedeia, xylitol has a lot of heath benefits, including reducing dental caries, ear and upper respiratory infections, and Candida yeast growth; it also helps remineralize teeth and bones.  I am happy with Spry cinnamon gum as a substitute for the name-brand gums I had bought previously, though it isn't perfect.  I do have to chew two pieces, as the gum seems to shrink over time, and the flavor is pleasant but doesn't seem to be quite as strong or last as long.  Also the cost of Spry is higher, since I can't take advantage of sales and coupons like with other gum.  These are minor complaints, though, and I am happily switching my family to healthier xylitol-based gum.
Good flavor but it's like chewing on rubber after about 20 minutes or so.Have the headache meds close by , you'll need them chomping on this gum.

The gum has a great flavor, however it does not last nearly as long as normal gum with all the artificial sweeteners. I would find myself chewing a piece for 20 minutes or so before spitting it out and having another. 100 pieces will not last you as long as you would think. But, for less than 5 bucks I would definitely say it is worth the money (I ordered it again).

I highly recommend this gum for anyone who gets aspartame headaches, or is looking for a more natural/healthy solution to typical sugarfree gums. The cinnamon flavor comes on a little strong at first, and then tends to fade rather quickly, but the sweetness/freshness of the xylitol lasts quite a long time. The dental benefits, fresh flavor, and natural ingredients are the perfect combination for me.
Great strong tasting gum BUT doesn't last long BUT is still worth it especially if your not allowed to have regular sf gum! The cinnamon taste is very great!

column9: initially too sweat, then loses flavor quickly. Hard to chew
column10: Initially too sweat, then loses flavor quickly. The flavor actually lasts long enough but comapared to the initial "too sweet" flavor it gives you the impression it has lost most of it. It is too hard to chew.

There is such a great cinnamon flavor to this gum!  The cinnamon oils lend a strong and natural tasting flavor.  It is made with no sugar substitutes which is why I bought it and the Xylitol ingredient is good for your teeth.  I was very satisfied with the length of the flavor as well as the texture of the gum even after a long chew.

Like other xylitol gum I've tried the flavor was good but the gum was hard and within minutes it was grainy and unpleasant to chew, unlike Trident gum, which is sweetened, at least partly, with xylitol, is good chewing gum and that's the whole point!
I am not a big fan of "FAKE" sugar anything! That being said...I really do LOVE this candy...and if you have had to give up all sugar but this....you will LOVE it too!
Great gum no surgar. Great for getting those little bits of food out after a meal just seems to make things unstick! Great flavor and nice burning sensation.
I did not care for this gum at all. There is much better gum available. It lost the flavor in just a few minutes.

I use this gum because it is good for the health of your teeth, does not effect blood sugar, love cinnamon taste, fruit flavor also good.  I chew a couple of pieces after every meal and sometimes in the evening.  Chew about 15 minutes, I do longer.  A friend told me the other day that my face was looking slimmer, I have not lost weight or exercised it - except for chewing!  Could be true!
I am a cinnamon lover, so I love the taste of Spry Cinnamon gum!  It's one of the very few gums on the market right now without aspartame in it.

While the flavour of this gum is nice, I agree with other reviewers who say the flavour doesn't last very long. Not only that, but the pieces are quite small, so you have to chew 2 or 3 of them to really get any flavour. Disappointing.
This gum has a great taste to me and it does freshen your breath but.... the flavor isn't strong and it does not last as long as I would like for the extra cost.

I like chewing this after meals since I don't feel like brushing but I don't want cavities either. I feel it makes a difference at cleaning teeth and the Xylitol does protect teeth to some extent. Can't go wrong.
My family loves this gum because not only does it taste good but it's good for you.

Let me just say that I normally don't review things that I buy from amazon, but I felt that it had to be known that this gum is less than spectacular. I chew about a  12-14 count pack of gum a day, but the flavor runs out on this in a mere minutes. I find myself eating 20-40 pieces. If you want xylitol gum, I think you should look for other brands, namely Trident.
if you like to chew on gum that goes flat within minutes and transforms into a hard flavorless lump, then this gum is for you.  It deserves no stars yet this wasn't an option.
I would never buy this - the taste hardly lasts half a minute and then you are just basically chewing on very hard rubber. Horrible gum.

The pieces are smaller than most of the chiclet gums (Eclipse, Trident, etc.) I'm guessing about 3/4 of the size. Give that, they don't hold a ton of flavor, 5-10 minutes tops. Otherwise no issues with the flavor.
This gum is great!  I love the cinnamon flavor and the fact it is made with Xylitol for the sweetner.
Fast service, great price.The gum taste great.  Will always buy this gum from now on.

column9: disappointing, the gum seemed old and stale
column10: I have purchased this same spry gum at the local health food store and love it.  I saw it on amazon and free super saver shipping.  The price was good and it seemed like a good deal.  Once I tasted the gum I knew something was wrong.  It seemed stale or old.  The expiration date was fine .... not bad until 2013 so then why.  I don't know if the shipping conditions were bad and exposed to heat or cold, but I will not be buying this from amazon again.

Don't let your Dogs get anywhere near gum with Zylitol in it. Don't leave it where a dog will accidentally get into it!!  They have no cure for dogs who eat it and it will, I repeat will kill them. There is nothing that will help.  They don't know yet why but if just a minute portion of a it, will kill your dog, what does it do to you?  I just don't chew gum anymore since it is so hard to find just old fashioned regular gum with sugar and no additives.  Aspartame;bad, Xylitol;worse. They all change motablism.  No wonder obesity is so prevalent now. I would like just regular sugar based gum.

I really like this product. I find they soften in as little as 10 minutes or so. I simply sort through them and pull out the kind of mushrooms that I'm after (either porcini or chanterelles, for instance). The best part of using dried mushrooms is using the flavored water that the mushrooms steep in, such as pasta sauces, risotto, etc. I never throw it away.As to other people's comments about dirt or rocks, this is my second jar and I have never encountered that. Like dried beans, you should visually inspect the dried mushrooms before you add them to recipes; sometimes the steps do not revive well and stay tough. In general, reconstituted dried mushrooms do have a chewier texture. I encountered this when drying my own mushrooms. Some of this is just the process, not this particular product. I went to Italy last year and bought several packages of dried porcini and some of them were a bit chewy, too.You do get better and fresher dried mushrooms if you buy them in small quantities, but they are much, much more expensive. I use for Italian mushrooms for special occasions, and use these for my everyday cooking.

column9: Tasteless- a big jar of disappointment
column10: I love dried mushrooms.  All kinds of them.  But I was very disappointed in these and am trying to decide what to do with this huge container now.  They have no flavor at all.  Reconstituting is a challenge, because  the different types of mushrooms require different amounts of time to hydrate.  But I worked with them, removing the different types from the liquid as they were ready.  The problem is that they have no taste at all to them. None. Neither does the broth.  I have purchased other types of Roland dried mushrooms and been very happy with them.  These are a big disappointment.

If I'd known these were from France, I never would have ordered them. The mushrooms I received look nothing like the ones in the image on Amazon. In the image, there are a lot of golden/light brown mushrooms, all I got were very dark brown to black. The aroma and flavor seem fine, but the color indicates either they were dried at too high of a temperature, or they are very old. And there are a lot of woody stems. Either way, the flavor and nutritional value would not be what it should be. I had subscribed for regular deliveries of these, however, after getting my first jar, I'm cancelling and going to buy in bulk and mix my own in the future.

these were alright once i got them rehydrated which took a long while and then some were a bit tough to chew. i ended up putting them through my spice grinder and making a powder which was easier to add to foods than whole. not sure ill order these again.

If you use 'mushrooms' in many of your prepared foods, these are an excellent choice. No wastage, just take a 'handful' soak in hot water and add to the dish. If you're doing a pasta just chuck them in the boiling water with the 'noodles.' Deal done.

I love these mushrooms.  They are very good - I soak them in water approximately 10 minutes then use them in any recipe that calls for mushrooms.  I live on a ranch and can't run down to the supermarket on a minute's notice; this way, I always have them on hand.

These mushrooms are just ok. Make sure you wash them and drain them well. I used them in soup and then had rocks and other really crunchy items in the soup with them.  I will not be ordering these again.  In fact. I may just throw them out.  Yuck!

I tried these dried wild mushrooms for a recipe for Wild MushroomRavioli.  These were wonderful, excellent quality, and greattaste.  I didn't even have to soak them for this filling ...just chop and saute with the shallots in butter.  I am looking forwardto trying them in other recipes.Suzanne

I use dried mushrooms frequently in making soup and thought I'd give these a try.  I would say that they are not as intense in flavor as others I've used.  In addition, one of the mushrooms in the mix is a sort of flat, slippery and crunchy variety - not a good mix with the others, which are more soft and meaty in terms of texture - and I usually leave them out of whatever I'm cooking.  Possibly they'd be good in an omelette but I haven't been that adventurous.

Three stars until I actually cook w/these. Seen comments elsewhere about roland branded mushrooms regarding country of origin. Fyi - at least for the ones shipped to me it's "Product of France". Price looks good too. Typical pricing in local Chicago grocery stores tends to be $4 an ounce & up.Fyi II - it's white text on a light blue background but if you look carefully on the jar image at amazon.com - you can discern "France" on there. Roland reserves the right to change that?
This soup is delicious.  It tastes like a combination of cream of chicken and cream of mushroom.  So it has a slightly muted chicken flavor.  I like the mildness of this soup.
These little microwavable soups are a staple in my lunch drawer at work. Whenever I need a quick snack, or a little extra warm up on a winter afternoon, these are really great :)

column4: A Research It Maven "Just the facts please"
column9: EXTRA GOOD! This creamy chicken "Soup at Hand" is fab!
column10: Campbells Creamy Chicken Soup at Hand is especially tasty when you need it: if you have no appetite, are getting a cold, or feel the flu coming on! These soup at hand ready to serve soups are extreme comfort when you, or someone you love, is just not at the top of their game! When I just can't face a meal, this creamy chicken soup is perfect for making me feel better - plus it gives a sick person something tasty to wash down all those meds, syrups, and other yucky stuff. And hot soup is so soothing when fighting a cold, flu, or just the "under the weather" feeling. This creamy chicken flavor is extra tasty for the amount of calories, too! Recommended!Calories 130 (per unit)4 grams protein890 mg sodium13 carbs9 grams fatwith 62% of calories from fat (which is ok when this is all you can have)

column9: If you are looking for taste, look elsewhere
column10: This is strictly a product of convenience, for it tastes about as you might expect (or perhaps worse) of something in styrofoam from a microwave.  I wasn't expecting a gourmet experience, but on the other hand I wasn't expecting chicken soup that tastes like some high school chemistry experiment gone horribly wrong.  A much better solution would be to buy yourself a ream of styrofoam cups and a dozen cans of Campbell's cream of chicken soup.  If you can afford the 30 seconds with a can opener and a spoon, you'll be rewarded with something that provides a reasonable facsimile of the taste of real soup.

I love this soup. I only tried it recently and went back to my local store to buy more. I have found locally that different stores carry different varieties of the Campbell's Soup At Hand and the Creamy Chicken is not carried at all my local stores, so I was very glad to find it at Amazon. Although it does not contain much actual chicken, this soup has a wonderful chicken flavor. It is so creamy and good and tastes like real comfort food. It is great for a quick lunch or dinner, either alone or combined with a salad or sandwich. I almost wish Campbell's made it available in larger cans, but that's true of all the Soup At Hand flavors.I hope that Amazon will continue to carry these soups, as the price is much better per container (about $1.30 each) than the individual prices at some of the larger grocers.

These cookies are amazing. I sprinkle coconut on top, sometimes roll into powder sugar, or put choco chips in! EXCELLENT. And great when replacing egg with flax seed when baking! You will not be disappointed with this product~
This makes BBQ so awesome!!!!  I would recommend this to anyone that wants to add that little extra to thier BBQ meats.
We ran across these at a remote filling station in the Utah desert and loved them.  Thus began our quest when we returned to the east coast - thank goodness Amazon had them!
You need more coffee product per cup than recommended, does not dissolve or stay mixed well, weak flavor

This is a great coffee, especially since it's a flavored decaf, which is hard to find.  I have tried some of the other flavors but find that the Irish Cream is not too sweet and has a nice coffee flavor.

column4: Kimberly J. Karas "a New England mom"
column9: Two stars for the Irish cream flavor only.
column10: I am a fan of Caffe D'Vita instant cappucino mix.  I have tried the caramel and pumpkin spice and I loved them both.  The irish cream flavor is not really to my liking because it's a little too dark and not what I expected.  I was thinking it would be a little bit sweeter, similar to International Delight (or similar) non dairy creamers.  It's nothing like that at all.  I either make it weak or doctor it up and still it's only just ok.  Likely I could buy the creamer mentioned and take the edge off this flavor.  I will continue to order this brand but not this flavor.
This is excellent coffee. Not too sweet like you get at the name brand coffee shops. The price on amazon is the best I could find anywhere. If you set up the automatic re-order it works great.
Excellent product, i like this beer, for many year ago. I hoping that many people buy for a not time.

column9: Tasty orange soda - zero cal - and all-natural!
column10: I happen to be drinking an Orange Zevia as I write this review.  :)I cannot compliment this brand enough.  I've been purchasing all flavors of Zevia for the past few years and absolutely love it.  There isn't an aftertaste at all, and it is simply delicious.  Zevia's Natural Orange is among my favorite flavors.  My other Zevia favorites are black cherry and root beer, however all their flavors are yummy!My favorite things about Zevia are that they are sweetened with all-natural stevia and do not contain any harmful chemicals.  Also, I love the fact that there are not any calories in it.  There are no artificial colors or flavors either.The only Zevia flavor I've seen caffeine in is cola.  All the others are caffeine-free.I deducted a star from this product due to the pricey price point of Zevia. I still continue to buy it, but not as often as I would like to due to the cost.I have emailed the Zevia corporate team and they are responsive, professional, and friendly. I trust this brand.I hope you give Zevia a try. I think you will be pleased!

Unfortunately, this soda just doesn't taste good in orange flavor. It has a strange flavor, I think it might be the taste of the stevia interfering with the orangeyness. It's mildly unpleasant, definitely not something I would want to pay extra for.The black cherry flavor of Zevia is much better, really very nice.

I found this product to be unacceptable.The first criticism goes to the flavor which I found to be missing.  The product is supposed to have an orange flavor.  I find it very weak.  I prefer a more robust flavor.  Secondly, to put it as delicately as I can, I believe it caused me lower abdominal distress.I will be canceling my second shipment.  I drank four cans and had the same experience with each.

column9: Orange Soda without worry about Sugar Elevation-PERFECT FOR HCG DIET
column10: What distinguishes this soda from the other diet soda's is that it does NOT elevate your blood sugars. Despite the fact that there are other Zero calorie soda's, they have Aspertame or Splenda which DOES raise your blood sugar levels - so this is really the best soda for those who have this concern.Also, unless you are truly living without sugar, this soda won't taste as good to you as others. It tastes MUCH better when you aren't ingesting either sugar or sugar substitutes.Best thing - EVERYTHING IN THIS IS ALL NATURAL!! Enjoy:)

column9: Love this beverage...but don't have it shipped to you.
column10: My family loves this soda.  We sometimes buy it from a nearby grocery store.  HOWEVER,  I had it shipped from Amazon and it is no good.  I believe that somewhere in the process of getting to my home the Zevia Orange may be getting too hot.  It was very hot weather the first time it was shipped to me.  It really tastes weird...not like when we buy if off the shelf.  I tried again in cold weather this time and though it's not as bad, it is still no good. It has an odd bite to it that I assume comes from it getting too warm.  It alters the beverage and cooling it in the frig does not reverse it.

column9: If Stevia is bitter for you, then this is the better tasting Zevia drinks
column10: Because of my genetics Stevia will always be bitter to me. I've tried other artificial sweeteners and stevia is by far the worse in bitterness no matter what brand I try.  I get no sweet taste at all. However, I have to limit my sugar intake, and sometimes I just get tired of other drinks, especially the carbonated ones. I like the orange Zevia because with the bitter Stevia taste it reminds me a lot of the "bitter orange" or lightly sweetened orange sodas that I got in Europe. I haven't tried the lemon or lime flavors, but I imagine the citrus lends itself well to the bitter flavor.

column9: I don't drink Orange Soda but I do Now!
column10: So I had to try this flavor as I like the other two ZEVIA Natural Cola - With Stevia (Case of 24) and ZEVIA Natural Twist - With Stevia (Case of 24).I haven't drank Orange Soda since I was a kid and for some reason I don't remember really liking Orange Crush but Zevia Orange is great and my kids love it as well.

Zevia orange really tastes like orange soda - and not like orange DIET soda either. How did they do it? I'm impressed. I wasn't a fan of orange flavored soda until now. This is so great! The cola and lemon-lime are delicious, too. All this and all natural - I'll never drink a diet soda again.

I was never an orange soda fan until Zevia.  It is All Natural which is important to me.  There are no artificial sweeteners or ingredients.  The taste is more subtle and refreshing then other orange sodas.  A terrific product that I highly recomend.  Try it!

I took a chance and ordered a case of this, since I like Zevia lemon-lime and think their cola is O.K. as well. Unfortunately, I find it pretty bad: the orange flavor--what little there is of it--is outweighed by a vile, bitter taste that gets worse with every sip. Bleah!!! :(

column9: Love This Line of Products(!) But This One Needs A Little Improvement
column10: Stevia sweetened colas has finally come of age and I love many Zevia flavors but this one has a strange and unappetizing taste after swallowing it.  Now my 5 year old likes it so theres a critic in the house who differs with me some, anyhow.  But seriously it needs more work to get the flavor to something not so odd and unlikable.

I've had a few different flavors- this is by far my least favorite.I gave it 2 stars because I can *see* how some people would like it.It just wasn't for me. I thought the flavor was off, it tasted nothing like orange soda. It was also a bit too sweet for me.But please try other flavors! The other ones I've had (black cherry, cream soda, root beer) are really good.
This is not like Orange Crush. It is less sweet and more refreshing, like the European orangades or Orangina, and I adore it!

column9: Unnatural orange taste and unpleasant to drink
column10: Ive tried Zevia Root Beer (loved), Cherry (loved) Dr. Zevia (just ok) and now Orange. This flavor has been the worst so far.I cant even finish a full can. Bitter with to me a chemical aftertaste, I'm not sure how people can drink this. It just tastes like a chemical experiment. I guess some of Zevia's product my taste buds can enjoy, some they can not. Definitely will not be buying this flavor again.

This soda hurt my teeth. Drank one a day for 6 weeks. The Enamel on my teeth has eroded. My teeth are now still very sensitive. Read ingredients before drinking.  Consider battery  acid or this soda if your goal is to erode enamel

They had this on special at a local market, so I thought I'd give it a try. The black licorice aftertaste was so powerful, it made it impossible to really taste anything else after the first sip. If I wanted to taste black licorice, I would have eaten some.Terrible, terrible soda. Terrible, terrible experience. Threw the other five cans out. What a waste of money and potable water.

column9: I loved the orange and root beer
column10: I love the Orange and Ginger Root Beer...They are pricey, but I'll pay a little more for something a little more healthy than a Coke or Pepsi.
This is one of the best diet sodas you could ever buy.  The flavor is great and it is actually healthy for you, nothing artificial !!!!!

column9: Good Product, Poorly Packaged and Shipped
column10: I love Zevia.  Can't say anything bad about a soda with no calories, no caffeine, and no aspartame.  My most recent shipment however, was less than satisfactory.  One case had a can that had ruptured, soaking the inside of the box, and the cardboard had begun to mold as a result.  Yuck.  It was not a particularly hot day when it was delivered, between that and the mold I'm sure the can burst long before it arrived at my door.Another case not only had a ruptured can, but was missing one as well!  One of the four sixpacks had only five cans, and an empty plastic ring where a sixth should have been.Maybe the packagers got thirsty.

When I was a kid, I loved Orange Crush.  Now, I don't drink soda with sugar and diet sodas contain a chemical sweetener of some sort that generally taste like crap.  Not this one!  It contains Stevia which is a plant that is naturally sweet but calorie free, no diabetic impact, etc etc.  It also uses Erythritol for sweetness which is a sugar alcohol.  I like the taste, it doesn't rot my teeth, and it doesn't make me sluggish or fat.  The one downside is the price.  Economies of scale rule the beverage business, and Zevia is a small player.  The product benefits offset the price in my mind and using Amazon Subscribe & Save offsets some of the cost.  That is certainly the cheapest way to get Zevia.

This soda has the most marvelous orange flavor with no poisonous colorings or additives of any kind and the water  is triple filtered.It is also clean tasting with a fine quenching pull in its after taste. It is simply the finest diet soda I have  tried and you can  feel the difference. A well balanced treat and worth the extra cost.Hands down.

column9: Not as Good as Cola or Root Beer Flavors
column10: This is the first Zevia flavor I got to try.  I didn't really want it but it was all Amazon had in stock and ready to ship for Prime members (more on that later).  I was so eager to try it I popped a can open right when I got it in the house.  My initial thought was that it was gross but I thought I could get used to it by the time I get through the entire case.  My wife tried it at room temperature and she hated it.  She didn't touch anymore orange or the black cherry I got later because of that first taste.  She's since had some nice cold root beer and cola Zevia which she was impressed with.  My nearly three year old son also had a taste test of the orange flavor.  He's not a soda drinker so maybe that had something to do with his reaction.  He drank about an 1/8 of a can which surprisingly all came back up on my kitchen floor about two minutes after he drank it.  He said he didn't like it.  Ha.  Out of the four flavors of Zevia, orange is my least favorite.  I will not be ordering it again due in part to its taste, which I would say is okay, but also the price for it.  I am willing to pay the price for now for a couple of the other flavors, but not orange.There are two major problems with ordering Zevia products.  First, they're expensive.  At just over a dollar a can they are pricey, no other way to describe it.  The second, is availability.  Amazon is really having some issues with keeping Zevia flavors in stock with Prime shipping.  The third party sellers all have exuberant shipping prices bringing your case of soda to over fifty dollars.  I've emailed Zevia about this and did get a response from them.  I hope Amazon can keep it stocked and Zevia can keep them supplied.  It's a good product but it's been frustrating trying to order due to Amazon's stock.  Due to the high price tag I put it on a monthly schedule to save 15%.  It helps but I wonder if Amazon will have it ready to go each month.The Zevia Orange is an okay tasting soda.  I will not be purchasing any more of it even if it's all Amazon Prime has in stock.

I have tried a few of the Zevias and this orange one is really pretty good and refreshing if you don't want to give up your sodas because of all the unhealthy things in them, especially aspartame and high fructose corn syrup.  This one is sweetened with stevia.  Highly recommended!

Good Product and shipped in a timely manner.  I tried to make another order through Amazon with the coupon but it would not accept the coupon code.  So I won't order again until i figure it out.  If anyone can advise on what to do.  I tried calling Zevia but could not get through to any human so I gave up.

For someone trying to stay low on the glycemic index, this stuff is great.  Stevia doesn't cause insulin reactions, blood sugar spikes, etc.  The Lime wasn't too tasty in my opinion.  The orange is pretty good.  I do wish it was just a little more "orangee" in the flavor department.

OK,..I'm speaking on behalf of the Orange Soda here. When I first popped the tab and drank a sip of the Zevia Orange,..it did NOT hit me with the anticipated sweetness that I had come to expect from say a Diet Sunkist Soda or any of your typical SugarFree Orange sodas. I wasn't disappointed per say, but just surprised a bit by the unexpected lack of sweetness.Now, with that being said,...and a few cans later,..this has quickly become my "go to" drink when I want a refreshing orange soda. It is very good and very quenching (due to the noticeable lack of sodium) on a hot summer day. The aroma is wonderful and the flavor is very close to as real as you can get before drinking straight orange oil. It's a really good soda and I'm now tempted to try the Root Beer and the Cola.

column9: Attention Moms- This is what your kids should be drinking
column10: Hello to all those Moms out there looking for something to hand to your kids that won't make them over-weight, rot their teeth out and make them try and climb the walls!  You need Zevia Natural Orange.  All kids LOVE soda pop, you can't fight it.  I have tried for over 9 years. This is why I am so pleased to have found Zevia Orange.  It has no calories and it's all natural, even the bright orange color.  As a Mom, I feel great about being able to buy soda pop for my son.
This does not taste bad at all; it just doesn't taste much, period .Like they didn't put enough orange in it. I am giving it away.

Ever since I learned about the dangers of sugar and chemical sugars, I have avoided them like the plague.  Then when I accidentally discovered an online ad for a "stevia-sweetened" soft drink named Zevia, well, let's just say I was hooked.Zevia is an alternative to diet soda that is sweetened with my two favorite sweeteners: erythritol and stevia. Wow! There is no calcium-removing phosphoric acid like you'd find in regular toxic sodas. And the taste is great! I've only tried the Orange and Natural Twist flavors with Orange being my favorite so far. I hear they came out with a new root beer flavor so that makes a total of four different Zevia sodas to choose from.Diabetics and those with Candida will welcome this new alternative to soda. I know me and my father sure did. Can't wait to open a nice cold one right after I write this review. Ahhhhhh!

The packaged from Coffeyville, Ks. arrived dammaged. Two of the Zevia cans had popped open and soaked the card-board container. Add to that, it took over 3 weeks to arrive. Not a very good experience.Regards

column9: Slightly variations from the Mint Flavor
column10: I tried several different flavors of Mentos gum, but was rather disappointed by the overall product.First of all, the good points. The gum comes in a hard, durable container, which is easy to carry around in one's pants pocket, and also facilitates dispensing. Additionally, I like the initial texture of the gum, as it has a hard exterior shell and a soft chewy interior core, which immediately releases a burst of flavoring. Lastly, the texture and consistency of the gum is maintained throughout the mastication process.Now, the bad part. The biggest drawback is that the flavor only lasts at most a few minutes, necessitating me to eat several pieces at once in order to maintain any semblance of lasting mint flavor. Compared to other rival brands such as Dentyne or Eclipse, this is unacceptable. I'm not interested in chewing a piece of bland plastic after just 2-3 minutes. Some have also commented that the hard container makes too much noise in one's pants pockets when walking around.In summary, the Mentos are best used as an ephemeral breath mint, rather than a long-lasting gum.Now in regards to this particular flavor of red fruit lime, I find that the flavor lasts slightly longer as compared to the mint flavor.  Still not long enough, but just a smidgeon longer.  Additionally, the packaging is deceptive, because the core of the gum is most certainly not green colored.

column9: Oh Danny boy...the matcha, the matcha is calllling....
column10: Irish cream teas tend to make me sad. What I've found is that they tend to taste like regular tea with a hint of Irish cream in the background, like you had poured a drop or two into your tea. Which is all well and good, but I drank Irish cream straight up when I was in college, and I want something that tastes like the drink itself. At this point, you're probably wondering if I did anything but drink in college. The answer is....no, not really. Ha! I want an Irish cream tea that I can splash into other teas to make them taste like Irish cream.So I cheated a little with this one. Just a little, I promise! I mixed my spoon of matcha with a few drops of my Irish cream agave before adding the water. I was blown away. It was so, so, so good. It got me through an incredibly long day at work and it kept a smile on my face long after it was gone. It smelled and tasted so strongly of Irish cream that my boss side eyed me a few times until I showed him it was just matcha. And then he was jealous.I love this tea. With the milk allergy issues, Irish cream was one of the things I had to give up and it was with a heavy heart that I did so. This is one of those teas I've been searching and searching for and once again, Red Leaf Tea did it right. I am constantly impressed by them...you'd think by now, I'd just expect their matcha to be amazing. But no, every time I get a new package, I'm floored by the tastiness.

I got this one special for my boyfriend as a surprise. Last time he got to pick out a matcha, we ended up with Cola, so this time I thought an alcoholic drink matcha was in order. More sophisticated? Well - more adult anyways ;)He is loving the flavoured matcha as much (if not more!) than I do! This one smelled sweet from the get go - creamy and .. tangy? Smoky? Not smoky! I'm trying to describe what irish cream smells like - it doesn't have the smokiness of whisky - but it definitely is sweet and creamy! I knew it was going to be a real treat - just like the real thing! What a neat flavour experience! I prepared the matcha straight and thick for the first bowl. In this state I tasted mostly matcha with an aftertaste of sweet cream that lingered after finishing the bowl. It was very creamy and pleasant.Next I tried it over ice with 18% cream and sugar. I thought my eyes were going to roll into the back of my head and be lost forever! This was mine and Mike's favourite way to enjoy it. It's sweet, but because you have control over the amount of sugar, it's not crazy sweet and cloying. You could probably enjoy cup after cup with the only buzz coming from the energy of all that matcha you're drinking!This one is so so good mixed with the Madagascar Vanilla matcha - it just adds a bit of something that takes the creamy flavour over the top. Come St. Patricks day, it would be an awesome drink to mix with mint matcha (Mint is on the way in the mail as we speak!) and hey - it's already green! No need to add any food colouring for your Paddy experience ;)Now - if a Guinness Matcha ever comes out - I know the perfect one to mix it with ;)

column9: Campbell's Beefy Mushroom Soup Is Still Made
column10: I'm another one of those people who have looked for years, without success, to find Campbell's Beefy Mushroom Soup on the grocery store shelves.  But, by searching on the internet recently, I came across the soup for sale on Amazon.  Others, as well as myself, have wondered if the product was fresh stock since it's very hard to find.  Well, I recently called Campbell's to inquire if the soup was still in production, and they assured me it was.  So, last fall, I ordered 2 cases of the soup on Amazon Campbell's Beefy Mushroom, 10.75-Ounce Cans (Pack of 12) and the expiration was in 2011 or 2012 (I forget).  I've already used up all the soup and I'm ready to order more.  When this soup first appeared in grocery stores years ago, the label had this YUMMY recipe on it, which I have used ever since.  It is my husband's favorite hamburger dish.  This recipe transforms ordinary hamburger into a delicious comfort food your family is sure to love.  It's so easy to make, but ohhh sooo good!  Here it is:"Campbell's Salisbury Steak"1 (10 3/4 ounce) can Campbell's Beefy Mushroom Soup1 1/2 lbs ground beef1 egg, lightly beaten1/2 c. fine dry breadcrumbs1/4 c. finely chopped onion1/8 t. pepper1/4 c. water1) Add 1/4 c. soup, egg, breadcrumbs, onion and pepper to the ground beef and mix well.2) Shape into 6 patties.3) Brown both sides in ungreased skillet, over medium heat; not cooking them completely.4) Drain off the fat.5) Spoon over the patties the undiluted Beefy-Mushroom soup and 1/4 c. water.6) Cover the skillet and simmer over low heat 20 minutes or until done, spooning the gravy over the patties occasionally.7) Delicious served with mashed potatoes, cooked green beans and rolls with butter.Serves 6

Rooibos is Afrikaans for "red bush." Grown in South Africa's Cederburg Mountains and harvested during the summer, this tea acquires its unique red color as a result of fermentation (in mounds) and oxidization, when it is spread out to dry in the sunlight; naturally it is green.Rooibos is known for its health benefits stemming from its rich content in vitamins, antioxidants, flavanoids and minerals (inter alia, magnesium, calcium, iron, copper, zinc, potassium, fluoride, manganese and alpha-hydroxy) and has a long tradition of medicinal use among the local Native population; among other things, it is known to help cure asthma, hay fever and other allergies, acne, eczema, colics, indigestion, insomnia, and nervous tension. Containing very few tannins and no caffeine, rooibos has a distinctive aroma and amber color.This tea blends well with various spices and condiments; my favorite mixture is a delicious loose leaf blend sold by my local tea store, which features orange peel, cinnamon, grated coconut, finely minced chili and red pepper. For a more commercial alternative, though, Tazo's Red Bush tea is a great choice as well: a rich, exquisite blend of rooibos, hibiscus, orange peel, rosemary, several lemon ingredients (lemon myrtle, verbena and balm), as well as a number of sweet spices. Enjoy!

And the price was good on Amazon too.
After reading some of the other reviews, I was expecting more flavor to the  tea.  It is good.  I let it infuse a bit longer than other flavors to encourage the flavor development.

I'm a fan of Tazo teas in general and Tazo's African Red Bush is one of my favorites.  The flavor is rich and delicious and I have yet to find another brand that tastes as good.  It used to be available for subscribe and save and free shipping from Amazon Prime, which made the price unbeatable.. but I'm not sure if it is still available for subscribe and save.

The product I ordered and received is what was advertised.  BUT, I think there is a bit of trickery going on since the can was half the size of a NORMAL can of cat food.  Of course, it's my fault for not checking the oz. in a normal can but, most people have never heard of a small can size of cat food.

wow def would love to buy in cases of 24 but the price is def way too much these are 99 cents each and he's trying to sell it for double what a rip off the should be for 23 bucks or 24. when you lower the price to that u will have a buyer.

This stuff is just AWFUL!One star is one star too many.The only thing raspberry about it is the color.I'm with one of the other reviewers - 5.95 bottles straight to the dump.  This is the first review I have ever written, but it needed doing.I think the person who gave Pappy's five stars might be  called Mammy ----Incidentally, the pomegranate syrup Amazon sells is good stuff.  It's a bit sour, so I mix it with something sweeter, fill the glass with ice and soda water and have it with lunch.

column9: Great Tead and Rasberry Flavor - Non Sweetened
column10: I have been drinking Pappy's Teas for years.Raspberry tea is delicious.I especially enjoy with a little Madhava Raw Agave syrup to add a little sweetness.My daughter drinks it over ice with no sweetener.

column9: AACK!  Down the drain it goes . . .
column10: I tried this product only because another brand (Oak Hill Farms raspberry tea concentrate) was no longer available on Amazon.  I regretted it after one sip:  the tea was very bitter and had no noticeable raspberry flavor.  The taste might be salvaged by a great deal of sweetener, but Oak Hill Farms required none.

column9: Not as good as the Sassifras
column10: I really like the Sassafras flavor and thought I would try this as well.  I'm sure it's good quality but the flavor is not as good so I give it a low score.These are not sweet and not sour.  I'm trying to think of something appropriate to use it with - it might be good with yogurt or ice cream.  I don't care for it with water.

column9: Soft Drinks Made With Cane Sugar for My Guests.
column10: Some time ago (September, 2009) I wrote a review for Mexican Coke. It came in 12-ounce bottles in a 24-bottle case. The bottles resembled the old fashioned Coke bottles. The main distinction between Mexican Coke and that manufacture in the USA was that Mexican coke was made with cane sugar whereas American Coke was made with high fructose corn syrup. Some people worry about possible health effects of HFCS and others simply don't like the taste as well. Personally, I think the Mexican Coike tastes a bit better. Gormet Coca Cola? Well, whatever, Mexican Coke has now become a big favorite and you can find it all over, even in restaurents.Now, on my last trip to my local Costco store, I found a 12-bottle case of "Vintage Soda," a variety of past-famous American soda beverages. There's Dad's Root Beer, Bubble Up, Nesbitt's Orange Soda and NuGrape Soda. All are made with cane sugar. They're quite good, but I have no standard bottles for comparison. Also, I only rarely drink sodas. I have a supply at home, but it's mainly for guests. Some guests want diet drinks and some don't care for diet sodas. so for the sweetend ones, I use the cane sugar varieties.They get good reviews and it makes for an interesting conversation piece. Gary Peterson

I'm a big fan of Quinoa pasta, but I was not satisfied with this particular product.  The three colors cooked at different rates so you were left with some hard, and some completely soggy pasta on the same plate.I had 3 boxes left, so I sorted them by color.  This works, but it's a pain to do.  I definitely would not buy again.

We've tried every brand (DeBoles, Tinkyada, etc.) and the Quinoa pasta is the easiest to cook.  Add a bunch of oil to the pasta water, bring to a boil, and pour in the pasta *while stirring*.  Bring to a new boil, turn down to a simmer, and cook for 6-7 minutes (depends on heat--test after 4 minutes).  Drain and if you overcooked it, rinsed under COLD water--sometimes you can save GF pasta by doing this.  The quinoa pasta is high in protein and an excellent GF pasta.
This cooks just fine,  . . just check the texture after cooking forabout 6 or 7 minutes. If you don't cook it long enough, it will behard . . just like any other pasta. I use this all the time.

We've tried most of the shapes of this pasta, and we really enjoy it.  We initially purchased it because of my daughter's wheat, egg and soy allergies, but we would eat it now even if she outgrows her allergies.

column9: Read the fine print on the box of QUINOA Ancient Harvest Supergrain Pasta
column10: While this pasta tastes better than many whole grain pastas, I am giving a ranking of 2 because although the packaging strongly suggests this product contains a significant amount of quinoa, the actual amount of quinoa in the corn-quinoa blend may be just slightly greater than the amount of dried spinach needed to color a few of the pieces green. So don't have your decision swayed by the side or back panels, which detail the wonderful nutritional profile of quinoa and its history of cultivation. Note that the company's website states "our Corn/Quinoa gluten free pasta is primarily a corn based product." So maybe they should be putting the word "corn" in the big print?

column9: Falls apart, leaving a gritty mess
column10: I really like the other Ancient Harvest GF pastas.  I tried two boxes of this and varied cooking times, sauces, and experimented with a few other variables.  Without fail, anytime I had to re-heat the pasta, it fell apart when I stirred it.  I am the only person in the house who has to be GF so I am usually the only one eating the pasta.  It is kind of a pain to make a single serving of my pasta and a pot full for everyone else.  I like being able to make a few serving to refrigerate and have something for lunch the next day, but the way this pasta just crumbles creates a texture I can't stand.  It's tiny pasta pieces and sauce, which I haven't had with the other pastas.  It's also the only brand that I had trouble finding a good cooking time.  The box says 4 to 6 minutes, but that always left hard pasta, even when dropped in salted water that was at a rolling boil.  I would check minute by minute and it seemed to be different every time, and sometimes it seemed like only half the noodles were cooked well and the others were too hard or over-cooked.  I'm a decent cook and don't have that issue with the other AH pastas, GF pastas, or the wheat pastas I cook for the rest of the family.  I will skip the shapes and stick to the other pastas made by Ancient Harvest.

I have candida and if you have it or know what it is, then you know what I'm talking about. This pasta made from Quinioa is fabulous! I'ts way better that rice pasta because it doesn't get mushy, but don't over cook it either. Six to seven minutes max.  Good luck and enjoy.

I love this stuff, but if you are expecting it to turn out like pastas made from wheat, you won't be happy. You can't just dump the box into boiling water and dump it into a strainer when the time's up; the pasta will stick together, and if you overcook, it's going to dissolve and turn gluey. But if you have even marginally passable cooking skillz, this stuff is really good and very far from nasty.
Cook too little, hard and nasty. Cook toomuch gummy and nasty. Either way, nasty. Why did I order a whole case??

Searching for gluten free items has gotten easier, but I cannot find Ancient Harvest locally.  Being able to buy it online is awesome!  I buy it by the case so I have it onhand.  It's just like regular pasta but wheat-free!  Even if you don't have wheat or gluten issues, try it ~ it's GREAT.

I have cooked this pasta several times and had no trouble with it at all. I have no gluten intolerance, so my use of this pasta started out as experimental, and my continued use is simply based on taste and texture.  I wonder if the negative reviews of this pasta came from people who don't otherwise prepare pasta correctly. I have had no trouble with it, as it cooks like traditional pasta. Generously salt the water, bring to boil and add pasta. Allow the water to return to a boil and continue to cook on full heat until the pasta is done.It's important to note, I suppose, that cooking time varies among all stoves regardless of whether or not the pasta is semolina based or gluten free. How much heat a pot of boiling water receives is going to affect cooking time. As for any pasta, the time on the box should be used only as a guideline to give you an idea of when to check your pasta. Pasta water must be salted, and the pasta occasionally stirred.This pasta may come out too hard if it's not been cooked long enough, I guess. Too soft means it was cooked for too long, (and perhaps that the pasta water was not salted), which is why you taste the pasta before dumping the pot into a strainer. Again, this is true for all pasta, so my guess is people who had a problem cooking this pasta were probably interpreting the cooking time too literally and not sampling a piece before straining. In my kitchen, all pasta colors cooked evenly.When the pasta is cooked correctly:the pasta texture is excellent and very comparable to traditional semolina pasta. In fact, regarding texture specifically, there is little discernible difference at all. My family of regular pasta eaters could not discern between this and regular pasta. I served it with marinara sauce which probably masked the subtle flavor difference. This pasta is made from corn and has subtle notes of corn to it, the way a spinach pasta has notes of spinach: it still tastes like pasta. These are mostly detectable when the pasta is eaten completely plain, but hardly when the pasta is sauced at all. In fact, the notes of corn actually work really well with certain dishes and I would certainly choose this pasta for certain dishes for that very reason.
This is a great pasta! Amazon has it LOADS cheaper than any of my local stores. It came out to almost BOGO! Love this stuff, will now have to order it at least once a month!

Mrs. Leeper's Pasta Organic, Corn Vegetable Radiatore used to be my favorite, gluten free pasta but the Ancient Harvest Quinoa pastas are just a little better. Nutritionally there is little difference as the Ancient Harvest pastas are mostly corn flour (as is Leeper's). The Ancient Harvest pastas cost a few pennies more per ounce but, in my opinion, they are worth it. But both products are very good.

I ordered a case of this product (pagoda pasta), but what came was rotelle pasta! Both are wheat and gluten free, but it was not what I thought I was getting. However, I think this brand is the best GF pasta out there.

I have never tried gluten-free pasta before but am doing a cleanse that doesn't allow gluten. I bought this from Whole Foods after seeing that, out of all the gluten free pasta's available, this one only had 1 left on the shelf. I figured if other people were buying it up, it had to be good. I had to cook it for about 18 minutes in boiling water with a little salt and oil, but the pasta came out great. The texture was dense and the flavors of the bell pepper came through in the orange pieces. I am extremely happy with it and will be purchasing it again.

This is by far the best bag of mushrooms that I have ever had. Although the price may seem high, it is definitely worth it seeing as how  you get 15 pounds (that's 6.80388555 kilograms!!!) of shroomliciousness. I ate the whole bag in one night because they were so dang good. Don't be fooled into believing that all your getting are mushrooms; you also get the neat bag in which they are delivered in. Your friends will be so jealous when they see you strutting your stuff with a bag that can easily serve all of your fungus needs (up to 15 lbs!).I'd definitely recommend that anyone buy these mushrooms, and I would do the same again if I didn't use my life's savings on them.

I've tried quite a few different brands of this type of microwave meal that doesn't need freezing or refrigeration, and most of them are not very good. What they lack in flavor, they make up for in high fat, salt, or other junk I'd rather avoid. They also have a tendency to taste like plastic.This Barilla Penne and Marinara were pleasantly surprising. The sauce smells a bit more like basil than I usually like, but tastes great, with a good combination of fresh tomato and spices. The pasta was perfectly al-dente. Actually, it was much better than expensive frozen dinners have been able to produce.Adding a little fresh parmesan, this was a tasty and filling lunch.The only downside is in the packaging, which seems overly substantial. The tray and inner sauce holder are both made of very heavy plastic, which seems like a waste. Fortunately, they are recyclable.

Barilla's Penne Traditional is a very tasty microwaveable meal with plenty of pasta.  The sauce compares well with some Italian restaurants - chunky bits of tomato, smooth tomato taste and nice firm pasta.  It cooks up really fast.  Once cooked, the sauce needs to be mixed with the pasta and that can be tricky if not paying attention.  The tray with the sauce needs to be carefully lifted off the main container and poured on the pasta.  Not a big problem but has the potential to spill.Otherwise, mix and enjoy.  Barilla also makes a spicier version of this pasta containing basil - not bad either but I prefer this one.

I tried another variety of these Barilla mezze penne dishes, so my observations on the basic product and its packaging are in that other review, with a good impression overall. I found the packaging to be user-friendly and love the fact that these meals have all-natural ingredients.I thought that the taste of this mezze penne meal with the traditional marinara sauce was just like the other one I tried, with the real difference being that the other one had whole wheat pasta. I don't know that I really distinguished any difference between the two, having them for lunch on two consecutive days, but I did enjoy both.In this one I noticed the chunks of tomato and onions. The sauce was thick enough for the pasta, yet it still poured easily from the separate container upon coming out of the microwave.I like that you don't have to add water to these dishes before microwaving; the pasta is already cooked and just has to be heated.Overall, my impression of this product was very good.

column9: Not the worst thing I ever tasted.
column10: Okay, this is not your sweet nonni's special Sunday sauce, and the penne aren't her own hand cut and rolled individually around the handle of her wood spoon little pastas that you grew up with (and if the food was that good, why the heck did you leave home?  Ask yourself!).  But it won't kill you.  And if you are up to here with tunafish sandwiches, on a budget, in a hurry, and trapped inside because Life As We Know It has come to a disasterous end, it's not a bad lunch.  It's not good, but there are worse things, and we've all probably tasted them. Canned spaghetti, for one thing. Or canned chicken noodle soup, lord help us and the poor chicken that died in vain for that stuff.If you are used to those bottled supermarket sauces, you might find this completely acceptable.  It is mostly salty and slightly tomato-ey.  The sauce is a tiny bit on the bitter side, probably from dehydrated garlic. It has that metallic aftertaste. But you can taste the basil, there are little red chunks that could indeed be tomato, and the texture of the pasta is not as bad as it might be. It has a sort of gummy/pastiness, but not that slimy tongue-feel of canned soup noodles.You have to cook it a bit longer than the instructions state, especially if you have an underpowered microwave.  The portion size is decent, but it's not exactly low cal, packing about 350 calories. If you add a salad and a beverage, you're looking at 500 to 600 calories easy, and you could have had a Big Mac or a ham and cheese sandwich or something really really good instead.If you work in an office where people steal food, offer the crooks a taste. This stuff is not so good that they'll be tempted to "borrow" a box when you're not looking.I would definitely buy this if I were a survivalist. A good change from the  canned beefaroni. I might buy this to keep on hand at work for emergencies...days when I forgot to bring something from home or going out for real food was not possible, and every restaurant in town suddenly stopped delivering. I would not buy them as an altenative or replacement for the real thing.  And the real thing is so easy to make...and takes no time at all.  Boil pasta according to package directions. Put a little olive oil in a frying pan, throw in some finely chopped garlic. Let it saute on low heat...but don't let it brown. Cut a pint of cherry tomatoes in half and toss them in. Add a pinch of sugar and a pinch of red peper flakes or some cayenne or chili powder. Diced chile peppers are even better, as many as you like for as hot as you like.  Cook for ten minutes. Drain the pasta, toss it into the frying pan and swirl it around so it gets all mixed up with the tomatoes and garlicky oil. Add some shredded basil.  You can throw in some diced mozzarela, sprinkle on parmesan or asiago or whatever Italian grated cheese you like.  20 minutes, start to finish, and you have something really nice. With crusty bread, a tart green salad and some wine, it's a feast. Buy some supermarket lemon sorbet and tart it up with grated lemon peel and some mint leaves and you are a chef.

I was impressed with this meal, I couldn't imagine the quality Barilla is known for being seriously ready for consumption in sixty seconds. What I love most about it was the fact that it had real sauce that is comperable to what you would put on your homemade pasta. Most meals like this taste more like an upgraded cup of noodles, where this is a nice meal in a crunch. Now I will say you really need to read the instructions before cooking. The opening instructions can be assumed and cause the sauce to go flying when the food is done cooking. With that in mind, it's not ideal for kids to cook on their own. The film was rather tight and I can see a child or pre-teen getting burned if they are not paying attention while the open the contents. With that, please be careful. Outside of that, it was delicious for a microwave meal.

My partner and I both work from home, and so we often need quick-fix meals for lunch in the middle of the day. So we gave these a try, and were quite pleased! The pasta softened up very well, and the sauce heated up with no problems at all. Very tasty as well, and while the portions could have been a little bigger, overall we were pretty happy with them.

The Barilla Mezze Penne with Traditional Marinara Sauce was ready in 60 seconds when cooked on high in my 800 watt microwave.  The penne came out perfect - not too hard or soft.  The traditional marinara sauce was quite good, but I prefer the spicy marinara sauce. It was a little hard to pull the cover off, and the sauce, since it was in a separate little container, did splatter a bit.  The meal consists of 320 calories and includes 6g of fiber.  For a 60-second meal, it is very tasty.  Just add a salad and slice of french bread - and this makes for a super quick meal.

column9: Just Ok, but a Brilliant Idea!
column10: Barilla's new pantry Mezze Penne products are an exciting lineup.  You can enjoy a hot pasta meal in 60 seconds.  Furthermore, the product stores at room temperature, which allows you to take it to work to use in a work microwave, or to have it shipped from a store like Amazon.com without worry in most climates.  This product includes the Traditional Marinara Sauce.The pasta sauce is stored in a bin above the pasta.  To prepare the meal, you peal back the top seal to expose the sauce and allow ventilation.  You heat it for 60 seconds.  Let it cool, remove the rest of the seal carefully, pour the sauce on the pasta, transfer it to a plate should you wish, and eat!  It's fast, and it is simple.  No refrigeration required.  It truly is a nifty idea.The only downside is that they are not the tastiest products.  I have tried the Tomato & Basic, Marina, and Spicy Marina.  It's extremely difficult for me to tell a difference between any of the sauces.  The sauces are not great.  Just ok.  My favorite is probably the Spicy Marina, but it's truly stretching it to call one my favorite and again, to even differentiate the taste between sauces is difficult.In terms of the pasta, it comes out slightly gooey and not as soft as it could be.  Just ok.  There are some additional instructions provided, to add some water to the pasta after the first 60 seconds and cook longer, but these instructions are not completely clear.  I tried this once, and the pasta did not change at all.Overall, a brilliant idea.  With the great storage ability, it's not bad to have one or two of these on hand for a long work day, when you want a simple lunch or dinner fast.  However, in general, I would not want to consume these on a daily basis.  Perhaps, over time, they will improve the product.  If they could include just a slightly higher quality sauce and pasta, it could be a real winner.  Right now, just ok.

This pasta was very good! I was a bit skeptical at first about the pre-cooked pasta in a container that did not need to be refrigerated, but I ate it and had no ill side effects :)The instructions to heat up the pasta and sauce were simple and because it's not a frozen meal, it only took about 1:30 in the microwave. The pasta was cooked well. The sauce, while simple marinara, was really good. Just enough seasoning to make it taste good without taking away from the great tomato taste. The marinara was also chunky and not pureed or watery or runny.Overall a very good product that I would eat again.

This Barilla brand meal comes in a microwavable dish and needs no refrigeration or freezing. I have tried other brands and they do not compare too this in taste. Plus the other brands I have tried all required the addition of water too the noodles before microwaving and this does not. Easy too store and cook!The Penne with Marinara Sauce is microwaved in its container for only sixty seconds and the pasta came out just fine. The marinara sauce was flavorful and when mixed made for a fast and delicious meal. I found it enjoyable and as I can no longer lift boiling water this is an excellent alternative. Not as good as home made but much better than canned pasta and other brands of microwavable meals I have tried. I would get this again.

I am a professor and associate dean at a local college, so my days are typically long and I rarely have time to make or buy food. Usually, I will grab a frozen meal to throw in the microwave at work. But this is not ideal because...well...we all know the good and bad of frozen meals. So when I saw that there was another option, I became extremely excited! I grabbed one of these meals and brought it to work. It is perfect! There are specific instructions on how long to microwave and what to microwave. When you follow the instructions, it is a really good meal! I won't say that it tastes exactly like when I make pasta at home, but it's definitely a better option than your typical frozen meals.

column9: Tastes FRESH and it is actually filling
column10: This product is hands down one of the BEST shelf stable meals on the market. It is easy to prepare but I do caution to pay close attention to the packaging as the sauce is separate from the pasta and you don't want to splash your clothing when you take the plastic film off after cooking so hold the bowl firmly.  The sauce is rich and has chunks of fresh tasting tomatoes,basil, oregano and other spices that you can SEE and more importantly taste! The pasta is cooked but firm and it holds up well to the rich sauce. There are NO preservatives which makes it even more remarkable for being so flavorful. I would highly recommend these for a quick lunch or to use as a mid afternoon snack if you are having a late dinner. I want to try all the varieties!

column9: Mediocre but passable in a pinch
column10: I can't say that I recommend the Barilla Mezze Penne with Traditional Marinara Sauce but neither can I pan it. Let me start off by saying that I do not usually eat microwaveable meals (i.e., soups, canned pastas, frozen dinners, etc.), not because I have anything against them, but because I can't find any that I like. So, I was very much looking forward to trying this simple pasta dish with marinara sauce, hoping I might finally find a quick, easy meal that I like. I was skeptical that the pasta would come out firm enough for my liking and was pleasantly surprised that the pasta was a fairly decent firm texture to it when cooked according to the regular cooking instructions. (There are additional instructions for those who prefer their pasta softer.) While the texture was good, the flavor was not so great. The sauce tasted OK but the pasta itself had a slightly "off" flavor to it that would push past the sauce flavor if you didn't put enough sauce on it. If you scooped up enough sauce with it, I found it to be OK (not good, but OK). My teenage daughter also tried it and she did not notice an "off" taste to the pasta but did find the sauce to be a little to "tangy" after eating about half of the portion.Preparation was easy. You peel back a small corner of the plastic and microwave for 1 minute. That's it. I did have a little trouble removing the plastic cover once it was cooked. I really had to finesse it carefully so as to avoid spilling the sauce all over the place, but other than that, it couldn't have been easier.All in all, this pasta is palatable if you are in a pinch but it's certainly nothing to look forward to.

When you sit down to eat one of these microwave meals you don't usually expect much. In this case I was pleasantly surprised.  The sauce had a good flavor and the noodles didn't taste like cardboard. For a quick lunch at work or at home this would be a good choice.

I was pleasantly surprised by this pasta meal. My last experience with microwavable pasta was Kraft Easy Mac, and this Barilla product is a huge step forward!The pasta is precooked, so it needs just 60 seconds to heat up. I was afraid of either too hard or soft pasta, but after 60 seconds in the microwave, it was a pleasant al dente. The sauce (which heats beside the pasta in a removable cup) tastes wonderful--neither too sweet nor too acidic. It is a chunky sauce, and the tomato chunks seemed a little slimy. That's probably not a problem for most people, but as a texture person, I didn't enjoy it.Overall, though, this is a great product. It's certainly much better than a brown bag lunch!

column9: Nice Taste But Package Difficult to Open
column10: I frequently buy Barilla pasta sauces, so I was prepared for the sauce to be pleasing and was not disappointed. The pasta was not overcooked if one followed the directions -- I even added another 20 seconds after opening the product and it still had a good texture, slightly chewy, which I like. Both the sauce and the pasta have all natural ingredients, and no preservatives. This would make a good lunch to have on hand in the workplace, as the soft-canning method of producing microwaveable products is becoming more popular. They cook faster than frozen entrees and have the advantage of being stored in one's desk. At only 320 calories, the Mezze Penne with Sauce lunch is satisfying without overloading the diner with calories. As with all pasta, it is high in carbs, which is not an issue for me but I do know people who try to keep their carbs lower. Because sugar is only 7 grams and carbs are 58 grams, there should be no blood sugar spike as occurs when the sugar and carb grams are closer in number. Each serving has 11 grams of protein and 6 of dietary fiber. The one draw back on the nutrition front is the amount of sodium in the serving: 700 mg is close to 1/4 to 1/3 of what most people should be striving to achieve on a daily basis, so you would have to watch your sodium intake for the rest of the day. I sprinkled a little over two teaspoons of grated Parmesan cheese on the pasta, which which brought the sodium content up to about 800 mg. The addition of the cheese was not really necessary, but I generally always add it to pasta dishes.My big problem with the product was the design of the package. It is awkward to open. It has a sauce dish and a pasta dish -- one is supposed to keep a thumb firmly on the sauce dish while at the same time pulling back the film with the other hand, otherwise you could burn your hand with hot sauce while attempting to remove the film. I finally gave up tugging on the film and used a knife to cut it open. The sauce dish then separated from the rest of the container and I poured it over the cooked pasta. Since I am retired, I don't usually buy frozen or soft-canned convenience food, but when I was working I found it to be easy to take to work. I might keep it on hand now for lunch if I don't have time to prepare something more substantial.

I don't know why I was surprised that this product tastes so good, but I was.  Perhaps it stems from the fact that I've been disappointed in microwave meals so often in the past.  I can now put all that behind me and make sure I have an assortment of these convenient meals in the house for quick, convenient, but most importantly, tasty meals.The packaging is designed so that the pasta sauce and penne noodles stay separate until you mix them together.  I liked it just fine the way the noodles turned out after the 60 seconds, but if you want yours a little softer there are directions for how to do that.  This traditional marinara sauce has lovely chunks of tomato in it.  There are other ingredients also, but nothing overpowers so it all blends well together.  At 24% of daily dietary fiber this is a good source of fiber, but you might need to watch out for the 29% of sodium.This was really a tasty meal which would be good for both lunch or dinner.  I added a salad with mine and it was certainly an ample amount.  I like that it is 100% natural and I like that there are no preservatives added.  And the carton is even made from recycled paper.  So I enjoyed the taste, had an ample serving size (9 oz at 320 calories), and even put the outside cover in my recycle bin so it can be useful again.  Not bad!

column9: Probably the Best Microwave Pasta Meal I've Had.
column10: "Barilla Mezze Penne with Traditional Marinara Sauce" is a 9 oz (255 g) single serving microwave meal that heats up in just one minute. Mezze Penne is smaller than traditional penne, and these have a ridged surface to better hold the sauce. The marinara sauce has a few chunks of tomato in a tomato-herb sauce. The sauce is in a separate container inside the oval serving bowl. Preparation is fast and easy: Peel back the film on the bowl to the dotted line to give it some ventilation. Microwave for 60 seconds. Remove the film carefully to peel it from the pasta bowl as well, where it tends to stick. Pour the sauce over the pasta, stir, and enjoy!My experience with microwave pasta meals is pasta that is overdone on the edges and sauce that is cooked to the bowl in places. Separating the pasta from the sauce has solved some problems. This meal is both tastier, faster, and has better consistency than a frozen microwave dinner. I'm very particular about jarred pasta sauces. Rao's is the only brand I'll buy. Barilla does not make the best jarred sauce, but it is not bad. The sauce is flavorful. The chunks of tomato are few but have good consistency. The pasta was not quite soft enough for me, however. The instructions recommend adding 1 teaspoon of water and microwaving for an additional 30 seconds for softer pasta.This Barilla Penne with Marinara Sauce was better than I expected it to be. It's easily as good as frozen pasta meals that are heated on the stovetop, yet this takes less than 2 minutes from start to finish, and it's convenient for one person. The bowl does not get hot, and it's easy to hold onto from one side that has a wider lip, so it would make a nice quick meal at the office or over a cluttered desk. You don't really have to put the bowl down to eat from it. It contains no preservatives, artificial color, or artificial flavors.Ingredients: cooked mezze penne pasta (water, semolina, durum flour, olive oil, salt, natural flavors), marinara sauce (tomatoes, citric acid, tomato paste, water, carrot puree, olive oil, onion puree, tapioca starch, celery puree, sugar, salt, garlic puree, basil, oregano, natural flavors). Contains per serving: 320 calories, 700mg sodium, 58g carbohydrates, 5g total fat, 1g saturated fat, 11g protein, 180 mcg vitamin A.

This microwavable shelf-stable meal from Barilla is surprisingly tasty. It takes only 60 seconds to heat up (unless you add some water to the pasta after the initial 1-minute cooking period and reheat it for 30 more seconds in order to soften the noodles a bit--which I did, and which I recommend). The marinara sauce heats separately from the pasta in a small container attached to the main tray; you simply pour it over the noodles and enjoy. I was impressed by how evenly everything cooked and how well the pasta and the sauce mixed. The noodles were tender, and if you've tried Barilla's jarred sauces, you can expect an almost identical flavor in this meal. At only 320 calories, this is an economical, tasty, and sensible lunch choice.

I'm always on the lookout for lunches I can take to work and store several in my desk without refrigeration, but that don't taste like pre-prepared food.  This Barilla pasta fits the bill perfectly.  The pasta is already cooked to perfection, and it is stored separately from the sauce, so you don't end up with a watery mess like some competitor products.  The sauce is flavorful enough to be interesting without being overwhelming.  It's a filling meal that is definitely staying on my shopping list.

The Barilla Mezze Penne tastes great. What impressed me the most though is the design of the package. Pop it in the microwave and the dish is ready in 60 seconds. Quick and easy and tasty. Just be careful when moving the sauce over the pasta. It is easy to spill over. I will be getting more of this.

I really prefer the Hormel pasta packages.  They only need to be put in the microwave - there's no subsequent stirring, etc. like you have with the Barilla packages.  These are very tasty though - don't get me wrong.  I like the food.  I just find the Hormel pasta packages preferable because they're more convenient.  Otherwise, these are quite good.

column9: Ok but there are better Barillas.

Sorry, this was a disaster from the beginning...Here's what just happened...This meal is not frozen, so I followed the instructions as provided. Note that I do use this type of packaged meal quite often, although normally frozen.The package says to pull the top back exposing sauce tray...I did...I microwaved it for 60 seconds. It was not done...I found this out by having part of the sauce fall out all over the place! Fortunately for my hand, it felt cool, thus I knew it wasn't even hot enough to consider eating...At that point, I saw that the sauce was in a separate container and, though holding it by my thumb as explained I had to pull so hard (something I didn't realize I would be doing or I would have cut it open) to continue to get the top off, that the sauce flew out, together with the separate cup coming partially out!Packaging is definitely a problem! I've never had this type of issue with any other company's product and that includes Stouffers down to Banquet which is just about the least expensive of this type of food...I then tasted the pasta...Now I like al dente...but this just was not done.For this type of food, I taste it to see how it "tastes" as made by the company. I was disappointed.Soooooo, I added onion and garlic power, salt, pepper and a little buttered oil...THEN I cooked it an additional minute beyond the instructions. Note that my microwave heats high and I rarely use the time suggested...so I have confidence that the instructions for heating will not make the meal hot enough for any microwave...With all the additional herbs/spices, I was able to enjoy the pasta.For 320 calories, I've tasted better and more pasta coming from other companies. There is no sweetner which I usually add to my own spaghetti, but I didn't add that for this trial. Without anything, this would be a very bland meal indeed.The sauce and pasta itself was fine for basic ingredients...but given the packaging, poor instructions, and lack of any "true taste" in the sauce. I certainly wouldn't buy it nor recommend it. Given the name, I had expected a tasty Italian sauce. Better check out Stouffers--their sauce needs little added, if anything! Too bad, because a package that does not require refrigeration would be useful to working people.
