And my husband started a saying then "an opened bag of these chips is and empty bag of these chips"  and once we came home we could not find them anywhere. No store around our town of Grand Junction Colorado carried the baked cheddar chips. So I looked to Amazon and there they were. So now we have them available and we will order more. Yesterday we had sandwiches for lunch and as my husband ate the last few chips and crumpled the bag up he said" an opened bag of chips is an empty bag and he laughed. They really are good tasting chips whether a person is watching their calorie intake or not. We will buy them again!

These chips are the best snack since the invention of chips themselves. They are actual baked potato chips, not potato powder or potato starch. And after you see the nutrition facts you wont feel guilty eating them!! Try them and you will be sold!

column9: Fantastic ! Best baked potato chip ever.
column10: These potato chips are absolutely the best baked potato chip I have ever tried.  They are so good that my husband and son will also eat them.  In fact, my college-aged son says he prefers these over the greasy regular potato chip.  With 65% less fat and baked, they are a healthy alternative to regular potato chips.  We got the lightly salted because husband is watching his blood pressure and these are perfect with just a touch of sea salt on them.  Sodium is lower than Lays baked and the taste is much better.  These look and taste like real potato chips, unlike Lays Baked which don't even look real.  Highly recommend these.
The best baked chips I've ever tried.  Yummy!  Also, crunchy enough to satisfy that urge to munch.  And low fat and not too bad on sodium content either.
These chips are the best I ever had.Very low in fat and taste great, I just wish they had less salt like amazon says they are.

These chips are the best chips ever. They are thick and crispy. No chip compares.These chips are gluten free. And should be considered a gluten free grocery. Ordering by the case really saves money compared to grocery store.
These chips are low fat 3 grams a serving very firm chip great for dips or just to eat all I can say Is I set up delivery 15 bags every 3 months. Yummy! Chuck from Baltimore

The chips that were delivered have little to no barbeque seasoning on them which makes them pretty bland.  I get seasoning on every third chip.  Keep in mind it is the seasoning that makes the chips worth buying.

They taste great while you're eating them...but wheeeeew...the aftertaste is awful.  Not only that, it's very hard to get rid of.  I like the sea salt, and the white cheddar, but the sea salt and vinegar is the my favorite (very, very, salty).

My son will only eat these hickory honey baked chips from Kettle Baked. He says their taste can't be beat. They are always sold out in our area so we buy them from AMAZON for the BEST deal! Stick with Amazon for the greatest bargains online.
I love these chips.  I no longer crave regular potato chips!!  They are so tasty and crunchy!! Alot of salt tho!!

I really love these potato chips.  It is great that they are made from real potatoes and do not contain any genetically modified ingredients or msgs like most other brands of chips.  This is a really great price for them as well.

column9: It's really hard to believe they could be this good!!
column10: I have been a fan of the Kettle Bakes for a long time now.  They truly are the best chips available anywhere.  In my opinion they are far better in every way than any brand of fried potato chips, not counting Fritos, which aren't potato chips anyway.  I don't see how they could really be improved.  The crunch is fantastic, the flavor is fantastic, and you sacrifice nothing but greasy fingers!  I have tried every flavor, and my favorite is definitely the Aged White Cheddar, but you won't see me turn my back from the BBQ, or the Lightly Salted.  The Salt and Pepper flavor is a bit peppery, so if you like that then you'll like them, and I even eat them sometimes.  The Salt and Vinegar doesn't work for me, but then I'm not a fan of vinegar potato chips anyway.Just buy these, please, any flavor that tickles your fancy.And then you can thank me later.=)

When I received this item it was labeled "Sea Salt." In  fact, the Sea Salt version of these chips is also described as "lightly salted," so you might think the two were one and the same. However, these are listed as having 115g of sodium per serving, while the Sea Salt version has 135g of sodium per serving. If this matters to you like it matters to me, stipulate that you receive the Lightly Salted version ONLY.

I wish I could be responding more favorably, but this is my honest experience.  I was excited to find lightly salted and low fat kettle chips on Amazon at a good price.  I was going to have them delivered every six months.  When I got my first order I got seasalted chips instead of lightly.  I called about it and they put through another order at no charge to me.  Second order again wrong chips.  So I called and cancelled automatic delivery.  The chips are good except they are a little too hard and hard on my gums.  Also too salty for me.  The above should have read (lightly salted)I have to admit though that I do like the chips because they are lower fat and may order again.  I just wish I could have gotten lightly salted ones.  "Thank you.  Irene Zalonski (zalonski @sbcglobal.net)
really, that's all i have to say! The chips can be a little....uh...crunchy at times, so watch the roof of your mouth, but the flavor is great.  I hope Amazon carries the salt and pepper ones soon!

This is the only company I know of that makes baked potato chips from sliced potatoes, rather than from reconstituted potatoes. It makes a real difference in flavor and texture. For those new to the product, expect something more like a baked potato than like a french fry.

column9: Excellent alternative to fat fried chips
column10: Full of flavour and crunch without the oily aftertaste,fantastic product. YummmmPackaging needs to better or UPS more careful when handling.
Being a chip lover from way back, these are among the best.  Where so many other baked chips taste like cardboard, these actually taste like a potato.  LOVE these chips.

column9: Like no other baked chip! Delicious but expensive
column10: I love these Kettle brand baked chips!  They are so close in texture and flavor to regular fried chips.  I just wish they were less expensive.  They really are greatly reduced in fat content as well.No other baked chip comes close.  I wonder how they do it?

Loved these chips.  They taste like real potatoes with less than one half the fat of regular chips.  I can eat these without feeling guilty and without sacrificing taste.  Eat them alone or with your favorite dips, and they are delicious.  When I found these I realized I don't have to give up one of my favorite snacks. If you are a potato chip fan but feel you have to eliminate chips from your diet, try these.  I did, and now I am a real fan.

Good alternative to the typical baked potatoe chips which are usually filled with other additives like corn and artificial ingredients. They're relatively low fat and taste like the real thing. My only complaint is that they are very salty even thought the manufacturer claims that they are "lightly salted".

I first tasted these on a trip to NYC and my wife and I were hooked.  Tough to find them around here and I was thrilled to find them on Amazon.  No other baked chip even comes close to these - you would swear they were kettle fried chips but with no greasy feel.  Our current favorite snack!

column9: Kettle Bakes are my #1 favorite potato chip.
column10: If you are craving Potato Chips and Dieting this is one to check out..They are better then traditional Potato Chips.  3grams fat per serving..it is remarkable..Try them and you will love them.

We are always searching for low fat, lower calorie snack foods to satisfy our strong snacking needs. These chips are one of the best we have ever found. They are delicious and satisfying and have only 120 calories per serving. They are terribly expensive at our local supermarkets, but  Amazon offers a great price!

Bought the pack of 15 and made the mistake of having them delivered to my office.  They were consumed in a week...couldn't keep anyone's hands off them, even those that are discriminating about eating healthily.  Great, crispy and super tasty. Yummy, yum yum!!! :-)

column9: not too salty and not greasy
column10: If you're a big potato chip fan, you might find these a little unusual because they are baked.  I personally am not big on the greasiness that most potato chips have, so I actually prefer a baked chip like this.  I also like that these chips have a little less salt than most chips, so the potato flavor really comes through.Let's face it:  a potato chip is never going to be a truly healthy snack.  Even without the extra fat that comes from frying and without the excess salt, a chip is still a bunch of simple carbohydrates.  If you can control yourself and not scarf down bags at a time, however, this is a reasonable indulgence to add to your diet on occasion.

These chips are great and so is the price! Other low calorie potato chips are made from a potato batter and usually have added sugar. These are real chips that taste great. Bet you can't eat just one.
These are great. Low fat, low calorie, low in sodium and taste good. A perfect snack. What more can we ask for?

I am so impressed with these chips, especially compared to the other brand of baked chips I've tried. The texture is very similar to the original kettle chips, plus there is a little fiber in each serving which is nice to see in a snack. I will certainly buy again!

My husband and I are on Weight Watchers and eat these chips frequently because they are much lower in fat than regular chips. One serving is equal to 2 Weight Watchers points (old point system). It seems that the local stores are always out of them so I ordered through Amazon, but was disappointed in the freshness date. All 15 bags had a freshness date of August 11, which was much too close to the date ordered. The ones I bought at the grocery store in June had a freshness date of October. Although we eat these almost daily, we won't be able to consume 15 bags by August 11, and did not want to be bothered with the hassle of returning them.

column9: Best Chips Ever - Non-greasy and Crispy
column10: These are the best chips on the market. They are very crispy and tasty. Because they are baked, they are not greasy. Also, they are not as salty as other chips. I love mine with beer.
These are my favorite chips now-bar none. They are crispy, delicious and are actually made with real potatoes...two thumbs way up!

These chips are amazing.  Though baked (i.e., much healthier than regular chips), they have a great and thick crunch to them.  The ingredients list is also pleasantly short:  potatoes, safflower/sunflower oil, and sea salt.  It's rare to find such a high-quality pre-packaged product these days.  Only real negative is price, but buying on Amazon helps in that regard.
These baked chips have a great crunch. Best baked chips I've had to date.  Not totally like fried, but a delicious way to cut fat and salt.
The chips taste good, are low in fat and easy to digest.  However, the company keeps sending me the sea salted instead of the low sodium version.

Kettle brand Baked Potato Chips are the best baked chips I have ever eaten.  They are real sliced potatoes (unlike some brands that are "compressed" chips).  They only have 3g of fat and 135mg of sea salt per 1 oz. serving but you can't tell that by their taste.  I have trouble finding them in my local stores, so this is a great way to buy them at an excellent price and keep extra bags on hand.

These chips have some of the best barbecue flavor of any chip without all the grease. The texture is a little hard, so sometimes if I get a thick chip it hurts my teeth. But the taste is worth it!  The irregularity of the size and shape of the chips tells you that they're real, not something created in a lab. Plus through Amazon I save almost 50% off the grocery store price!I just wish Amazon carried the baked salt and vinegar flavor. It exists, but is not easy to find. I manage to snag some every few months or so but at almost $4 a bag I can't really stock up the way I could if they were available through Amazon.

column9: Better healthy chips compared to most
column10: Great baked chips, but it taste most like sour-cream-and-onions than cheddar. It still a great product.

column9: I have died and gone to Heaven
column10: I love potato chips, but since I have an "efficient metabolism," I can't eat them. However, I can eat these! They are low in fat and calories but the are DELICIOUS and taste better than regular chips. Try them!!

column9: Much better than other baked chips
column10: These are my favorite chips.  Very crunchy and tasty.  Not processed and mealy like other baked chips.  You'd never know you were eating a reduced fat product.  The best!!!

These Kettles bake chips are the best!  They taste like fried chips, but they're not, so much healthier for you.  I have trouble finding them in stores, so I've started buying them on Amazon by the case...  we use them up!

Yum, yum, yum! These baked chips are so delicious I keep forgetting they're baked. They taste like thick fried kettle chips. My husband prefers lightly salted chips, and he was thrilled with these. We only have a couple bags left and will order more when they go on sale again. My only complaint is that they're a tad pricey.In case you're wondering how big a 4 oz bag of chips is, the bags are in-between the larger bags you usually find at the supermarket and the small individual serving bags you might get at a sub shop. The nutritional info says each bag contains four servings. Well, of course, that depends on your appetite and restraint, but I'd say it's more like a two-serving bag.  :)I received the chips on August 30, and the expiration date is December 14... So I wouldn't order these if you don't think you'll eat them within a few months. Not a problem in our house!

These potato chips rock.  I've been looking for a low-fat real potato baked chip for a long time and I finally found it.  What's even better, it tastes like a real potato chip.  Not those other baked chips that taste like a salted piece of dried plastic potato mush.  Love these chips.

Well, baked potato chips have finally gone mainstream after years of being some obscure brand in the store that you bring home and just try to eat while they crumble in your hand and taste bland while they're doing it.Now some of the big national snack companies have "baked" chips, but why are they shaped like hexagons?  Some of those baked chips from national manufacturers look like the result of some mad scientist experiment.Not these!  These look like somebody sliced up potato and baked it in such a way that they still hold their structural integrity when the process is complete.  They're crispy just like traditional potato chips and the seasoning is balanced just right.  Once I get through this box I'm looking forward to trying other flavors.

These are great chips, relatively low in fat and calories. A great snack when you have the craving for something slightly salty.Glad they have these on Amazon. Can't find this inexpensively anywhere else, when you can find them at all.

These Kettle Bakes potato chips are incredibly good.  They have a more intense potato taste, and they are not too salty like a lot of other baked chips.  If you open the bag, heaven help you because you are probably going to eat the whole thing.  Luckily, the bags only contain 4 oz.

These are great chips, low in fat, high in potassium. When I had difficulty finding them in Publix, I cheched out Amazon.com. Happy that I did. Not only is it more convenient, but less expensive, also!

Kettle's hickory honey BBQ chips are fantastic! There are a lot of snacks on the market that are supposedly healthier alternatives to their full-fat counterparts, but in my experience, reducing the "bad stuff" usually causes similar reductions in taste and quality. Moreover, in cutting out the fat, almost every snack adds artificial sweeteners, fillers, preservatives, or fat substitutes, nearly all of which can be health concerns for consumers. (For example, any product with sucralose/Splenda in it makes me extremely ill!)However, with Kettle's chips, consumers can easily identify all of the ingredients in the package, and in the baked chips, you can essentially eat an entire bag for about the same amount of fat you'll find in a single serving of most other brands of chips. Even better, the BBQ flavor is really great in these chips, ensuring that your snack is really satisfying and truly filling your cravings. I love the fact that more salty snack options are appearing on the market, and I hope that Kettle continues its trend of producing simple, healthy, and absolutely tasty products. I guarantee that chip lovers will not be disappointed by this yummy offering...

column9: Potato Chips are Back on the Menu :D !
column10: If you crave real potato chip taste without all the fat, this product is for you. If you've bought other 'low fat' chips and were disgusted, just try one more - this brand.  They look and taste like real potato chips, because they are.  A green company, and a great product.

It is unusual to find the perfect snack food that dazzles bag after bag.  They are almost addicting which is a good thing in this case.  I feel it is safe and not going to do too much damage to the health conscience system.  More to it than a baked potato but almost halfway healthy.  The flavor of course and the crunch texture make this chip a rare masterpiece of monstrous culinary excellence.  Good job there Northwest.  Wish I could find a life coach that was this good.
I love Kettle's baked lightly salted chips. They taste better than regular chips, are less greasy, and have a terrific crunch!!!!
Product was fabulous but I would like to be able to purchase 1 ounce bags

column9: good but definitely taste different from fried chips
column10: these are good, not like the baked lays that are made with processed potato flakes.
Great flavor, much lower fat than regular chip. Good to have healthy alternatives for children (and their parents!!)...
best low calorie chip yet.  hard to tell that they are baked.  very, very good!!
These chips took me about 5 minutes to get used too. It tastes and smells just like aged white cheddar chips should, very strong.
Just received this from amazon, great condition and fast shipping. Great buy, 15 bags for $20...crispy chips with just the right amount of seasoning.  Much cheaper, than buying one bag for $4...
These are nothing short of amazing. So good you hardly miss real chips. We keep re-ordering them and the whole family. They definately fit the good and (sort of) good for you (at least not too bad!).

I have fallen in love with these chips. They taste great and I can eat a handful for less than 100 calories. A great little treat to have in my desk at work and on the counter at home. Try them they're great!!!
These are the best chips EVER!  Fantastic potato flavor and crunch.  I don't even want regular chips again.  You will not be disappointed!

These are absolutely the best tasting baked chips out there.  You can't even tell they are baked except that they're not greasy.  Great flavor - though I  think they would be even better if they put even more seasoning on them.
These are a great snack for those who love potato chips and want to watch their fat intake.  The flavor is very delicious!
These are great baked potato chips for those who are watching their fat intake!  Love them!

column9: Weird after-taste for me (try one bag before you buy a box)
column10: I bought a box of these baked barbeque Kettle brand chips from Amazon in somewhat larger-sized bags, because they came so highly recommended by other reviewers, but I really don't care for them at all (though other people to whom I've offered them  munch through them quite happily, and are pleased to take the rest of the bag home with them when I make the offer).  I can only conclude that individual palates may respond very differently to these particular chips.So, if you've bought a bag of Kettle's baked chips in this particular flavor recently in your local grocery store and found them quite tasty, you'll probably be quite happy with buying these by the box-full from Amazon.However, if you haven't yet tried them, do NOT invest in a multi-bag shipment until you first discover whether or not these particular chips appeal to your particular palate.I'm busy giving away every bag I bought, because I developed a distaste for them after eating the first few chips from the first bag I opened (which I ended up throwing away half-full).  But my dislike for these baked barbecue-flavor chips from Kettle brand (whose other, 'full-fat' chips I've almost always relished) is definitely a minority opinion among my friends and neighbors, so far.

column9: Great chips, but a little too salty for my liking
column10: Considering these are baked, they are very tasty.  They are super crispy and taste like fried goodness, but without the oiliness.  The only bad thing I have to say is that these are supposed to be "lightly" salted but I still found them overly salty (that's why I only gave it 3 stars). I actually found the Baked Salt & Malt Vinegar ones less salty than these. So for those watching their sodium intake or don't like things too salty, then you may want to consider the other flavors.

column9: Not as good as I hoped
column10: I had high hopes for these chips, I love the Kettle Brand and I love cheddar. But they were TOO crisp,they were sharp and hard. And the taste was salty but it didn't remind me of good aged cheddar at all.

column4: R. W. Taylor "Wil O' The Wisp"
column10: I hope that one day this snack can reach the point where it is truly healthy and consistently good.A) Claiming to be healthy, at least - last bag I munched on had nutrition info that would in one serving give you the bare minimum healthy cholesterol score (<300) for an entire DAY. Many snacks do this. Like peanuts. Or popcorn. The idea is that since the products are from 'natural' sources, there is less control over the batch. But seriously - less than 300mg per serving? Give me a break. This gives no one trying to help themselves in this area any hope of control. It's almost like writing a blank check. To yourself. To state that your product's single serving falls less than the daily total max recommended is garbage. Read the label.B) The batches may be uneven in cholesterol, and they may avoid legal issues by setting it at the 'max'. But the uneven textures and flavors you may get (I consumed, along with family and friends, several cases of these over 2 years or so) don't add up, either. I had burnt tones, teeth-cracking textures at times.I used to love these chips, much as the majority of the reviews portray. I thought I was enjoying at the least a fair product, staying healthy, keeping the fat away. But - they are simply simple carbs with a little twist of fat that get you by in the place of their higher-fat brethren. In case you are not sure of where I stand, I am one of those people who think carb-laden chips are not a great food. You don't miss health until you lose it. These chips will not help your health. They might, at best, make it slightly less worse than everyday chips - at twice or more the price.A leading non-profit consumer org concluded this was 'junk health food'. They cited other causes, as well. I wholeheartedly concur that this is not a healthy food. It is a junk food that is masquerading as one.ADDENDUM:Just got around to adding this. My wife purchased a bag of the "Hickory Honey BBQ" at the beginning of July. They were real dental-rattlers, uneven but thick-cut and baked into seriously hard material. The spices were horribly uneven.Lot mark: 12JUL12 090227921:37

I've ordered this item three times.  Lightly salted, right?  Three times I've gotten my order, and three times it's been wrong.  Very disappointing.The chips themselves are very tasty, though...just WAY too salty for me.
The chips have dark rings from overcooking and have a burnt taste. I contacted manufacturer but no reply. Hugh disappointment.

So you want some tasty flavorful potato chips, seriously why bother with these. Please understand they are baked. Even so, they taste like seasoned cardboard. Ur better off with a rice cake. Or how about you walk around the block and then enjoy a handful of the standard kettle chips, well worth it!This product Skip!

I bought these shells for a rather unusual reason: housing for my colony of shell-dwelling cichlids, Neolamprologus multifasciatus. On the off chance a fellow fish fancier is looking for shells, these are the ones you want. They're 100% clean (no soaking required), and the perfect size for any of the shelldwellers. My multis just hatched out their first batch of eggs in one.I can't say how good they are for serving escargots in, but if you're breeding any of the Tanganyika shelldwellers, you can't go wrong with a box of these shells, and the price is right. They arrived in perfect condition, without any breakage. One box will furnish up to a 20-gallon aquarium.

I also bought these shells for my shell dwelling cichlids. The shells are a nice size for multies and arrived in excellent condition. I just washed them off real quick and laid them across the bottom. My multies quickly began picking out their new homes. Awesome product!

column9: good usable shells arived in 1 piece
column10: I used these to cook Roland snailsRoland Giant Snails (12 Count), 7.75-Ounce Cans (Pack of 12)These shells were large enough to perform the task at hand for those snails which I thought were large. If they were much larger it might have not produced a good enough seal around the snail to keep the butter in. I call them "just right"

I bought these shells based on an earlier review saying these are great shells for shell dwelling cichlids.  And they're everything anyone could look for in a shell for this purpose...they're very pretty shells and lightweight so the tiny fish can move them where they want them.  They were packaged carefully so none were broken or cracked. I was really surprised at the quality for such a great price.  They're definitely 5 stars.

After reading the reviews, I too bought these shells for Tanganyikan cichlids, and I was very surprised and happy to see that so many people were reviewing these shells for this purpose rather than just for haute cuisine!Due to a childhood with French food fanatics,  I do also know that these shells would be great for use when serving escargots as well.  They arrived in great shape in terms of minimal breakage because the shells clearly belonged to sturdy, well fed and cared for snails (before the...tragedy)!  The company also makes sure that the shells are cleaned, so that they are hygienic enough for a kitchen and, thus, they would make for a great presentation on the table right out of the box with a cursory rinsing.They are beautiful, and I plan on buying another box just to put in a vase on display.In fact, I would recommend them across the board-- whether you are looking for homes for cichlid shell dwellers, are a food fanatic or French person (same difference), or are just looking for a beautiful decoration!  You have to love a product that covers so many needs!!!

Like most, I purchased these escargot shells for a fish tank setup (30 gallon). None of the shells were broken when the packages were open and they look natural in the tank. Highly recommended, especially with the low price.
I bought these months ago for my L. multifasciatus. I think that these shells are perfect for them. Just add water.

Like many others I purchased these for my shell-dwelling Cichlids.  Absolutely perfect!  I ordered two boxes.  There was not one broken shell out of 72 shells.  They are uniform large shells and are very, very clean.  You cannot go wrong with these.  Absolutely great shells!

column9: Works perfect for African Shell Dweller fish!!
column10: I bought these to use in my African Shell dweller aquarium and they are perfect!! One box of these is good enough for a 20g long setup and although there were a couple cracked ones none of them were broken to the point of being unusable. They look great in the tank too!!

I am a Tropical fish enthusiast and wanted to set up a new aquarium.  The "shelldwellers" from the African Lake Tang. require many shells for their homes.  These shells, with stripped coloration, made a nice contrast to the white sand substrate, and are the perfect size for my "multies."  Fast service, quick delivery, terrific product and price!
These shells are perfect for Shelldwellers from Lake Tanganyika!  Multies, Occies, and the rest of those awesome little fish!  Take it from a fish head like me, get 4 boxes!

column9: PERFECT PRODUCT FOR AN UNUSUAL PURPOSE
column10: Like some other buyers, I found this product a perfect solution to my need, but not for the purpose that the manufacturer intended.  You see, I too have an aquarium for Tanganyikan cichlids - some of which are shell dwellers.  Appropriate shells for these fish are difficult to find as these fish are rather rare.Internet sites (including Ebay) and Tropical Fish stores did not really offer good solutions. The shells must have large round openings, be lightweight (so the fish can move them to their liking) and offer a roomy interior (for breading and hiding).  The Escargot shells are all that and the perfect size as well!!!The price was reasonable, shipping was fast and I was amazed that none of the shells were broken.

I too use these snail shells for shell dwelling fish.  These shells are perfect for them.  They are the right size, have good deep colors, and out of the two packages I've ordered, only 3 shells were cracked.  Overall very good product.  I would order them again.
The shells came in promtly and in great packaging.  I really pleased my guests who were lookin forward to this entrey.

column9: Good quality, unfortunate error in counting
column10: I recently ordered some shells (in order to cook escargot) from another website (the frenchy bee). Poor quality (alot of broken shells) so I decided to order from this place since the reviews were much better!  I must say, these are a better quality shell. Thicker than the previous ones and very few shells were chipped.  Out of 72 shells, I had 1 broken one, 2 chipped and 5 that were non-existent. It only came with a total of 67 shells.  It's a simple counting error.  I honestly would buy from them again because the quality was very good.  Much better from "the french bee"!  They were a very very good price too!

They should change the name of this product to Premium Shell-Dwelling Cichlid Shells. I brought these shells for my colony of Neolamprologus multifasciatus cichlids and these shells were perfect.  None of them were cracked and it was just the right size for my cichlids, if not bigger.  My cichlids spawned in the shells just two days after I put them in the tank.  If you are looking for shells for your "multies" or shell-dwelling cichlids you should purchase these shells.  They are light, clean and perfect! And at a great price too!

column9: Good quality, but so so package
column10: The shell is good for cooking snail, but it was not well packed and I got some cracked shells I believe they were damaged during delivery.

The shells were in good shape with no breakage of any in any boxes I purchased. They had good color, although I hoped the shells would have been larger.  I used them to fill a large glass urn I bought at Pottery Barn. They look beautiful in there.

My dog is used to MilkBones... she clearly likes these way better. They must even smell great, because she is not usually entirely attentive for the "sit" to get her treat, and I had her full attention with these from the get go.OTOH, she always likes anything "new", so the real test will be whether she likes them in a few months. But they are a big hit right now!

I haven't used them long enough to see a visible difference but my 4 Chihuahuas seem to like them. This is the perfect size for a dog 5-10lbs.The mini bones are not too hard or too soft so it keeps them occupied for a while as they go to work. My dogs are spoiled and they eat these.

To see if the claims were true I decided to do a taste test with the Hartz Crunch 'N Clean bone-shaped biscuits and chop-shaped treats from another national brand.Not having been snubbed before with the chops, I was somewhat surprised to see my pups choose the Crunch 'N Clean biscuits first.  These dogs have never been known to be choosy eaters, and all the biscuits were eventually consumed, but it was apparent they they liked the flavor of the Crunch 'N Clean treats.The biscuits have a texture similar to whole wheat Danish crisp-bread just not as tasty or savory (yes, I tried one, too).  They also break into pieces with uneven edges to help scrape off gunk from tooth enamel.So all in all the dogs like the flavor of the biscuits, the treats are crunchy, and the texture helps keep their teeth clean.Pretty good.

My little Maltese liked these a LOT.  They're really hard, so I'm sure they're good scrubbers on his teeth.  Although they call these small, I wish they were a bit smaller (they are about 2 inches long by about 1 inch at the wide part of the bone).  Generally I would break a biscuit this size in half for him (but he's only 7 lbs, so for a "normal" dog they would be fine).

column9: Crunchy, Smelled Good, Large, Heavy on Wheat
column10: Our Ridgebacks and Dobermans all scarfed these up immediately. Opening the box the treats smelled fresh, there was no greasy feel to them when I handled them and they did not have that icky odor that some of the chemical coated red colored, cheap biscuits have. I also liked that each biscuit was really large and thick. Even the elderly dogs liked them and the 16 year old Doberman with very few teeth left had little trouble eating this biscuit. These are hard, crunchy biscuits, but they do break apart with a little effort so they can be managed for an older dog. Our whole pack seemed to like the flavor and texture and there were no crumbs left on the floor afterward.Two days is too soon to tell if the Crunch 'n Clean biscuits will actually help with bad breath or tartar on their teeth or not. Honestly, no dog biscuit or treat or food is going to eliminate tartar on your dog's teeth - only annual cleaning by the vet will do that. (Proper nutrition will certainly help keep the problem in line)The reason for the four stars instead of five is simply due to the primary ingredients. We have Rhodesian Ridgebacks and they are prone to food allergies with regard to wheat and corn. The high wheat content in these biscuits means I cannot give them to the majority of my dogs. Many other breeds out there have the same allergen issues as well - if you are feeding an organic or wheat/corn/soy free diet for an allergy prone dog then you'll need to stay away from the Hartz treats.

My dog is actually a bit picky when it comes to treats. When you give her something new, it takes her 2 or 3 tries before she decides to try it. So I was pleasantly surprised when she immediately decided these dog biscuits were acceptable. She chowed down pretty quickly and was looking for another one. This is the highest praise I can give a dog treat product. I don't know how effective these biscuits are at tartar control, because (a) my dog is still pretty young, and (b) it takes a long time to see a difference in doggie dental hygiene. But as far as taste is concerned, Stella votes yes. I would definitely buy these again!

My Pug likes these biscuits more than the usual peanut butter ones we give him, but the jury is still out on whether they really do clean his teeth.  I notice some improvement, in particular in the realm of doggie bad breath; but he's a young dog and tartar isn't a big problem for him yet so it's difficult to determine how well these are working.  However, the dog likes them, his breath IS improved, and so I'd consider buying these again!

I have a Rottweiler puppy and he really loves these. He loves to gnaw on them for a few minutes before actually eating them. The medium size is just about right for his since he just a puppy. They biscuits are mostly protein with a few percent of fat. I have purchased other biscuits and he just refuses to eat them. He will sniff them and just ignore them. He didn't even hesitate with these. I had these on the counter and his nose was right up there trying to figure out if that box was for him. These biscuits are loose in the box. They are not sealed in a bag and in the box. I threw these in a plastic container to seal the scent and to keep them fresh. Although, I don't think dogs really care about freshness. I will be purchasing these again.

LILY, my Ridgeback rescue and MIKE, my Wheaten terrier poodle rescue both give these medium size biscuits five stars. I don't know if they really help with tartar but it seems to me that their DOGGIE BREATH is a lot less offensive and that is a big plus.The biscuits take longer to chew than one would expect for their size which is a good thing, No little bits are left on the floor, they really enjoy these. The list of ingredients is long and sugar and salt are both near the top - for that I took away 1 STAR. I would purchase these again and might try the large size as both dogs are strong chewers.

column9: Very pleased with these biscuits & will buy more.
column10: I am reviewing the "small" size Hartz Crunch 'n Clean dog biscuits.I believe I've finally found a biscuit to help with the tartar problem I've got with both my dogs -- a dachsund and mini-pin.  When the box arrived, my dachsund became so excited he was shaking from the smell!  Now, he eats anything and everything, but he was especially anxious to gobble up these biscuits....and even started a fight with my other dog over the shipping box!  Even my mini-pin ate 2 of the biscuits right away, and he is a very picky eater.  Of course, I didn't taste the biscuits, but the smell was similar to that of seasoned "curly fries."  They are shaped like a small, short bone with flared ends -- dimensions are 2" long, 1" wide at each bone end tapering to 1/2" wide in middle of the bone, and 1/2" thick.  I noted that pieces crumbled off, as opposed to splintering off, when the dogs were eating them, which I liked for safety reasons.  I just tried to break one with my hands and could not, so, even though I don't see any immediate teeth cleaning after just two biscuits, I would assume that the hardness will help remove tartar after a few days.There is along list of ingredients in these biscuits, many of which are vitamins.  There is also "sodium hexametaphosphate," which is a tooth whitener found in Crest toothpastes.  Other ingredients are flavorings, meals, flours, fats, and sugars, and I didn't see anything in the list that made me reluctant to feed them to my little guys.  The suggestion is to feed dogs 4 of these biscuits daily "for maximum dental benefits."I will be buying more of these, as my dogs love them, and it's very hard to brush their teeth, the little monsters.

column9: Dry and Not as Appealing as other treats
column10: I love the idea of this dog treat, that it cleans teeth and freshens breath.  However, to get the maximum effect of that, the box suggests feeding him two bones a day every day for the cleanest teeth.  I normally don't treat my dog that often, because I don't think it's that good for him and also the cost of treats.  I'd have to buy a box a week to keep up with that!  But as to the taste of it, my dog was very unappealed by it.  He still ate them, as he is a dog afterall, but he would put it down and come back to it and work on it almost in the way he does actual dry bones.  I just think it lacks the taste and therefore his interest.  He much prefers tastier treats as he gobbles them up or spends his time gnawing on his bones. But I still give 3 stars as it does seem to help his teeth and breath!  Now if they could just make it more appetizing.  My guy is not, by far, a picky eater, so if he's pickin' there's a problem!

column9: My Doggy Gave this 2 Paws Down...
column10: Wayyyyyyyy down.  I received a box of the small biscuits for my 15 lb, West Highland Terrier, and mind you, she's a little piggy.  The saying "will work for food" describes her perfectly, but these?  She wouldn't even take them out of my hands!!  Now, that's just crazy!To be fair, her treats include more holistic brands like Old Mother Hubburd, and Innova Evo Dog Treats, which includes no chemicals, by-products, or grain.  It's a rather high protein, low carb treat....the complete opposite of these which is filled with all sorts of fillers including grain, by products and chemicals, and hardly, if any real meat at all.Hence why I don't blame her.And as for the price, it's kind of high for being in the same category as milk bones, and for only a dollar more, you can get much better quality dog treats out there, such as Innova Evo and Dogswell.She gives these 2 paws down.... way down, and I can't say I blame her.

My dog loves the taste. Even more importantly, she tolerates them very well, which is not always the case as she has a very sensitive stomach and is normally on a limited ingredients diet.I don't know how the teeth cleaning factor is supposed to work. It does not take my dog long time to eat a biscuit. I believe more in dental bones as she spends considerably longer time chewing on them.
these might be good for cleaning your dog's teeth, but so far I haven't been able to get my dogs to eat them - they just hide them.  Hopefully they will start eating them eventually.

I used these as treats for large sized dogs to cut down on caloric intake. They chewed them thoroughly. It did help with their breath and keeping their teeth clean. Instead of brushing weekly, I was able to cut it down to monthly. I would buy these dog treats again. Product works like it says.

column9: Dogs liked it better than I did
column10: Hartz isn't the brand that comes to mind when I consider 'quality' dog treats, and I wasn't sure mine would eat them.  My "small" dog weighs in at 25 lbs, and these biscuits were just right for her.  Her big sister, at 65 lbs, did also have to chew them before swallowing. I also tried them on my boss's crew of 5 miscellaneous dogs, and they all ate them except the one who won't eat anything. I wouldn't put much faith in their effectiveness as teeth cleaners though.As a "dog mom", I was not impressed with the ingredients.  These biscuits had far too many ingredients that just didn't measure up as "health encouraging" to inspire much faith on my part.  I can find treats that are far healthier, and chews that are far better as tooth cleaners than these biscuits do either one.All in all, its a 3 star ho-hum product.  Nothing to get excited about, and I won't be excited enough to seek them out at the store either!

column9: Better than green beans, not as good as kitty poop
column10: My Boston Terrier eats these, but does not appear to enjoy them any more than Milkbones. They are very hard and crunchy, which should be good for cleaning their teeth as advertised.My ancient Pekingese mix (with a very small mouth, and snaggly, horrible teeth) either can not, or will not chew them. She just holds them in her mouth or sets them down. I broke one in half to see if the size was the problem, but she still did not eat it.I did not try these myself, but I'm going to say that my household consensus is that these are not a favorite.

column9: A big box of hard biscuits
column10: The biscuits were pretty hard.  They came directly in the cardboard box, without any airtight seal to keep them fresh.  However, my dog does enjoy them, licking up the crumbs.  I was afraid the green specs might stain the rug, but it doesn't appear they will stain.
All I can say is that my dogs love these and they do a great job cleaning all the tartar off their teeth.

column9: A bit large for a small mouth, but definitely enjoyed
column10: Length:: 1:59 MinsWhat better way to review a dog biscuit than to show how much a dog enjoyed eating it? That was my logic behind this very amateurish but heartfelt video review starring my 1 1/2-year-old Shih Tzu, Missy.The video was very impromptu and, in hindsight, I realize that I didn't do a great job of explaining why I only gave the product 3 stars, so I'm adding some further explanation here.First, I took a star off because I felt that if you're going to make a multi-sized dog biscuit, the small should be small enough for the very small breeds like Yorkies and Chihuahuas.  As you can see in the video, this small biscuit is not only 2 inches long and quite thick but VERY hard, so I feel like a very small or more delicate breed may have trouble with even the small biscuit.Second, the ingredient list on the box is almost 3 inches long.  Sugar and salt are within the first 10 ingredients and, while there are a lot of vitamins and minerals included, there is also partially hydrogenated vegetable oil, several food colorings and chemicals I can hardly pronounce.  I just prefer to feed Missy more natural foods and snacks.Third, the "feeding instructions" (which hardly seemed necessary) direct me to give Missy 2 biscuits twice a day.  That's 4 large (compared to the small Mother Hubbard bone-shaped treats she usually gets) treats a day, which seemed a bit much, especially much considering my issues with the ingredient list.

column4: Tom D. "Opportunity is limited only by imagin...
column9: Passed my dog's taste test: And she is quite fussy
column10: Length:: 1:59 MinsMy dog, Ichi, is 10 years old and is a fussy eater -- and she usually doesn't even like dog biscuits. But she does like the Hartz Crunch 'n Clean Dog Biscuits (for small dogs).She is missing a couple of teeth (had to have them extracted) but she was able to eat (and obviously enjoy) these biscuits. So hopefully they will also protect her remaining teeth.Watch her in action in this video review! :-)

Hi, my name is Herdle and I am a fox red lab.  Milk bones are my usual brand and though I am a recovering biscuit addict, I decided to try these.  I've never met a treat I didn't love ...greenies, milk bones and when I can snag it, people food.Anyway, these treats are thicker and shorter than my usual brand (~1inch x 4inches) and they have a few lines and dots stamped in them along with Hartz on the top.  I actually preferred them to my regular brand when tested -- three times out of three.  I was given the option to freely choose one or the other.  This is not unique for me as I often love a new brand of food, but tire of it before the bag is empty (why does she buy those bushel bags?).The biscuits smell like people food.  The box says they contain 'denta-shield' and breath freshening crystals.  The crystals are really small, but the buiscuits do seem to leave my mouth smelling better than usual... kind of a 'fresh bread' smell.  oooh I love bread and marshmallows too.I could eat the whole box tonight but she's only giving me one per day.  I highly recommend them.  ingredients (in order from the box):  wheat flour, ground whole wheat, chicken meal, wheat germ meal, sodium hexametaphosphate, Poultry fat, salt, poultry digest (what?), Sugar (I LOVE SUGAR, but my vet sez it's not so good for me), Dried Whey, Malted Barley Flour, Dried cane molasses, calcium carbonate, brewer's yeast, citric acid, corn starch, choline chloride, sodium metasibulfite, partially hydroxogenated vegetable oil (if it's not good for mom, can it be good for me?), mono-diglycerides, mixed tocopherols (preservative), veg oil, rosemary extract (there's that people food smell), chlorophyll, aritificial coloring (red lake #40, yellow, blue) ferrous sulfate and other vitamin supplements (E, B12, zinc, A, copper, Niacin, Manganese, Riboflavin, D3, thiamine, Calcium Iodate, and Folic acid).Calories per biscuit - 170  wow, it's kind of like a candy bar for dogs.  Treat that tastes great, but not so great for you.

column9: Hard Biscuits -- I didn't taste them, but my dogs liked them
column10: I have two dogs and both love their daily biscuits. To keep their weight within reasonable parameters I do limit their treats, but am nonetheless familiar with most brands.These biscuits are quite different from any I've purchased in the past. They are at least twice as thick as a normal dog biscuit. I know this because I usually break biscuits in half, and in this case it was accomplished with great difficulty. I assume the hard consistency is part of what helps remove tartar on teeth.The dogs loved them and begged (yes, they did) for more. Notably there were absolutely NO crumbs at the bottom of the box -- NONE. That's something I've never encountered in a box of dog biscuits -- more evidence of the thick, tough texture.So, why didn't I rate the Crunch 'n Clean five stars?  Additives. I read the labels for my food and my dogs, and I don't like, in particular, added colors. And, not just one color, but three were added (why?) Yellow Lake #5, Blue Lake #1 and Red Lake #40.Also, it seems a bit incongruous to me to add sugar and dried cane molasses to tartar control dog biscuits. How good is sugar for dog teeth? I admit I'm not a chemist, but I suspect the sugar might be best avoided.  Salt is # 7 on the long (46 item) list of ingredients -- something else I believe isn't too good for dogs.Some of the many ingredients are unpronounceable and worrisome. Some are vitamin supplements. I prefer ingredient labels to reflect a simple straightforward list of deciferable food stuffs, and I'd rather no added vitamin supplements to treats because almost all basic dog food includes them. It is time consuming to keep track of it all. That said, my dogs loved the biscuits and I liked giving them something really hard to munch on.

column9: Four Dogs like Crunch n' Clean but they don't read ingredients
column10: I received a package of Crunch n' Clean Dog biscuits and Wow, did my dogs like them!  A Sheep hound mix, a Jack Russell, Chihuahua and Mini-Pinscher all loved the biscuits with equal enthusiam.  Four solid stars.But... I might point out that the above dogs like chicken, cheeze bits, kibble and dead birds and mice not to mention the odor of other dog's butt.So as I dog owner, I read the ingredients and found it to be typical of commercially prepared pet foods, relying on grain, meat byproducts and sugars for the bulk of the volume.  I can't endorse it as a "healthy snack"  for my pets.  But then again,  just like I visit McDonalds occassionally as a treat, neither can I complain.

I got this for my friends dog (I don't know much about dogs). I always thought a treat is a treat, but apparently, her dog has high standards. We went over for the weekend, and I brought them. She warned me of her dogs narrow tastes and was fairly certain that Tobi would not like it. Well, to her surprise, she was wrong. Tobi ate the treat and wanted another. The weekend was a success, and my friend now has a new treat to offer her dog. This was pretty hard and I wonder how good it would be for a small or small/medium sized dogs teeth. I suppose the hardness helps to remove the plaque. I suspect it would take more than a weekend to evaluate how well it cleans, and I'm sure that you still will have to take your dog for cleanings, though I don't know the frequency. I would guess this would give you a little more time in between cleanings. I think the most important thing is that a dog with picky tastes enjoyed it and also did not get sick from it. Just getting back to the hardness, it is not really harder than some of the other chew toys I have seen other dogs eat, e.g. bones, etc. Lastly, for the price, it seems like a good value. You get a lot of biscuits....and I suspect this 24 ounce box will last a while.

My dogs, a pug and a pomeranian both love these biscuits. Only problem, they fight over them! Since they usually turn their noses up at dog biscuits, I was surprised at this reaction.I will be buying more of these to keep for "doggy treats".

It is so hard to review dog biscuits!  I can say the box was nice sized and was filled to the top with biscuits (unlike potato chips).  I got the large size even though I have a beagle and she did just fine devouring them.  She seems to really enjoy the biscuits and eats the whole thing in a single sitting which is always a good sign.  I also like that they clean her teeth so that is a bonus!

I gave my dog one of the Hartz Crunch n Clean dog biscuits and he was very excited. He ran around the house with it in his mouth, drooling like a faucet. After playing for a while, he laid down to eat it. I could definitely tell it was harder to crunch up than the similar sized milkbone, he had to work it around and position it in his jaws just right. Once bitten into a couple of pieces, he ate one half and then took the other half and buried in the couch cushions. Sadly, I think that's probably a "paws down" vote from my dog. Also, at 35 calories, it's a pretty significant contribution to the daily intake for a small dog compared to a small Milkbone at 20 calories and a Liva Snap at 13 calories. If my dog had liked it more, I might give them to him as a special treat which wouldn't really help with regular dental cleaning because it is recommended to give them two biscuits a day (we would have to short him on kibble if we added the treats at that quantity). As he isn't in love with them, I think we'll just see if one of our doggie friends likes them better.

When we brought our new pup for her first check-up with our longtime family vet, he told us that the two ailments he and his partners see most often in their practice are pets that are overweight or have tooth problems. Both can lead to serious issues and health risks, but as he pointed out, by maintaining good habits, we owners can reduce the chances our pets' health will be affected.However, let's face it, no matter how eagerly our dogs greet their daily servings of healthy kibble, there are a whole lot interesting smells in the world, especially when your sniffer is so much more powerful than those of your human companions.Our pup, who loves to eat, is a lab -- a breed noted for its appetite and its wheedling expression as much as for its happy nature.  In our household, that means accurate measuring at mealtime and strict rationing of treats.Because she's food- and praise-motivated, we've been able to use bits of dog biscuits when introducing a behavior and to transition to clicker StarMark Clicker reinforcement and praise pretty rapidly ... and save the "treat calories" for a substantial chew or bone each day.I was eager to see what our pup would think of the Hartz Crunch `n Clean Hartz Crunch n Clean Dog Biscuit, Large  because it's got a pretty nutritious list of ingredients and includes a product developed at a dentistry university that's designed to block formation of tartar on teeth. Right out of the box, the bone-shaped treats have a nice heft and mild, pleasant aroma. My expert hovered hopefully, tail wagging, and seemed surprised that the treat was much heavier than her usual Checkups-brand treats. She nosed it around and licked it a few times before settling in next to my herb garden to polish it off. More later on this.While I'll have to wait for her next check-up to find out whether these biscuits are helping with our regular toothbrushing program, I could tell from the very first biscuit that her breath was better. (She has an unfortunate habit of nosing in our fish pond; thankfully the fish are faster than she is.)Our pup's daily maximum is 1,100 calories, which means that we're picky about the content and calorie count of snacks and treats, since they come straight from that bottom line.  To crunch a few numbers, these Hartz treats contain 170 calories each, and the recommended feeding is two per day. There were 14 treats in the carton. By comparison, her usual treat comes in at 137 calories, with a recommendation of two to three per day. The most we give her, though, is one a day so we don't have to short her on kibble. So far, she's seemed fuller for longer with the Hartz treats, which counteracts the slightly higher calorie count.When offered her choice between the two today, she promptly and politely chose Hartz, and headed straight to her niche between the rosemary shrubs. Turns out she's not just a chow hound but also a bit of a gourmet -- these treats are flavored with rosemary extract.

Hartz Crunch 'n Clean Biscuits for Dogs are formulated to help care for a pet's teeth between brushings and professional cleanings. Their DentaShield technology is clinically proven to block dental tartar buildup, the manufacturer reports. Two biscuits twice daily ensure optimal dental health, according to the company.But what about the chemicals? My two mutts are truly organic, but I figured I would try these.Neither of my mutts is finicky, they are very "piggie eaters", but they wouldn't even try these. They stuck their noses up and walked away.

These very hard biscuits seem to do their job. I have given one to each of my three Miniature Schnauzers and have not had any adverse effects.One of my dogs has a rather sensitive stomach and I was a little nervous about giving her these biscuits and so with anything new I usually try just a little to see how she can handle it.  She handled the biscuit just fine so these passed the sensitive stomach test.  I am now comfortable with giving her the whole biscuit and have not had any problems.Another one of my dogs has a tendency to wolf down his food so I was pleasantly surprised to find that the density of these biscuits to be hard enough to warrant him breaking the biscuit down to chunks to eat it rather than one bite and it's gone.None of my dogs stuck their noses up to the biscuit but only one of my dogs is a real food snob so that's not saying much.I'm not big on giving my dogs junk food even those which are supposedly healthy or beneficial such as these but if you don't have time or don't want to take the time to clean your dog's teeth and treats such as bones just don't do it for you then these are better than doing nothing.Ingredients listed is: wheat flour, ground whole wheat, chicken meal, wheat germ meal, sodium hexametaphosphate, Poultry fat, salt, poultry digest , sugar , Dried Whey, Malted Barley Flour, Dried cane molasses, calcium carbonate, brewer's yeast, citric acid, corn starch, choline chloride, sodium metabisulfite, partially hydrogenated vegetable oil , mono-diglycerides, mixed tocopherols , veg oil, rosemary extract , chlorophyll, artificial coloring (red lake #40, yellow, blue) ferrous sulfate and other vitamin supplements (E, B12, zinc, A, copper, Niacin, Manganese, Riboflavin, D3, thiamine, Calcium Iodate, and Folic acid).Calories per biscuit - 170If I was to recommend anything to Hartz it would be to get rid of the food color, lower the sugar content and add real chicken. I don't have a clue what chicken digest is, is it the stomach or extremely cooked down chicken?Four out of five stars for me.Though my dogs like these and they didn't upset my dog's stomach so no adverse affects at the end of the box I won't be repurchasing. I think I can find a better options for the health of my dogs than this.

My big girl dog has an indoor crate where she spends her nights, usually by choice, and some time while we are out. On top sits a box of milk bones and a big bag of cookies from the farm store.  They have sat there for months, we occasionally replenish them, and she never bothers them, she waits until we give her one.  My plan was to do a video review of this product, I was going to go outside and put out a couple of different brands, and see which one she ate.That night, when I got home, she was wagging her tail, obviously happy to see me as she always is when I return to our pack. And the cookies were gone. Oh, the milk bones were there, and the generic cookies were there. They still are. But these were gone.All I can say is that she has a sensitive stomach, and eating a box of these might have upset her stomach, but it didn't. I have no idea how they would have kept her teeth clean in the long run, because she ate them all at once!I'm rating them by how irresistible my dog found them. A product like this won't do any good unless the dog eats it, and she ate it.

column9: Not Only Clean, But Crunchy Too!
column10: Not much I can say considering I didn't eat any of these, but they were certainly a hit with the dog.  As far as it's breath freshening abilities, it's no bull.

column9: Dog loves it and breath smells better
column10: My dog loves these treats. She will take them over others (we put a few down and she went for this one first). they also make her breath smell fresher, which is a plus for me. It is a win win for both of us.

My dog and his friends agree.  These dog biscuits are a good thing.All the dogs I've given these to were unsure at first, but then grew to like them very much, thank you.  When one dog gets one, the others line up for theirs.  My dog and his friends aren't as passionate about these biscuits as they are for their beloved Greenies, but Greenies are very expensive, and Hartz Crunch 'n Clean are not.I'm unsure how much cleaner his teeth are because of these biscuits, but I am sure that biscuits that don't get eaten do no good.  I do think I detect a small improvement in my pup's teeth.If you want to give your dog a dental treat without getting him hooked on very expensive Greenies, (and they do get addicted), this might just be for you.

column9: Our dog is crazy about these
column10: Our dog, a 10 year old bichon frise, goes wild when he sees these coming, so the flavor must be pretty great; he is not a huge fan of dry dog treats usually.  After his recent difficulties with a teeth cleaning at the vet, I resolved not to have him go through that again, so it is a good thing to have the extra dental shield ingredient that protects teeth from tartar build up. There are also a lot of vitamins in the biscuits. The recommended feeding is 2 biscuits twice a day, which I think is way too much. This would be too filling and cause the dog to not eat enough of its dog food. If 4 biscuits per day are needed in order for the dental benefits to be realized, that is not good. Overall, I would use these biscuits several times a week to possibly give the dental benefits, but not as often as recommended.  :)

column9: the smalls not small enough for small dogs
column10: I guess when they did the taste test for these and stated preferred two to one sadly my dog (Chloe) was sitting in the other group. I have a 12 lbs. Papillon and give her the competitor bones and she loves those. I don't think it was the flavor as much as the size with these. For being `small' the bones are twice as large as the other ones. I think that was the issue for my `Chloe', she could not get her poor small mouth around it. She would try to suck it until it was ready to break. Even if I broke it, the pieces were too thick. I think if they were not so thick she would not have any issues. As far as the breath factor I did notice it improved in that area! That alone I would buy them but the size is what would deter me. I gave some to a bigger dog, a 55 lbs lab mix and he did not have a problem chewing them but still had to break the bone up. Over all I think it is a good idea but the size is not what I would consider small. Maybe a small treat for a bigger dog but too big for small dogs.

This is a very large dog cookie that has 170 calories -- roughly what my dog would get if I fed him a candy bar.  The package says that for maximum benefit I should feed two of these to my dog a day -- 340 empty calories.  While my dog eats these enthusiastically and wouldn't object, that won't be happening any time soon.  The downside of this product is obvious, while the benefit of its contribution to cleaner teeth is much harder to assess.

I can't really do this review justice since it already has two video reviews on it What I can tell you is that I gave these biscuits to three different dogs and they all loved them. A Pitbull, a Rottweiler and a bird dog are now fans of this product!!Guaranteed Analysis:Crude Protein  14%Crude Fat  2%Crude Fiber  4%Moisture  12%Calories Per Bisquit: 35

column9: Tastes Great - but lots of filler
column10: I have two pound puppies (well not puppies) who are not picky eaters - apparently living on death row in the pound will open up the horizens on edible vs non-edible.  Though they are both considered "medium sized" dogs, we give them the Large dog biscuits because they THINK they are large dogs.  Normally they each get one large biscuit every night before bed.So the box came in the mail.  I admit that I was surprised when I opened the box that more of them weren't smashed or broken in transit - I generally can't get the box home from the grocery store without smashing half of them.  So they now have a box full of non-broken snacks.  As the doggie mommy I inspected the ingredients - and was a bit dissapointed.  Lots of wheat and grains.  I had hoped for at least animal by-product or something as the first ingredient.  What really bothered me was the fake coloring, there's a list of artificial dyes - now I've never met a dog who would turn anything away based on color so I don't understand the point of colored dog treats.  The last ingredient was added on vitamines - so I was happy about that.  Still, lots of salt, sugar and grains in the box.Then I read the directions - feed 2 biscuits twice a day, so that's 4 biscuits per dog per day... that's a LOT of snack food for a dog.  After closer inspection it seemed to be stating that for maximum DENTAL benefit to follow that feeding routine.Rosco, our 30lbs 2year old sheepdog figured out pretty quickly that the box contained snacks.  After a sit then shake, I gave him one.  He was curious at first (he's a cautious doggie after having been abused so badly) there was some sniffing, some poking with the nose, but then once his big brother started moving in - Rosco crunched happily away at it.Indiana Jones (aka IndyBear) our 60 lbs 12-13 year old mix (maybe spaniel and austrailian shepherd? Who knows) has been on a weight management diet for over 10 years now, but severe arthritis and hip displaysia prevent much excercise.  Indy will eat anything - though I have recently started to worry about the hard food on his teeth.  Once Indy figured out that we were testing new biscuits, he went through the routine, sit, shake, laydown, situp - then he took off with his new snack.  Indy wolfed it down and came back for more.Over the next 24 hours there were no upset tummies or 2am walks due to the "runs" so we'll at least finish off the box.Final Opinion:The Good - hard and crunchy to help prevent additional tartar buildup.Apparently very tasty.The Medium Size is good for the 25-40 lbs weight range.I liked the added vitamins.The bad/questionable - I wasn't a fan of the dyes included.Smaller or older dogs may not be able to chew these comfortably.The dental benefit is only to PREVENT NEW buildup - not to help with current dental issues.Feeding Directions may lead to plump puppies - especially with the ammount of non-meat ingredients.Doesn't seem that it would be as beneficial on the teeth as a rawhide, at least with my dogs.Please remember - Doggies need their teeth brushed too, even if you give them hard treats like these.

column9: My dog wasn't big on these...
column10: I got these treats for my extra large Chihuahua who will eat anything.  She wasn't a fan of these.  Whenever we decide to give her a treat we ask her if she wants a "snackee" & she gets very excited.  She'll run in circle & stand on her hind legs.  When we gave her this for a "snackee" she just looked at it, smelled it & then looked to us like we were joking her.  We left it there & she looked at it again & smelled it & then chose to walk away from it.  This dog turns down nothing except for lettuce.  After it sat there for about 30 mins I put it in her dog dish & about 6 hours later she decided to get it out & contemplate eating it for about 10 more minutes before she decided to finally try it.  She did finally eat all of it but we know she wasn't big on it because the next couple times we gave her one it was the same routine, it sat for hours before being eaten.Her opinion is that she's not big on them & wouldn't recommend them but if given one she'll eventually eat it to make it go away.

These biscuits are probably better than nothing, and they did seem to clean some of the yellowish gunk off his teeth; after three of these over the span of a weekend, my dog's teeth were noticeably whiter, although spots of tartar and plaque remained in the remoter portions of his teeth.I generally prefer organic dog food with short, simple ingredient lists, and at first was a little concerned when I saw that the  list on these things was half the height of the box. However, spot checking the ingredients shows that most of them (Calcium Pantothenate or Pyridoxine Hydrochloride for example) were just vitamin supplements; a few were harder to decipher, though (Sodium Hexametaphosphate?)  The most common ingredient is wheat, so if your dog has a wheat allergy, avoid these.As to taste, I refrained from trying them myself, but it did seem a bit dryer and more powdery than other treats I feed him; he didn't seem as wildly enthusiastic about them as he is about his organic kibble, but he sure ate every speck, and started noticing when I got the box out. (To be fair, he'd probably eat bark if I put it in a bowl with some kibble and water).Overall, these are probably a good option if you want to do something for your dog's teeth; they're certainly far cheaper than the other dog dental treats I've seen for sale. I don't think they're going to be an adequate substitute for getting your dog's teeth cleaned at the vet, though.

column9: Dogs love them! But certainly not a dental supplement.
column10: I have 2 dogs, a sheltie mix and long haired chiauaua, I will say that the "LARGE" size biscuits were way to big for both of my dogs so I broke the large biscuit in half and gave each dog a piece of it. The dogs loved them! In fact I went to my front door to get the box and normally my dogs don't get excited about boxes. But this time I guess they could smell the treats inside because they both went crazy! I'll say that the box is bigger then I expected, contains approx 16 biscuits. The "serving size" on the box I'm not sure about as it says "for best results give 2 twice a day. If my math is right they want you to feed your dog a total of 4 of these a day and at that rate the box will last 3 and a half days.  If the treats were healthier and not so much filler I wouldn't see a problem with this IF it really helps the teeth, but with it being mostly filler I couldn't see feeding my dogs 4 of these every day. They are a good treat every now and then, but certainly not to be used as an on-going dental treatment because you would go through 2 boxes a week and at the current price it would be about $48 a month and that is just for 1 dog. These in my opinion are purely TREATS and not dental supplements. I will be submitting a picture of my dogs with these treats if you would like to see how excited they were when I got them out! I rated these at 3 out of 5 simply because of the healthiness of these compared to the "recommended serving." As far as my dogs go, I think they would give it a 5.

column9: My dog eats it like it was candy.
column10: We have a pretty picky dog when it comes to food and treats.  If she doesn't it like it, then she won't eat it.Well, she has no problem eating this biscuit and this thing is HUGE.  Can't comment on the cleaning ability yet, but taste is apparently out of this world to my dog.  :o)

column9: Hartz Crunch n Clean Dog Biscuits (Medium)
column10: If your dogs are like mine, then they love pretty much any treat you give them, but I must say then when I pick up this box they do seem a little bit more excited then with other treats. Also, my dogs will not let me brush their teeth at all, so I always look for treats to help protect their teeth. After about a week, I have to say I notice a difference. They have no plaque build-up and their chompers are pretty white and clean looking. So I would have to say they product definitely works. And seeing as how I am always curious what my dogs are eating, I took a bite of the treat myself, and now I see why they get so excited, it's pretty tasty. Yeah, I'm weird like that. For almost two pounds of treats, the price is also very good. I have a Boston Terrier, a Pug, and a little Chihuahua / Beagle mutt thing and the medium is a good size for them, though you might be better off with the small size for those breeds. Great product all around.

My dogs started eating these the minute I gave them to them, and they seemed to last a little longer than other biscuits I've bought for them.  I can't say if these biscuits really will cut down on the amount of tarter on their teeth just yet, but I'm sure time will tell.  For now I see no harm in giving them the 2 two biscuits each day that the box recommends, and hopefully it will help cut down on the tarter.  That they really liked them was an added bonus.

These biscuits are a hit with my German Shepherd. He loves them, and they really have made his teeth cleaner. I try to brush his teeth, but it can be a challenge to get to all of those back teeth before my pup is over the process. After only a couple of these treats this week, his teeth are noticably cleaner already.

My dog loves these new Hartz dog biscuits with DentaShield.The front of the box really boasts all the dental advantages pretty obviously, so I will just speak for my dog in that he loves the taste and chews them up really fast and it's something he looks forward to.Since it has it's benefits and he likes them, I'll continue getting these as well as Greenies which are also good for teeth.

Our 5 year old (healthy) pomeranian took these, although I could tell they were not his favorite treats, and ate them over a period of about a month.  I began to notice that his gums began to be sore, and he was having tenderness in his mouth.  I took him to our vet to have his teeth checked, and discovered that several of his teeth had become loose, and he had to have two of the front bottom ones extracted, and 5 more molars extracted.  A third (front tooth) is just hanging there tonight. The vet told me that several more were loose, and he could have pulled more.  I am heart sick that I fed these to my pomeranian....hindsight being what it is, they are way to hard for his little mouth and his teeth.  I thought I was HELPING him by giving him "Denta Shield" and instead he lost several of his teeth!  The small ones (for dogs up to 15 pounds) seemed OK for our bigger golden retriever, but are way to hard and thick for a small dog.  :(

column9: They're a little hard for small dogs but they love them.
column10: They're a little hard for small dogs - I actually have to break them up for my Shih tzu & Pekinese but they love them.

I have bred and sold dogs for over 45 years.  I know my dogs.  And I know what dental scaling and cleaning costs.  I discovered these biscuits and tried them and I am wowed.  They're fantastic.  All my dogs have polished white teeth now, and clean breath too.  I am so pleased with this product.Problem is that each and every store in America keeps running out of them.  So when you go to Amazon to find them to keep your dogs on the proper regimen (you can't bounce dogs around with their diet, it must be habitual), you get prices that are out of this world.  Wall Mart sells this product for under three dollars.  the LOWEST price at Amazon is OVER NINE DOLLARS.I have been a solid shopper at Amazon for over 15 years, but these prices have run me off to Wall Mart, where the shipping is free.  Shipping on this product is SIX DOLLARS OR MORE.Come on store owners!  Why do you want to screw your customers?  Are you JUST concerned with your own investment or your stock holders that you would screw your customers?  DID YOU REALLY SNAP UP ALL THE SUPPLY TO GOUGE US?  We want reasonable prices for products and a box of dog biscuits is NOT WORTH TEN BUCKS.  GET REAL!!!!

...judging by the list of junk food ingredients I wouldn't give them enough to even try to see a difference in their dental health.  But my dogs are raw fed and very picky about any grain based "treats" and they gobbled these down in a heartbeat.  They're a good snack but I wouldn't rely on them for any kind of dental health and they certainly are no substitute for brushing their teeth.

these are hard to find in the stores anymore. a bit overpriced through Amazon as most grocery/pet items are. packed well, hardly any broken biscuits inside the boxes. Amazon is great, but as I said, this item was a bit overpriced.
After giving these to my dogs they both developed bloody diarrhea! I'm throwing out the box and never buying this product again.

column9: No way older dogs can even bite these
column10: I have 7 dogs ranging from Shepherd to min pin, all are older and NOT ONE of the dogs liked or could bite into these biscuits.

column9: My dog laid it on the ground and looked at me funny
column10: I bought the Hartz Crunch 'n clean biscuits (small) and my Pekingese hated them. The first time i gave it, he took it with excitement and then laid it on the floor and looked at me as if he were thinking, "where's the REAL treat?".  So later i tried it again and even broke it in half. No, not interested at all. I'm glad to know that i can go to the Hartz website and get a refund. It's a hassle to do that, but i appreciate it.

My dog is 15ys old, he doesn't chew much and I felt awful after his last dental appt. He looked so ill, and I paid $300.  Luckily, I found Hartz Crunch and Clean.  These are magic!  I give him two a day, almost all of his tarter is gone.  I have to scrape a tiny bit.  It has been several months, and Mom's dog eats them and my sister's cats use the kitty variety. Their tartar is almost all gone too.Update: Roswell, now 16 at 26 lbs gets 4 a day (for 2+ yrs). Just had a vet check, and vet was amazed at how good his blood work is.

Reviewing dog biscuits is a little difficult. Did my golden retriever eat the biscuits? Yes, quite readily.  Did her teeth and breath get noticeably cleaner? Perhaps, but having only tried one box--which lasted a couple of weeks--I am not sure I can guarantee such a result.  Like all dog treats, they seem to recommend a lot per day.

column9: Great treat for your best friend
column10: I am sure my dog could do a better review but seeing as he can't type, I will try to translate.  My dog(Welsh Terrier) is actually a very picky eater and only likes a handful of things.  Believe it or not, he loves these treats and can't get enough of them.
