Of course all dogs are different, but typically, if my dog is happy, your dog will be happy.Now for what I love about this product:- the medium size bone is a perfect treat for a medium sized dog (25-35 lbs)- if you want to break them into pieces (for training or just to give a small treat), it is easy to do.- thes bones don't break into a billion crumbs when your or the dog cracks into them- they have relatively no smell, yet my dog still loves them - they must have great flavor- My dog has problems with tartar build up.  These bones appear to help reduce the tartar and certainly don't add to any build up.- One box seems to go a long way.  I don't treat my dog everyday but my first box is still half full.  I am guessing around 50-75 bones in a new box

My dog enjoys hiding and then eating the biscuits. I gave Crunch and Clean 4 stars because they don't seem any different than other dog biscuits, but if they really do clean better than most, than add another star!
My order arrived timely and without any damage.  I (actually my dog) was very happy.  It's has been hard to find this favorite treat for her in the local stores I shop.  Thank you.

I have two Shih-Tzu/Pomeranian mix dogs that can be a bit finicky when it comes to what they eat. It did take them a while to warm up to these, but now they seem to love them. One of them will eat every crumb, then go check to see if his brother left any crumbs. Though I don't think these will ever replace my dogs' favorite "Greenies," these are a good change of pace for them.

column9: Sick Beagle on crunch and clean hartz
column10: My dog was fine and I gave him a Hartz Crunch and clean as we were going to bed. I knew something was wrong when I noticed that my beagle, Cocoa, who rarely lets me out of site, did not follow me to bed. Cocoa, who has been sick once in 5 years that I know of, has been throwing up for 2 hours. He has also been drinking insane amounts of water, and ran outside to eat lots of grass as fast as possible, which is uncharacteristic of him. He has stopped throwing up, but I suspect it is because he either has nothing left to puke, or is fighting it off as his diaphram is still jumping. He wont even lie in bed, which is where he lives. The list of ingredients is pretty long. My dog has a healthy diet(science diet), so this could just be a reaction to a healthy dog eating unhealthy food. Anyway, I am done with Hartz, and probably on my way to the vet.

I love the idea of a dog biscuit that will freshen your doglies breath.  I have 5, so I'm always trying different dental bones and things to help me out there.  These bones are the perfect size, smell great~~like human food, actually~~but out of 5 dogs, only 2 would eat them.  I actually put one in my youngest dog, Tobey's mouth, and tried to coax him.  He spit it back out!!  Not sure if it was the smell, or the taste, but I hate to report that it would be a waste of money for me to buy these.  I have 4 Lhasa Apsos, and a Schneagle~~the Lhasa's I do have to say are pretty picky eaters, and 3 of them are the ones who wouldn't touch them, so take that as you will.I WISH they loved them so that they COULD Crunch n' Clean!!

column4: mahlers2nd "The Only Way Out Is Through"
column9: Dogs give them 5 stars... their dentist not so much
column10: These biscuits are advertised to "clean" your dogs teeth.  My dogs were very happy and willing participants in the experiment.  They loved the biscuits (but frankly... if it comes from a human hand, they will gulp it down even if it were garbage... they're dogs... that's how they're wired).However, after using these, I couldn't really tell a difference in the cleanliness of my dogs teeth.If you want to give your dogs a treat, these will work great.  However, don't expect them to replace regular cleanings at your dogs at the vet.[NCJVR]

I have a 50 lb retriever mix and she loves these bones for treats.  I have noticed no tarter build-up although I do brush her teeth 1-2 weekly.  Even so, I think these are helping.  For some reason, bone snacks like these are not something she normally likes to eat but these must taste really good to her because she gobbles them up!!  I do recommend them!

My dogs love these.  I have a 65 lb, Golden Retriever that will eat anything I give her ... she operates on blind trust, and if it comes from my hand it must be good, so of course she eats these happily ... but hey, she drinks from the toilet so how picky can her palate be??  On the other hand I have a 9 lb Tibetan Spaniel that covets ownership of any and everything that has been dropped on the floor or has been offered to the Golden; however, he doesn't wolf it down ... instead he carries off any treasure he finds to his pillow where he will carefully, delicately, and privately decide if he actually wants it.  If he doesn't, she can have it after he is done inspecting it.  He is VERY picky about what he eats, and generally turns his nose up at most treats (after carting it away for the inspection ritual - mind you, he doesn't really want it; he just doesn't want HER to have it).  However, even this picky little critter enjoys these and gobbles them up, so ... while not having tasted them myself, I can honestly say most dogs will enjoy them thoroughly.  On a medicinal point ... I have not found any improvement to the Golden's bad breath after using these ... this is no substitute for brushing.
My Scottie just loves these treats...the extra added bonus is that they help keep his teeth clean!  Another winner from Hartz!!

My dogs absolutely loved this product!!! They don't leave that "meaty" smell in their breath, and they were hard enough for them to enjoy each for about a minute (versus 2 seconds of some other treats)!! It actually made their teeth a little cleaner after a few, but then again, I brush their teeth often, so I can't really tell.

These biscuits are huge, almost a meal. We have 3 dogs, and they did eat them, although they were sort of luke warm in the process.  They did not bolt them down like they do with milkbone.  We only had the one box and I did not notice any difference in the way their teeth looked or their "dog breath."Because it is a vine product, I do not know if the price of the item is fair. I think I will just stick with Milkbone products.

So I got a box of these for my 3 year old Norwegian Elkhound. All dog owners know that there are many, many products out there that claim to clean your dog's teeth. So do it better than others, and some my dog flat out won't eat.When I first opened the box of these I was amazed at the size of them. The box does say large, but these things are huge. I would recommend this size for much larger breed dogs than my 50 pound elkhound.The benefit of them being so big is it does take her a little bit of time to chew the whole thing up and eat it.Results? Not really sure. The box says to feed at least two of these to your dog per day. But quite honestly, that would get really expensive and I am not sure what the dietary 'after effects' would be with that dose and I really  don't want to find out. So I can not really speak to the cleanabability that this product does.I can say my dog enjoys them and does take a little time eating them.

column9: Dog loves them, and they seem to work at cleaning teeth
column10: When we first received the box of Hartz ProDent, which proudly proclaimed "Taste preferred 2 to 1 over the leading brand," we couldn't help but roll our eyes a little.  And as I tried to break a biscuit in half for my little dog, a couple snide remarks ran through my mind: "Geez, these things are hard as rocks - they're more likely to break teeth than clean them!" and "I hope those greenish-blue specks are just minty dental crystals..."  Over the course of a few weeks, however, my skepticism faded since a) it is very apparent that the dog LOVES them - they're by far her favorite treat now, b) her breath has actually improved noticeably (though i did NOT french-kiss her to verify this for a fact), and c) her teeth do look a bit cleaner.  I still think that the best way to take care of your dog's teeth is to brush them, but for those who don't want to bother with that, the biscuits will likely provide a handy/easy alternative.

My cocker spaniel dog Lucky is always looking for treats. So I thought I'd get him a box of Hartz Crunchn Clean dog biscuit treats.  Lucky was initially skeptical of this new treat. We put the treat in his dish and then poured his regular dog food on top of it. Soon, Lucky was digging through his food looking for the treat; like a child looking for the prize in a box of Cracker Jacks. Over the next several days, Lucky chowed down on every treat in the box. The biscuit is also supposed to clean the dog's teeth, or improve dog breath, or something. It didn't seem to do that for my dog, but Lucky seemed to really enjoy these. So I'll probably buy more of these treats for him in the future.

I got these for my black lab.  When I hold one of these, I can easily get her to follow any command:  Sit, Jump, Lay Down -- Whatever I ask of her, she'll do it to get one of these treats.  That these clean her teeth while she's enjoying a snack is an added bonus.  I know they won't take the place of brushing her teeth, but it will make it easier to make sure she has healthy teeth and gums.

I have inherited the world's most persnickety shih-tzu. I have bought her every brand of designer, organic, healthy treats on the market and she promptly turns her nose up at all of them. I was sure that Hartz Crunch 'n Clean dog biscuits would end up at the Humane Society (where I donate all Lily's cast-offs), but lo and behold she actually tried them and seemed to enjoy them. While she would gladly choose "Tiny T Bonz" over these at least these are good for her. Her veterinarian said she is going to have to have her teeth cleaned in the next year because there is some tartar on them which could lead to tooth loss. I'm hoping that Crunch 'n Clean Dental Biscuits takes care of that problem because I know how traumatic a teeth cleaning will be for her highness. I give her one every other day so she doesn't get tired of them and not respond when I try to get her to come inside by saying "do you want a treat?", which usually gets her running. I am interested to see what the vet says at her next appointment. If there is a major (or even minor) improvement in her teeth then these dog biscuits are worth every penny.

I have two dogs, one is a Terrier, and the other is a Chihuahua. They are extremely picky eaters. They will only eat Cesar dog food, and the only biscuits they ever eat are the ones you get from Sam's Club. The multi flavor Members Mark brand. So when I got these, I knew they would be better for their teeth, but I honestly didn't think they would eat them. Well I was WRONG!Now I usually leave a little pile of the regular dog biscuits on the floor for them to get when they want one. So I decided to do the same with these. I put a small pile of these right next to the ones they usually have. They went straight to these. First my Chihuahua took one, and jumped on the couch. She wouldn't part with it. Then the Terrier got one and jumped on the living room chair. The Chihuahua ate it and the Terrier immediately started growling at her thinking she was going to get his LOL. She has continued to eat these and the pile of the regular ones haven't been touched since I got these. I guess I now have to change what biscuits I buy for them.

Our dogs (a Boston terrier and a dauschund) like these biscuits.  The size (medium) is a good one for them and I have noticed less doggy breath since they've been using them.  I already brush their teeth but the biscuits seem to improve things more than brushing alone.The boxes are a good size and there are a lot of biscuits in the box.  It is a good value for the price.  I'll be buying more when we run out.

column9: Good dog treats, but make sure to monitor eating of them.
column10: I have two dogs and one tends to chomp down whatever she gets and the other one tends to sniff it out first before chowing down. I got the medium sized Crunch 'n Clean and the dogs I have are a border collie mix and a black lab mix.Amber, my black lab mix, took to the treat instantly, eating it very quickly. As for Palmer, my border collie mix, it took him a little while before he was ready to try the treat. However, after his initial taste, he would grab the treat whenever he is offered it.The size of the treats are pretty good for medium dogs. It takes more than a few bites before they can swallow the biscuits completely so make sure to monitor them when they are eating this. Amber tends to swallow really fast without chewing so I can see these as potentially a choke hazard for any dogs who do not like to chew. Therefore, make sure to watch the dogs as they are eating these treats.

column9: Very yummy dog treats for dogs of all sizes
column10: Very tasty dog biscuit meant for large dogs.  I have a lab and a min pin and I just break it in half for the min pin.  They both love this treat. The only bad thing is that it crumbles very easily so feed this treat to them outside, they tend to make a bit of a mess when they eat it.  It's so large and they have to break it into pieces, when it breaks, it creates a bunch of crumbs.  I'm not sure if the advertised Denta Shield ingredient really does block new tartar formation, but the dogs love it.

column9: she likes it, but what the heck is DentaShield?
column10: We received Hartz Crunch 'n Clean biscuits through the Vine program, and our medium-sized dog can go through a large-sized biscuit in about a minute.  She enjoys them, but I'm concerned about the patented ingredient, DentaShield.  "Invented by researchers at Indiana University's School of Dentistry, the same researchers who developed flouride for you and me," DentaShield might be the sodium hexametaphosphate listed as the 5th ingredient after wheat flour, ground whole wheat, chicken meal, and wheat germ meal.  It sounds like a salt, which isn't necessary to clean tartar from teeth, as the box claims.  Other ways are better to clean dogs' teeth.These biscuits are definitely loaded with non-essential ingredients like partially hydrogenated vegetable oil and artificial color (they're uniformly tan, so where's the color?).  The blurb about the same researchers who developed fluoride set off warning bells, as many people know the issues with mass amounts of fluoride in our drinking water, but people unfamiliar with those issues may feel this is a good advertising tactic.Our dog likes them, but dogs tend to like junk food, including human food.  So, if you're conscientious about what you feed your critters, consider buying locally-made biscuits or make them yourself from a recipe online.

column9: My dog isn't crazy about them
column10: Normally when I take out treats or bones for my dog she starts doing her tricks right away and whining in anticipation.  When I take this box out she doesnt even get up. When I hand her a bone she lets it drop to the floor and just sniffs it.  Sometimes she'll eventually eat it. Other times she just walks away from it.  I will update my review after she's been using them for a while to report back whether her teeth are any cleaner.  That's assuming I can get her to eat them.

My dogs loved these treats. Do they reduce tartar over time? I have no idea. You see, my dogs loved these so much that when I was at work, they somehow got the box off the table and ate them all! Stinkers! And they are VERY picky about treats.The biscuits are a fairly good size, about 4 inches long and about 1 inch think, which is much thicker than standard biscuits. They are very hard and crunchy. It took several minutes for my dogs to eat the ones I gave them, and they are good size dogs and big chewers, weighing between 50-85 pounds each.I'll be looking for this in my local market. If they don't sell them here locally, I'll get more from Amazon. Looks like I'll have to put them WAY up the top shelf in my kitchen though!

I gave this to my family's two one year old Cocker Spaniels who enjoyed them. The biscuits are larger and a little harder than the usual dog biscuit. They are very good in the toys that need a treat in the middle, for the dog to liberate. They also don't get mushy when they are chewed on but break into little pieces. That it helps clean dogs teeth is an added bonus.

My dog, Max, will eat almost anything, and he's never found a dog treat or food that he didn't like.  The Hartz Crunch n Clean biscuits are no exception.  He is a miniature American Eskimo, around 20 pounds, so I got the medium size for him.  They are pretty stout for a medium (in terms of thickness), but they were a good size for his mouth otherwise.  He really enjoys them.  My mom's dog, Gypsy, is a frequent visitor to my house.  She prefers soft treats to hard and generally snubs any hard treat (to Max's delight, since he'll steal it from her).  I gave her one of these, and to my surprise, she devoured it.  She loves it!  That gets a gold star from me.I deducted a star because I couldn't tell whether or not they were actually cleaning the teeth.  (I suppose this isn't the fault of this product specifically but of all dog products which claim to clean teeth.)  Max's teeth don't seem to be getting dirtier, but they don't seem to be getting cleaner either.  Perhaps one box isn't enough to be able to make a judgment call -- but with Max and Gypsy both loving this treat, chances are I'll be buying it again!

I tried on three different occasions to get my two dogs to try these biscuits.  They just sniffed and turned away, both of them.  They are not fussy, so I was surprised, and I'm assuming that the teeth cleaning ingredient may not smell good to them.  They are a nice size for a small dog, and the smell (to me) is mild, but I can't judge how well they clean teeth if the dogs won't try them.

column9: My pups will eat anything--but they won't eat these unless they're the big ones
column10: I haven't had the same success as other reviewers here. My two sibling dogs are Rhodesian Ridgeback/Beagle mixes, and they are basically breathing vacuum cleaners. If it hits the floor, they eat it. I normally treat them to Stop & Shop brand treats in the assorted flavors (and colors) because they love them. The medium sized Hartz Crunch n Clean biscuits have been spit out repeatedly by my two 55 pound dogs. I even broke them in two to make them smaller for my dogs' mouths and they still reject them. It seems to be not only the size, but the fact that these biscuits are extremely hard. I'm sure that is what helps remove tartar, but my dogs only like a tough chewing job when they are enjoying a rawhide bone.On the other hand, the LARGE variety go over better, but not so much as quick treats but as if my dogs think I've just given them a rawhide to gnaw on. They're just in for a surprise when, after enough chewing of these hard bones, they actually break apart and become edible.Some of the main ingredients include wheat flour, ground whole wheat, chicken meal, wheat germ meal, poultry fat, poultry digest, sugar, dried whey, malted barley flour, dried cane molasses, citric acid, corn starch, and partially hydrogenated vegetable oil. Aside from also having vitamins in the ingredients, these treats are loaded with ingredients that are hard to pronounce and sound like things you learned bout back in chemistry class!

I have 3 large dogs and they will eat almost anything.  Anything but these dog biscuits, that is!  Two of the three, would turn their faces away refusing to take the biscuit in their mouth or even lick it.  The third dog would readily eat them but she also has a nasty habit of eating dead animals and squirrel poop.  After giving my single "test subject" 2 biscuits a day for 2 weeks I did not notice any reduction in the visible tarter on her teeth nor did I notice fresher breath.  Perhaps with a longer test trial, some benefit would become obvious, but given that the majority of my dogs won't eat them I doubt I will be purchasing this product in the future.

Well, not really. Nuala says "arf," and occasionally "arrrrroooooooooroooooo." But she likes these better than similar products and they ABSOLUTELY remover tartar. To give you an idea of whether these are size-appropriate for your dog, she's a 45-lb lab/terrier mix, about nine months old.So why did I only give it a four? When I first gave her one, she thought it was a toy.  It took her a good ten minutes to figure out it was food. This suggests to me that the flavor could be made more appealing (though I'm not planning on tasting them to find out); on the other hand, she goes straight for the crunch nowadays, having figured out what they're for (well, other than the tartar removing part, I'm pretty sure she doesn't much care).

The first time I gave my dog one of these he sniffed it intensely, as he does with anything new. When he was satisfied with it he gulped it down. I give him half of one first thing in the morning when he does his business and the other half when he comes back into the house. He loves them.

We bought these for our two dogs, an English Bulldog and French Bulldog, who both seemed to love them. They were larger than I expected, about 4-5 inches long and 2 inches wide, so we had to break them in half, but the larger size kept the dogs busy for longer than a normal treat. If I purchase these again, I will probably get the Medium Sized bones instead. To be honest, I didn't really notice a difference in their breath after eating the bones, but like I said before, both of our dogs really enjoyed them.

Hartz Crunch 'n Clean Biscuits are vet recommended.  The front of the box claims they remove 2 times more tartar than plain doggie biscuits and have a meaty flavor.  The small size seems to be just right for my two dogs (a pomeranian and a little terrier mix) and they absolutely love them!  There are only 35 calories per biscuit, so they make a good snack.  Directions state to give two daily.  Great product!

As the first review for trying out a Vine product, this one had considerably more success with my dog than I anticipated. It's not her absolute favorite, but she does seem to enjoy them and eat them (most of the time) when we give them to her. It also never hurts that it's a useful cleaning device for our dog too.Our dog is a German Sheperd/Retriever/Labrador mix and she is a year and 8 months old.

column9: My pup and grandpup loved these
column10: The pups did not hesitate over these new treats. They seemed to enjoy them and I was happy their teeth were getting clean.

My 3 dogs (Black Lab, Blue Heeler and Rhodesian Ridgeback) didn't really know what to think of these at first because I've never given them doggie bisquits before... they just dropped them and looked at me like... don't you have any REAL bones?  But now as I just fed them the last three, they definitely know what to do with them and welcome them.  Each takes his/hers off to a remote place and works on it until it's gone.  Mine are the large variety so they last them a while.  I don't know if it's doing a job on their teeth, but there's enough chomping going on that it certainly should be cleaning them well.  I'll buy more of these!

There's not a lot I can say about the tartar fighting amazingness of Hartz's new tartar fighting Crunch 'n Clean dog biscuits. However, I can tell you that they MUST be delicious. Lily and Lola are Boxadors and large ones at that so the biscuits lasted mere seconds during the shark-frenzy-like consumption period.They did not bark at the UPS man when he delivered the biscuits which meant they were not a box of crumbs from a launch-delivery as he ran scenario. Lola, the finickier of the two (though both will eat fresh deer droppings, go figure ) didn't hesitate to snarf them down. And when I hovered the biscuits over their heads the Pavlovian drool strings appeared as if I was offering something truly dog-delightful (I suppose like a plate of wildlife droppings). Both Lily and Lola licked up every crumb of Crunch'n Clean after the biscuits broke up while being chewed.I do like the idea that the substance, DentaShield, coats the teeth to block new tartar formation. And I like that I can feed the girls treats that serve a purpose besides just tasting doggie-delish.

I hope you do not mind but I told the old two legged humans to take a break while I let you know how we liked Crunch 'n Clean.  For the record, we are 9 and 10 year old Yorkies and if you know anything about Yorkies we are weird when it comes to eating.  Sure we are adorable, loving and just the best pets in the world but we are picky when it comes to eating.  The humans, bless their heart, bring home some of the weirdest stuff you can imagine.  Stuff that comes in boxes, bags and who knows what else.  They got smart a few years ago and only bring home small bags, etc.  We take a sniff and walk away unless we like the stuff.  If we don't like it, they give it to some other dog and that poor old thing is huge, loved and not lacking for food.  He has his own stimulus plan.Sorry for the elaborate history but Hartz has done it again.  We really like these small biscuits and know full well that the humans will get more.  I can't wait to see the Vet to show off our clean teeth.  Even though it has been only a few days the difference is quite obvious  They almost sparkle and by the time we get to the end of the box they will look like TV teeth.  We simply do not care about all those human considerations like calories, fat, fill and such.  We care about taste and the ability to knaw and eat something that makes our mouths and tummy feel good.  Hartz Crunch 'n Clean fills the bill.  Thanks for stopping by and y'all come on back.  Wuff Wuff.
I had ordered the large bones, and they are truly large.  And instead of being the usual flat style doggie bones, they are very thick.  These are great for big dogs.

First off, my dog loves these buscuits.  I'm not sure if it is still just from the novelty of having something new, but even that would indicate that they aren't just the same old treat in a different box.  Now, like most dogs, she gets excited for just about any type of treat, but she clearly favors some over others, and she does enjoy the Hartz Crunch n Clean Dog Biscuit, Small.My dog is also 60 lbs, and would not be considered small -but these aren't too small for her.  The biscuits are very hard and might be a bit big for a really small dog.  I usually buy small to medium size treats anyway, so they are a good size for my dog.If you have concerns about ingredients:  these do contain artificial food colorings, lots of 'unpronouncables' and a high wheat content. I generally avoid these in dog food, but since this is the equivalent of doggie junk food, I can dole these out sparingly as rewards and not a diet supplement.The dog says five stars, but I'm leaning towards three stars because of the ingredients, so we have settled on four stars overall :)

column9: My dog likes the other brand better.
column10: I gave a Hartz to my dog and he ate part of it and stopped. Then I gave him the "other" brand and he ate it up. So my dog only will eat this if there's nothing else around. It's hard to write a review since it's up to the dog whether he likes it or dislikes it. Each dog is different on what they feel is good so I didn't get to the point to see if it helped his teeth or not.

We have a Jack Russell & a Rat Terrier. We give them some kind of teeth cleaning chewie every night (usually Greenies). Our rat terrier can be picky... be she loves these. When she sees us get the box, she runs to her crate for her bedtime "treat". They are the perfect size for our dogs.

column9: Tasty biscuit according to my dog
column10: As another reviewer mentioned, these biscuits are a bit large for a very small dog.  I have a maltipoo and do not usually give him bones this big so I would break them up -- which is no easy feat since these are hard as rocks.  I guess that is what helps remove the tarter?  Anyway, I would put a biscuit in a sandwich baggie and use a small hammer to break up the biscuit and give him a little piece as a treat.  My dog probably only eats one full biscuit daily since I don't want to over-treat and worry about weight gain.  He does love them though and he always enjoys eating them.  I cannot say that his teeth look cleaner to my eye but I do try to keep his teeth clean and am for anything that helps accomplish that with ease as these biscuits do.  I took off a star for the somewhat questionable ingredient list and also for the size.  An extra-small would be a good idea or a small treat size nib.

column9: A bit more protein a bit less wheat
column10: First, I do have to say our dog Mitzi (a black Chow) enjoys the biscuits and the size is no problem for her, even though she is only 40lbs (small for a Chow). I can't tell if it actually removes tartar, but I am giving it an extra star for that if it does. I am deducting a star because the main ingredient is wheat and a dog should have more protein and fewer carbs in its diet.

column9: Mixed opionions from my two dogs.
column10: I have 2 medium sized dogs, a siberian husky who is a bit of a picky eater and my puli who is a trash can. They both are typically fed Wellness brand products, so I wasn't sure how they would like  the Crunch 'n Clean biscuits.My puli, being the little trash can he is, stared at and played with a biscuit for a while before digging in, which is not his usual form. However, after a few minutes he snarfed it right up and he has continued to do so for the past several days.My husky on the other hand initially left her biscuit and stared at it. Then she licked it and stared at me, leaving it on the ground and walking away.  I tried again the next day with similar results. On day three she begrudgingly took it and ate it, but she left bits of it all over the floor, which is not her MO for our normal brand.I think, therefore, it is likely that how well your dog will or won't like these treats is dependent on how finicky your dog is.They do appear to assist with removal of food particles. I could not ascertain whether they assisted with tartar build-up removal as neither of my dogs really have this problem. However, if the loose food is removed, I suppose you could argue that it would reduce the potential for tartar build-up in the future. It did not make their breath smell remarkably different.The caloric content is high considering the ingredient list (50 cal/biscuit). This could be a problem for anyone with pets that have weight issues as the recommended serving is 2 biscuits twice a day for 200 calories total. The ingredient list also sports a number of grain products, wheat, barley flower,  and corn starch, which could be a problem if your pet has allergies. It also contains partially hydrogenated oils and sugars, neither of which are particularly good for either pets or people. So those people who worry about what their dogs eating, or those with pets with allergies will probably not find this product to their liking. I am most concerned with the calorie content and wonder if the reason I did not notice noticeably fresher breath was because I fed my dogs half the recommended serving (so 1 biscuit twice daily) as I have one pet whose weight I have to watch.All in all I think this is a split decision. I think many dogs will like the biscuits, like my puli and be just fine with them. They are a good size for the medium breeds and they probably will prevent future tartar build-up. For finicky eaters and/or owners, or those pets who have grain allergies, a different choice may make more sense.

I've been giving these out to customers at our grooming shop for the last several days, and the response has been very positive.  Most dogs are anxious when they're at the shop, so very few will eat a treat.  However, I've had several dogs eagerly enjoy these while waiting to go home.  If a dog will eat these while waiting for their owner, they must be pretty darn good.

column9: the dogs love these - but they love all treats
column10: If you are looking for non-wheat based treats - these are not them - the first ingredient is flour. The second is wheat meal.Some people are very wary of this sort of thing for their pups, so I wanted to get that out of the way. Do they clean your dog's teeth? I can't say as we brush their teeth nightly - but they are quite hard biscuits - so they have the potential - as do most other very hard treats - to help clean teeth.Size - small - well, really, they are on par with other medium biscuits - so if you have a toy breed - as in less than 10 lbs - they will likely have trouble with these as they are larger than most 'small' biscuits.The dogs love them - of course, the dogs love all treats - but they don't spit them out in disgust ;)Overall, they are fine - the pups have gone through most of the box so far (we have 3 and they get treats a couple times a day). No problems at all.If you have a 15-50lb dog - and are looking for a hard treat that might help with keeping their teeth clean, this is a good option.
The dog gobbled up everything without playing around and spilling the contents out the bowl like it would usually do with its regular dog food.

column9: Can people use these? they work on dogs bad breath
column10: I have a 12 year old sheltie with older teeth, despite yearly tooth cleanings, his breath is not as good as it should be. He can no longer chew his tooth vet approved tooth cheweys, so I thought I would try these.I am not sure why so many reviers are hung up on "taste", as a 20 year dog trainer I suspect they have very spoiled dogs that are over weight and need to be a bit hungry.The goal of these cookies  is breath work!!! not taste!!!They are cruncy! suggest you do not feed on carpet!  and after two days his breath was better when we played toys. I think they have made an improvement in his breath, and suggest you try a box.two days later,, we skipped a day,,, and I could tell he needed one. ****I have fed them for two weeks and the teeth  have improved.  If your dog has bad breath, try one of these a day. doglady forest grove

column9: I'll buy again: dog loves 'em, good size for large dogs, ingredients so-so, somewhat pricey
column10: The good:The 1st test of any dog treat is how much my dog likes them (after all, they are treats for him!). He loves these biscuits; in fact, I usually give him a dog supplement with each treat and he refuses to eat his supplement until AFTER each biscuit crumb is gone.I also like the size of the large biscuits: my lab needs to actually chew these; can't gulp them in one bite.The so-so:The ingredients are pretty standard; I home feed my dog, so I do pay attention to ingredients. Still treats are treats, and as such, the ingredients in these once/per day treats are acceptable to me.The amazon.com price for the large biscuits is $3 per pound --- way cheaper than some of the other things marketed as teeth-cleansing, but still, $3 per pound - even with free shipping - is a little high. I checked and these are not offered as subscription items, which would knock off 15% of the price.Overall summary: I give this product 4 stars, marking down just slightly for price & ingredients.  That said, I'm placing my 2nd order now ...

column9: Good Clean Treat for your Dog
column10: I got worried about this brand of dog biscuit when my golden retriever (18 months old) licked it a few times and then sat there. She then ate it all up in a little less than a minute. She didn't attempt to jump for it (she often does for cheese or other treats) but my dog Georgia seemed to be happy with the treat. I don't think this brand of biscuit will appeal to all dogs (picky eaters may not enjoy it though that doesn't seem to be a problem with most dogs) but it is a great alternative for dog owners who want only the healthiest products for their pets.

column9: Lunch for less than 50 cents. Yummy!
column10: I love these noodles. Sure, they have no nutritional value what-so-ever but they are conveniently packaged and well preserved enough to easily stockpile hot noodle goodness for years to come. Armageddon, Zombie Apocalypse...it really doesn't matter. I will be prepared for anything with my well seasoned, deep fried ramen.

Comparing these to a local mass market retailer per each, this is a really good price + free shipping.  Currently less than $0.50/each can't get them cheaper elsewhere.  These spicy noodles are great, gives more of a kick compared to the regular chicken flavor.  Personally I think they are just spicy enough without needing to constantly "cool off" your mouth after each bite.These are INSANELY full of sodium; however most Maruchan noodle soups are high in sodium.  Some are upwards of 50% of your allowable daily value so this isn't surprising.The nutritional values from the package are:Calories -- 290Calories from Fat -- 108% Daily Value*Total Fat -- 12.0gSaturated Fat -- 6.0gTrans Fat -- 0.0gCholesterol -- 3mgSodium -- 1190mgTotal Carbohydrates -- 38.0gDietary Fiber -- 2.0gSugars -- 1.0gEasy ways to reduce the sodium is to shake off some of the seasoning prior to adding the water or don't drink all of the broth.  Overall, this is a convenient lunch, easily made with hot water and really delicious.

My kids loves these as an afternoon snack.  The flavor is good and not too spicy at all. I will purchase more for them when they get out of school for summer break. The vendor delivered on time, great price for great product.
i just keep buying different flavors and so far i have not been dissapointed at all and got a very good price also

This flavor is all right... Not spicy at all in my opinion (i eat thai chilli pepper with my rice) !!!! original beef flavor is still the best one for me. Def wont buy this flavor agn. shipment came on time.

This is the option I used for my daughters birth announcement. I do not smoke and did not want to promote it as it is not allwoed to smoke in the office. This was the best option I could find. I did find the gum a little bit lacking on quality it was near stale. However, it is more to celebrate a occasion.
We've been using Heinz Spicy Brown Mustard for years and are very happy having it available in convenient packets which we can take on trips, etc. The taste is great, too!

Excellent african coffee.  I has a good medium-bodied flavor without coffee bitterness.  While it is not as good as the Starbucks Africa Kitamu coffee (which is about impossible to find anymore), it is a good cup of coffee if you like a rich coffee flavor without bitterness.

I was very pleased with the cheese selection I received. It was packed in a styrofoam cooler with ice packs and arrived quickly after being shipped. They won't deliver in summer, but it's worth waiting for cooler weather. There was a lot more cheese than I expected because each one weighed well over a pound. It seems to be a reasonable price, even with shipping, for everything that I received. The pepper jack was nice and hot, the mild cheddar was smooth and mild. Very good tasting and definately not your grocery store cheese. I would definately buy this again.

column9: Versatile with just the right amount of bite
column10: I'm a hot sauce aficionado (my kids typically buy me at least one bottle for Christmas & Father's Day).  A friend recommended the Everidae sauces, so I took a shot and tried Everidae medium and am so glad I did. The flavor enhances rather than competes with the food it's paired with. The mix of sweet & spice is most excellent. I tried it on pizza, cooked inside a burger, on scrambled eggs. Putting it on eggs was akin to reaching breakfast enlightenment - without it scrambled eggs now seem sadly lacking, so it looks like I'm a committed Everidae convert.

This dandy chili mix makes great chili. It is one of the best things I have tasted in a long time. It has a clever concept, which explains why it is a `kit'. The bag has 4 separate packets: a main chile packet (the chili powder has almost no heat, but lots of flavor), a small packet of cayenne, a small packet of salt, and a larger one with masa harina. This way, you adjust the heat, salt, and thickness to your liking; some chile mixes has everything combined, and you cannot change it. One kit is enough for 2 pounds of meat, so larger batches will require more kits.Course, I did not follow the included recipe. I tossed the salt (I used sea salt instead) and masa flour (it was plenty thick without it) packets, used beef chuck cut into 1 ½ inch cubes instead of ground beef (course, it took that much longer to cook, but so what?), and all of the cayenne packet. Boy was it good.

I'm on the website today to order a second twelve-pack of this mix.  I haven't shopped around a lot; Carroll Shelby's is the first and only mix I've tried, and I'm very happy with it.  I found it on Amazon earlier this year after being unable to find it in local stores, and I've just recently gone through the first twelve-pack (okay, I gave one pack to my mother-in-law).I've converted my daughter and my mother-in-law to it, as well; they're both chili lovers and we use this recipe together with dark red kidney beans, diced tomatoes, a small can of tomato sauce, and ground turkey (healthier, and cheaper, and there's a small difference in texture and none in taste from ground beef).  We recommend going with the recipe option that calls for a large can of diced tomatoes, and about half the cayenne packet, and about 32 oz of canned dark red kidney beans, drained (the recipe only recommends 16 oz), and between 2 and 3 lbs of ground whatever.Ground beef, not too lean, or chopped chuck, or cubed pot roast are all good candidates for the meat.  As the package used to say, fifteen years ago, don't waste your money on expensive cuts of beef here.The directions are pretty basic and perfectly adequate to produce a good hearty meal.  Use a _big_ frying pan, 13" if you've got one, and have a larger stew pot/saucepan of some kind standing by in case your ingredients are too much for the pan.  Do stir frequently once you've added the spices and flour, because there's some tendency for the mix to thicken up and form a skin on the bottom of the pot, and you'll lose good flavor that way (not to mention the bottom might get burned and ruin the whole recipe).With 2-3 lbs of meat, two cans of beans and a large (28 oz) can of diced tomatoes in tomato juice, the whole thing makes six or seven _really_ generous portions (12-14 oz each).  I make it and freeze most of it in individual portions, taking it in to work and microwaving it at lunch.

column9: Delicious Chili Kit with Lots of Flexible Customization Options
column10: Friends, I love good food. This Chili Kit by Carroll Shelby is excellent. It creates an extremely savory basic chili that is easy to adjust to your particular taste in the areas of: spicy/hot, salt, or thickness.The flavor created by the spices in the main packet is the best attribute. Lots of deep, low, earthy tones that have excellent complexity and subtlety.Another great feature is the brilliant strategy of putting the cayenne pepper in a separate pouch. I only put in a little. My wife likes her chili slightly warm: warm enough to be interesting. So, I put about 1/8th of the cayenne pouch when I cook the chili, then I sprinkle extra on only my serving when I eat my bowl-full. I like a little more warmth to add to the complex flavors without so much heat that I begin to loose the ability to taste all those wonderful layers of tastes.It is another exceptionally brilliant idea to put the salt in yet another separate pouch. Again, my wife does not like very much salt at all, so I don't put any in while cooking. I salt my bowl-full with some sea-salt, and in my opinion a little sea-salt REALLY brings out the complex flavors in this chili mix. I hope more products begin to put the salt in a separate packet. I think most folks would be appalled to see exactly how much salt is in the average meal-mix they buy: like Hamburger Helper for example. Plus for some reason good sea salt just tastes better than the cheap salt.Lastly, Mr. Shelby puts a packet of thickening powder in his kit - in addition to the main chili pack, the cayenne packet, and the salt packet. The thickening agent is simply finely ground corn meal and it does a nice job of thickening the chili if that is what you like and prefer. I have prepared this kit many times both with and without the thickening, and I like it both ways. I now just alternate for variety.PREPARATION TIPS from my personal preferences:*Saute LOTS of onion to go in the chili. At lease one large yellow onion, and I sometimes do one-and-a-half.*Always use the optional 15oz can of diced tomatoes (don't forget to reduce the amount of water used, like the direction on the box say.*Always use the optional 15oz can of beans. My favorite are dark kidney beans, but greatly enjoy black-beans, pintos, or about any chili-style bean. TIP: drain the liquid from the can of beans into a bowl, and use the liquid as substitute for part of the "water" called for in the recipe.*Some favorite toppings in the bowl: sea salt, cayenne powder, diced white onions, pepper jack or cheddar cheese, black olives, guacamole, salsa, sour cream, tortilla chips.I will address some of the complaints by negative reviewers:1)A few said the chili was not very flavorful. Unfortunately in the USA most folks confuse "salt" with flavor. Since the mix has separate salt packet and none in the mix, I believe that nay-sayers have just not put in the prodigious amount of extra salt that they are used to associating with "flavor". As I wrote earlier, the chili benefits from some sea salt, but for my taste, does not need large amounts.2)Some may say the lack of heat is not flavorful enough. Well, there are folks who like things thermo-nuclear-hot, and you just can't get there with the little extra cayenne packet supplied in the kit. The chili with no cayenne at all is slightly warm, and varying amounts of the cayenne powder will satisfy the tastes of 99.999% of folks. For those who like more heat, add whatever crazy-hot stuff you require to get the heat you want.3)If your complaint is that it does not taste exactly like you want right out of the box (like some other brand perhaps), I disagree strongly, because I believe that the customization offered by the different pouches included, is a greatly beneficial feature. If they made it to taste exactly like YOU want, then it probably wouldn't taste like many other folks want.

I've been using this Carroll Shelby chili mix for years, but finding it in local stores has been hit or miss.  It had gotten to where I was buying several packages at a time whenever I could find it anywhere.I was amazed to find it here on Amazon, and for considerably less than I've paid in stores in the past.  I love chili, and usually make 1-2 batches per month during the winter, and at least a batch every couple of months during the summer.There's a recipe on the package, but I don't know anyone who actually follows it to the letter.  I suppose if you've never made chili before, it's a good starting place.  You can then decide how you might want to modify it.I usually use half ground beef and half ground turkey (approx. a pound of each), a chopped onion, a 28-oz can of "redi-cut" tomatoes, a small can of tomato paste, a small can of black beans, a small can of pinto beans; then, from the chili kit, I add the spice packet and the entire cayenne pepper packet.  They used to include a tiny bottle of tabasco sauce; they discontinued that in favor of the cayenne.  I like things a little spicy, and the amount of cayenne here makes for a low-medium "burn" level.Only occasionally do I find I need to use the masa flour.  Usually, my chili is thick enough without it.Finally, I top it with shredded colby-jack cheese, and serve it with cornbred muffins.  We're talking serious yum here.It makes amazing chili dogs, too.  And chili mac.  And chili cornbread casserole (thicken the chili a little, put it in a square baking dish, top with dollops of cornbread batter, bake at 350 until cornbread is puffed and starting to brown).Carroll Shelby's mix has just the right combination of spices to make the best tasting chili I've ever had.  I'll so glad that it's available right here on Amazon.

column9: Real Chili....... just the best! Used it for YEARS!
column10: After living in East Texas for a number of years it became second nature to make chili using the venison provided by a generous neighbor..... ( then it was FREE..... now we pay for it, but it's "green" sustainable and healthy and delicious).This makes really wonderful, authentic chili..... as long as you don't add beans to it! Two kits and four pounds of venison is just the right amount for us. We use : one beer in place of the water, the tomato sauce as called for,the masa mixed in water to a slurry ( for the mineral taste in the masa) and 2/3 of one pack of the cayenne..... perfect .But DON'T brown the meat! Just let it simmer in the spices until it's tender and juicy, then add the cayenne, masa slurry and some of the salt..... give it 20 minutes to thicken up (add a bit more beer if it's too thick for your taste.Top with raw minced onion and cotijo cheese, crumbled fine, a couple of thin slices of raw jalapeno for crunch and a hunk of hot water corn breadon the side bread.....Divine!That's the best part about having the components all seperate.. YOU decide how hot, thick, or salty you prefer...but his spices are spot on. We never add a thing.If it plays in Terlingua, it plays for us.

column9: It's how it's supposed to taste
column10: I've been eating chili made with this since I was a kid, so for me, this is how chili is supposed to taste.In my family, growing up, Mom did most of the cooking. Except tacos, chili and barbecue which my dad did. My dad, a bit of a racing fan, always got this kind of chili mix for chili. He would make it with chuck steak ground into thick meaty chunks, tomato sauce and use just a touch of the cayenne,half the salt, a bit of the thickener, and the chili flavor packet. Mom would make corn bread to go with it. The chili was served topped with cheese and onions with a thick slice of cornbread on the side dripping with honey and butter. My brother and I both loved chili night.Skip forward to my adult years and my marriage, I explained to my husband one day that I wanted chili for dinner. He said we would get the things to make, and I told him "Dad always made the chili. I don't know how to, so you have to make the chili." He replied that he didn't know how to make chili, so I explained to him how to make it and told him what kind of seasoning to get. The same sort Dad always got. Now it's in boxes instead of brown bags, but it still tastes the same.We make it to our tastes, and both of us make the chili. If I make it, I sauté a large onion then put in a lb of ground turkey and brown it. Then I add a large can of tomato puree and a can of kidney beans, and mix in the full chili packet, put the salt aside for popcorn another night, a bit of the masa thickener, and a pinch of cayenne and let it simmer for an hour. When my husband makes it, he makes it with very lean ground beef, tomato sauce, kidney beans, chili packet and a bit more pepper than I use, sometimes adding bell peppers and onions in while it's simmering. We usually serve it with tortillas on the side and topped with a sharp cheddar.And my teens love chili night as much as I did when I was younger.

column9: Not as good as homemade, but GREAT for a mix!
column10: I've made this several times now, and I like it quite well.I always add onion, and I usually add green peppers. This chili mix makes THE best chili I've had. My dad used it when I was younger, and now I use it in my own chili. That is the only thing similar to my dad's chili. I don't use the salt (growing up I had to limit my salt intake to nothing), and the masa (mine usually turns out thick enough). I use about 1/2 the packet of cayenne and instead of 2 lbs ground beef, I use 1 lbs ground beef (or even moose or caribou since I live in Alaska) and 1 lb of pork sausage. Also, when browning the meat, I use 1/2 the chili mix packet as seasoning, and use the other 1/2 about 1/2 way through my cooking time. I then place the beans, browned meat plus 1 can italian stewed tomatoes, 1 can water and 1 can tomato sauce. set the slow cooker on low and about 1/2 way through I add the other 1/2 seasoning packet. Turns out GREAT every time and I've placed in many chili cook-offs using this recipe.

column10: With ingedients in four packets, make it hot or not as you wish. Start with the recipe on the box. I also sauteed with the meat 3/4 cup onion and 3/4 cup mixed Anaheim and Jalapeno chopped peppers.Thicken with a roux made from the included Masa flour (corn flour) or not depending on your taste. Unlike other clueless people this is the Spanish version of Nutella and it is really similar or the same. So if you like Nutella (which most Americans are familiar with, this is the same thing)Composition of Nocilla and Nutella:Sugar, vegetable oil, hazelnuts (4% Nocilla; 13% Nutella), skim cocoa (8.5% Nocilla; 7,4% Nutella), powdered skim milk (4.5% Nocilla; 6.6% Nutella) etc. so clearly the Nutella has more of a nutty flavor but overall Nocilla is a great snack.

I wasn't exactly sure what to expect when I tasted this stuff, but I guess something that tasted at least a little like, say, chocolate and maybe hazelnut?  That's definitely not what I got with this - it definitely didn't have any hazelnut taste at all and any taste of chocolate was very faint to stay the least.  It sort of tasted like marshmallow cream, except much sweeter (and not in a good way).  It also had a strong aftertaste of artificial vanilla.  Not only did it taste horrible, but the texture was really strange - it was nearly liquid. column9: Break the cycle of overpriced coffee pods once and for all !!
column10: Just because these come in a tea bag type of pouch does not mean they can not be brewed in a single cup ($20) coffee pot. I have been using this curry paste for several years now, and it makes a great dish. Although it doesn't beat eating Indian out, its the best paste I have used for at home dishes. Even though this is a "hot" paste, I would consider it mild.

Patak's sauces have many uses but I always make a basic chicken curry.  A friend from India taught this recipe to me, and now I always have a jar or two on hand.  If you want you can get one of the Indian pickles/relishes as a garnish.  This is easy but is a bit time consuming with all the dicing and sauteing.  Typically the recipe as written takes an hour or so from start to finish, and serves 3-4 adults.  I always make at least a double batch; it's just as easy and that way I have leftovers to freeze and everyone can have plenty to eat.  You can use any rice, but basmati is so fragrant that it is what I prefer.  Some Indian groceries have frozen Naan you can heat in the oven for an even more satisfying dinner.Ingredients:1-1 ½ lbs chicken breast cut into 1-2" cubes1 cup nonfat plain yogurtSalt3 tbs Patak's curry paste, flavor/heat depending on your taste1 (generous) tsp cumin seed1 (generous) tsp mustard seed1 small onion diced3 cloves garlic diced2 medium potatoes, diced same size as chicken cubes2-3 carrots, diced same size as chicken cubes1 14 oz can diced tomatoes with juice½ cup frozen peas2-3 tbsp cooking oilSalt to taste1. Add chicken yogurt, curry paste and about ½ tsp salt to a bowl; mix thoroughly and let marinate while you prepare vegetables2. Heat oil in large frying pan over medium heat until hot3. Add cumin seeds and mustard seeds, stir.  They are ready when mustard seeds start to pop.  Do not let them burn.4. Add onion and garlic.  Saute until soft.  Stir constantly or else it will burn.5. Add carrots and potatoes.  Saute until potatoes are just about ready to eat.  You have to stir very frequently or they will stick/burn.  I do not let anything caramelize.6. Add chicken/yogurt mixture.  Saute a few minutes until chicken is about half cooked through.  Lower heat to low.7. Add tomatoes and let simmer until the juices cook down a bit, and chicken is cooked through.8. Add peas for color.  Add salt to taste.9. Serve over freshly cooked basmati rice.  Remember to soak the basmati rice prior to cooking or it will be hard.
Patak's makes the best curry around. I frequently use it in my Yellow Chicken Curry Dish which is a favorite with both my husband and seven year old.

They crumble easily... and by easily I mean my 3.5 month old Wheaten Terrier destroyed these in less than 30min, and she's only about 15 pounds right now. They are recommended for dogs 6 months + with pretty much a full set of permanent teeth because they can shred the bone more easily and to a finer debris. For my dog this was BS... she destroyed these into tiny little flakes that can be easily digested AND managed to get them all over her underbelly and tangled in her fur. The mess wasn't an issue.. the durability was. This is basically an expensive treat, I much rather give her bullysticks over this as a treat (and they last longer). If your dog is teething, this is def NOT the Nylabone version you want. Stick to the original plastic flavored bones or frozen towels. Both work great.

I was under the impression when I bought this at our local pet supply store (based on salesperson's advice) that this bone, while edible, would take several days of working on to be consumed.  Great.  It's a little pricey, but I have a teething 5 month old puppy who has recently been spayed; she can't get her regular course of exercise so I bought this as a nice treat to help keep her occupied in her restless state.  I took it away from her (mad dog!) after 45 minutes.  Just one end was left.  I had bought her the largest "souper" size.  After reading the other reviews, I count myself lucky that she got that much time out of it.  Yes it's a "treat", but at $6, it's a treat I cannot afford to give her very often.  Health wise it's not a treat I could make a habit of feeding often; I feel I have to give my puppy less dinner tonight to make up for the large amount of calories she just wolfed down.  I hope that it doesn't make her sick as it did another reviewer's dog.  I could take her kong, put a spoonful of kibble in it, break up a slice of cheese and shove it in there, stick the whole thing in the microwave for a few seconds to get the cheese melty, let it cool down, and THAT will take her a good 15 minutes to manage to get out.  All for a LOT less money.  That said, I give it 0 stars for value, 5 for "my dog loved it".  It gets a 2 overall from me and I probably would not buy again, nor would I recommend to a friend.

column9: Once in a while special treat
column10: My 9 month old 45 lb pit bull is an avid chewer who has and will eat just about anything he can find, including my hard wood floors.. while picking up bird food I grabbed one of these relieved that at least when he devoured it he wasn't eating chunks of plastic and hence wouldn't get mad when I had to take it away and throw it in the trash.  I came home, read a magazine, he sat quietly on the sofa beside me happily chewing and by the time I had finished my magazine he had finished his bone.  While certainly not a long lasting chew it is something I'd pick up again when I get bird food since I know he enjoys it.  I used to buy the stuffed regular bones but then I'd end up with him wanting to play fetch with the empty bone and would end up throwing it away so at least I know this isn't something that months later i'm stepping on getting out of bed.
My dog chewed it up & made it disappear in about 5 minutes, while I was emptying the box. He definitely likes it but its a little costly to go so fast.
The product was exactly as described.  Wolf is Healthy Edible's code for large.  I do wish that this vendor would sell more than 9 units of this item at a time.

I wish I had read the other two reviews here. I picked this up at a local store for about 6 bucks. My dog just ate half of it in 5 minutes and would be done with it now if I had not taken it away. And he is only 5 months old...so an older bigger dog could destroy this even quicker. I can't believe they actually sell these...at that price at least. He absolutely loved it and is quite mad I took it away...but not worth the money.

As the initial reviewer stated, the biggest issue with this product is its durability, or lack thereof.With the Nylabone brand name on it and a price approaching $10 you might be under the impression that this will last quite awhile.  I timed how long it took my dog to eat the largest one they make (the one shaped like a fist).  It took him 11 minutes to leisurely eat and about 2 minutes to 'clean up' the mess.  If he were actually hungry he probably could have done it a few minutes faster.  So, almost a dollar a minute for this product when viewed as an entertainment/chew toy product.  It's possible to get them for about half price from some of the amazon vendors but this only makes sense when buying large quantities due to the expense of shipping on small orders from them.I was hoping this might last awhile and be better for him than the 'plastic' Nylabone products which exit the dog in solid chunks (eww!).My dog thoroughly enjoyed this but at these prices I can't justify it.

I do NOT recommend these.  My six month old Golden Retriever, who is not a strong chewer, devoured this in less than five minutes.  It is a very expensive treat and I'm just hoping we don't have to pay a vet bill on top of the price of the Edible Nylabone.  I will never buy these again!!!

If I were wealthy I'd be eating these every day.  Full of flavor, richly fruity taste and great crunch.  Some have mentioned the hard raisins.  Wow: different strokes!  I LOVE the raisins.  They have an almost carmelized taste.  But they ARE hard, and best enjoyed like any hard "candy".  Actually, I like to sort them out of the mix and keep them in a separate jar.The only reason I give the "Munchies" a four rather than five star rating is 1) the cost, and 2) the non-airtight package.  For maximum enjoyment, find a truly airtight container and dump the fruit into it as soon as the package arrives (and, if you're like me, separating out the raisins as you go).

column9: Love 'em!  Great price and great taste!
column10: I have bought this item multiple times and I am going to buy again today.  For me it's a great mix of all my favorite fruit.  I love how the Just Tomato brand doesn't add sugar and the "dried fruit" isn't slimy like other brands, which is one of the main reasons I keep coming back.

column9: The raisins are too hard to eat!
column10: I purchased the "Just Tomatoes Just Fruit Munchies, 8-Ounce Tubs (Pack of 2)" The fruit mixture is good until you eat the raisins. Some of them are very hard and I almost broke my tooth. I would not buy this product again because of this. Buy the Strawberries they will not break your teeth and they are excellent! I would suggest the company not include the raisins in this mixture anymore. Thanks! :)

column9: A great way to let little ones snack on healthy fruit
column10: All of the fruits in the Just Fruit Munchies were perfect for the little ones except for the raisins which were too tough and crunchy amongst all the softer pieces.  But overall, having picked out the raisins, my kids just love to get their fruit this way and so do I.

This is one of our favorite Just Tomato items. The price is good on amazon, however, amazon failed on their packing. We received the tubs smashed and one busted. We were actually going to use one of them as a gift, along with another (smashed) tub of vegies. Oh well, good thing we like these, and good thing we didn't mind opening them right away. Since these are dehydrated/freeze dried, I would be worried about them gaining moisture during shipping if damaged and it was raining. Amazon won't take back food either.

Love them! All the Just Tomatoes products are great and tasty - a wonderful snack and so much better than chips!  Amazon does a great job delivering them to my door quickly and without crushing the products!

column9: My whole family loves these munchies!
column10: The fruit mixture is a great mix of tart and sweet fruits. My 18-month-old son and husband can practically finish the entire tub in one sitting!

column4: S. Marine "BE YOUR GUEST - PARTY PLANNER"
column10: As much as I think this product yummy, becareful with it, because I broke my tooth on it and have been running back and forth to the dentist from it.
not my favorite of their products. The rasins are Hard and sometimes Burnt, it takes to long to soften.

Well, this product was a great disappointment.  All the fruit kinda tastes the same, except maybe the banana chips.  The fruit is very tart!!  And the pieces of fruit are too small and tend to turn into dust.  Must be a better product out there.  I am on the hunt  --
I purchased the dried strawberries and they tasted great. The price is a little prohibited but otherwise a great product. I hope they offer discounts for return customers.

I love these little munchies! Every morning at work, I throw a few in the bottom of a styrofoam cup, scoop some oats and a little brown sugar on top, add some hot water and ta-da, yummy breakfast! The water plumps up the fruit very nicely. Much tastier than oatmeal pouches, and much healthier than the craisins, dried blueberries, and other sugar-fortified fruits I used to add to my oats. A handful of these fruit munchies also makes a great mid-afternoon snack.

I absolutely love Just Tomatoes's dried fruit products, such as these Just Fruit Snacks. They are crunchy and flavorful, like eating a fruit candy, only much healthier and "reduced guilt"! I especially like eating them plain or over greek yogurt.They are unfortunately pretty expensive, but I find them worth the cost. The large pouches last quite a while, though I recommend transferring them to snap-top containers to maintain maximum crunch and freshness. I've ordered them (and the Just Fruit Salad variety, also quite yummy) several times through Amazon.com and have never had a problem.

When I travel I bring a wide ceramic mug, plastic spoons, baggies of this, and instant oatmeal packets (Dr McDougall's are good). I put the fruit in the mug first, then the oatmeal, and cover with hot water from the coffee maker. The fruit softens up perfectly for a great healthy breakfast or late night snack. They are also good for straight snacking, but there are less expensive brands. I recommend trying these and Sensible Foods cherry fruit blend to compare on taste and price.

column9: DANGER!!!! - Was Fantastic, Now Somewhat Disappointing
column10: This is sooooo good - I cannot stop eating it!  If they threw in some of their dried strawberries, it would be the ultimate perfection.However, the mix is sooo tasty... it's going to start becoming lunch and/or dinner!**Update**This product has changed. It used to come in a plastic tupperware-style container and now comes in a bag. That change I like. However, the quality and taste of the dried fruit also seems to have changed. Sadly, it's gone downhill :(The fruit before used to have several different types and flavors. Now, they primarily taste like light caramel popcorn and are not nearly as delicious. For the price, I'm afraid I won't be ordering again.

We love the Just Fruit Munchies!  My husband and I can, and will, eat an entire 8-oz tub in one sitting.  They are just so delicious.  My favorite fruit in the mix are the crunchy grapes - I try and pick all of them out to eat for myself!

I tried the organic version of these at the health food store last week and loved it! so I had to buy some online. I think these snacks are really good. my daughter LOVES them! a great snack for on the go. I haven't found any really hard pieces yet, so it gets an A+ in my book.
These are so good in yogurt.  They are like fruit and cereal in one - very crunchy.  I love the contrasting sweet and tart aspect of the mix.

I was VERY pleasantly surprised with these - although as in another review - the packaging left alot to be desired (the Amazon boxing of it)  I also received dented containers inside the box which was barely holding together.  but the product is great and I am buying more today!
The fruit munch was very good and nutritious.  I still have a tub left.  All I can say is it was very delicious, tasty and tickled my taste buds.

I love this mix. The one thing that really did it for me were the crunchy raisins. I can only eat raisins in Kellog's Raisin Bran and Little Debbie Raisin cream pies. But I loved these raisins so much that I purchased them separately. But, they weren't crunchy. How do I make the raisins crunch?!Anyway,Just Fruit Munchies is a great snack, if you don't have a problem with the crunch. I only gave it four stars because I could do with the mango/apples. Still good, but unnecessary.

It is great, only if you use it in yogurt or something to cook with.  You definitely cannot just snack on it-they are all way too crunchy.  However, if you leave it in yogurt for a few minutes, then it tastes really great.

column9: Tart and crispyTHIS IS A VERY LIGHT WEIGHT SNACK FOR PACKING
column10: This is a very light weight snack for packing; it is tart and not too sweet.  The raisins are chewy, but much of the other fruit is crispy.  Very good!

This isn't bad personal lube.  It is silicone based, so that's good.  However, the formula for this particular one is pretty thick.  The consistancy is about twice as dense as other silicone based lubes (Astroglide X, Wet Platinum) which are really good.  I wouldn't use this for anal with my wife (or whatever you're in to, I won't judge) but maybe for foreplay and massages, this is fine.  It's way too thick for toys, anal or just fast penetration.  Think of it like putting 80 weight truck oil in a small car that should have some thing closer to 30 weight oil to work properly.  It'll still work, but not with the performance you'd like.So as stated, if you like anal or just like it fast and rough etc., stick to Astroglide X or Wet Platinum (silicone based lubes with a fairly lose consistancy).  They use Wet Platinum in porn...  System Jo premium, use it for massages and foreplay.

This is a good tasting relish but it is sweeter, milder and wetter than I expected. I drained the extra water and applied a couple table spoons to my breakfast burrito to get the best taste. If you want a sweet mild relish with good flavor this is the one.
contains salt - if you want just Cashews, Search for a salt free alternatives, Really should have listed this on the label or in the description.
It's delicious but for my family a little bigger size would be better. Also less salty would be 5 stars.

The pharmacy in my hometown used to sell these and their green (actual medicinal cough-drop) alternative. The others were great for if you had a sore throat, but these.. oh, these were amazing for me. I was a little kid and the local pharmacy sold both types, but I would always fake sick so my mom could get me these since she knew I wasn't really ill, I just wanted the candies.I had to move across the country and quite frankly, I hate the cough drops and hard candies that Walmart sells. I was aching for a taste of my hometown, so I went as far as hunting them down online, since I didn't remember the name. I'm glad to know I can get a steady supply of them online from now on.They just arrived today - rather quickly - and I tore into my first pack. You're paying a very cheap price for a box of 24 packages, each of which has 9 tasty drops.. Trust me, one is all you need to satisfy your sweet tooth and leave you tasting like honey all day long.I will probably continue to buy these for as long as I live.

My husband and I love to cook.  We just ordered all the Palouse Brand products and are so excited about the quality of each of them.  We had many ask for the recipe, but it wasn't the recipe it was the great quality of our ingredients.  Palouse brand isn't just packaged cutely it is the real deal.  If you like to cook this product is a must try!  Thanks Palouse brand for bringing fresh, great ingredients to my family table!

Palouse Brand Lentils are the best lentils I have ever had.  These lentils hold their shape and texture, they are tender, and the taste is beyond compare. They are great is soups, salads, chilli, you name it. This company produces a lentil that is a true connoisseur's delight and well worth the dollars.  "Palouse Brand" is delivering on their promise of an outstanding product!

Pardina lentils are my favorite.  They hold their shape when cooked so, being a vegetarian, they are great as a meat substitute in things like sloppy joes or casseroles.  The dryland hills of the Palouse in eastern Washington and northern Idaho produce the best lentils, dry peas, garbanzo beans and wheat, much of which are exported to India and Asia.  Pardinas are great in soups, salads, casseroles and rice pilafs.  Palouse Brand are the only brand of lentils in my kitchen.

We have cooked these lentils in the crockpot, added a little Texas Pete, chopped onions & dried red sweet peppers. Allow to cook several hours in crockpot, & check tenderness of lentils.  Added smokey salt for flavor or optional: smoked turkey leg or county ham hock.  Add some cooked brown rice before taking up & serve.  Great complete meal!

These are really good tasting lentils. The first thing I notice was the lack of that shinny coating you see on store bought lentils. When you open the big you can tell right away there is something different about these. They cook easily and hold their shape and taste great.

Brown lentils are actually difficult to find in the grocery store. These are much better quality anyway. They are bigger and the end product tastes better than your run of the mill grocery store lentils. To the reviewer who gave a subpar review due to the bag not having directions...google is your friend.
I love these lentils becasue the skin is less noticable when you cook them. I bought some for my mom and she said they are the best ones shes ever seen.

My one year old loves lentils, so I was happy when I found a good sized portion of GMO Free lentils. They cooked well and tasted delicious. They are a little smaller than what you usually get at the grocery store, but that might be cause they are Spanish Brown.
These are excellent lentils -- clean, flavorful and easy to cook to perfection. Highly recommended. Especially with carrots, garlic, cumin and spinach.

Lentils are as staple of our diet, and these are great. There actually is a noticeable difference in taste from standard store bought lentils. I love that they are certified GMO free and the packaging is quaint and rustic. But, really, the flavor and the knowledge of where it came from are the biggest selling points for me, and the price for the quantity is spot on also. I will buy these again for sure.Enjoy!

These are excellent lentils, from a great agricultural area. I've been to the Palouse several times, a wonderful, amazingly beautiful region of rolling green farmland in eastern Washington/northern Idaho, famous for photography, rich soil, and, well, lentils.  They even have a lentil festival every August, no kidding. When I saw these lentils on Amazon I had to try them - I belong to Amazon Prime, get free two-day shipping - and they are excellent. Like others say, they are small, firm, and really flavorful. They take more time and water to cook than most other kinds of lentils I've used due to their firmness, but retain their shape really well.  They are also chewy, not mushy, and the flavor is kind of nutty. You can do anything you want with them - make curry, soup, salad, mix them with rice or quinoa or chopped veggies, season them any way you like. I love lentils in general, other faves are red lentils (sweet and mushy, make great soup) and black lentils (tiny and round, and a great alternative to black beans) which I can get at local health food stores, but these are truly top shelf, and I've never seen them in stores. I agree with what someone else said, too, they are very clean, I haven't found any rocks or twigs in them. Just great lentils. I'm ordering a five pound bag this time so I can have them on hand for awhile - and I love knowing I'm supporting a great gem of a growing region by buying them.

My wife cooks a lot of lentils. This product is far superior to other brands on the market, and we've tried them all. The flavor is amazing and cooks nicely. From now on, our family will only buy Pardina lentils. And, we like that it's made in the USA and GMO free.

Lentils have the ability to take on the flavor of whatever they are cooked in.  I have made two different batches from this mini potato sack of lentils.  The beans have turned out well and I have yet to find rocks or other strange colored objects that appear in bags of store bought beans.

All lentils are not created equal. I have has lentils that were more expensive and less expensive. These are by far the best lentils I have ever tasted. They cook extremely fast, they are tender and the taste is off the charts. Every one that has tasted them raves about them. Excellent value for your money.

column9: Just buy them - they are excellent
column10: I think I may have just made the most delicious lentil soup of my life!  This is an excellent product and you will not regret your purchase.

At $15 for 5 pounds these lentils cost $3 a pound.  My wife was very unhappy with me as she can get them for a dollar a pound at the store.  I told her - these are super lentils and she said they better be for the price.  Kidding aside - don't buy these, buy your lentils at the store!
Lentils in a big bag. It came with no cooking directions or suggestions and when I emailed them the response was blah!I didn't see the great customer service they bragged about. It must not be there.

column9: Enjoyable, but just not for Me.
column10: I liked these candies but not enough for what I paid for them. This is possibly due to the fact that I have never had Japanese candy and this being my first experience I may have gone into this with the wrong mindset. I may  be willing to give these a second chance in the future.

I love wasabi and thought I would try this product out. I hate to have to run to a restaurant every time I have a wasabi craving.You mix this powder with equal amounts of water, let sit 10 minutes and you've got wasabi sauce.It tastes good and has a good kick. It will burn your sinuses. The color isn't a bright green like I usually see in restaurant but is kind of a pale, pea-soup color but it doesn't affect the flavor.The texture is like when you take powdered mustard and mix with water, the texture is a little different than restaurant wasabi. It is more like a sauce than a paste.If the color and the texture doesn't bother you then I recommend this product, it still has all the wasabi taste.Amazon does sell wasabi paste on here also if you are interested in more of paste texture. I'm pleased with this product, it's great on food and since it's a powder, you can sprinkle in food like a spice. Yum!

I normally have used tube "wasabi" (aka horseradish). I tried this for a change. What a mistake! Maybe it's the product, but this was completely bland, virtually no heat. A bad batch??
