I can't recommend this.Edit:Well, I found out where the heat went. You have to let it sit for 10 minutes of so after adding water for the "heat" to develop. But still, if you have an asian market near you, you can pick up a large bag of powder a lot cheaper and store it in jars, etc.
I love this stuff and use it often.  It is easy to use, tastes great and you can be creative with it. There are many uses for this in your kitchen, it not just for sushi.

The power is not as strong as I've had before. evidently preperation of redishes vary or some start as hotterredishes. I have tried to doctor some almonds that had wabasi treatment tried to dampen and sprinkle withwasabi to give hotter taste--marginal results--.

column4: North Pole RVer Traveler "North Pole Consumer"
column9: Great Tasting Tarrazu Coffee Great Price
column10: Reggies Tarrazu is a good brand. Has great flavor and an affordable price for Dedicated Tarrazu Coffee Drinkers.  We have tried many brands and will stick with this one and this package

We were not pleased with the coffee we received.  However when we contacted the company they were very cordial and have replaced the coffee.  Will comment more on this after we receive the replacement coffee.
I normally prefer the Hazelnut coffee, but this brand is simply wonderful!The ground is quite fine so be careful with the filter.
I love it. It is easier for me to get more fruit daily.  When hunger strikes (which is often) I grab my bag and not junk food.

We have two labs...they wait all day for (a) their dinner and then (b) for our dinner...then once that is done they do their act, their dance and their demand for their "chewy!"  They love them.  And we trust the product.  Good for their teeth...and lasts more than 4 seconds compared to all the other brands.
This is a travel must have for my Chocolate Lab Lizzy. As soon as she is in the back of the SUV and the engine is started she is looking for her chew. These chews keep her busy and occupied.

column9: Provides Scottie Pup Healthy, Safe and Fun Chewing.
column10: After some unpleasant experiences with unwholesome "rawhide" type dog chews (some from China and Mexico) we found these Purina brand "HeartyHide" (real beefhide) chicken basted strips a great diversion for a 7 month old Scottie with a need to chew.  Our dog spends hours working these strips over and actually consumes some of them.  He prizes the chewed on pieces and tries to "bury" them under pillows and chair covers.  He likes to carry his current chip around and will take it to bed and sleep with his head over the chip.  Wonderful, safe and wholesome dog chew.  The chicken flavor coating does not stain our rugs but the original (beef?) flavor has a dark brown coating that did stain our rugs...the light tan chicken basted strips seem to taste good to MacTavish and do not stain.  Your dog will thank you trying these.

I love how this cereal is not only high in protein and low in sugar, but it tastes great too! It's light yet has that nutty taste. I'll be honest in saying that I normally do not like eating Special K Cereal. All the other Special K variations they've come out with has not hit home with me. I feel like there is a disconnection in the flavors with their cereal. But this one is really good, however. I am finding myself buying it over and over. I never get sick of it. They don't sell them at Target for some reason so I find myself hunting down Amazon or Walmart to get my boxes! This cereal is relatively healthy and with many benefits. Great start to day!

I was thrilled to find a high protein, low carb cereal again.  I found this cereal while traveling out of state, liked it and attempted to find it when I got home.  No dice.  No store in a 25 mile radius had it.  Found it here and with auto ship it's the same price as the grocery.

column4: RLHT "NYC to NJ to DC and back"
column10: Delicious and perfect healthy cereal, but it is bland.  Add cinnamon and Splenda for a delicious taste.

Kellog Special K High Protein cearel tastes better than the other varieties of Special K and is much more filling. For some reason I can't find it in my local markets, so I am happy I found it on Amazon.

column9: BE WARNED: Contains High Fructose Corn Syrup
column10: I used to love this product, for a whole 2 months, until I read the words "high fructose corn syrup" (hfcs) within the ingredients list.  Now I just can't justify spending any money on cereal that tastes like cardboard AND has hfcs in it, even if it has a great protein to carbohydrate ratio.

I read the reviews before buying this cereal thinking it would be somewhat decent. But it's lacking one essential thing: flavor. I give this product 2 stars only because of the nutritional value.  I'm so glad I only bought one box from a local grocery store instead of buying the 4 pack here, as I am already having a tough time finishing off the  one box by itself!

I see quite a few people saying how wonderful this tastes, but that was not my experience.  It tastes horrible and I have it away to someone else (she hasn't reported back if she liked it or not).  So....either some people truly like the taste of this or the cereal company has people writing positive reviews.  I've loved all Kellogg's cereals until this one.  Blech.
Special K Protein cereal is good but I like it when mixed with Special K blueberry.  Sometimes I have it for a sweet instead of candy.
I wasn't a huge fan of this cereal.  It is not as sweet as other Special K cereal.  I think it does have a good proportion of protein though.I would not buy again.

I decided to try this to up my protein intake. After my first bite I thought it wasn't so bad. After my second, I changed my mind. It may be the worse breakfast cereal I've ever eaten. I told myself to finish the bowl, but couldn't and had to spit out my last mouthful to prevent myself from vomiting. It was that bad. I honestly wonder if people on strict diets lose their sense of taste.

column9: High in Protein, Low in Carbs
column10: I started eating this cereal when I found out that I had gestational diabetes with my current pregnancy. It is very difficult to eat an almost Atkins like diet, be vegetarian and have keep your choices varied. It is VERY low in carbs, yet high in protein which is different from almost all other cereals. It tastes good and fills you up.

column9: Let me save you the trouble...
column10: I am looking for ways to increase protein intake--so I jumped on this cereal--and bought four boxes. The minute it was delivered, I poured a big bowl. This is a huge disappointment. Cardboard has more flavor. It's wretched. I am sure there are many other sources of protein that you don't have to choke down. I hope reading this review will save you the trouble and expense...

I was looking for a new cereal to enjoy, since Product 19 can't be found on grocery store shelves anymore.  I know Kellogg's is really pushing the "Special K" diet and all, but this is the worst tasting cereal I've ever had.  After I choked down most of the first bowl I immediately pitched the rest in the trash.  Thanks Amazon for making Product 19 available; wish I had thought to look here earlier before buying the Special K Protein Plus.

column9: If you like eating shreds of newspaper..
column10: One word- Yucka. After not being able to finish just one bowl of this, I've decided I'll give it to the birds. Seriously so nasty. People always complain about how fiber cereal tastes like cardboard. Well, I think Kelloggs tried to fix this problem by making this cereal 'thinner'. But by that it just turned it into newspaper instead of cardoard. It takes forever to chew! The people who think it's good are probably old, taste-bud-less, or just choking it down for it's fiber benefits. There are easier ways to get fiber.

I relied on the Special K name when I chose this cereal.  The pecan variety was wonderful so, after reviewing the grain content, I figured that Protein Plus would be comparable.  I could not have been more wrong.  After an hour of chewing, I finally choked down a bowl.  Was almost late for work.  It tasted like "All Bran" from the 60's, but worse.  I asked my spouse if he tried it and without coaching, he said after chewing forever, he finally got through a bowl.  'Nuff said.  Kellogs, try again.  Worst cereal I've ever had in 50+ years.

I love cereal and must watch carbs carefully. This is the only low carb cereal on the market. It's not as sweet and regular Special K, but tastes very good.Hard to find in stores.Adding to this review: This product contains High Fructose corn syrup. I contacted the company and they will not be changing the product so I will not purchase again.

Normally, I don't add reviews to Amazon, but after seeing the reviews for this cereal I just had to. My wife and I started dieting and eating healthy within the last year and have changed most of the foods that we eat. Our diets differ in the sense that I watch my caloric intake and my wife is on a low carb diet. I picked this cereal up for her at our local grocery store a few months ago and decided to try it myself because it does have really nice nutritional value listed on the box. However (and this is the main reason for my review), it tastes totally horrible!! I noticed that there was not only a few people on here stating it tasted great and wonderful and they saw flowers blooming, the sun come up and so forth when they ate some. The only conclusion as a clear thinking adult is that these people are used to eating saw dust or whatever comes out of their paper shredder normally. To sum it up, if you want to eat this cereal because of its nutritional value then go for it. That's a great and noble reason and I'm with ya, but PLEASE do not tell other unsuspecting people considering whether or not to purchase this product that it tastes good.

This product might have the greatest nutritional profile in the world, but I will not be eating it again. Even after soaking in milk for fifteen minutes, the flakes had a dry (almost cottony) texture and a flavor worse than tofu.I had high hopes, because I like every other Special K cereal and food bar I've ever had, but this was a huge mistake, as far as I'm concerned.
Tastes like and has the texture of cardboard. This garbage doesn't deserve to be called special K. Instead of the light, crispy special K texture, this is like eating a bowl of wood chips.

column9: Best tasting "cardboard" I ever had . . .but not any more!
column10: ** This review was done for the old formula - see update below for review of the "improved" formula **  Last year, I stumbled across a website that evaluates your current breakfast cereal for nutrition, satiety, etc. and this cereal was at the top of the recommended list as an alternative to my former option.  I've always found that original Special K left me more hungry and the suggested serving size was laughable.  The artificial chocolate pieces in Choco. Delight were vile, so with those strikes, I was a bit reluctant to try Protein Plus.  It didn't help that some reviewers didn't like the taste - ordering 4 boxes that I'd be stuck with was uncomfortable, but I went for it.That was nearly a year ago and this has been my "go to" cereal ever since.  I think it tastes pretty good, so I advise that you decide for yourself on taste.  It has a light and sweet cinnamon flavor, I love the added protein and it's very low in sugar (2 g's per .75 cup serving). The flakes are sturdy (great crunch) and dense - not airy at all - holds up well in skim milk or yogurt, but I typically eat it straight up - out of my handy measuring cup.  I don't need to sweeten it at all and a serving size, or just over, leaves me satisfied (really hard to do) and a box seems to last me awhile - another huge plus.  I even carry a bag as a snack - especially when I travel - so that I'm not tempted to make less healthy choices. While I can't give all the credit to Protein Plus, as part of an overall reduced calorie daily intake attempt, I've lost 20 lbs in the past year - and although near my goal - have no intention of taking this off my grocery list.**Update 8.5.12** - the  formula and stats have indeed changed, and significantly IMO.  I am not thrilled and I wish they left well enough alone.  Examples:  Calories from 100 to 120, Sugar (now the 3rd ingredient) from 2-3 to 7 grams (double - really?!), fiber and protein same, but the old box claims 5 grams of fiber when the fine print says 3.  The new box just has 3.  Other stats have changed too, I just don't have the old box available to refer to.  I am eating the new boxes since I have 4 from Subscribe and Save, but I got no warning of the change and there is a huge difference in texture, sweetness, etc.  Overall, it tastes okay, but it lost its edge.  I have cancelled this S&S and I am going to look locally to see if I can still find the old formula and stock up.  Big fat BOO to Kellogg's - other than the easier opening inner sack,this was a stupid move.  If I could choose no stars - I would.  I have found the old formula locally and I am stocking up!

column9: Long time user is giving it up - They sweetened it!
column10: I have been enjoyng the Special K Protein cereal for at least a year but Kellogs decided to "improve" it, and I say, Yuk.  The "Extra" means they've added extra sugar! Now it does taste like cardboard, but cardboard that is sickly sweet.  Another case where corporate America is determined to keep America's sweet-tooth in high gear.  Thanks Kellogs, for making a good product bad.Update:  A good, less sugary low-carb, high-protein substitute for this cereal is Hi-Lo Low Carb Cereal by Organic Milling, which is also available on Amazon.  Hi-Lo has 1/7 the sugar of the Special K, more protein and more fiber.  And it tastes better.

column9: Formula changed to make it LESS healthy
column10: Boo to this.  I was SO happy with it when I had finally found a low-carb cereal in which I could add my own sweetener to control how sweet I wanted it, and safely - with Stevia or something else.  Even just a couple of sliced strawberries.  This was the only one to fit into a reasonable daily carb allowance.Then they changed it to be sweeter and loaded up on more sugar and carbs.  I complained to Kellogg and they replied that they did a taste test and found people wanted it to be sweeter.  A TASTE TEST.  On people that probably had no interest in its intended purpose to be a healthier option for people that actually need to watch their diets closely - they evidently didn't test for value when it came to its health benefits, they tested purely for flavor.  Shouldn't this have been tested on people that WERE concerned with health...?  It's that essentially the goal demographic?  The general public has TONS of sugary cereals to choose from.  Can't we just have ONE?You've lost my business, Kellogg, as well as many others that follow a low-carb/keto diet.  I was once recommending this cereal to everyone that was trying to be more healthy so they didn't have to give up all the types of food they love--those on Atkins, Protein Power, the huge following of low-carbers on reddit, to name a few.  Now we're back to pretty much no cereal options once again.

This used to be one of the healthiest cereals available. As an almost vegetarian it was one of the only ways I could get enough iron and protein, plus it had loads of fiber. Now it has less fiber, way more sugar, and more carbs.After 7+ years of this being a staple in my diet I will no longer be purchasing this. Such a shame.I am SO disappointed and I know others are, as well. So, I created a petition in the hope that if enough people sign they might eventually return the original formula.That said, since I've found Hi-Lo cereal which is even better (carb, sugar, and fiber-wise) than the original formula of special k low carb I kind of don't care what Kellogg's does.

BUYER BEWARE!  I have been enjoying this cereal for quite some time.  I was so disappointed when I received the "Now Tastes Even Better" boxes of this cereal.  I guess Kelloggs' idea of "better" is adding sugar and reducing the fiber.  Sugar is now listed as the 3rd most prominent ingredient.  REALLY???  Had I wanted more sugar I could just add that myself.  The description of the cereal I bought from Amazon reads:  Product Features - 100 calories  "4 boxes of 13.5 ounce Special K Protein Plus Cereal  Protein-rich combination of tasty, low-carb wheat, soy, and rice flakes  10 grams of protein with just 2 grams of sugar and 3 grams of fat in each serving  Lightly sweetened and deliciously crunchy for a great breakfast or snack  Good source of fiber for overall dietary wellbeing and sense of satisfaction"The new numbers are 120 calories, 7 grams of sugar, just 3 grams of fiber and at least the one positive of only 1 gram of fat, reduced from 3. It may taste better to some, but to me it was fine just the way it was.  I would have appreciated knowing about the change before I purchased this cereal again.

I tried the new formula other day and its terrible. I tried two days in a row and its like someone poured a box of fake sugar sweetener on the cereal and not a good kind. I had the worst after taste  for hours even after i brushed my teeth. Anyway i emailed them and complained and asked why fiber was reduced to. I told them i would be taking it back to the store and buying a different cereal now. I am so disappointed. Here is the email response i got from them below. And there was no coupons attached either. WHATEVER.I'm happy to hear you've enjoyed them for many years! Thank you for your comments regarding Kellogg's® Special K® Low Carb Lifestyle Protein Plus cereal. We are sorry you did not enjoy the reformulated product.As you might imagine, we conduct extensive consumer tests to determine consumer acceptance before introducing a food into the national market. Reformulated products are of special concern to us, so we use panels of regular product users across the country to ensure acceptability. Tests on this reformulated product showed that most consumers preferred the new product to the old. However, we realize that taste preferences do differ and can certainly understand your feelings.I've compiled a list of cereals with high fiber counts. You may wish to try:Kellogg's FiberPlus® Berry Yogurt Crunch cerealKellogg's FiberPlus® Caramel Pecan Crunch cerealKellogg's® All-Bran® Original cereal< BR>Kell ogg's® All-Bran® Bran Buds® cerealWe appreciate your comments and will share them with the appropriate company officials. We have enclosed some coupons which we hope you will use to purchase other products that you enjoy.Thank you again for sharing your thoughts!Sincerely,Ruben R.Consumer SpecialistConsumer AffairsTLXRXR01/cl025968680A

Two Words = "New Coke"You took a product that had more protein than net carbs and had a great branny flavor and ruined it, Kellogg's.Why would I buy this cereal anymore? I'll just stick to your other brand, kashi.How stupid do you think the average cereal shopper is- "now tastes even better" - what garbage.I could go on but I'll just stick to voting with my wallet.

The new formulation of this product does taste better. Kellogs accomplished this by more than doubling the sugar and halving the fiber. The thing is, I wasn't buying it for the taste, and now it has as much sugar per serving as some kids cereals.

column9: Bad change in formula to "Plus" version
column10: The previous incarnation of this "protein" cereal was acceptable ( nutty tasting, good with fruit) and relatively low in carbs for junk food.  It has been my mainstay for breakfast for years.  I used to travel with it in the days when it was hard to find because I wanted to stay on track with eating while traveling.  I was not the only one to do this: I recall that a business passenger who was on the airliner that landed in the Hudson river a few years ago voiced his distress on air to a reporter that a box of this hard to find cereal was certainly lost along with his luggage.Now I just bought four boxes of the new "Plus" version and I am trying to give it away:  sweet, bland, overly dosed with chemical flavors. It has gone from 9 to 19 gr carbohydrate with sugar as its third ingredient.  I am irritated at being forced to change, but on the positive side it has prompted me to do the sensible thing and jettison commercial breakfast stuff entirely.
This cereal is about the ONLY low-carb high protein good tasting breakfast food for low-carb diets. I hope they don't stop making it!

column9: Perfect Balance between Healthy and Tasty
column10: This Special K is very tasty. It is crisp until the bottom of the bowl. The high protein makes it a meal that stays with you for hours. I am adding it to a healthy eating plan for weight loss and health. Five grams of fiber is a big plus also.I like this much better than the plain Special K due to the fact it sticks with you longer.

Used to love this cereal. Low sugar, high protein, and actually tasted pretty good. Sadly, as others have pointed out, the "new improved formula" ruins this cereal. It has changed from 2g of sugar to 7g of sugar without even improving the taste, unless you prefer to eat sugar for breakfast; I do not. Guess I'll have to scour the local stores for the old recipe version and eventually find a new breakfast option. Big letdown Kellogg's.

column9: Was a Five Star Cereal - They Ruined Something Healthy
column10: I used to buy Special K Protein Plus all the time, but now that it "tastes even better" (read: now that they added sugar as one of the main ingredients), I won't be buying it anymore. More calories, more sugar, less fiber- but alas, now it is supposed to taste better. Maybe it does, but I won't be finding out.

column9: If you are looking for low carb/low sugar this cereal is not for you.
column10: Special K protein plus recently changed up their ingredients.  It states it is better tasting; however, it now has 7 grams of sugar.  I don't see how protein plus is any different from any other special K cereal, other than the 10 grams of protein.  The whole point of getting the protein plus cereal is to get a protein boost without the added carbs.  This cereal now has an addition 20 calories and 5 grams of sugar, and to be quite honest tastes worse than the original.  I don't care for overly sweet cereals.  I prefered the whole grain taste of the original special K protein plus.  It now tastes like a box of Tony's Frosted Flakes.  Yuk!

As others have stated, this product has recently undergone a reformulation. Sugar has increased from 2g to 7g, fiber has decreased by 2g, sodium has increased, potassium has decreased, and several other micronutrients are no longer listed (presumably removed?) or have decreased. Also, the serving size has increased by a few grams. Buyer beware, this product is not nearly as health as it once was due to this new "tastes even better" formulation and Kellogg's has lost me as a customer because of this change.

The new "Now tastes even better" version increases carbohydrates, decreases fiber, and increases sugar content. Exactly the wrong direction to go for most customers of this product. Enjoyed this for years but must now look for an alternative.

This had become my favorite cereal, both because of the great taste AND the low sugar content.  Unfortunately, the box now reads "Now tastes even better", which translates into more than DOUBLE the sugar.  Shame on you, Kellogg's.

column9: WTG Kelloggs on adding sugar and salt
column10: This was a staple to my lower carb diet, loved it with walnuts and a sprinkle of Truvia floating in almond milk. Yum! Now, it is OFF my shopping list. I did find an alternative at a local health food store and it's very good, comes in 4 flavors http://www.amazon.com/Nutritious-Living-Vanilla-Almond-Cereal/dp/B0081SMO7K/ref=sr_1_11?s=grocery&ie=UTF8&qid=1344600644&sr=1-11&keywords=low+carb

column9: Why did they add so much sugar?
column10: I agree, the new formula is disppointing. The whole reason I was purchasing this cereal was because of the low carb/sugar count. Anyone have any suggestions for an alternative? Just by looking at labels is seems like Cheerios is the best option from a carb standpoint, but I'm sure there are other options out there?
The new version does not taste as good and has so many more carbs it should be called protein and carb plus.  I wish Kelloggs realized people can add sugar but they can't take it out!

column9: Nutrition facts listed here are wong
column10: Special k protein plus has recently changed their recipe to involve an additional 20 calories per serving, and decreased the fiber by 2g, effectively adding a bunch of carbs.  I used to buy this cereal by the dozen, but I will have to switch.  Now I have a dozen boxes of cereal I don't like sitting on the shelf.  This makes me very unhappy :(

I was very disappointed that they have now raised the carb count in this cereal from 9 net carbs to 16 net carbs.  I have insulin resistance and my nutritionist told me this was the only cereal I could have.  It tasted great!  My local ShopRite stopped carrying it a while ago because it wasn't selling, so I had to purchase it elsewhere.  I called the company and they said they were relaunching it in July.  I was so happy to see it back on the shelves, but now they've change it.  Even the sugar level went up.  I just wish there was another cereal on the market that had 9 grams of carbs or less.  Oh well, I'll surely miss it.

column9: Thumbs down on the New Improved Formula!
column10: I just spent the past 90 minutes scouring the shelves of my local grocers with the original Protein Plus formula.  What on earth were they thinking with changing the formula? Caloric load went up 20%, sugar content when up 350%!!, carb content went up 36%, and fiber content decreased 40%.. Yes, fat content decreased, but it's better to have some fat with those carbs. This product, as originally formulated, was good for people on isocaloric (kinda like Zone: roughly balanced macronutrient ratios). It no longer is.I am furious.
So yummy and ridiculously healthy! I strongly recommend this over original or flavoured brands of Special K.

column9: New Formula: More calories, more sodium; less fiber!
column10: This is a big disappointment.  Suddenly the formula changes - for the worse.  I have canceled my formerly wonderful "Subscribe & Save" Amazon subscription.  Might as well buy Cap'n Crunch or Frosted Flakes.  "Now Tastes Even Better!" the company says.  Well, it depends on who's doing the tasting! It is now far too sweet, as well as being significantly less healthy - look at the increase in calories and sodium.  What a pity.  Farewell, Special K Protein Plus, old style.  It was nice knowing and eating you.

I just called Kellogg and told them how disappointed I am in the new formula for Special K Protein Plus. I also told them that the reviews on Amazon are horrible. The woman I talked to was very nice and she took down all my info and it will be forwarded to the Quality Control team. She said there has been many other complaints as well. She also mentioned about the taste testers liking this. And I pointed out that I would be interested in knowing how many of these people are health conscience and are not looking for sweeter food but healthier food. The taste testers preferred it because it is sweeter. I told her that most cereals are sweeter and that those people should just stick with those cereals and that Kellogg should have just left well enough alone. Now there are many people who have enjoyed this cereal for many years and have to go find another.

Sadly, Kellogs has chosen to ruin a good product by turning into a sugary children's cereal. The nutritional value have changed dramatically and it now has a cloying sweetness that is almost inedible. I have eaten the older version for years, but I wont buy the new version again or serve it to family.

column9: Beware - they ruined Special K Protein Plus
column10: Used it for years. Now, the new version with the yellow top band has killed that. The original taste was pretty good for the benefits, but that is gone. The flakes now actually look like some cardboard fell into the box. Awful texture. I am moving to Hi-Lo (also not so tasty unfortunately). The nutrition numbers are worse as well. Considering the health-mindedness of this cereal's customers, this move is hard to understand.

I must say I really dislike the new recipe.  I liked the old "low carb" version and had been enjoying it for years, but somewhere along the way Kellogg's decided that people really just wanted high protein and high carb. No doubt the new formula will appeal to some, but for me, it no longer is that different than a range of other cereals out there.  Unfortunately the old one was pretty unique and I have not found a suitable alternative.

Crisp flakes, with a good amount of flavor. For cereal lovers, it's a good way to get protein in the morning, and the total carbs are low enough for my diabetic diet. I sweeten with a little sprinkle-on Splenda or some fruit and I don't get the 10:30 "hungries" like I do with higher-carb cereals.

I have incorporated this good-tasting, high-protein, high-fiber cereal into my diet after being diagnosed with Type II diabetes and learning the simple carbs were killing me...using this cereal as a mainstay in a very revised dietary discipline, I've gotten glucose down to normal levels WITH NO MEDS. It can happen, just need a plan (and some sacrifice). Besides, like others said, it stays crisp to the bottom of the bowl! Go with the regular delivery and it's cheap too.

column9: Kellogg Doesn't Care About Our Weight...they have doubled the sugar and cut the fiber
column10: I wrote this to Kellogg...YUCK!!! I do NOT like the new formulation of Special K Protein Plus....WAY TOO SWEET! And you REDUCED the fiber from 5 g. to 3 g.!!! WHY?????? You are making this cereal much less healthy by putting MORE SUGAR and LESS FIBER in it. Please change it back!!I don't understand why they are calling this a HEALTHY cereal, which it obviously IS NOT anymore. When you base your business decisions on the fact that people WANT SWEETER cereals, you are doomed to fail. You are neither HEALTHY nor FRUIT LOOPS. As a nutrition major, I know that some FAT...the right kind is good for us. It provides SATIETY, so we are satisfied with less and feel full faster.I would rather have a little MORE FAT and LESS SUGAR, which all of the experts know leads us down the road to increased diabetes and heart problems. Also, as a nutrition major, I know that in our society, PROTEIN deficiency is NOT a PROBLEM. We eat so much meat, chicken, fish, soybeans, tofu, we don't need more than 25 grams per day.I can see that Kellogg is not going to reformulate SPECIAL K, until the public DEMANDS IT, so count me as one person who will buy whatever remaining 5 g. of Fiber SPECIAL K that I can find and then I will get my cereal elsewhere and it WILL be HEALTHIER THAN SPECIAL K. Goodbye KELLOGG and thanks anyway.

The nutrition facts are outdated. It has 7g sugar per serving rather than 2g. It tastes way too sweet for me! Unless they switch back to the old version, I'll have plain Cheerios instead (only 1g sugar per serving).

I want to be clear, this review is about Special K Protein Plus "Now tastes Even Better". The "original" was great, FIVE STARS!! This one has more than triple the sugar, and is sugary sweet. And it now contains aspartame so it has that awful after-taste. I just cancelled my "subscribe and save" 12 boxes each month. I'm very disappointed. Unless you are looking for "frosted flakes", don't buy this.

CAUTION:  The nutrition chart below is for the original version of Special K Protein Plus, not this product.The net carbs have almost doubled due to popular demand for more sugar (attention obese Americans).Check out Kelloggs.com for the correct nutritional information.[...]Kelloggs has shafted their loyal customers who depend on a low net carb breakfast cereal.

column9: really not that good but it is comparatively healthy so that's worth something
column10: Okay, so I had high hopes for this one. I would NEVER eat this cereal alone. It's just not very good at all. It's an odd texture, not very filling, the serving size is not GREAT. just normal/small. I believe theres ~100 calories per serving, so not bad in that regard but I'd have to eat 300 calories to feel even remotely satisfied.Nutritionally speaking it is pretty good. There is sucrolose in it though so if that's not something you want to consume then do not buy this product. Lots of protein--from soy but still a pretty hefty dose if you're deficient.I don't plan to purchase it again but I'd eat it if nothing else was available.

column4: Jerad Heffner "geek, car buff, and dad"
column10: I bought this because I'm watching my carbs, and as any low carber will tell you, cereals are amonth the highest carb-rich foods you can find. Fortunately, this is only 9 net carbs per serving.Taste is always subjective, but I've found these to be quite good. Sure they're not the sweet taste of Fruity Pebbles or the crunchiness of Quaker Oatmeal Squares, but I would still eat these if I wasn't on a low-carb regimen.
As someone on a low carb diet the thing I missed most was cereal.  Then I tried this cereal. I've stayed on my diet and I've lost 25 pounds to date.

This is a great cereal all around. It has low sugar, high fiber, high protien, and tastes great! But my favorite thing of all is that I can eat it at 6 a.m. and make it to lunch time without getting that starving feeling mid morning. I eat it every day with blueberries or banana. It goes great with fruit of any kind. Of course I never add sugar, it's just sweet enough on it's own. Its also a great snack anytime of day because of the fiber, low calorie count, and its ability to stave off hunger. The reviewers who wrote that hey didn't like the taste must have been Froot Loops and Coco Puffs eaters because it's nothing like cardboard (have they really eaten cardboard?). I'm a huge fan of this cereal and tell all my friends about it. Try it !

column9: One of the better low carb cereals
column10: This is one of the better low carb cereals I have tried.  I eat it most everyday with some splenda and unsweetened almond or soymilk.  Great for low carb diets.  I think it has a nice flavor.  One poster noted that it was not as sweet as other Special K cereals.  That's the point, less sugar, less carbs.  You can always sweeten it to taste with splenda or other low/no carb sweetener if you so desire.

I've just spent a few minutes reading all of the other reviews and I guess its true what they say about opinions and elbows--everybody's got one.No, its not Cocoa Krispies or Capt Crunch but to me it taste pretty darn good.  Frankly I gag on any type of protein bar (I've tried several ones already) but with the cereal you don't taste any of that.  The best part is that it fills me up big time.Here's how I eat it.2 measured cups of PP1 cup of skim milk1 packet of splendaCalories (Via "Lose It!"--coolest app I've ever seen) 350Fat  8.2 gFiber 13.3 gProtein  35 gNot too shabby for something that will keep me stuffed for hours.P.S.  I don't care if you think I work for Kellogs, Amazon or anyone else who might profit from the sale of PP--do us a favor and get a life.

This cereal is a great way to start your day. Just by itself, I will admit, it is a little bland. Here is how I eat it every day. 1 bowl with two teaspoons of splenda, some cinnamon, and unsweetened vanilla almond breeze almond milk (half the calories of milk, can be found at Trader Joe's or whole foods). Wonderful!
This used to be the only cereal I bought until they added more sugar , disappointed and looking for other options.

column9: Used to love it - now less healthy and tastes terrible
column10: This was a good, healthy cereal - a way to eat cereal and get protein and fiber without a lot of sugar. This new formula made it less healthy and it tastes like a poured aspartame down my throat. It's just gross. Should have left well enough alone. Never eating it again.

I've been eating Special K Protein Plus for years, because of its high protein and fiber content.  I didn't taste too bad if eaten with fruit.  The last time I bought a box of it, I plopped it into my shopping cart without noticing that it "Now tastes Even Better!"  A serving of this new formulation has more calories and less fiber than a serving of the previous version, and it contains sucralose, which I believe is not healthful.

Had a 4-box-a-month subscription for at least 2 years. Late 2012 reformulation turned a really good cereal into something with an unpleasantly too-sweet taste and a terrible stick to your teeth texture. 3 unpoened boxes in trash, one cancelled subscription. Yuck. (Saw a note from a company rep on another bad review that market research indicated most people liked the change. I think they tested 6 year olds.) How about the health aspects -- ramp up sugars and carbs, drop fiber. Why do you think we bought it?

column9: Special K Protein Plus ruined with added sugar!
column10: Idiots!  Why destroy the health benefits of one of the best breakfast cereals on the market by adding sugar to it??!!  They might as well have added more salt while they were at it! I'm sure that would have made the cereal taste better too. I don't know anyone who is happy with the new Special K Protein Plus recipe. They need to restore the original!  Until then they have lost my business.

Honestly I am so upset with Special K for changing the formula of this cereal. I LOVED the old 100-calorie for 3/4 cup, 12g protein version--it was higher fiber and lower sugar. What's the point in making a cereal like this for low-carbers if you're going to INCREASE the net carbs? BRING BACK THE ORIGINAL!

column9: Just what a diabetic needs -- more sugar!
column10: This cereal used to have nine grams of carbohydrate which wasn't bad. Now it has nineteen grams. The data has not been changed on Amazon, but the box has. I'm sure it's going to stay that way so Kellog has lost a customer.

column9: If it's not broken, don't fix it!
column10: Kellogg's Special K Cereal, Protein Plus, was the perfect cereal before they made some ingredient changes.  They state now on the box "Now tastes even better!"  WRONG!!!  It was perfect before with less sugar in the ingredients.  This product has lost its distinctive flavor and healthy ingredients by adding 7 grams of sugar to it.  I want the "old" better version please.  So disappointed in this new box of cereal.  As soon as I can find a good protein cereal that tastes more NATURAL, I WILL CHANGE.

Like many other reviewers, I've been eating this for YEARS and am in total shock that Kellogg made such a drastic change for the worst. This is a completely different cereal now, and one that I wouldn't buy. It's definitely not worth the price anymore. Not only is it less "healthy" (the reason most of us bought it in the first place!), the texture and appearance is like a 99 cent generic bag of corn flakes. Except those taste better than this does.The product I received is NOT what I paid for; after weeks of trying to like it, I'm ready to request a refund. Yes, it's that bad now. If you used to like this cereal, don't buy a 4 pack until you've tried it.I'm so disappointed. It WAS the only high-protein, somewhat lower carb cereal that didn't taste (or cost) like diet food. I'd eat a bowl and not feel hungry before lunch. It was slightly sweet, even my kids liked it! Guess what? They don't like the new version, either...kind of a big deal considering Kellogg TRIPLED the sugar!Definitely putting my Subscribe & Save on hold. Maybe Kellogg will take a hint. If not, bye-bye!

Before you think all the '1-star' people are just nuts, please consider this.This cereal was a nice, 100 calorie, way to start the morning, while getting some other goodies (vitamins, fiber) along with the high protein.  The cereal was a little 'bland' by most measures but as you see, this is why most of us liked it.  It didn't need sugar.  It was great for the nutritional value and we liked it as it is.Kellogg's decided that it's customer base for this cereal is a bunch of 7-year olds who want sugar stuff.  Tripling (yes, tripling) the sugar in a cereal to improve it and 'make you feel full longer'...is really NOT an improvement.  And, oh yes, lowering the fiber.On its own, is the new version okay? Yes.  But for those who had sworn by the old recipe (like me), we won't be buying this product again.  Good riddance.

column9: New Protein Plus is too Sugary!
column10: I just bought a box of protein plus expecting it to be the protein plus I have eaten religiously over the past few years. Instead what I tasted was basically frosted flakes so I read the panel and saw that they had added 5g of sugar and reduced fiber. Seriously?! Will be buying Kashi or HiLo from now on.

At the suggestion of my doctor, I have been eating Kellogg's Special K Protein Plus cereal for breakfast every day for several years now.  Today, I opened a new box and discovered they have made changes in this product.  What a shock. I absolutely hate the new product.  I do not like the taste, I do not like the color, I do not like the slimy texture in milk. I loved the old Special K Protein Plus. I liked the taste.  I Liked the color.  I liked the texture.  I looked forward to it every day.  It was a great way to begin my day.  Now I am in misery.  It's as if my best friend is no longer here.And I looked at the nutrition information and see that they have reduced the fiber from 5 grams to 3 grams per serving, a reduction of 40 percent.  And they increased the sugar from 2 grams to 7 grams per serving, an increase in dangerous empty calories by 250%. I do not need more sugar in my life.And the front of the box states "satisfies hunger longer--see side panel for details. I looked at the side panel and it says "Special K Protein products are designed to promote a reduced feeling of hunger by increasing daily intake of protein and fiber".  So they added this statement to the new box while at the same time they reduced fiber by 40%.  And they also reduced the amount of protein in the box by about 10% because they changed the serving size.  The old box had 13.2 servings and the new box only 11.96 servings.  Fool me once.  Shame on you. Fool me twice.  Shame on me.  I will not be eating Kellogg's products anymore.

column9: Great taste. Eat it for breakfast every work day.
column10: For the very few people that rated this cereal with one star and said it tasted horrible, what do you normally eat? Frosted Flakes? If you compare the flavor of this cereal to other sugary cereals then of course this will taste bad to you. But compared to other nutritional cereals on the market, this is one of the best tasting and nutritional. I ate Kashi Go Lean for years. I liked the taste of Go Lean Crunch better but could not eat it very often because of the higher sugar content. I tried Special K Protein Plus on a whim and I loved it! I not only eat it for breakfast every work day, I sometimes eat it for lunch too. It's filling, full of nutrition, tasty, and low in sugar. I hope it never goes away.

I'm a diabetic and  Special K Cereal Protein Plus is high in Protein and lower in carbs, compared to other cereals.I eat my  Special K Cereal Protein Plus with Vanilla Soymilk that's also low in carbs. I like the taste of Special K Protein Plus.
Pretty dam good. Much better than any other high fiber cereals out there. Perfect for a low carb dieter like myself.

column9: Great price, great vendor, and excellent service
column10: I cannot say enough about this product/service. We love this product and by using the subscription service we get fresh product delivered on a schedule that insures we always have some on hand at a price, including SH, which is considerably less than the local (and big box) stores. Well done!

This is the only cold cereal I've found that doesn't make my blood sugar spike.  It's low in carbs and has lots of fiber.  And I really like the taste.  It's just sweet enough, and somewhat nutty-tasting.  If you're accustomed to cereals with added sugar, you might find it bland, but I love it.

I have been eating this cerial for about a year and I really like it. When I first ate it I thought it had a bit of a cardboard like quality, but after eating it for a week I really like it. I have it with Safeway organics soy milk, which is slightly sweet, which I think makes a big difference. I usually have 2 servings, which is quite filling. It is still low in calories, so I don't consider this too much food for breakfast.

This cereal doesn't taste very good, and it turns to mush the moment my almond milk touches it.  However, it is the only cereal I can eat on my low carb diet - and sometimes I just need to eat cereal.
I love this cereal and I am thrilled that I can keeping it coming on an ongoing basis.  I eat this cereal everyday and enjoy the faint sweetness.  THANKS!
Great cereal!! The only one I've found that has an equal balance between carbs and proteins.The price is right as well as the delivery to my door !!! What more can you ask for?

This cereal is so tasty, makes a great evening snack with 10 grams of protein and 5 grams of dietary fiber, you can't beat it.  I call it my dessert, look forward to it nightly...  very good price also.

I have tried the origional Special K cereal and I liked it but I noticed the flakes went soggy in the milk very fast. The Special K with protein has a different taste, that I like better than the origional, and the flakes stay crispy in milk. After a bowl I feel satisfied and also I feel like I made a healthy choice.Ordering in bulk therefore was the best option for me and I found I saved money too.

This is a barely sweetened cereal that is loaded with protein and fiber and has a reduced sodium content--in short it is actually one of the few healthy cold cereals. If you like a sugary tasting cereal, then this is not for you, but it most definitely does not taste like "cardboard," especially if you eat it with fruit or flavored yogurt.Here is a comparison with Regular Special K: 2g sugar vs. 4g; 5g fiber vs. 1g; 110mg sodium vs. 220 mg; 10g protein vs. 7g. This costs more than Regular Special K, but the extra cost is worth it to me because I feel that I am getting more for my money.In the spring and summer, when I stop eating my hot oatmeal each morning, I mix this with Kashi Go Lean Crunch (which is another great cold cereal that I have reviewed on Amazon), add milk, and then add some fresh fruit. This is a great way to start the day and more than holds me until lunch time.My wife mixes this with flavored yogurt for her breakfast, and is also good to go until lunch time.The price on Amazon is less than my supermarket, and if you sign up for the subscription service (as I did), you will pay even less.Bottom line: If you want a filling, healthy cereal for breakfast that tastes good, and depend on fresh fruit or flavored yogurt rather than a sugary coating to satisfy your sweet tooth at breakfast, then you will really like this cereal.

column9: Can't miss a week without it!
column10: This is my second 4-box purchase of this product.  My thoughts after my first bowl of this was, "Really?  Does protein cereal HAVE to taste so dull?"  But, I thought, this is an excellent source of protein, so I was hoping I could "flavor it up."If you add some berries and two packs of Truvia or Splenda, you really can create a high-protein, low-carb cereal that tastes great.  Be creative!  I eat it with different types of berries (blackberries, strawberries, raspberries), usually 2-3 times a week (the rest of the week it's eggs and/or greek yogurt).  It's really helped me with my cereal cravings and high-protein, low-carb diet, and now I couldn't make it a week without it.

column9: Best low carb cereal--South Texans eat with HEB Mootopia milk!
column10: I am a superbly picky eater because I love sugar. This cereal tastes a but like raisin bran to me. I eat it with HEB Mootopia milk, which is also lower carb than regular milk, and it tastes great. Also, it helps my digestive system lots. :) Try it! Cereal sold at Wal-Mart too.

column9: Very Healthy for a Breakfast Cereal
column10: First ingredient is Bran which will tell you a lot about what to expect from this product. That is why it has so much fiber that will help keep you fuller longer. The protein comes from soy which is a great protein for body health especially heart health, it is not good for muscle building. Also if you are a male try not to over do it on soy as there are numerous ill side-effects that you can Google on your own time. For the sake of this product, I would imagine this amount of soy protein could benefit anyone who isn't allergic. Don't fret about the High fructose corn syrup as there is hardly any in this product. Obviously this isn't the best tasting cereal, one reviewer said it is the "best tasting cardboard" which is a very accurate description. This item would be great to use for a diet or simple to benefit your health.

I've been hooked on Special K since I was in high school (I'm 25).  I've gone from the regular cereal, to Special K with Strawberries, and now I'm hooked on Protein Plus.  There is just something naturally sweet and tastey about this cereal- I eat it at least once per day.  And you can't beat the price!  I subscribed to it on Amazon, and get it delivered for $2.50 per box.  In the grocery store, when I can find it, it is $4.50+ per box.  Love it, and love Amazon!

Hi,Bought these for my parents and I am glad that I made right choice. Parents as well as myself I eat them regularly. I eat my whey protein powder in milk before I mix these cereals. My father has diabetes but he has no complaints.

I've started a high protein diet since I began exercising recently. I wanted a simple breakfast in the morning that would be easy to make, nutritious and specifically high in protein for my muscles. This cereal is just perfect for that. It's a bit plain in taste although very crispy, which I don't mind at all, especially since I'm not into sugary tasting cereal. In conclusion, very good nutritional cereal for a healthy life style!

column9: Low Carb cereal that works for me
column10: Item arrived well packed in plastic.Great price with subscribe and save and expiry date 9 months later.I was worried about the taste especially after reading some of the reviews but was pleasantly surprised.This is a  cereal I can eat without sweetening further.Am on a low carb diet for gestational diabetes(pregnancy related) so as you can imagine- I'm hungry all the time in this my 3rd trimester and so am glad I found something that will fill me up without affecting my blood sugar as the usual cereals do.

New years resolution season and all, bought protein plus to have a healthy cold cereal choice in the morning. It provides nutrients and the taste is best described as "non-offensive". I added sliced banana this morning and it was really enjoyablePros: High in nutrients, non-offensive taste, pairs well with fruitCons: A little bland

column9: Perhaps the best cereal you can buy without
column10: the unnecessary high sugar content.This cereal is far superior than most so-called nutritious cereal you'll find at specialty nutrition stores.  A lot of these so-called nutritious cereal are still high in fat, sugar and sodium.If you find a cereal low in fat, chances are they are high in sugar and/or sodium.As a health guru for at least 20 years, this is truly one of the best and most nutritious cereal you can find.  Ralph's (Kroger) quit carrying this cereal because I was told that no one was buying them.  I understand why...It was just too healthy for the majority of cereal consumers.

This is a breakfast staple that I've bought for years and is increasingly hard to find in local grocery stores, for some reason. I usually cut it with another sweeter cereal, but the additional protein is really helpful to get me through the morning. I use Amazon's subscription service to buy this and that has been fantastic for me. I've used it for several months and it always reliably ships.

column9: Best, most nutritious cereal I know
column10: Special K Protein Plus is by far my favorite cereal, & the one that packs the biggest nutritional wallop out there in cereal-land.Even the wimpishly modest portion of 100g delivers 10g (12% DV) of protein, not counting the milk you'll add.My usual portion of this is 50-100% bigger. On top of it I sprinkle a measure of kosher whey protein isolate (about 52% DV).Then I dump sliced fresh fruit on top: say, a banana, a peach or nectarine, pitted cherries, blueberries, blackberries, raspberries, yellow raspberries (yes, often all at the same time), & finally pour in enough 2% Lactaid milk to suit my taste.Not only is this delicious, nutritious & healthful, it gives you at least as much protein as you'd get from a gigantic steak. And it's a lot better for you & easier to digest. Try it!

This is the high-protein member of the Special K family. For some reason I have not been able to find it in any stores. It is delicious and lets you start your day with protein (energy and power) instead of sugar (buzz and crash).

I was so craving cereal and being on the atkins diet I had to research low carb cereals. I read about this online and went and bought some, with apprehension. But WOW!!! You wouldn't even know it was low carb unless you read the box or someone told you. It was very light and flaky and had a sweet flavor to it. It kept it's crunch quite well. It also makes you feelfull which is great. I used Almond Breeze no sugar vanilla almond milk. again WOW!!!! Go out and try it... You'll be glad you did. Also... This can be used as a low carb breading.

I love this cereal.  I bought four boxes, and I plan on buying many more.  I love that it is high in protein without the added sugar of most cereals.  The taste is fairly bland (as it should be), but add a packet of splenda and some fat-free milk and this stuff is glorious.  Great for people interested in upping protein intake but leaving calories out of the equation.

Tastes exactly the same as regular Special K, with the bonus of added protein. I had gastric bypass surgery, so I'm always worried about getting enough protein in my diet; this allows me to continue my lifelong breakfast routine (cereal and milk) without adding protein powders (which mostly taste awful). The four-pack lasts me just over a month, and it costs just about the same as the grocery store - it works out to about $3.43 a box, as opposed to the $3.49 I pay in the grocery store (I'm an Amazon Prime member, so I don't pay shipping) - so I don't ever have to worry about running out.

I went ahead and ordered the cereal because I've tried the regular Special K(which tastes pretty good),and figured this would be like that except with protein.You can imagine my "if it sounds too good to be true.." moment when I had my first bowl.Now I'm a pretty utilitarian kind of guy, I like good food, but I can eat just about anything edible just for survival.This is what this cereal is all about.Eating out of necessity.The taste is almost non-existent, which I can live with, but the texture is what kills me.All I can think about is cardboard boxes which were ripped into flakes and hardened. (The color of the cereal doesn't convince you otherwise either)Now I don't care about high fructose corn syrup and all that, but if something tastes this bad.... it should at least be 100% good for you.I don't think I will be ordering more.Protein is good, but you know.. life can be rough... you don't need to start out each day with rough cereal

I just finished my last box of this tried and true cereal, so opened my new order of 4 boxes.  Low and behold, they have changed the formula and it no longer fits into my low carb life style!!  How infuriating. New nutrition facts:  Total Carb 19g (was 14g) Fiber 3g (was 5g) Sugar 7g (was 2g) Calories for 3/4 cup 120 (was 100) sodium 190mg (was 110mg) potassium 125mg (was 280mg)  Protein remains 10g for both  Total fat 1g (was 3g) calories from fat 10 (was 25)Amazon doesn't allow returning of food products, so my daughter-in-law offered to try this cereal (she's on low calorie diet)  Why would they change this cereal after so many years?  I'm miffed.

I'd been doing without cereal for such a long time. I went 'low carb' a couple years ago and haven't had any cereal since.This formula has a few more carbs than I'd like, but not so much that I can't have a little now and then.I go with almond milk, this low carb Special K and some Splenda and I get my cereal fix in.Highly recommended.
I like this cereal very much but do not need 4 boxes every two months. HOw do i Cancel the automatic reorder?
This is a great product at an excellent price. It costs a lot less on Amazon than what grocery stores charge. Perhaps other grocery items are a good deal as well.
this cereal really delicious, a good mate with milk or soymilk. I like it very much and will keep eating it for my breakfast.

Cereals are generally one of the most expensive foods per ounce. Nutritionally they deliver less bang for the buck than most foods. Along comes Special K Protein Plus Original.Great stats! great taste! and with subscribe and save it can't beat. Five stars here.

This ceral is great if you are trying to reduce carbs, even other cereals that are supposed to be healthy have atleast double the carbs.  This doesnt taste like lucky charms so if you are a sugar cereal person you will not like it.  If you are into healthy eating you will love it.  To add flavor I sprinkle it with cinnamon and fresh fruit.

column9: Yummy cereal that is good for you
column10: I love this cereal.  It is a quick way to get protein with the first meal of the day.  Even my 8 year old likes the taste.

The product is fine but Amazon makes it very hard to complain. I paid over $13 for ONE of these. I thought there would be more because the description  of this product is plural. I also paid over $9 for 8-1/2 lbs shipping weight. It weighs about 4oz. I am ready to kiss Amazon goodbye!

column9: Unfortunately, Hawaiian Punch has switched to using sucralose.
column10: Hawaiian Punch has switched to using sucralose.I'm not talking about the "diet" version - I'm talking about the regular version. Some (but not all) of the high fructose corn syrup (which is worse than sugar) has been replaced with sucralose. The result is that the drink is less thick than it used to be, and there's also an aftertaste. I plan to finish what I just bought, but I'm not sure if I'll be buying any more.The switch a long time ago from sugar to HFCS was already bad enough, but the introduction of sucralose is far worse.

If you are looking for an organic brown rice at an attractive price then this is the way to go. The flavor is very good and almost as good at as Lundberg and Rice Select brands but at a lower cost. For the price and flavor you can't go wrong.

column9: A Pretty Decent Brown Basmati Rice, Especially At This Price!
column10: I have used this Arrowhead Mills Brown Basmati rice to make some very tasty the stir fries and casseroles and have even used it successfully in jambalaya.I like this rice a lot better than the Texmati brand rice.  However, the Arrowhead Mills Brown Basmati Rice doesn't hold a candle to Lundberg Family Farms Brown Basmati rice, which I think is just about the best brown rice I have ever tried.  But, considering that the Lundberg rice is two to three times more expensive that this rice, this Arrowhead Mills rice usually wins the spot in my pantry!

column9: smells like Basmati, but doesn't taste or look like it
column10: When cooking, this rice smells very much like Basmati.But I haven't noticed this rice tasting very much like Basmati.  It tastes fine as a brown rice.  It also doesn't elongate when cooked as white Basmati normally does.  Maybe that's the nature of brown Basmati??The second time I ordered a pack of six, the box it came in said it was Basmati, but the bags inside said it was long grain brown rice (a lower priced product, I think).Amazon sent us a another box with no hassles and this time it was the right stuff.

I ordered this 6-pack of rice in November.  It arrived with a "best by" date of January.  Even though I'm sure I could eat it after its "best by" date, it's still too soon in my opinion, considering that I'm buying in bulk.

The first thing I will say is to disregard the directions on the bag! It took me about 3-4 batches before realizing the hard bits weren't the imperfections that are very prevalent in this brand. After upping the amount of water to 2.5-3 cups I haven't had a problem and the rice has been great.I was excited about this product because brown basmati is a rare find in my area and is generally over $3 per lb. My only issue is that I do have to pick over it a little better before cooking if I don't want unattractive black bits of some part of the rice in my finished dish.I do see the price had raised quite a bit since I purchased mine, but I would still buy more, especially with the deal offered with subscribe and save.
Very good rice to have on hand. Will buy again when I run out. Grains in my area are MUCH more expensive, pound for pound. happy with purchase

FWIW (For what its worth) 28 ounces times 6 is 168 ounces or 10.5 lbs or pounds.i am ordering my 2nd 6 pack...i live alone and this with my 5.5 cup rice cooker (5.5 refers to the dry "white" rice cups of, per potential batch) works very well, one (1) package and 8 cups water makes a good quantity of rice...rice vinegar, low salt tamari, and organic extra virgin olive oil makes a decently palatable "gruel" i can consume frequently!

Yes, it is a good basmati rice, and being brown it is more healthful than that with the bran (nutritious exterior) removed: just what I'm looking for - BUT - yesterday the price went from right around $20.83 for one-time delivery, to […]. That is very close to a 50% increase.I cannot know whether this is Amazon's choice or whether the supplier suddenly raised its price. But in light of the earthquake in Japan, a huge jump in the price of rice has the smell of nasty profiteering, since there now will be a need for countries with rice supplies to replace damaged goods in a highly-populated, rice-intensive nation. You do what you want, but for me the answer is to not encourage this kind of price gouging. In other words, I'm not buying. I'll look elsewhere.
These yogurt covered pretzels combine saltiness with a touch of sweetness that is addictive. It is difficult to only eat one pack but what harm is another 100 calories?

Nabisco 100 Calorie Pack Yogurt Flavored Pretzels, 4.68 Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)There aren't enough words to describe how fantastically, astronomically, unbelievably delicious these yogurt pretzels are. These low cal snacks are great. Not only are they great for calorie watchers but kids and non calorie watchers love them.  My daughter and my grandsons can't get enough of these nor can I. It is very difficult to eat just one bag at a time. It takes an extreme amount of self control. This is one low cal product that is a must in your pantry.  I highly recommend this snack to anyone dieters and non dieters alike.  Buy them you'll love them.

OK, these pretzels are seriously the most AMAZING combination of yummy yogurt-y vanilla-y goodness and salty pretzel deliciousness!! This box is really big and you get a lot of bang for the buck! The pretzels really fill you up and the portions are perfect! I am addicted to these yummy yummy delights!!! a definite must-buy!

column9: Not what I was looking for
column10: I was looking for some jasmine extract to make some thai desserts with.  When I opened this bottle of jasmine extract, it sort of smelled like jasmine, but also had some other weird (not so great) smell to it. I tried using it once, and dumped the rest down the drain. It also came in a plastic bottle, which I found curious, as I was expecting glass.  I have since found much better jasmine extract elsewhere online.

Soft and chewy, these gingerbread cookies are absolutely delicious! I made them for my company holiday party along with XO Baking Co's Double Chocolate Chip cookies and everyone loved them! Not one person even knew they were gluten free until I told them! I recommend rolling both types in a little sugar before baking, makes for the best tasting cookies! You will want to share these with all of your friends, gluten free or not! Enjoy!

Even though all the cookie mixes are fantastic, I would say that gingerbread cookie is my favorite!  You can really taste the flavor of the ginger...yummy with a glass of milk.  I highly recommend any of the products from XO Baking Co.~~ Top notch quality.  I will buy more!

Based on recommendation from King Arthur Flour (KAF), I bought the vanilla bean paste. It came in quickly. I tried it and came to several conclusions. First, the flavor is outstanding..rich vanilla flavor. As described at KAF, the paste contained small vanillla bean specks which were visible in the lighter colored preps I made, like French Vanilla ice cream. It gave the preparations a special touch. One caution. If used in a thin batter, the specks will sink to the bottom. I learned this when I made Creme Brulee. The vanilla flavor was great, but at the bottom of the ramekin were all the bean specks. Use the paste in recipes where the specks will stay suspended and not sink.

Nielsen-Massey is my favorite vanilla extract, of the four or five I've sampled, and this is probably the most affordable way to buy this stuff on-line. If you're regularly making recipes that call for a tablespoon of vanilla at a time, you can't go wrong here.

I bought both this product and the LorAnn Extreact to compare, as they were both comparable prices.  Unfortunately they were not comparable in product.  The Nielsen-Massey had no flavor to speak of.  The LorAnn was very aromatic.  Also, I was very disappointed that this product had sugar in it.

We bought the 32 oz. vanilla extract.  Here are the ingredients, as listed on the label: Water, Alcohol, Sugar, Vanilla Bean Extractives.As others have noted, the added sugar was a big disappointment to us as well.

column9: Great buy on gluten free vanilla!
column10: This vanilla has great flavor and what a bargain for the size jar.  Although the jar is large it is easy to use and not a problem at all.  I will be buying this again since it is a superb quality product at a great price!

column9: Great vanilla flavor, not weak as some are
column10: This is the first time I have purchased this particular brand of vanilla and I normally would not purchase such a large bottle, but I found that the flavor is just wonderful. I'm glad I bought it because I like to bake and the size of this bottle will keep me busy for a while
Who knew they produced huge bottles of this fabulous vanilla extract! Great price! I will definitely purchase again, although  it might take a while to use this one in its entirity!

I purchased a bottle of the Nielsen-Massey Madagascar Vanilla about a year ago through Amazon and noticed how the vanilla enhancedthe flavors of whatever I used it in. Cookies had a richer flavor as well as pancakes and other baked goods. When I ran out I purchaseda couple of smaller bottles of vanilla at my local market, but the flavor just wasn't as intense.  So, I recently purchased anotherbottle of Nielsen-Massey and am very satisfied again with this product.  Keep in mind this is "pure" vanilla as opposed to "imitation"

Nielsen-Massey Madagascar Vanilla is BY FAR the best vanilla I've ever used in my baking--and I've used a lot of vanilla from numerous companies over five decades of baking.  There have been store-brands, spice company brands, the famous vanilla sold door-to-door years back, and even vanilla brought home from a foreign country.When I opened this bottle of vamilla, the aroma was fresh and fabulous.  Then I tasted the "old" cakes and cookies I've baked umpteen times.  I could have sworn they were new recipes, and my guests responded likewise.I proudly recommend Nielsen-Massey Madagascar Vanilla for your use.  Buy the 32-ounce bottle, because you're going love baking with it :)

column9: Exactly as promised, and excellent follow-up from the merchant
column10: I received this item with several other items - it was carefully packed in an individual, padded box within the larger parcel Amazon delivered.  While I prefer vanilla bean paste as a general rule, extract is much more economical and this is fairly good quality product with a standard alcohol base.  The value is hard to beat.

Stop what is going on and bring out the baking materials because a cake is on the way and it will be the best cake ever as long as Nielsen-Massey Vanilla is one of the ingredients.  I have used almost every type of real vanilla over the years and none is better than this one.  The taste fits my needs perfectly and those who eat the end result agree.  Even though cheap imitation vanilla is readily available at a low cost per unit and other real vanilla is also readily available this one is the absolute best.  I thought that the 32 ounce size would be too much and it might not get used before expiring but I was just plain wrong.  It will be gone long before its expiration and all the consumers in this house will say thank you.  There is nothing quite as pleasant as having one of the church ladies or a guest extolling the goodness of a pound cake made with Nielsen's.  I know the vanilla is just an insignificant part of the total product but it is the one element that adds so much to the flavor and goodness.

column9: Best vanilla extract + best price per ounce
column10: This is the best per-ounce price I've found anywhere.  I like this vanilla extract better than any of the others I've tried, from good old Schilling/McCormick to Penzey's to some of the Tahitian vanillas.

Bought this for Christmas Cookies and Whip Cream.  You can taste the difference.  I have used store bought vanilla, made my own vanilla and now Nielsen-Massey Madagascar Vanilla.  The best tasting is Nielsen, you can see the vanilla specks, I will definately use again.

This vanilla is really good and I like using it in my baking.  Since I largely bake gluten free, I use a lot of vanilla (these recipes call for more than "regular" recipes) and it gives the baked goods a good taste.

column9: Good vanilla at a great price!
column10: I used to find smaller glass bottles of this same product at retailers like Marshall's and TJ Maxx. Good vanilla is expensive, and if you use it a lot this is a great deal. Just figure out how much it would cost to buy a 'quart' of real vanilla at a grocery store!

I bought the vanilla bean extract but I was very disappointed to find that it has a stronger alcoholic flavour to it than the actual vanilla flavour. The extract was also not as thick as the other extracts I have used. I have not tried the vanilla bean paste of this brand and maybe that is of a better quality than the extract.

Superior vanilla beans come from the Madagascar "Bourbon Islands," Mexico and Indonesia. I find the flavor was truly superior to normal vanilla extract. While you don't want to use vanilla beans in everything (too expensive!), you will definitely want to consider using them in custards and when you make ice cream.Vanilla enhances everything from creamy porridges to custards and cakes. The list goes on and on. There are so many uses for vanilla. Vanilla is derived from the seductively aromatic vanilla bean. Vanilla beans are actually the cigar-shaped seed pod from a fragrant climbing orchid native to tropical America.Yes, vanilla extract is much more economical, but using vanilla beans is rather gourmet. The extract is created from chopped vanilla beans that are soaked in an alcohol/water solution. It takes about 100 beans to make 1 gallon of extract.You can use the vanilla beans, rinse and dry them, so they last longer. After drying, you can store them again in the glass tube or in their own plastic bag for reuse.~The Rebecca Review

After researching brands of vanilla bean paste, I decided to go with this one as it consistently has the best reviews. However, I'm not happy with this product at all. The vanilla taste just isn't there. It's great for adding the vanilla bean "look" to my recipes, but I found that even if I use a lot, I still can't achieve a good level of vanilla flavor. I used about 1/3 of the bottle for a frosting recipe but it still didn't have the vanilla flavor I was seeking. I had to add vanilla extract for that.I thought it would be thicker and have more vanilla beans in it, but it's about the consistency of maple syrup. It shouldn't be called a paste, as it really isn't. Pastes are very thick and don't run. I won't be buying this again.

column4: E. S. Noyes "liza lives to read"
column10: THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN REALLY GOOD VANILLA AND THE STUFF IN THE TINY BOTTLE FROM THE SUPERMARKET IS AS GREAT AS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN TELLICHERRY PEPPERCORNS AND, WELL, YOU GET THE POINT. THIS CALIBER OF VANILLA IS RIGHT UP THERE. MY BOYFRIEND, WHO BAKES, WON'T GO BACK TO THE NASTY STUFF. SO IF YOU MIGHT USE THIS ONCE IN A WHILE, I STILL THINK IT'S WORTH BUYING THE BIG BOTTLE. IT'S SO GOOD YOU MIGHT FIND YOURSELF ADDING A SPLASH TO PANCAKE BATTER OR SMOOTHIES OR....
Easier than getting my favorite (Trader Joe's) in smaller bottles (only) - and ALMOST as good. Sugar is listed as an ingredient - shouldn't be.

I feel bad writing a bad review, but I feel cheated and I don't believe other people should buy this product based on my experience with it. Maybe other products of theirs are good, but this one is exceptionally bad, especially since it is supposed to be gourmet. The small bottles of vanilla that you can buy at Walmart taste much, much, much, much, much more like vanilla than this product, which tastes to me, like vodka with a dash of vanilla in it. I feel like I have been cheated, even though for the price it should be a good value. I am actually scared to purchase vanilla now on the Internet in bulk other than from companies I can find and try out in the stores. I can only speak about the bottle I purchased. I would recommend something else. Most vanilla is gluten free although many have corn syrup in them. This one has sugar in it. I really don't understand positive reviews about this product. I bought it because it was cheap (for the amount) and gourmet. It (I think, tastes worse than the imitation). Imitation at least tastes like vanilla. I apologize for writing such a review but other people need to be aware of this product. If you want to buy from this company try something that will have more vanilla in it.

column9: 80% of a good on the go tea experience
column10: This is a decent set to take with you for good on-the-go tea making. I've got three things I would change about it that stop it from 5 stars:#1. The bottom of the pouch is not sewn on. So when you open it it opens from both directions which I find slightly annoying. That might just be me though.#2. The can that holds the infuser is lined with foam. This protects the infuser but forces you to make sure that it is 100% dry before stowing it. Again just a little annoyance to me.#3. The real reason this gets 4 instead of 5 stars. The cans do not have the plastic air seals on the lids like the Teavanna tea holders do. Because of that the tea cannot be left in these cans. This is my biggest compaint because I feel like I am loosing freshness when I put tea in here for more than a week (even though I cannot prove that).Overall, a great buy if you really like your tea and feel like taking it with you. I wish it was $5 cheaper but in the long run I will get enough use out of it to justify the cost.

It's perfect for it's intended use. The kit comes with 2 small airtight canisters, a pouch, an infuser, and case for the infuser. I personally love this set because it keeps everything together so I can just throw this in my tote and I'm ready for tea anytime. To correct the last reviewer you cannot use the canisters for actually preparing/steeping tea they are merely used to store the tea and infuser. The pouch feels very durable and the quality is good. The infuser opens up and acts as a scoop so you can scoop up the desired amount of tea. It's a great set for the office or for travel.

Edit: I've given this three stars vs my previous 1 star when I was told the can was not meant to brew tea in. I still would  prefer a "total travel solution", then it would have been 5 stars.Original Post: The can to brew the tea leaks. I sent the first one back thinking maybe it was defective. The second one leaked also. And, the can gets super hot, to the point of not being able to pick it up.  I also posted this review on the Teavana website, it has not been posted....just an FYI about neg reviews sent to them.

The worst popcorn in the world!  At one time this might have started out as popcorn but the product I received was as stale as if it were extracted from King Tuts tomb.  What was supposed to be cheddar cheese was some alien goo that seemed to be spray painted on creating a coating for this stale mushy 'stuff' that was billed as Double Cheddar Gourmet popcorn.  I did contact Cornzapoppin and they have ignored my concern.  Garrett's of Chicago is a far better product that arrives with crunch, and at a better price.

column9: Strong Brown sugar and molasses flavor.. Good quality
column10: These are very high quality.. The taste is not for me because they have a strong brown sugar and molasses flavor.. The ones I had from austinuts were more cinnamon flavor which I like better. But if you like brown sugar and molasses and would like a very high quality product I would recommend these.. 3 stars solely for personal taste preference

I have two finicky Burmese felines with very sensitive stomachs.  My girl cat will not even eat cat treats.  They've been on dry food since kittens and I've yet to find a brand they don't eventually throw up from.  They both suffer from runny eyes and occasionally nasal discharge.  I recently started them on this 95% organic food.  Both my cats, even the girl, devour it like wild animals.  And to our delight, they have stopped vomiting.  Both of them have bulked up slightly, have even healthier coats and less eye and congestion problems since this change in diet as well.  I hope this review helps.

I'll keep this short: My cat rarely meets a food he doesn't like, but no other food has made him PURR when he sits down to eat it. I order it on subscription now, and there are two open boxes of it currently on the kitchen floor, and he sits by it, occasionally rubs his face on it, and knows when it's time to get a new can...and he goes nuts! It actually seems to fill him up better than other organic cat foods, and he eats it a little slower, too. All around a good choice for this feline...

I have three cats, one with a very sensitive stomach.  Am in the process of switching them from a prescription diet that they have been on for a long time (since the one cat had serious stomach problems) to Organix products.  They all love the food, and there have been no stomach problems to date (2 months).  Therefore, I would highly recommend this brand of cat food.

I'm pretty sure that's what my cats are saying as they gobble this stuff up.  Neither one of my cats really liked soft food, but they love this stuff.
