All of the Jules Destrooper cookies are made in Belgium with good quality ingredients and packaged well.  They are quite attractive and whenever I serve them to someone who has never had them before, they always comment on them.The thins are especially elegant, thin and crisp, wonderful with ice cream or a warm beverage.  My only complaint about Jules Destrooper cookies is that it is very difficult not to eat a whole box at once.  Whenever I see them at the dollar store, I stock up and try to hide a few boxes in the top cabinet.Ginger Thins - These have plenty of nice chewy little bits of translucent candied ginger (5%) that contrast with the almost brittle cookie and have a good balance of spice (ginger and a hint of cinnamon) to sweet.  These are wonderful with tea.Almond Thins - Crispy with lots of almond slivers and slices (10%) and a pronounced flavor of both brown sugar and butter.  I appreciate that they aren't loaded up with almond extract, making the taste more delicate in than the usual almond cookie.  Especially good with ice cream, crème brûlée, or any custard-based dessert.Butter Crisps - These are also nice and crunchy but with a more neutral flavor, very buttery, similar to an ice cream cone.  They are excellent with a thin smear of jam and hot chocolate or with ice cream.Paris Butter Waffles - These are not quite as brittle or elegant as the others but because of the deep waffle pattern, they are the perfect vehicle for hazelnut chocolate spread (Nutella) or speculoos spread (Biscoff spread) and a cup of coffee.  This variety does have artificial vanilla, which is actually preferred by many for baking cookies.

I should add, the cookies are in two plastic nests of four cookies inside a foil package inside the cardboard box, so a good clamp keeps the opened cookies crisp and whole. Bon apetit!

column9: The Swedish Chef Would Be Proud!
column10: Let me start by saying that I am a huge fan of all things swedish, from Lingonberries to salt cod to Lutefisk to those yummy red candy fish. When I saw that Jules Destrooper had invented yet another Swedish delectable, I could not wait for my package to arrive!After assaulting the UPS driver and absconding with my "butter waffles" (which are more like cookies), I went into my kitchen and sat down in my breakfast nook to eat them. A hearty glass of milk was all I needed to drench the entire box and consume it. In reality, I ended up saturating the cardboard box and must have eaten that as well, because when I was done there was nothing left save for some soggy nuggets stuck to my ceiling. I assume they are from my delicious waffles and not from my earlier experiment of stuffing a cornish game hen with popping corn to "make its own stuffing." I am still picking bits of hen from my bushy, inappropriately dark eyebrows.Also, some recipe ideas for these waffles include topping them with olives, tuna salad, anchovy and pretzel (an old Slavic favorite) and peanut butter. Sometimes I give these to the neighbor children when they behave themselves, and actually I have only given one out to one neighbor child. My neighbor's kids are usually misbehaving and absolutely do not deserve any of my tasty cookies! Anyway, it turns out the one kid I gave it to was actually a lawn jockey statue, which makes sense because my neighbors, the "Davenports," have very light skin. They are actually quite pasty and I am waiting for the day when one of them develops melanoma, because they are always out in the sun, in their pool, having a "heck of a time," under the sun's deadly rays, oblivious to the cellular damage they are inflicting on themselves. I prefer to stay inside during the daytime and nighttime hours, usually venturing from my house every fortnight to collect my mail. However, when I know a delivery of Jules Destrooper Butter waffles are arriving, I am on "high alert" and spring from my rascal mobility scooter whenever I hear a car door close.Overall, I LOVE these waffles. Buy them, and If you don't love them too, send them off to me!!!

I use three of these across one of my storage shelves in my kitchen. I also have the large drawer that fits under the Keurig. Essentially these 54 pod drawers are for my overflow.This particular brand - Nifty - is... well.... quiet nifty! It's reasonably priced. I would recommend this drawer to anyone.

It would be nice if it had been made out of slightly stronger metal that didn't bend as easily. Also, some of the drawers slide very smoothly while others pull out a little harder because the wire that they slide on is a bit bent as well.

I was pleasantly surprised at the quality of this product!  The construction of the item is durable and each drawer extends fully so you can view all of the coffee pods - no guessing what is stuck in the way back!  This item was exactly what i was looking for...  and is perfect for organizing.

The only drawback is that it's too deep to fit in a cabinet.  Luckily, it looks very nice sitting out on the counter.  It doesn't look cheap like a lot of others do.  The drawers are sturdy, and fully functional when completely filled.  I bought this as a Christmas gift for my sister-in-law and brother and they love it!

Excellent for pantry storage of 54 K-Cups, I have a Platinum from Costco (came with 60 free K-Cups all for $149) So added a 36 single tray From Bed Bath And Beyond with 20% off coupon placed under the machine for all decaf, and a 30 carosel for variety party selections. Favorites are Half and Half Decaf, Tully's Decaf Home Blend and Tullies French Roast Decaf. Highly recommend all.
Great for the purpose intended.  Now I have easy access to the pods and have the ability to organize by type of pod.

I had been searching weeks for the perfect sized K cup storage item for my counter and found this item on Amazon.  It's the perfect size for limited counter space. The black wire mesh 3 drawer holder matches my Keurig and they are attractive sitting side by side. I highly recommend this storage product.
These drawers are sturdy and easy to open.  I store it next to my coffee machine with coffee mugs on top.  This is a quality product.

This is the perfect storage unit for my K-cups!  It fits perfectly next to my coffee maker.  I love the fact it stores up to 54 cups too.  I would recommend this for anyone looking for a storage unit.

Overall the Nifty 54 drawer is a nice solution for large capacity k-cup storage.  However there is one thing I dont like about it, but have learned to work around it.  When pulling the drawers open, the tops of the kcups catch the drawer above it and tip over, or drag.  Just have to pull it out slowly to avoid problem.  Ive added a picture in the gallery also.

column9: "Sturdy" comes to mind as the best description!
column10: If asked to sum up this coffee-pod drawer in one word, "sturdy" would be my enthusiastic answer. It is one hefty piece of metal sliding-drawer perfection - it weighed in at 4 lbs. 11 oz. on my postal scale!The drawers slide in and out with barely a hitch. Large rubber feet on the bottom means it stays put on your counter. The drawers have stops on the bottom so you won't accidentally pull  them out completely. And best of all, 36 K-cups fit in perfectly, nestling cozily in 3 individual rows per drawer thanks to 2 divider bars in each.Seriously, you can't go wrong with this product if you have only a couple of boxes of K-cups you need to store. So much more attractive than boxes! I do plan to eventually paint mine with metal spray-paint to complement my kitchen's color scheme.

We are very happy with this purchase.  It looks nice, holds more K-cups than other containers of the same price, and arrived in perfect shape.  The only thing I dislike about the product is that the bottom two drawers are sometimes difficult to pull out.  Instead of gliding out, you have to sort of wiggle and shimmy them.  It's really not that big of a deal though.  It's a minor annoyance but, overall, the product is everything we hoped for.  We just store are least favorite flavors on the bottom (the most difficult to pull out).

i was concerned that the drawers would be hard to open / close, but to my surprise, they are easy peasy!!!  it is very sturdy, and does not take up too much space on my counter! i love how the top is flat so i can store other items on top..... i love having my kcups organized and easy to access!!

Before I got this drawer, boxes of pods were taking over my cabinet, like some sci-fi horror film. Now I can easily see what varieties I have and what I am running low on. I am a new Keurig user and this has greatly added to my enjoyment of the system. More organized than a basket, holds more than a carousel, and looks great too.
i got this for Christmas and it holds 54 K-cups no extra. All draws open perfect once filled and looks awesome.Arrived early and packaging was great.

Holds alot of kups.  Nice solid design.  Pretty nice looking.  Trays slide out easily, easy to fill and dispense.  The top of it is good for cups/sugar/whatever.  I put water bottles on mine, since that is what I had there before I got this holder.  I bought it for a party I had so I would have a good selection, but I will use it regularly because I like it, and the way it looks on my counter.

I wanted a place to store my k-cups because the carosels didn't hold enough so I was constantly filling them.  This holds the equivalent of two carosels and takes up only a bit more room.  I ordered a second one to hold the teas and hot chocolates while the first hold the various flavored coffees we like. The Pod Drawer is sturdy and well made.

The Nifty 54 Coffee Pod Drawer is the perfect solution for me. It sets nicely beside my Keurig and holds 64 k-cups. The drawers slide easily and have a catch so they don't fall out when fully opened. The top is perfect for my sugar dispenser and extra mugs. It is well made and worth the money. The black mesh design fits any decor.

For those of you who have limited counter space, this pod drawer is ideal.  It is made of metal, so you don't have to worry about sagging plastic causing drawers to bind. There is just enough room for a coffee cup to sit upright in front of the Mini, but not upside down. The Mini fits perfectly within the boundaries of the top shelf. And if you load the drawers using the up/down technique, you can fit 21 pods per drawer instead of 18.

I was looking for something that would hold a lot of kpaks and not take up a lot of space.  This is it!  I really like this pod drawer.  The one thing that is sometimes frustrating is when you have to pull a drawer out to get to a kpak in the back if you don't have the paks in there just right it gets hung up.  But overall it works great and takes up little space!
A great buy. I've got a small counter space and not a lot of storage all around. Great way to organize and store my coffee.

I have this next to my Keurig on the counter.  I had the revolving carousel for K-cups but decided to try this because it can hold more K-cups.  I like it a lot and it doesn't take up a whole lot of space. I put my container of coffee stirrers on top of the drawers and it's like having a coffee station on my counter.  I really like this product.

I read the review and I was hestitant as it was reported the drawer did not come out easy.  Well, it comes out easy.  I have room for plenty of choices in the drawer as my family likes hot chocolate and tea.  Personally I like coffee. The best thing is that it is a space saver.  I put the Kcup machine on it and I have plemnty of room for condiments.  With other storage syatems you place it next to the Kcup machine.  This takes a lot of spce.  Space is important in my cottage which is now my home.  I think this was a great buy for me.  It is funny how sometimes you buy something and it turns out to be a dud.  This is definitely worth the money.

Finally a drawer unit that will hold 3 boxes of K-cups. It has no slip grips on the bottom and can be stacked for more coffee storage. Attractive design. No unsightly half full boxes on your countertop. Thank you.
Great product, drawers slide easily, coffee packets fit perfectly. Looks good on the counter and is sturdy enough to place coffee related items on top.

column9: Store a bunch of K-Cups and get rid of the boxes!
column10: These drawers look great in the office.  There is a little lip on the top of the drawer so they can stack or you can put more K-Cups.  Looks so much better than boxes!  Invert every other K-Cup and it will hold 63 K-Cups.  The drawers pull out smoothly & evenly (it might need a bit of wax after a while).  The drawers have a nice little stop to prevent the drawers from falling out accidentally (nice little plus that).  It is kind of long so it might not fit into some cabinets.  If you were wondering about this well, just get it.  We are thinking about getting another one.  Great product, accurate shipping, worth the money.  Thanks!

This pod drawer for my K-cups is perfect. It is made very well. Drawers slide in and out great. It sits right next to my Kergi Coffee maker. So convenient and handy.I had looked at several different K-cup drawers. None of them worked as well as the pod drawer. Thanks
Perfect under cabinet storage for all of your beverage brewing cups. Excellent quality for those who have limited (or no) counter space!

Great storage container for the coffee. Holds plenty and drawers don't fall out easily when digging to the back. Perfect for my application. ....and the price was right with free shipping!!! Only took 3 days for me!
Very good quality and drawers slide easily.  The metal is heavy.  Holds a lot of coffee pods.I love the color and the quality.

column9: Realy holds a lot of K-cups!
column10: Since I buy my K-cups in bulk at Sam's Club, I really needed a way to store them attractively.  The Nifty 54 Coffee Drawer fits the bill and then some.  It's made of metal so it's durable, the drawers slide great even when full.  The top which is also made of metal is strong enough to sit containers of creamers, equal, etc. on it.  Bottom line is I love it!

I love the fact this holds 54 pods, however, it sticks when I fill the entire thing up and makes it hard to open and close. There was also a time when it ripped open one of my pods of coffee. I don't recommend this product because of this. My kids absolutely hated it and wanted me to return it.
Nifty is a good name for the product.  The unit works well. The drawer slide smoothly and do not get crossways or hung up.  The pods fit very well. Looks nice on the counter. I recommend it.
My wife has a wide taste in coffees and teas so this rack really fits the bill for maximum storage.

This is exactly what I needed for my new keurig. It fit more than the caddies and the drawers slide smoothly. It fits perfectly next to my keurig. I use one drawer for coffee, one for cocoa, and one for teas! I may want a second one so I can stack them hahaGreat product!
Great k-cup holder.  Definitely recommend it over the smaller 36 cup holder.  Top tray works well for mugs, sugar, etc.

I've been looking for a stand for quite awhile.  I almost bought the bamboo stand sold at BB&B but couldn't get past the $32 price.  I'm glad I chose this stand instead because of its large capacity.My family has about 4-5 Kcups on a daily basis.  It's so nice to have them handy on our counter.  The stand is very sturdy and does not eat up to much counter space.  (my counter is on the larger side)I highly recommend this product . It keeps our cups neat & organized!  Aloha from the 50th state!
Purchased this item to clean up the counter in my kitchen.  Its looks so good now.  The reveiws I read were helpful and I made the right decision.  Quality product.

I ordered the 54 pod drawer with the 36 pod, flat drawer. They fit perfectly together and leave space for creamer and sugar. So much better than basket or the constant refilling of the swiveling pod station.

column9: a great way to store your k-cups.
column10: This shelf takes up little room , but hold a lot of k-cups. It holds 54 if all are turned right side up. If you turn every other one upside down you can fit 21 per drawer!

column9: Very handy for organizing K Cups
column10: I love this organizer. I am able to organize my K Cups by caffeine level, flavor, etc. Drawers easily slide in and out. I agree with the other posts that tell you to alternate cups up and down to get even more cups in the organizer. Great price on Amazon.

Great way to store K-cups, especially in an office where lots of folks want different flavors at their fingertips.It looks great and the drawers open/close easily.  We have been using it for several weeks and no problems.

This is a great k cup holder.  Before I bought it I think I saw in one of the reviews about putting them in with every other one upside down and that works perfectly for getting a few extra in each row.  This is the perfect size for a tight spot yet you get a lot of k cups in it.  We're extremely happy with our purchase.
This fits perfectly in the coffee "garage" on the counter.  The garage fits two side by side.  However, I wish it was one level higher.

My husband and I use about 4 k cups a day, sometimes a little less or a little more, give or take. I was looking for something that is compact and holds a lot because of my limited counter space. We have the keurig b-40. This pod holder is very well constructed, compact and holds a lot of k cups. Sits nicely next to the keurig and has a flat top so you can put the sugar bowl or splenda packets- or whatever on top of it. Love it and worth every penny!

I highly recommend this K-cup coffee organizer. I did a lot of research when searching for a K-cup organizer for our home, and this is by far the best deal. In fact, I ended up buying two of them! It holds 54 cups, the quality is great, it's very easy to use, and it looks nice! And you can stack them too. My entire family, including my mother-in-law, absolutely loves this K-cup coffee organizer!

For those of us who place their full size Keurig coffeemaker on the counter under kitchen cabinets, this is the perfect solution for storing K-cups.  I started out with the single drawer, under-the-Keurig type of storage, but found that although it fit fine under the cabinet, I couldn't raise the front to remove and replace the K-cup, and adding water became tricky.  I found the 3 drawer side storage unit to be the perfect solution for this problem without having to move the Keurig to a counter space with no overhead cabinets.
I love my 54 K-cup holder it looks great next to my Keurig and holds all my varieties of coffee!  I would recommend it to everyone looking for a great looking durable k- cup holder!

Exactly what I was looking for! Very attractive, brushed black powder coat, drawers open/close easily and the sleek top doubles as a coffee mug holder (or whatever coffee/tea accessories you want). I'm a 1-2 cup a day coffee drinker and I buy samples of K Cups from various online venues - this is perfect way to organize them all, and it looks sharp next to the Brewer....

This is a quality product and like the other reviewer stated you can easily fit 63 K-cups instad of the advertised 54.  You just alternate within the rows, one up, one down.  SO each row will take 7 K-cups, so each drawer will hold 21 K-cups...your total is 21 K-cups x 3 drawers= 63 YEAH!!!!For the price this is the best value for K-cup storage.  And the price on Amazon is the same as in store at Bed Bath'N'Beyond.Worth the price if you like organization, and not a bunch of K-cup boxes piled in your cupboards.

I bought two Nifty 54 Coffee Pod Drawers and am very happy with the quality and space economy these provide. I plan on buying more as my wife loves her Keurig so much and the variety it allows and as such we have quite a few pods.

After reading all of the reviews, I decided to go with this one because of its dimensions, ability to stack and even store in a cupboard if needed. If you are looking for a way to store all of your extra k-cups, this is definitely worth the $! I'm getting ready to purchase another one since my husband is hooked and now has his own variety of flavors :)

This item is great.  It sits right next to my Cuisinart Single coffee maker.  It stores and keeps neat many K-cups, exactly as it is descrived.  I am thinking of buying another to stack on top of this one for more storage.

column9: The perfect drawer for my kitchen
column10: The product arrived on time and was well packaged. It's a durable construction, there is enough space for the 54 cups it says it can hold and the product looks great next to my Keurig coffee maker.I ended up buying this design drawer as I think the carousels use up too much space for the number of pods they can hold, and after reading reviews for drawers to put underneath coffee makers I figured that with a drawer underneath my coffee maker there wouldn't be enough space left between the top of my coffee maker and the cupboard to be able to lift the top of the coffee maker open to put new cups in. If I would have had enough space, I would have probably bought the Nifty storage drawer to put underneath my coffee maker. Nevertheless I would recommend this product.

I purchased this because I have alot of k cups & this holds the most that I could find.  I put all my extras in here.  I just sit it on the counter. It holds alot.  Thinking of buying another to try & stack them.  I would recommend this to others, already have.

This is absolutely the best K-Cup holder!  Sits next to the Keurig, on top sits the basket-napkin holder; both the Keurig and the holder are tucked against the wall and the Keurig opens easily under the upper cabinet.  For our home, this provides a much better use of counter space than the flat pod holder.  LOVE IT!
This K-cup storage is stylish & space saving. K-cups are easy to retrieve and select. Drawers slide out to completely allow you to select cups. This holds 3 18ct k-cup boxes.

Absolutely wonderful!  Holds plenty of K-cups and looks neat and tidy.  Love that I can put sugars and creamer on the top.  Looks great next to my coffee pots.  Great price too.  Several of my friends after seeing it have all decided to get it. :)

We looked at the drawer that you set the coffee machine on but figured it would not work with our cabinets. We looked at several different versions of this type of drawers and decided on this one because of price and other reviews. I am so glad we got this one, it is made very well and looks great. We get compliments all the time from people that see it.

My husband and I really use our Keurig, but storing all the boxes / K-cups "WAS" a real pain. Until we got this Pod Drawer. Freed up so much counter / cabinet space along with being super organized and stylish. We love it!!

This is just perfect. It holds 54 and fits my space just right. I was going to buy the other kind that pulls out and slides down so I could put it in a top cabinet but the review's were bad. I just keep this one in my under counter cabinet and it works fine.

Before I bought this Niffty organizer, I read all the reviews available on it and on the single drawer organizers. It took me quite awhile to decide which type I preferred for the space I wanted to put it in. I even did some measurements. LOL When I got it it fit perfectly where I wanted it to!!! I really love it and have filled it and nearly emptied it already. The drawers on mine work smoothly and the individual rows in the drawers seem uniformly sized. I hadn't really thought about alternating them top to bottom to get 7 in each row until I re-read some of the newer reviews.  63 is the maximum capacity which is great.This is the first review I have ever written for a product that I have bought thru Amazon or any other online "store".

Saw item on Amazon was looking for something not to big or too small for hubbys kurig coffee pods. This arrived in only a few days and fits perfectly on the counter with the coffee maker. It holds enough coffee to keep you in coffe for a couple weeks depending on your intake that is. It's made of metal and also has enough room on top for your two large size coffee cups. Would recomend this product to anyone looking for a place for your kurig pods. Neat and size is perfect for small areas.
very good quality and helps utilize space and helps visibility of keeping track what cups are left since I enjoy 3 or 4 differant types of coffee

I bought this item when it was out of stock.  It was only a few days before it was in stock again, and Amazon shipped it immediately.  When I received it, I noticed that it was pretty heavy duty and well constructed.  Comes straight out of the box with drawers ready to go.  A definite value for your money!  Fits great on the counter top with room for up to 5 regular mugs on top.

I looked at a lot of different types of holders for Kcups then finally decided on this one.  I am not regretting that decision. It's great that it has three segrated drawers.  I use one for decaf, one for regular and one for teas and hot cocoas.  Everyone knows just where to find their favorite.  It is also of very sturdy construction -- heavy, not cheap.  Top acts as a little shelf for condiments too.  Very happy with this purchase!

This was a great addition to my kitchen, next to my Mr. Coffee/Keurig machine.  It doesn't take up much space and makes retrieving my k-cups so much easier than digging around in the boxes.  Each drawer holds 3 rows of 6 kcups, however, if you alternate each one (right side up, then upside down), you can get an extra kcup in each row. This is great if you organize your kcups like I do, with one type of coffee in each row. If you just toss them in there haphazardly, turning some upside down isn't the greatest idea.  Great product!

This "Nifty" 3 drawer holds 54 pods and is a very good item to keep your coffee k-cups in and out of the way. It frees up the pantry shelves. I looked at "other" drawers for more money, but this one had very good reviews. The convience, price and good looking product. I liked it so much, I purchased another one for a gift, and they love it too!...If you need extra space for your k-cups, you won't be dissapointed...also, I always check with Amazon before looking anywhere else. Thanks Amazon.!

I purchased this after I bought my Cuisinart Keurig Coffee Maker.  My coffee maker sits towards the font of my counter and the coffee keeper sits sideways behind the maker.  It fits perfectly and doesn't take up a lot of space.  I love the 3 different sliding drawers.  I use one for regular coffee, one for decaf coffee, and one for tea and cocoa.  I have no regrets in buying this.  It works beautifully in my kitchen.

I absolutely love this organizer!  It helps me see what flavors I actually have while storing the boxes in the pantry, since counter space is always at a premium.  This is the best of all the organizers for k cups!

I liked it so much I just ordered a second unit. We have the chrome carousel on the counter and use these in the pantry for extra storage. It would look good on the counter too. It is all metal, welded construction with a nice paint job. It also has good neutral colored rubber feet so it shouldn't leave marks on counters or shelves. One thing I didn't see mentioned is that the drawers will not come all the way out. Great because your k cups don't end up all over the place, not so great for cleaning. Still think its great, especially when you consider the price. Definitely would recommend.

column9: Very nice! Just the right size!
column10: I am quite fond of this k-cup organizer! I sort with the 3 drawers* Sturdy & Smart* Easy to use and clean* Came assembledFor now anyway, this is how I'm using it..Tea in one drawer, coffees in one drawer and in the other: ciders and cocoa - the cocoa may need it's own drawer the way my girls are drinking it!!

I received this yesterday, and is very pleased with it. It was well made and looks good next to my coffee maker, much better than the stack of boxed of different kinds of coffee/tea. easy access with the 3 draws and I can put other stuff on the top. I like to try different type of coffee and tea, thinking about get another on to stack on top.
I love this Coffee drawer makes everything look so clean and organized!the product was received on time for Thanksgiving. Thanks, for the great product!

I purchased this item and am so pleased.  I never write reviews, but I could not help but write one to say what an outstanding experience I had with Kitchen Clique.  The pod drawer was perfectly wrapped and arrived quickly.  It is sitting on my shelf and will get much use.  Thank you Kitchen Clique, and thank you Amazon!!!!

I bought this along with the Nifty Drawer, it keeps all my k-cups I order in bulk in order. This product is for my teas, cocoas, and cider. My kids, ages 13, 9, and 4 are able to pull the drawers out to pick out which one they want. It's sturdy construction, easy to clean and restock with k-cups. It's compact for small counter spaces, like I have, and holds 54 k-cups. I love it and highly recommend it.
Great all around. Delivered quick w/ Prime. Holds at least 54 k-cups, read another review about putting every other one upside down to increase capacity.

These pho bo spices comes in a mesh bag with no extra impurities like msg and sodium.  It is not the weird powdered stuff you usually see as "pho seasoning" but actually whole spices.  Sticks of Cinnamon, pods of cardamon, licorice and whole stars of aniseed. I highly recommend this!

Just got the chance to try this yesterday on a batch of mead. Of course added yeast energizer and nutrient to batch, rehydrated in a yeast starter and pitched after it started working. Really like this yeast, fast starter and strong fermenter ( airlock is really chuggin' along ).Also low foamer which to me is a big plus.

column9: Yup, not the pictured Biscuit Buddy.
column10: Yup, this is not the pictured bag. It is inferior. The clip is weak. There isn't pockets on the side as pictured. Got the one pictured at PetSmart for $9.99.

The Biscuit Buddy that was sent to me was NOT the type pictured. The style in the picture is made of a high quality, thick, durable material. The pouch that was sent to me is flimsy, thin, and has none of the awesome features that the pouch in the picture has (no zippered pocket, no locking clip).I have returned this product and requested an exchange for the style of pouches that are pictured, or a refund. I will leave more feedback after the exchange/return has been completed. I hope the company does not let me down.UDATE (3/16/2010):Received my requested exchanged item, and to my extreme disappointment, it was exactly the same product I'd received the first time. BEWARE: the product pictured is NOT the product you will receive. The product the company sends is inferior and has none of the same features as the much nicer, higher quality Biscuit Buddy in the picture. I've now requested a complete REFUND from the company. Will purchace the Biscuit Buddy in the picture from a different website. Disappointed.

column9: Good, but could easily be a lot better.
column10: Pros:- Holds lots of treats, or treats and a tennis ball.- Flexible top seal closes well and is easy to use.- The Biscuit Buddy is attractive.Cons:- Belt clip is flimsy and weak. You WILL lose your Biscuit Buddy if you rely on it.- Belt clip is riveted on, hard to replace with something stronger.- Belt loop clip is flimsy plastic and way too small. It took a lot of effort to get it on my Levi's belt loop, and even more effort to get it off.- Belt loop clip has to be destroyed to remove it for replacement with a bigger metal clip.For the above reasons, I would not buy this again if this one were stolen. But it's good enough for the reasons on top for me not to trash it...yet.

column9: Dont Buy Falls apart VERY easily!!!!
column10: I bought one cause it looked like the best one to suit our needs, and now it has become a joke to us to see what falls apart or breaks on it each time we use use it!

I have purchased this item twice, once for myself and once for a family member.  Both times I received the product exactly as described.  It has a belt clip, a keychain clip, an external zipper pocket, and a large treat pouch with a drawstring.  The keychain clip is a big tight and snapped after a few uses, but the belt clip is very sturdy and the whole item is remarkably chew-proof.  I have labradors who love nothing more than to gnaw on anything that smells like food!I have attached a "Bags on Board Bone Dispenser" and a clip to hold used poop bags.  Now when I walk my dogs, I only have to grab one thing as we leave the house.  I clip it to my waist band and it holds my keys, treats, poop bags, and a way to carry them and still hold two leashes.I highly recommend this item.

Do anybody on this site ever check what is written in product description?Ingredients list:Vegetable cellulose, magnesium stearate (vegetable source), silica.and pray tell,what is working as a diuretic?
If indeed this is a 4.4 pound box, it's $11.99 in the grocery stores on the west coast.....

This is the best-tasting brand of powdered milk I've tried. It tastes much better than normal skim milk from a carton. Since it tastes so good it's perfect for anything that calls for skim milk - mixing with Ovaltine/Chocolate syrup, and all kinds of recipes.
This dry milk is super easy to mix. My kids will drink it in a cup, on cereal or in baked goods.  Great product for the money.

First, for all of you who have been looking for this product, Nestle's had a problem with their production.  It will not be available until they get their act together.Second, I have tried many instant, non-fat powdered milk brands and this is still my favorite.  I bought the Saco brand at Christmas, and while it was good, it is a bit different than the Carnation brand.Third, I don't think it's over-priced.  Dairy has risen and will continue to rise because they are using corn for fuel instead of feeding it to the cows.  I live in the Dallas-Fort Worth area and I don't believe I have ever seen a box this big even offered in any of the stores I frequent.  This size combined with free shipping--I think it's a great bargain.If you keep it in your freezer and take it out as you need it, it will have a better flavor than leaving it on the shelf.  This goes for all powdered milks.  I even keep my homemade hot chocolate mix in the freezer for the same reason.I hope it becomes available soon!  Amazon, thanks for offering it for sale!

This product itself is fabulous; creamy  with a good taste. However, the price plus shipping is greed, pure and simple. Shame on the seller and shame on Amazon for not policing the retailers who chose to take advantage of the consumer. BTW this comes in a plastic bag that you can seal, The problem is that the bag can split at the seams. The box was a much better package.

column4: A Research It Maven "Just the facts please"
column9: Good milk for non fat, but way overpriced!
column10: Carnation has always been the American dry milk choice, but this price is way high! Check out Nido, which is dry whole milk: Nestle Nido Milk Powder, Imported, 14-Ounce Cans (Pack of 3) and also is a great (good fat) coffee creamer and makes awesome bread and mashed potatoes!
I use two dry spoonfuls in my coffee for a fat free creamy cup of coffe without cooling it down too fast.I get it at BJ's for $13.49.

Here's an item we always have around the house, although we often buy it in smaller containers. It's an excellent product and we can make up a batch of skim milk in very short order. My wife uses it for cooking and baking. She adds it to the baby's food. She uses it as a creamer for coffee and tea. We take it along for camping and it provides milk without the need for a fridge. We rely on it when we inadvertently run out of milk and can't immediately get to the grocery store. The taste is excellent, especially if you are used to skim milk and drink it very cold. This is very useful stuff to have around.Gary Peterson

This is a great product, especially in places where you can't buy fresh milk every day (or on hand for when you're snowed in), But I can no longer find it anywhere on any shelves, and now, not even on Amazon.com!

This shelf stable milk has increased the amount of milk used in our household.  We used to never buy milk because even the half gallon would go bad before we could use it all.  I'm placing my second order today and plan on keeping this milk in the house at all times.  The shelf life on my first order was a year or more from my date of purchase!
This is the best boxed/canned milk I have found.  It is really good.  Taste, almost, like what I buy in the refridgerated section.  Since discovering this wonderful product, I NEVER run out of MILK.

This is the real thing, folks -- oatmeal as it should be. If you watch "Good Eats" on the Food Network, you've seen Alton Brown praise steel-cut oats and dis rolled oats (the "Quaker Oatmeal" stuff). I personally love rolled oats, but if you don't, don't let that stop you from buying the McCann's. The texture, the taste, the "oomph" are nothing like your ordinary breakfast oats. Where rolled Quaker oats are a bit slippery and thin, these steel-cut oats are much firmer with a lot more tooth and a much heartier, nuttier flavor.Be aware that you have to invest a little time to cook this cereal -- half an hour on the stovetop. Or try boiling the water the previous night, turning off the heat, and then putting the oats in to sit overnight. Then finish cooking them in the morning for 10 minutes or so. There are other shortcuts, too -- try a Google search. Whichever way you try, you may be spoiled for other hot cereals forever.

My husband and I love this oatmeal!  I prepare it the night before by boiling 2 cups of water.  I take the pot off the burner and pour in 1/2 a cup of oatmeal.  I let it sit covered overnight.  At the same time I place some raisins in a small container with water to plump them up overnight.  The next morning I cook the oatmeal for 10 minutes, I throw in the plumped raisins, an apple- sliced, cored and cut up, add cinnamon and some agave (natural sweetner) and the rest is history.We aren't hungry til lunch.  A great way to start the day.

Having been turned onto steel cut and Irish oatmeal by Alton Brown, I much prefer these to any other oatmeal out there.I make Alton's overnight oatmeal recipe in my Zojirushi rice cooker Zojirushi NS-ZCC10 5-1/2-Cup Neuro Fuzzy Rice Cooker and Warmer, Premium White. The results are outstanding all the time. It is delightful to wake up to this creamy breakfast waiting for me. True breakfast comfort food. I like these oats because there is still a bit of bite to the oatmeal after it is cooked.OVERNIGHT OATMEALEquipment:Rice cooker with timer or slow cookerIngredients:1 part steel cut or Irish oats4 parts watercreamdried fruitMethod:The night before add ingredients to rice cooker/slow cooker. For rice cooker set the program to porridge and set the timer for when you want it to be ready. For the slow cooker turn it on low heat.Wake up to breakfast.2 Servings:1/2 cup oats, 4 cups water, 2-3 TBSP cream, dried fruit as desiredKeep the 1:4 ratio of oats to water and it should work out well.Variations:apples and cinnamondried coconut and coconut milk instead of some of the waterflax seeds for fiber and Omega 3 fatty acidsLook to pre-made packages for flavor inspirations and make your own, healthier oatmeal. You won't be disappointed.

McCann's Steel Cut Irish Oatmeal has the best flavor & texture of any oatmeal available.  However, it takes a little experimenting with all the methods of cooking to find the cooking method that is right for your individual taste.  I invested in a small (6 cup) microwave rice cooker and use the following recipe:  Bring 1 cup of water to a rolling boil in an uncovered microwave rice cooker.  Stir in 1/4 cup oatmeal, cover and lock rice cooker lid and allow to sit overnight.  The next morning place rice cooker in microwave and cook for approximately 12 minutes at 40% power (Using reduced power keeps the rice cooker from overflowing).  Remove from microwave and let sit for 7-10 minutes.  Remove lid and add toppings of your choice (brown sugar, butter, milk, dried fruit, stir & enjoy. Makes 1 serving.

column9: Steel Cut is the most healthy form of oatmeal
column10: I really prefer McCann's steel cut oats to any rolled oats I've ever had, especially the "al dente" texture, slightly nutty flavor.I often have difficulty finding McCann's at my local grocer, and really appreciate the ease of ordering it from Amazon. With Prime, the shipping is free and the shelf life of this product is well over a year.Steel cut oats have nearly twice the fiber of rolled oats and seem to stick with me a bit longer. Since it does take 30 minutes to cook this up, I make a batch of 8 cups every other week or so, and store it in 1 cup Ziploc or Gladware containers. Under cook the oats about 5 minutes, then in the morning you just pop the container (without the lid!) in the microwave for 2-3 minutes on 50% power. You have a fast and very nutritious breakfast.To vary things a bit, I mix in chopped pecans and maple syrup, or chopped dried fruit (apricots, blueberries, cherries, peaches whatever you have on hand) and honey, or just brown sugar. I always have about 1 Tsp of SmartBalance in with it also. My cardiologist is pleased that I eat oatmeal 3-5 times a week, as is my heart!

I'll admit, until recently I didn't even understand what "Irish oatmeal" was. In case you don't either, here's a quick explanation. Most oatmeal we see is rolled oats, meaning the miller gets the oats moist and then runs them through heavy metal rollers to flatten them. To make Irish oatmeal, the miller simply cuts each oat into about three pieces. So, the shape and texture of the two kinds of oatmeal are completely different.Let me also admit that McCann's is the only brand of Irish oatmeal that I've tried. Therefore, I'm really comparing it to the many kinds of rolled oats that I've had, rather than other brands of steel-cut oats.That said, this is the best-tasting oatmeal I've had. It has a much more interesting texture than rolled oats, and a richer, nuttier taste than even the best rolled oats (like Silver Palate). Whereas I find that other oatmeals need butter, sugar, etc. to be palatable, I enjoy McCann's with just a few spices (such as cinnamon, allspice, nutmeg or mace) and some chopped nuts. As a result, it winds up being healthier for me just because I'm not adding so much fat and sugar.So, why only 4 stars? I've found the occasional oat husk in my oatmeal. Husks are unpleasant to eat, and stick in my teeth. It doesn't happen in every bowl, but I still wish they could thresh just a little more thoroughly.

This is the absolute best oatmeal!  It helped my husband lower his cholesterol significantly.  It takes awhile to cook - but I just cook a big pot of it once a week and then warm it up in the microwave each morning.

Takes a while to cook, but the wait is worth it!  Once you have this you won't want to go back to the old soggy stuff.  The cans are nice, but the boxes are a bit easier to give as little gifts to friends and family members who haven't yet had the pleasure of McCann's oats.

This is my favorite oatmeal.  It has great flavor and texture. I cook up a batch while we sit down for dinner and then keep it in the fridge for weekday breakfasts.  It heats up nicely when a little water is added before microwaving it.  I like to eat it with a little brown sugar, pecans, toasted wheat germ and a splash of cream.  YUM!  NOTE: when cooking it ahead of time, I have found it helpful to use an extra cup of water (5 c water to 1 c oats) so it does not get so thick and rubbery in the fridge.

column4: Bruce James Madden "a bear in the meadow"
column10: This is the best oatmeal I've ever had.  It's the real deal.  The best method of cooking it is to boil water the night before and put the oatmeal in the hot water overnight.  The next morning, add either water or cream and simmer on low for about 20 to 30 minutes.  Perfect texture!  I like it with berries, a little butter, and some real maple syrup.

column9: Product good, but packaging not stable.
column10: McCann's Steel Cut Irish Oatmeal is delicious.  But when it arrived the product packaging was so worn/crushed and labeling taped over, that they would not even stand up individually on the shelf.  Since it was ordered through Amazon, the disppointment in the condition of the packaging was a surprise.  But the good quality of the product was exactly what you expect through Amazon.
Great product. Terrible shipping. Three of the boxes had broken plastic windows and as result loose oatmeal was all over the place.

After reading all the reviews, and with a young toddler at home, I had to try this to see if it is indeed better - as it seems healthier.Well, it is great, and soaking it really cuts down on prep time.  The fiber is definitely apparent, as we found an obvious difference for our son the first couple of times we gave it too him (sorry to be graphic).We're not over-the-top in terms of eating only local, only whole foods, etc - but that is our magical (unattainable) ideal - so, we will continue to look for products like this, that are high quality, and good, real food (although in a box).Great Amazon price - great tasting - many steps above the boxed envelopes and cans of quaker we've come to accept as oatmeal.

A couple years ago, I tried to eat oatmeal regularly and bought a box of instant oatmeal. I stopped eating oatmeal as soon as I finished all of the packets in the box. I just did not like it.Last month, Consumer Reports rated Quaker Steel Cut Oats the top choice, so I began contemplating trying those (for whatever reason, they did not rate McCann's Steel Cut Oats). When I saw these on sale, I decided to try them, fearing that six 16-ounce boxes is a lot if I do not like them, but I am glad that I did. McCann's Steel Cut oatmeal is very tasty and I like the texture a lot. You cannot even compare this to instant oatmeal.I cooked mine in the programmable coffee maker. Before going to bed I put 1/2 cup of oats and a pinch of salt in the carafe, added water per cooking instructions on the box to the coffee maker's reservoir, and set the timer to start brewing the next day 30 minutes before I usually have breakfast. It all worked perfectly. I just scooped it out of the carafe into a bowl, added some blueberry preserves, and had a great breakfast.I would definitely recommend this product.

Regular rolled oatmeal is just downright boring compared to these steel cut oats.  These have a great texture and much better flavor than rolled oats.  It's become a bit of a tradition for Saturday breakfast to have these oats really done up right with a recipe from America's Test Kitchen that I found on the Valley Fig Grower's website "Perfect Oatmeal with Honey Fig Topping with Vanilla and Cinnamon."  These oats really don't need much help to be a filling, fueling, delicious breakfast, but that recipe just sends them way over the top.  I haven't tried any other brands of steel cut oats, and to be honest, I haven't seen any other brands in our local stores.

We first discovered steel cut oatmeal on a trip to northern Minnesota several years ago. My wife ordered oatmeal at a restaurant and I tried it since she was going on and on about how good it was. I wasn't a big fan of oatmeal, but it was really good. We recently discovered McCann's and it has become our regular breakfast. The prices at Amazon are great, the delivery prompt and the product is wonderful. Add brown sugar, a little butter and cinnamon to the oatmeal after it's in the bowl and white raisins to the oatmeal while it cooks. Fabulous!
This is the best oatmeal!! It has a nicer texture and much tastier. Not gloppy like regular oatmeal. It is whole grain and sticks with you all morning .

I am a huge fan of the McCANN'S steel-cut Irish oatmeal.I make it in batches (the entire box, adding 11 cups of water) in a kettle.  I then spoon it out into small containers and store individual servings in the refrigerator.  When I want a quick breakfast, I pull a serving out, plop it into a bowl, add a bit of water, and heat in the microwave for a bit over 2 minutes.  VOILA! The perfect, quick breakfast!I have found that McCANN's is the best steel-cut oatmeal out there.
This is so easy to prepare and taste so great. It is the best Oatmeal. Thesoak overnight method works so perfect. The seller is fantastic promptdelivery I will continue to order from this seller.

Once over the age of fifty, pants are to be worn up to the chestline, andoatmeal is a necessary part of one's diet.  Not so with McCann's steel cutoatmeal.  It should be a staple of diets for the young and old.  The slowcooking (25 minutes), kind tastes better than the rapid instant variety,plus sets the tempo of the day, punctuating the virtue of patience has itsreward.For weeks I tried to persuade Jewel to continue replenishing the slow cookMcCann Oatmeal, to no avail.  Inadvertantly I discovered this product might be procured through Amazon.Com at a significantly better price.  Be-cause I eat this stuff faithfully I put the purchase on a regular schedulefor a further saving.  All in all I claim to be satisfied with McCann.  Asto the art work on the container, which was a one time expense, it has norival.  I get the oatmeal in a box then pour that into the cool lookingcan.  Good stuff!Cheers  Dennis
I've wanted to try steel cut oats for years and I'm so glad I did. Yum!

column9: Can fix quickly & so worth trying
column10: I really don't care for the regular oatmeal.  It's too easy to cook too long and gets too mushy.  Sorta just grows in my mouth when I try to eat it.  These steel cut oats, taste sooo much better.  I don't follow the directions for cooking.  It's just me and I'm not going to go through that much trouble.  I just measure out about 6-8 teaspoonfuls, put in small pot and add enough water to cover the oats well.  I bring it to a boil, cover, remove from heat and let sit for about 3-5 minutes.  They are chewy and not mushy.  I enjoy them with sliced banana, apples & cinnamon (sliced apple, sprinkled with cinnamon & microwaved ~ 1 1/2 minutes), or a little agave, and maybe some milk (I use soy milk, due to milk allergy).  They are also good & add a nice texture when used in baking cookies, bread, brownies, etc.

column9: Takes a while to cook...but WORTH IT!!
column10: This oatmeal is much better for you than rhe flat stuff in store. It takes about 30 mins. to cook, and brown sugar and cinnamon...YUM. Also very high in fiber.

column4: Janet L. Helfand "with many years of life exp...
column10: I just love the consistency of McCann's steel cut oatmeal. I have started cooking it for several days worth and keep the remainder in a plastic container in the refrigerator. I then add frozen strawberries to it and nuke it hot. Add some yogurt and start off with a great breakfast with all the nutrition and fiber I need.I like buying it in the boxes so the oatmeal stays fresh.

column9: Excellent Product, Particularly If You Own a Pressure Cooker
column10: This superb oatmeal has a marvelous nutlike flavor and texture all of its own.  I am an oatmeal lover and eat it every season of  the year.  The McCann standard Steel Cut product is my only choice, and well worth the extra cost.  Its only drawback may be cooking time, if you prepare it with conventional pot on the stove techniques.  According to package instructions, you must boil it until it thickens, then simmer for 30 minutes.  Most of this can be avoided if you have a pressure cooker, which it use.  Cooking time with such a device is only 7-minutes.  I combine 3-1/2 cups of water with 1-cup of oats.  This makes 4 large servings, which I refrigerate and savor for several days.  Bon appetit.

column9: Not as good as Bob's Red Mill (price and taste)
column10: Any steel cut oats are better than than instant or rolled oats, but among steel cut oats, McCann's are not the best.  I enjoyed McCann's until I saw their prices increasing, which encouraged me to try other options.  Bob's Red Mill steel cut oats are just as satisfying, filling, and beneficial, but with a MUCH lower price.  In addition, Bob's won the world porridge competition last year.  So perhaps you will agree that they also have a better taste!

column9: John McCann's oats are my favorite
column10: I've tried all of the varieties of steel cut oats that I know to be available (with the exception of Hamlyn's pinhead oats which I only recently found -- on Amazon, of course!).  Some are not good, some are OK, but McCann's is consistently a great product!

This is good oatmeal, takes a while to cook but well worth the effort. It has a lot fewer hulls than a couple other brands I have tried so you aren't fishing them out of your bowl often.I've found that making a big pot and refrigerating it for later microwaving works really well. It keeps its firm texture and if anything tastes better.
Although these oats take a long time to cook, they are good in the end.  I like that there is no sugar added to them. I can add sweetener if I want, or fruit.

If you like your oatmeal with a lot of bite, you will love this! It is whole oats, cut into halves or thirds. Like brown rice, because it has the hull, it takes longer to cook. The directions are for about 4 cups of oatmeal, using 4 cups of water to 1 cup of oats. I use 2 cups of water to a slightly heaping 1/4 cup of oats, to make a single serving. I cook mine 20-25 minutes. Keep an eye on it and add bits of water if needed. Hope you enjoy yours as much as I enjoy mine!

These Oats are the best.  Hearty tasty awesome nutrition.  Great source of long lasting energy keeping your hunger satiated easily to lunch.  If you like food with less processing and more texture this is for you.  One thing to consider is cooking time but all you need do is look on the McCanns site for shortcuts or any food site for that matter.  The other thing to consider is that despite all the popularity of steel cut oats the rolled oats offer virtually the same nutritional value showing some difference in glycemic index.  But in my opinion these steel cut oats win out over rolled in flavor and texture.

I have been a fan of this oatmeal for three or four years now.These steel cut oats have the concistensy and taste that you will not find in other oatmeals. Plus Aamazon's prices beat the local stores. Definitely thumbs up.

Great quality oats, if you haven't tried them you only thought you knew what oatmeal was. I myself didn't like the oatmeal you buy in most grocers, like the quakes. These are totally different, good and hearty. Arrived well packaged covered with shrink wrap, they must have read some complaints about some shipments and started wrapping.All in all great quality product, not much in one box, but none the less fantastic!

Best oatmeal ever.I cook four portions (4 cups boiling water and 1 cup oatmeal - simmer for 30 minutes) and 4 breakfasts are ready to go.I add blueberries and half a sliced banana. For seasonings, for health, I add cinnamon, turmeric and ginger. Sometimes I throw in some almond slivers or peanut butter. Yum
This is the best cooked cereal I have ever tried. The nuggets of whole grain are surprisingly delicious.  Even though it takes a little longer to cook, it is well worth the effort!

Wonderfully rich in texture and filling for breakfast.  The price for the set is very reasonable as compared to the price at a retail store for the exact same product, except that the retail stores' Irish oatmeal is more nicely packaged in a tin can vs. a box---I don't need fancy packaging, just a good, healthy product and it is that!I joined the regular shipment club and receive add'l % discount which makes the cost less to the regular old fashioned oatmeal that we buy at the stores----and the Irish Oatmeal's healthier.
McCann's Steel Cut Irish Oatmeal is simply the best oatmeal you can buy. If you like oatmeal you owe it to yourself to try McCann's just once. And, what's more, it's good for your health!

My family loves this oatmeal. It is easier to make than you think, and it is so yummy, especially with some brown sugar sprinkled on. mmm! Sometimes, my 14 yr old will make a bowl of it for a snack and as soon as my 21 month old sees what he has, he'll go climbing into his lap begging for some from him. It is that good!

I use my electric rice cooker to make the McCann's steel cut oats.  I just add raisins or currents set it and go out for a walk or jog.  Its done in about 50 minutes.  You can make it as wet  or dry as you wish by regulating water or milk. By using electric cooker you don't have to watch it on stove  which takes about 35 minutes from the boil.
This oatmeal is the best money can buy.  Take a while to cook, but well worth it.  Nutty taste and crunchy to the pallet.  Highly recommended.
Recommend soaking night before preparing.  Very filling with a nutty firmer tecture than rolled oats.  Not as hungry before lunch after eating this for breakfast.
Other oatmeals just don't come close to McCann's. I live in Germany so I make sure that I always pick some up whenever I'm in the States...

It's porridge to me, but regardless what you call it these oats are 100% wholegrain and are suggested by people in the health/medical fields to be a vital part of our diet.  They tend to take a little longer to cook, but there is a suggestion for reducing the amount of time they take to cook.  If you like porridge (oatmeal), you should definitely buy this product.

I have been a fan of McCann's Irish Oatmeal for a couple of years.  The only problem was the cooking time - 30-45 minutes is a long time for folks on the go.  Since I have discovered that you can put it in a crockpot with cold water, and wake up to nice hot oatmeal in the morning, we enjoy it a lot more.  Try this, and you'll never eat the rolled oats (or ugh, the "instant")ever again.

I've always wanted to like hot cereal -- I've tried all kinds on many occasions (grits, rolled oats, wheat, etc.). Unfortunately, I've never been able to get past the texture . . . until now.  I picked this up at my local health food store and fell in love at first bite.  We've not tried the overnight method of preparation.  I bought a non-stick saucepan with a lid and cook it at low heat for about 40 minutes; with the non-stick finish, it only requires stirring once or twice in that time. My husband and I have been eating it for breakfast 4-6 days a week for almost a year now.
I really like this oatmeal better than rolled outs like Quaker.  I'm definitely buying again but next times gettng the instant.
This is far and away the best packaged oatmeal available.  I would just about kill to get it here in New Zealand and I'm chatting up a local importer to see if that can happen.

I love the texture of this more than the Quaker brand.  I cooked it and then in the last few minutes added cinnamon, chopped pecans, raisins and chopped dried apricots, and honey.  It was so yummy.  I made more than I could eat (this stuff is filling!) and so I brought it into work the next day...  same texture and flavor.  It kept very well over night.

Very tasty with good texture. It is clearly different from the rolled oats. I like the nutty flavor.It does take 30 to 40 minutes of constant attention if you start from scratch. I did not try the "soak over night, boil for 10 minutes" methods.
I have thouroughly enjoyed preparing and eating this product. Reasonably priced compared to grocery store prices.
Twice the fiber of regular oats and much tastier.  Once you try these you will never eat rolled oats again.Cheaper on Amazon than in the grocery store and you don't have to leave home!!
I really love this oatmeal for breakfast.  It has a very pleasant taste.

column9: Happy I found this here on Amazon
column10: My co-worker turned me onto Steel Cut Oatmeal and then I introduced it to my family.  Although I can find it in my local grocery store, it is at least twice the price.  My most recent order here on Amazon I paid an average of $2.14 a box using Subscribe and Save and an additional discount that was being offered.  Can't beat that deal and it keeps my cupboards stocked.For those that don't know what steel cut oatmeal is, I suggest trying it locally before buying in bulk. It is not your "usual" oatmeal. It is thicker, chewy and much more filing. A little definitely goes a long way! Additionally there are some wonderful overnight cooking recipes out there worth trying too.
I like this oatmeal.  It isn't mushy, it has a nice crunch. It's good for you and many stars eat this, as in Rachel Ray's back pages of what is in stars refrigerators.

The oatmeal is delicious, as I already knew it would be. But the notices I started getting from Amazon Subscriptions: "Product no longer available", "Product available on different date", etc..Hey, you've either got enough of the stuff for a steady supply (as in subscription service), or you don't. Don't sell me stuff under false pretense. I hate that "back ordered" crap.

While delicious - the long cooking oats do need to be soaked overnight before cooking in the morning.  A bit of a hassle and the long cooking version has no more fiber than the quick cooking version - next time, I'll go with the quick cooking.

I prefer steel-cut oats to the rolled oats.  My local grocery store stopped carrying the McCann's.  So I am glad to know that Amazon carries the product.  McCann's is great with milk, a bit of sugar, and fresh fruit.
It's the best since Aunt Patys Chicken Thyme. I thought that I would never taste this soup again! Don't stop making it! Please!It should be on tv commercials! Everyone should taste this soup!
Excellent and you can use chicken broth and rossiterie chicken instead of water and fresh chicken.  It is excellent.  The barley instead of rice makes it firm and not mushy. Try it.

This has to be one of the best bargains on green tea ever.  No, it's not a high-end gourmet tea - but it's not intended to be.  What it IS, is a terrific everyday green tea.  Mellow, slightly earthy, and very pleasant on the palate.  Second brewing yields a good cup, as well.  As with every Davidson' tea I've ordered, the quality of the leaves was wonderful, with very little dust, or stems.  It's obvious that they care about their product, and it shows. The origin is not stated, but who cares?  The tea is just fine.EDIT: I recently received my third order of this tea, and this batch was, quite simply, awful. The bag was mis-labeled, and is not green tea.  As we immediately store tea in sealed containers when it arrives, I do not have the original packaging, and can't return it (thank heavens it was inexpensive).  I have had great luck with Davidson's in the past, and assume that this was a fluke mistake, but, BE CAREFUL TO CHECK THE CONTENTS!

I like tea, in fact I like it a lot. I've had some good gunpowder green tea in the past from adagio as well as Twinnings and it is a beautiful thing. You put what look like little BBs of green tea into your cup or teapot, add the water, and you can see the tea practically explode into nearly full size leaves of tea (hence the name).Davidson's tea disappoints. The tea leaves really don't expand much which tells me they weren't really rolled the way gunpowder green tea is supposed to be. This tea also lacks flavor (at least compared to the other gunpowder green teas I've tried). I used the same amount to brew the same cup of tea I've been enjoying with Twinnigs and frankly the Davidson's version tasted more like hot water than green tea. This may be because the leaves aren't as compacted as a proper gunpowder green tea so the same tablespoon of tea now has less actual mass of tea leaves, it could be because this tea has a lower quality tea leaf in it, heck it could be because this is an old batch of tea for all I know.The point of this review is to say that this tea was a complete waste of money. I am sorry to say I paid for an entire pound of it. I will try it once or twice more, but if the results remain the same I will likely have to throw out the rest of the bag and that would just make me sad because it would mean that I've wasted both money and tea.I have added a photo of the actual tea I received (compare it to that in the original product photos and you'll see a huge difference). Mine is the one that does not look like it is magically hanging in the air and defying gravity.TL;DR version: Don't buy this tea. It isn't really gunpowder green tea and is not worth your money.

Perhaps I received a "bad" batch, because I found this tea to have a significant amount of dirt and debris.  I found sand-like grit, black and slightly metallic-looking  flecks (not in anyway related to the tea) and so far, one piece of some sort of fuzz-like fiber and some other cork-like debris.  I did not expect this.  As for the taste, it's okay; not our favorite gunpowder green, but for the price, the taste was acceptable.  Although, we felt it's a little too smokey, bitter and not enough "grassy".  I think this would be a good tea mixed with other things, such as mint.  A little of this goes a long way.  I'm not sure if I'd order this brand again, perhaps one more try sometime in the future.  Hope this helps!

This was my third shipment of gunpowder green. The first two shipments were great. This one was worse than horrible. I had to throw it all away. I think they got it confused with the rotten, moldy tobacco.

I'm not a connoisseur of fine teas.  But, I do enjoy my tea, and gunpowder green has been a favorite of mine.  A big problem, though, is trying to find it.  There is a tea store near by that is very expensive.  If you buy 2 oz or more, it's $4.00 an oz.  Too expensive.  I finally found a couple of health food stores where it ranges in price from about 70 to 85 cents an oz, but it is such a hassle to drive there; and too many times they're out.  I've found it on-line, but the shipping costs haven't made it such a good deal.Well, with the "subscription" purchase, this is a great deal.  It's cheaper than anywhere I've found it, at $10.20 a pound or less than 64 cents an oz.  And I love that 48 hrs after placing the order, the post office delivered it to my house.So, the big test, then, is how is the tea?  Well, like I said, I'm not a connoisseur, but I do enjoy Davidson's Gunpowder Green.  It's as good as any that I've bought.  Since the stores where I have been buying it are anywhere from 10 to 25 miles away, and not even near anywhere I normally go, I can say that I have found my new source for tea.  I would recommend it if you're looking for a great deal on a very good tea.

column9: Make sure you like gunpowder tea first!
column10: Caution: I had never tried gunpowder tea before ordering.  My wife refused more than the first tiny sip of this tea.  I forced myself to try brewing this several different ways before giving up.  We consider it completely unpalatable.  This is very different from a normal mild green tea.  Yes, it is very smoky and somewhat oily; a very powerful tea.

It's okay.It's doesn't suck.It's the worst gunpowder green I've had.I drink a lot of tea.I like green tea even if it's bitter or grassy.I have a mustache.It doesn't expand the way gunpowder is supposed to BLAM!It's not wrapped properly.I'm not talking about the packaging.The packaging is GREAT!The price is okay....probably too high for the quality.They ship it lightning quick.THE TEA:flavors: bitter, acidic, slightly fruity, very smokey (like the hibiscus of green teas), not pleasant aftertaste.mouthfeel: oily, thick, darklook: bright green - almost radioactive green with a heavy brew, light green and kind of smokey with a light brew.I've had very good gunpowder before. This is not very good.If you're a tea pounder (guzzleguzzle), get it.Otherwise, stay away.

column9: You get what you pay for, and more.
column10: This is pretty good tea! It's not the best gunpowder green that I've ever had, but it is certainly a bang for your buck for the price. Someone previously said that it's a good "everyday" tea, and I 100% agree with this. It's good, it's almost great, but it's not a tea that I would anticipate curling up with in a blanket on a cold evening and savoring the experience. It's just a good cup of organic green tea. I'm still so pleased with it and the price--you can't beat that! Buy it!

This used to be really good tea. For two years we drank it and really liked it.The last two batches have had some kind of sludge that comes off it, so much so that it cloggs the filter on the coffee maker I use to brew it. (The same one I've used for years.)It would be good if we had a way to contact the manufacturer so we could alert them that their good product just went bad, from one month to the next.Hope this helps.Frustrated Green Tea Guy

column9: It was good tea before they switched supplier
column10: I had been subscribing to this gun powder tea; it was very good tea given the price. But now it is terrible, I am not sure I can even call them gun powder tea anymore - it doesn't look like it, doesn't smell like it either. Time to find an alternative.

This tea is an awesome value, and tastes pretty good for the price. It is slightly smokey, like a gunpowder should be, but still grassy to remind you that it is still a green tea. The leaves can be brewed at least three times. I love this tea, and the price.

Product was as described, and arrive quickly and in excellent condition.  Flavor is good, but not great, a little more smoky and less grassy than I would have preferred.  Overall a good product, at a great price!!!

Awesome value AND an awesome tea.  Much more robust than a traditional green tea, as gunpowder teas ought to be, with a slightly smokey/toasty flavor.  I dunno what 'grade' it is, but what matters is that it's delicious.  Don't hesitate.

I've bought this tea before and was quite happy with it. This past purchase though,(and I bought two 16 oz bags) rather than getting gunpowder, tightly rolled balls, all the leaves had unfurled -- disappointing to say the least. Still, tasted fine -- but I wanted gunpowder.

I "subscribed" to this gunpowder green tea. The first pound was pretty good, and was what one expects from "gunpowder" tea... each leaf was tightly rolled into a ball as it is suppose to be. The second pound that I received does not look like gunpowder tea at all. Simply hard little blobs of nearly flavorless tea. NOT the same quality as the first pound. This all sounds like tea-snobbery, I know. But when buying loose tea, one should be able to expect consistency. I am going to cancel my subscription. Unfortunate- I would have been a customer for life.

I'm by no means a connoisseur, but I am very pleased with this tea, and the price is unbelievably good for organic green tea.It's gunpowder, so it's in nice little tightly packet "pellets" that are nice and green and they smell very fresh.The flavor is subtle, and what I expect from unflavored green tea. I always steep about a gallon with fresh ginger and drink it cold.I will definitely buy this product again.

This is the worse tea than any fresh green tea. Indeed it was "Green" tea by the time they are produced. Poor storing condition, not in the sealed enviroment, exposed extensively in the air make this tea lost all the flavor. Don't know how old of the tea is but in my experience it's at least 3-5 years old in loose condition in the air. Junk.
I have been drinking gunpowder green tea for quite a few years, and this tea is perhaps the most bitter that I've had.

I don't see how I lived without this!I let my coffee addiction subside (one cup a day but every day) and I needed some kind of caffeine alternative. What better than green tea!?Get your caffeine AND your anti-oxidants!I used one of those ball infusers and then a plastic one until I finally got a Finum stainless basket.... perfect combination... I put a cm of tea in the bottom and it blossoms up 20x by the time it's infused!I let it steep and steep and steep and make a nice strong tea! It's an acquired taste but delicious (and powerful!)My buddy says he doesn't like gunpowder teas generally -- I think he must have been traumatized by smoke-flavoured foods as a child. The tea IS smoky but not terribly or undesirably so. I love it.People who mix it with honey or milk etc can probably make a really lovely tasting green tea out of it... mellow and tasty.The beauty of this is that you just get so much tea for such a good price! Quality, delish, does the job.Can't recommend it enough.I'm hooked for life.
The shipment I received had soooooo much powder it made the tea undrikable.  Looks like all the great reviews are older.  Very dissapointed!

column9: Not a good gunpowder green.  Buy the Green Boxed Gunpowder Instead!
column10: So I had just finished my third 1KG box of China Green Tea Special Gunpowder 1 Kilo (1000grams or 35.27 Oz) Guaranteed Authenticity in the last year and decided to see if this Davidson's was any better.  To my dismay, it's not, but it sure costs a lot more!  After four brews with the Davidson's, I'm very dissatisfied.First off, the color of the gunpowder pellets are no different between samples, but the Davidson's uses bigger pellets, meaning bigger, older fan leaves.  The Temple of Heaven (ToH) gunpowder green uses smaller leaves, so when you brew there appear to be many more leaves because there are.  The Davidson's often has several leaves and their attached stem rolled up into a single pellet.  The Davidson's also has significantly more dirt, dust, and loose stems in the package.  In fact, it looks like I got the bottom of the barrel.****  Your Quality Control Is Terrible, Davidson!  ****The idea that it is organic should have some impact on the flavor, but the Davidson's is more bitter, and the tea is orange/yellow after 3 minutes of brewing in RO filtered water heated to 170-180F in a French press.  The ToH tea is a greenish yellow, and has a better flavor with less bitterness.Overall, I am very unhappy with my Davidson's purchase.  The ToH gunpowder green is better quality for less than half the price!!!When compared to the other gunpowder green tea options available, Davidson's Gunpowder Green Tea is a 2 star gunpowder green tea for flavor that loses a star for poor pricing and very poor quality control.

column9: Ruins the reputation of gunpowder teas
column10: I'm a student who regularly drinks tea my father brings back from China. Gunpowder (tie guan yin) tea has been one of my favorites, particularly for its light, aromatic flavor.I bought a bag of Davidson's after finishing the gunpowder tea from China, impressed by its low price - as comparatively, it does indeed have a great price.While the signature brisk top note of the tea is detectable, it is quickly washed out by a tannic, bitter aftertaste that some reviewers called "earthy." In my palate's opinion, that "earthiness" is NOT a mark of quality. And though it's of equal degree, the bitterness of this tea does not contain the nuanced richness of dark-roast coffee that makes the latter pleasurable.I would recommend this tea only if you are buying primarily for price - me, I just want something caffeinated that's not coffee - or if you enjoy the dull bitterness of 7/11 coffee.

column9: First order excellent, second order awful!
column10: My first order was wonderful: fresh, tight pellets w/ a lovely sheen, very flavorful.  My second order was terrible:  stale, dry, crumbly, little flavor.  Don't know whether to risk a third...

This is the first 'gunpowder' tea I've tried, so I don't know if I am not crazy about the type in general or Davidson's brand, but the tea has a slightly bitter after-taste which I don't like. I often brew from China sourced sampler sets, which I've found to have a slightly sweeter, smoother taste. Still looking for a reasonably priced standby for green tea.
I didn't care for this tea.  The taste had an ashtray undertone.  I have bought other brands and loved them.  Not my cup of tea :(

I was hoping that it would taste at least as good as the lowest cost brand in the super market. I was disappointed. It has a earthy (dirt) after taste. The only way I could drink it is to use very little.

column9: Makes a good strong green tea
column10: This will make a knock you socks off iced green tea! I agree with another poster that it needs something else such as mint lime or lemon.
This is great full flavored gunpowder, be sure to follow the brewing directions - oversteeping should never be permitted. Well worth the price for organic tea - love it.
This Gunpowder is Ok. Not the best, not the worst. You get what you pay for...
First time order, cannot believe this was called "green tea". Very bad quality, do not waste your time and money.
Wooh. Man, it is bitter, perhaps the most bitter green tea I have had. But, I guess thats what gunpowder tea is all about.

I bought this tea, thinking it was a great value, but I discovered it's weaker than more expensive teas. I have to use more tea to get the taste of more expensive teas. Therefore, it's not as cheap as I thought and costs close to the same as expensive teas because I have to use more tea to make a pot. It's an okay tea, but not the deal I was hoping for.

Excellent green tea.  It has the perfect scent, color, taste, everything.  We've been drinking this and the English Breakfast Blend for about a year now and love both of these.  They both make incredible hot or iced tea.

column9: There might be better Gunpowder out there but I love it!
column10: This Gunpowder arrived fresh and it is an excellent value. It also makes very good iced tea.. I drink Gunpowder green tea in the morning, Sencha in the afternoon, and Genmaicha in the evening...all from Davidson's and I am very satisfied with all three!

column9: Genuine finely chopped green over dehydrated tea this time around.
column10: My first batch of Davidson Gunpowder green tea looked like the original images posted in this listing.  They were rolled tea leaves, but not as tightly as competitors.  Put them in water and the leaves would unfurl and reveal nice complete long leaves.  The taste was good.  For the price I thought it was great.  However the green tea I received around a month ago arrived and they didn't bother trying to roll the tea leaves at all, they simply diced up the leaves into small pieces and completely removed all moisture from the leaves to the point that they are so dry you can rub them easily between your fingers and the leaves crumble to a fine dust. There is nothing gun powder about this tea at all anymore.  Davidson needs to get this under control.  It wasn't worth the hassle of sending back so I am stuck with a pound of this barely palatable tea.  I've purchased lots of Davidson teas over the last year and had been extremely happy with all of them with the exception of this latest batch of Gunpowder green tea.  They should either bring back the Gunpowder that we expect and paid for or simply stop selling this inferior stuff that barely passes for tea.

I love this tea, at $11 a pound delivered, it's a bargain.
