I can afford to make it good and strong, and usually do 3 brewings from a single pot (custom I learned in West Africa) I also take a cue from my Peace Corps stay in Senegal, where they add mint to the pot (tho I avoid the traditional sugar) As far as I can tell this "gunpowder" green is the same stuff they used in Africa. so the nostalgia factor is a big part of the experience, especially late at night during Ramadan.
I went looking for cheap bulk tea, and I found it. Quality is pretty good - if you over-steep it, it gets a little bitter. A good choice for some every-day tea.

I just brewed my first pitcher of this tea using the Mr. Coffee device, and I must say it has a great flavor and a little bit goes a long way. I easily brewed 3 quarts with three tablespoons of bulk tea. My 16 ounce bag will last for a while.

column9: Least favorite. Good for iced tea only.
column10: Makes a mildly refreshing iced tea for outside in hot weather, but it's not pleasant for drinking hot. If I knew someone who likes this tea, I would give it to them. We won't buy again.

column9: Medium Quality Tea, Decent Value, Goes A Long Way
column10: This is a medium quality tea at best, at a decent price.  Tea from Chinese tea specialty houses such as Tenren is far better, but costs approximately four times as much.  Twinings Gunpower Green (which I haven't tasted) is selling for a higher price than the Davidson, and Twinings tea, in my experience, is not high quality tea.  It has better reviews than this tea as well.Twinings Green Gunpowder Tea, Loose Tea, 3.53-Ounce Tins (Pack of 6)Gunpowder used to be rolled by hand into the little gunpowder pellets, but today almost all gunpowder is made on a machine.  Because it is rolled into the pellets, you may want to use a little less in your measure for the strength of tea you prefer.  In other words, because it is compressed, there is more tea per teaspoonful, and you may find the tea stronger than you expected.  I do like a strong cup of tea, and the slightly smoky quality of this tea is pleasant when brewed on the strong side.Similarly, a strong cup of gunpowder probably has a higher caffeine level than a comparable cup of other green tea.  This is anecdotal, partially based on the compressed nature of the tea and partially based on many mornings of research.Historical Note: the tea that was dumped into the Boston harbor by the patriots in 1773 was probably gunpowder tea.A suggestion: a pound of this tea will last you a very long time, and will be a bit stale when you are done.  Suggestion:  put half of more in the freezer and you will have fresher tea when the first half of the bag is done.  I have had my bag about six months and wish I had done that!Tiger

column9: Smokey, Good Flavor, and best of all CHEAP
column10: I'll be the first to admit I'm no tea connoisseur. I'm a college student who likes drinking 3-4 cups of tea a tea, usually green tea. I'm used to buying in tea bags but over the last 6 months I've been buying from Teavana and Kungaloosh, which in the end got a bit expensive. So I decided to give this tea a try based on the positive reviews here.First off, let me point out that this is a LOT of tea for the price. I couldn't even believe it when the package arrived. It doesn't fit into one of my Teavana airtight containers, I had to put the rest in a small tupperware container. So you get incredible value. On top of that, you get TWO infusions, and the great flavor is still there on the second infusion.Next, let me address the quality: It's definitely got a smokey taste. You're gonna see particles floating around. It's not the cleanest tea in the world. But, it's green tea! Every green tea I've tasted has tasted similar to this. It's got a strong taste, a bit bitter, but a clean aftertaste unlike some tea bags. So I'll definitely come back and get another bag, you know, whenever this huge order runs out. Probably in 3 or 4 months.Overall, it's a great bargain for a good tea.

column9: Great value for some good tea!!
column10: The bag I received was a very good batch! You can tell it was very fresh, and it makes some darn good tea. The leaves smell slightly sweet but mostly grassy. It brews in a light-greenish tint, which is a good sign of its quality. No 'other particles' in the bag, just leaves as expected. All-in-all, a great value for the 9$ I paid for it.This isn't AMAZING tea, but it is definitely worth 10 or 12 bucks as a simple everyday tea that is great for you.

I may not be the tea connoisseur that some of my fellow reviewers are, yet be that as it may, I find this a fantastic green tea. It's got a mild, mineral flavor with a distinct herbaceous headiness while remaining characteristically "green". I like to brew mine extra strong to emphasize bitter notes. Davidson's packaging is fantastic: opaque outer paper and a moisture-resistant inner liner helps preserve the tea over time.And thanks to Amazon's Subscription program, I get this tea delivered monthly. I've even had to double my order I go through so much!

column9: Some of the best green tea out there
column10: Hello,I bought this tea on a whim after reading about "Gunpowder" green tea on another site.  I was intrigued by the description and the name and thought I would see if Amazon carried it.  The minute it came in I was immediately impressed with the quality of the bag, Davidson's bags are resealable and keep the tea fresh for a long time.  I brewed my first kettle and immediately knew I would continue bying both this tea and this brand.  This tea is very flavorful and works well both hot and cold.I have purchased Davisdon's tea multiple times since the original purchase and have alsways been impresses with the quality.  Highly recommend this brand and this style.Mac S.

This is, by far, one of the better organic Gunpowder teas we've tried!!  Believe me, we've tried plenty of them.  The taste is smooth & not bitter, like many Gunpowder teas we've tried.  The price of Davidson'ss tea is fantastic & we'll continue to buy it on a regular basis.

Bought it as a gift for my tea-loving wife based on the 35 five star ratings on Amazon.  MISTAKE.  This is undrinkable and tastes so earthy, it's like dirt.  It also has a severely smoky smell and almost ash-like aftertaste.  We'll probably use it to compost and that's about it.

This is an unbelievable deal. For the same price as the mystery cube o' leaves you find at Asian grocers or internet vendors, you get a full pound of Organic leaves. The Gunpowder Green has a hint of citrus, a hint of nuttiness, but most importantly, it tastes clean. You don't have to worry about undoing the health benefits of green tea with heavy metals or other pollutants in non-organic products. The 16 Oz. bag lasted me over two months with several strong cups per day. I highly recommend this tea.

column9: Nothing robust, smokey, or toasty about it
column10: I'd never had gunpowder tea, and the reviews led me to believe this was something special.  Well, the tea I received tastes like green tea. Period. It's drinkable, but I personally like a bit of extra flavor to my morning tea.  Anyway it will last a long time, maybe too long.

This is not a great green tea. It contains a lot of dirt / powder that goes through the tea ball and makes the cup look like a suspension rather than an infusion. The taste is weak so one has to use a lot of this tea, which results in an over-caffeinated beverage. Finally, even the color of the tea itself is on the yellow side rather than green. Not a satisfactory purchase!

Bought this one because there are some positive reveiws, but I got to say I really hate the ordor of this product. When you brew it, it smells like an old, musty carpet. Awuful, very very bad, and I can't even finish my first cup. this is definitely the worst tea I have ever tried. Pushes my bad experiences on horrible teas to a whole new level. Totally waste of money.

I decided to try Davidson's teas, both this gunpowder green and the irish breakfast.  Both were a good price for a pound of organic tea and moreso, to my happy surprise, the quality of the tea is superb.  Not the best that money can buy but far, far better than I expected in this price range.  Both teas have leaves that are nicely dried, with care, mostly whole (as opposed to all broken up), and the Gunpowder especially has a lovely luster to it.  Well done, Davidson's!

column9: Wonderful flavor and aroma, beautiful unfurling
column10: I cannot believe how much I enjoy this green tea. I typically despise green tea because the only way I have ever had it before was through a plastic bottle made by some large company or in tea bags, also from a large company. It was always a disappointment. However, the flavor in this tea is wonderful. I actually felt something in my stomach while I was drinking this, it seemed to calm it a bit because I was hungry. Maybe it was the placebo effect because I have read so much about green tea and I want it to do something good for me, but overall despite the supposed health benefits it was actually just good to drink with some honey.Sadly I don't have proper honey, just highly filtered and processed honey, but it still helped mellow the tea out just a little bit, which it needed because I steeped way too much the first time I tried it. That is in fact my only complaint, that I don't know what I'm doing, so it's going to take some trial and error to determine the amounts that I enjoy the most. I used a full tablespoon, which when you see the leaves unfurl you begin to realize is way more than necessary, and then you drink it! It was very strong, but still excellent.

The vacuum pack bag is great. The tea is blah. There is a hint of tea flavor. There are many whole leaves, but also quite a few small bits of leaf. I didn't find any stems in my first cup of the tea (brewed directly in the cup without a filter).

column9: steep for 1.5 minutes and it's not bad
column10: Steep for 3 minutes and it tastes ghastly. I just tried at one and a half minutes though and it tastes much better.
The price on this tea is awesome and it's organic and great tasting to boot. I put this in an airtight container and it lasts for a very long time. I doubt I'll ever go back to tea bags again.

Gunpowder grade green tea is often iffy in quality, but this green tea is TOP NOTCH! I would have to say this is the highest quality gunpowder green tea i have ever got, will order again from Davidson's no doubt!
Clean, normal "gunpowder" shape.  Tast good, no strange smell.But never expect this one has the quality as the $50/lb one.  The price is $13/lb, and it worth but only worth this price.

I use this green tea to make Kombacha. The flavor and consistency of it is always great. I can count on this tea to be perfect every time I make it. The flavor and texture of the tea as a hot drink is delicious. This tea is consistently good.
This is anything but the sickley taste I have grown used to in green tea.  It is robust, tasty and aromatic.  I recommend it.

Im not a big fan of paying HIGH AMOUNTS of hard earned money for fancy dried up leaves (SORRY TEAVANA) but i am however a tea lover.This green tea is great. i've probably brewed through about 32-48 oz of tea with this tea. it is great. its not super high quality, so if you dont brew it just right you wont get that nice green hue to your tea, which i love so much. BUT i have been able to get the right color and flavor with the right temps and steep time. i give this a great rating, plus they shipped it quickly and it arrived with no damage or anything. A+

I recently started drinking loose tea from a local chain, and I really like it. I tend to really enjoy the straight unsweetened slightly bitter green teas of the stronger varieties, and I've had a gunpowder tea before that I really enjoyed. However, I wanted to try a less expensive variety, as I felt guilty when I used a five or ten dollar an ounce tea as the liquid base of a smoothie. And who knows - I just might get lucky and it'll be great tea. This is not a great tea. It's a little too strong, bitter, unsubtle, and the only word I can think of to describe the taste is "dusty". These qualities make it the perfect green tea base for a fruit smoothie! The tea flavor really comes through, unlike the finer teas. Yum.

column9: Well... it is tea and it's cheap.
column10: This is my first bag of this tea (got it about a month ago). I brew it with hot-not-boiling water (bring to boil; let sit a couple of minutes before using); three teaspoons of dry tea in a regular-size ceramic teapot. I drink it hot and w/o sugar. My impressions so far, real quick:Good:- It is undoubtedly tea.- It's inexpensive.Bad:- Tastes like mouldy cardboard.Questionable:- Is it really green? It doesn't look very green, and, when brewed, it results in a light-brown liquid that is kind of like a weak regular tea.Bottomline: I don't think I will reorder; two stars.11/18/2011: I did reorder, so let's  bump up the starrage. I just don't think of it as tea. More like a generic drink. To make it more palatable, I drink it hot and add orange peel to it.
Superior product.  I love the taste of this tea.  We use less of this brand than we have of other, more expensive gunpowder green teas.  Love it!!!
This was my second purchase of this tea. I found the quality higher than the name brand I had been drinking with far less dust and debris. Its a bit stronger too, requiring less per pot.

I tasted many teas and read dozens of reviews and product descriptions before I settled on this tea. Most product descriptions don't tell the truth.Pros: I was pleasantly surprised at the taste of this tea. DON'T OVER BREW or it will be bitter! JUST 2 minutes is perfect. I can get three pots out of this tea but I let the last pot sit at least 10 minutes. I've ordered a second time and will order this again. This is now my daily tea.However...Cons: I read that if you gently press the little balls of rolled "Gunpowder" tea, they should give and be pliable. This is the sign of fresh tea. This tea crumbles, a sure sign of older tea, stored who-knows-how-long. I would like to get a fresh shipment but I also like the reasonable price of this old tea. I guess that is the trade-off. If someone knows where I can get fresher "Gunpowder" tea at a good price, please let me know.

I drink about a quart of green tea every day, so the cost can really rise if I were to purchase a nice Chinese tea.  I purchased this tea primarily for its price.  I brewed it as I usually do, 180 degrees and 1 tsp of tea to 8 oz of water, and wow do these leaves really expand.  I usually leave the leaves in the bottom of my water bottle or glass, but with this tea you end up with 50% of your glass occupied by the leaves.  You really have to use a diffuser or pot.  The brewed tea is quite cloudy which is a little disappointing.  The taste is not particularly strong or very herby, but it is not unpleasant either.  For the price, this tea is tough to beat, but it is definitely a quantity over quality tea.

If you want to drink a green tea, gunpowder is the one I consider with the best flavor.  The value here is great, and the tea perfect.  I'd suggest you not brew it for longer than 3 minutes and do not use boiling water, and the taste will be perfect.  Water at about 180 appears to be best, hotter or longer times will just make the tea bitter.  Enjoy.

column9: a little goes a long way
column10: Good value, I am not a tea expert, it swells a bunch, fills up the tea infuser. put less than you think you need in the infuser. would buy again.

This isn't tea of a super high quality, but it's superior to anything that you'll find in a teabag (and much cheaper, also).  For the price, you really do get a large quantity of tea.  I've had this for a month now, and I probably drink this particular tea maybe 4 times a week, and I still really haven't made too much of a dent on the bag.The flavor's robust and 'smokey', it's not very delicate or fragrant,  but still tasty nonetheless.
The tea was good quility and came very quickly. I have ordered alot of gun powder tea on line and this was the best experiance I have had with it.
Just a great tasting tea at a good price.  Sorry, no sophisticated palate here, I just know what I like.  This is pretty hard to beat.

I am very impressed with this green tea. I used to work in a specialty coffee and tea shop and I know for a fact that they spent much more for tea of this same caliber. The bag does seal tight and I just do my best to get all the air out and it stays fresh. I was a bit skeptical given the price, but I will be singing the praises of Davidson's Tea to anyone who will listen!
I've seen some bad reviews on this tea,but this is a good tea at a good price; I've had worse teas at much higher prices

column9: The grade tea is good for the price
column10: I found that the grade of tea is good for the price. I has a nice flavor and also blends with other green tea as I like a little stronger flavor on the loose leaf tea.

column9: Good Everyday Tea for the Price
column10: For the price, this is a great tea for me to get my morning going. I usually get 3 brews from one serving. I like my green tea fairly strong, so I use more than the recommended 1 tsp leaves per 8 oz of water. Don't over-infuse because (as you probably know if you're ordering bulk green tea), it'll become bitter.I use this tea with the Aladdin Tea 12-Ounce Infuser Mug, Blue, a great product for keeping yourself in reach of hot tea all day long.

column9: Excellent Tea The first time, less quality on the second order
column10: The more I drink of this tea the more I like it.  It compares with teas twice it price. (On the first order.)I am on my second order of this tea, the flavor is just as good but I seems to have come from the bottom of the barrel.  Instead of the Gunpowder Tea I was expecting, it is more a powder like it has been crushed and none of the leaves are whole.  Though this does not impact the flavor it does make cleaning out the tea ball a lot harder.

Great deal - especially w/ the 'subscribe and save' option.  Clean, not as smoky as alternatives - no ashtray aroma:)  We place in clear glass jar upon receipt - always (we have ordered several times) clean, no dust/debris.

Echoing what many of the other reviewers have written, this is an eminently drinkable tea and a great bargain as well.I normally gravitate to more peculiar teas (lapsang souchong is by far my favorite) but I developed a taste for gunpowder green tea after trying it at a friend's apartment.  Most tea shops will sell "pearls" of this tea for upwards of $9.00/oz and so I was skeptical when I saw a pound of this tea for such a cheap price.This tea is everything that a gunpoweder green tea should be: a bit dry, a bit earthy, and not too acidic.  It tends to brew a bit strong, so I usually brew 2 cups out of 1 & 1/2 teaspoons of this tea which makes it a perfect, if not too fancy, everyday tea.As an added bonus, the leaves are absolutely huge (uncut) when they unfurl which makes cleaning them out of a tea infuser to be an absolute snap.  One major drawback of other loose teas is the small leaves which necessitate disassembling the infusing and/or rinsing the filter a few times to clear them out.  The leaves left behind from this blend can be easily, and neatly, removed by hand.  Awesome all around!

column9: Great, high quality green tea at an affordable price... and YUMMY!
column10: This tea is great! Nowhere else can you get one POUND of high quality tea for $12 shipped to your door. I used to pay $30 for a sub-par product, but no more!You know it's a fresh, high quality tea when it takes 3-6 days for a fresh made batch to start to stink in the fridge. I used to drink Lipton every day, and it takes between 1 and 2 weeks for Lipton (a lower quality tea) to 'go bad' in the fridge. If you know anything about tea, you will know that the more 'processed' and less 'natural' it is, the longer it stays fresh. Davidson's starts to smell anywhere between 3-6 days for me.Highly recommended, you'll love it!

I have been a green tea drinker for many years.  I love gunpowder because you get the whole leaf and not bits and pieces.  This is high quality tea.  I I read a review saying this tea was bitter; I completely disagree.  Normally you get the bitterness when you steep it too long or when you squeeze out the leaves after steeping.  I have done both with this tea and still get no bitterness.  I also use less of this tea than normal.  The gunpowder expands so much you only need a large pinch per glass.I've paid much more at health food stores and Asian markets, but haven't come across anything that can beat this stuff.  Proceed with confidence.  I bet you'll give it 5 stars, too.

Love that this is high quality tea rolled up in little pellets before opened up in hot water.  The taste of gunpowder green tea is a little stronger than we are used too, so we are trying a more conventional green tea next time.

I made it too strong to start; it tasted like good soil (dirt). column9: not just for deli -- use to make POT ROAST (really!!!)
column10: First off, these are great on sandwiches or in salads, or on pizza.But, thanks to Myron (google "amazing beef" for the original recipe), we can also make an extraordinarily fine pot roast with them.  Sounds disgusting, right?  I know -- but we tried it once with misgivings and have since made it countless times with total delight.  Unbelievable, but true.Here's my adaptation of Myron's recipe:1  Scrape and then cut into four long spears each of two huge Idaho baking potatoes (or substitute potatoes of your choice, enough for four servings).2  Scrape and leave whole 6-8 large fresh carrots (frozen will not make a good substitute, neither will "baby" carrots).3  Peel and leave whole 4 small sweet onions (but leave just a little on the root, to hold them together during cooking -- can also substitute onions of your choice, enough for 4 servings, but best to leave whole if possible).4  Take a small chunk of raw beef (if you're watching your calories, try about 1.5-2 pounds of a top sirloin roast; otherwise any pot-roast-suitable cut will be fine) and remove from wrappings.5  Layer vegetables on the bottom of a 5, 6 or 7 quart crock-pot, and put meat on top (be sure top can still cover with a proper seal).6  Upend over all of it the contents of a jar of these wonderful pepperoncini WITH THE JUICE, cover, and set on low for 10-12 or high for at least 6 hours (or start on high and then switch to low).  DO NOT REMOVE THE COVER before done.  It doesn't matter if it cooks too long; just be sure it's at least 6 hours on high or almost 10 on low).VOILA -- an extraordinarily fine pot roast, suitable for company.  Can leave on keep-warm setting for literally 24 hours thereafter and serve seconds the next night without having to reheat.  Or even firsts -- the whole thing actually tastes better the second day.ALTERNATIVE USE FOR LEFTOVERS (from Myron):  Slice cold beef (I warm it up briefly in the microwave with the peppers, so that they're steaming hot, then drain so as not to make the bread too soggy);serve on high-quality crusty bread, topped with fresh sliced tomatoes and then the cooked peppers.  My favorite sandwich ever!!These pepperoncini are fabulous; we keep jars in the pantry so as to have them available at a moment's notice.  You may find you use them far more often than expected and are very glad to have them!!P.S.  Use the remaining broth from the pot roast as the cooking water for whole-wheat couscous or brown rice, and add the peppers -- divine.
