I compared this to the Creole seasoned nuts from Peanut Shop of Williamsburg (also called "Mardi Gras" flavor nuts), and the Williamsburg nuts have a much tastier seasoning. These nuts are good nuts and roasted well, but I don't find the seasoning appetizing. There's a lot of herbal flavor, possibly oregano and bay leaf, which overpower the onion and garlic flavors. There's very little heat. It's not unlike the flavors in a gumbo, which are good flavors, but not so great with peanuts, in my opinion. The salt level is high, but I like salt.

Earl Grey is supposedly the second most popular tea in the world. Traditionally Earl Grey is created from a blend of black teas, usually Chinese and Indian teas, sometimes with a smokey flavor, and scented with the citrus fruit bergamot. Earl Grey tea has an interesting history. Legend has it that the first tea scented with bergamot oil was presented to Lord Grey from a Chinese mandarin whose son was saved from drowning by one of Lord Grey's men. Twinings and Jacksons of Piccadilly both claim to be the first to have commercially blended this tea.Tazo shows considerable expertise in the blend of this top quality tea. The black teas utilized are as the box states  "the worlds most sought after teas from the high-elevation gardens of Nuwara Eliya, Uva and Dimbula in Sri Lanka and Assam in northeast India."  They provide the perfect complement to the strong bergamot essence in this blend. The fragrance is powerfully floral, in particular lavender, citrus, and the woodsy-malt scent of premium black tea. The flavor of this splendid potion is rich and perfumed. A tasty, sensual delight!Earl Grey is traditionally served black, sometimes with lemon. I prefer it with cream. On a warning note, if you keep this tea in the cupboard for too long it will get old--the taste becomes very thin and harsh. Brew it from fresh teabags and you won't be disappointed!From The Book of Tea by Okakura:"There is a subtle charm in the taste of tea which makes it irresistible and capable of idealization."

This is actually my favorite flavor.  I have it on recurring order very 5 months.  In betweent those months I have different flavors coming.  The price is much cheaper than if I purchased at the grocery store.
I am very impressed with the way these taste!  They taste just like a sour (in a good way) fruit roll-up.  You don't taste the fruit that it's suppose to be, but they still taste wonderful!

In a relatively few words I will say that I love sardines and a happy with my purchase. It seems that in recent years while the prices have soared finding top quality sardines on the market shelf is increasingly difficult. King Oscar is the best I have tried and the price through Amazon is really right. When I have consumed this dozen I will order another.

From what I can tell, King Oscar Mediterranean sardines are now distributed by Bumble Bee, packed in Poland, and inferior in quality when compared to the Brislings from the near-arctic icy waters of the Norwegian fjords.

The sardines in this two-layer can are half the size of those packed in one layer (obviously) and for whatever reason, I find them a lot tastier and more tender then the larger sardines. My local grocery sells them for around $3.50/can, which is not much more than tis deal. However... I buy mine in a certain big-box store when they come in four can packs for $8, which comes to only $2/can. At that price they're a pretty good deal. But even at $3/can they're not bad.

I really love the Mocafe frappes.  We always have between 6 and 7 flavors to make lots of smoothies, with or without fruit... I really don't like the vanilla much, though.  I was surprised it doesn't really have much of a vanilla flavor.  I taste mostly the powdered milk flavor.  I think the white chocolate is better and creamier and I use that one instead of vanilla. (Honeydew is by far my favorite flavor!  And do try the white chocolate with banana and peanut butter - mmmmm good!)
This is a tasty snack but the small bags do not contain much product. This is not a value for what you get of the pistachio crunch.

Its a great protein snack to give you a hit of energy without a crash like sugary candy. It comes in a perfect small portion, so you don't overdo it on the nuts. They taste great and everyone I offer them to loves them. Chewy and just slightly sweet for when you get tired of plain old nuts. Excellent blend, healthy and not overpriced. Great, cheaper alternative for a bag of chips at the office vending machine. Highly recommend having these on hand at your home or office.

I am forever looking for a better trail mix mostly because they're all so calorie-heavy.  The other day i was looking for a healthy option and found this.  Against what i thought would be my better judgement, i bought it.  To my delight, the calories were not outrageous and there was still enough to stave off an angry growing hunger for a good hour.  To add to the delight, it had pistachios, which i have adored the taste of since i was a small girl (who else ordered pistachio ice cream???).  It also had just the right amount of both sweet and salty!  Finally, i have been successfully participating in a popular weight loss program for about 6 months.  I found that this little gem was only 5 pts--a pretty reasonable and highly nutritious snack on a "work out day".  I HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!  Thanks Mareblu!!

I really enjoyed the mild, but flavorful variety of teas in this white tea sampler.  It's a great way to enjoy tea that has body, but not too much caffeine.I've often given Heavenly Tea Leaves's samplers as gifts, and they're always a big hit.

I'm sorry to give this product 1 star, but I have to. The quality is just not there compared to other teas. The leaves are chopped up and flat, and not rolled like higher quality teas. The photos also do not accurately portray the amount of sticks/stems that are in the teas. Once you get past the looks, you will still be disappointed by the taste. The 2 that I tried have a grassy/earthy taste, and do not taste like any other white tea that I have had before. I only took a few sips and threw the rest away. Please save your money and buy from somewhere else. Such as teavanna. they might be more expensive but i have been impressed with every tea that i have bought from them.

I purchased this and the organic green tea sampler to break in my Ingenuitea teapot (buy one of those now, btw). I'm not usually a big fan of white tea & bought this for my wife, but all 4 flavours are exceptionally good. I actually like the white tea sampler more than the green (which is also very good). It's amazing how many times you can infuse 3 tsp. of this tea. I've probably done it 6-7 times and the last cup was not weak at all. I probably could have done more, but wanted to try another flavour. Highly recommended.
Impressive selection & well put together. I've been dabbling in to the world of teas & these are probably among the best Ive tried to date. Thank You. We have really enjoyed them.

White tea is an acquired taste and I have acquired it through the terrific teas of Heavenly Teas. Quite honestly, I used to be a real coffee person but I started drinking tea in the past 1-2 years. At first I was a solid black tea only person (Earl Grey was always running out at my house) and then I moved to green tea and lately I was introduced to white teas from Heavenly Teas ...I have had only top quality from them and highly recommend that every coffee lover gives this a try....

I was very excited to find this product, but once they arrived (the firts time) , I opened the box, and was hit with the odor of rancid oil...the cups were rancid...I contacted amazon, and a replacement was sent VERY QUICKLY, but alas, no odor, but the cups were stale and nasty...Amazon refunded my order promptly, but I am still disappointed that the cup were so awful.

I own a tea shop and was asked if I could find this wine for a client. I ordered this tea and not only did that client love it both hot and iced, I sold every tin I had on hand. I am ordering it again and ordering more than last time!

column4: Southern by the grace of God "Transplanted So...
column9: Just a little bit of the South...
column10: After moving from the South to the northeast, I could no longer find my beloved GRITS. Amazon allows me to enjoy them again! These are authentic southern style. Good quality and consistency from Quaker. Easy to prepare in convenient packages.

As a lifetime member of Weight Watchers, these fabulous bacon flavored grits are terrific to add pizzazz to soups and vegetable dishes, as well as a filing side dish.  I can no longer find them in the local store.  So I've turned to Amazon to find them.

Geez, this stuff is actually good. I'd given up on these cup o' soup death-by-sodium concoctions, but this one has a lot less salt, much more healthy ingredients and most of all, it tastes great. Haven't tried all of Dr. McDougall's products, but the ones I have tried are darn good.
I have tried a lot of prepared just add water kind of foods because I am a very busy college student but this is by far the worst!
can not find this one any more in Illinois??? will need to order on line. This one is the best of all of them.

column9: Please try this brand! You will never go back to any other bloody mary mix ever
column10: I must admit I am a huge fan of day drinking. Bloody marys in particular, so naturally I have tried this mix and that mix, making them at home and tasting them out and about. An old friend of mine made bloody marys for me and some friends a year ago, and I've never bought any other mix since.Most mixes you need to add additional measurements of spices into the mixes even though they claim they don't need it, and this is the one mix I've ever gotten, (I live in Los Angeles, so trust me there are many mixes to try here), where you do not need to add ANYTHING ELSE!I wish it was easier to find on the shelves now a days since Ralphs has slowly faded it from their shelves. You can also buy the other varieties (original, the works, hot & spicy) if you would like to try those from peppers.com if it ever sells out on here!

This salsa is delicious with a very nice flavor and a strong unexpected kick that lingers. It's *very* thick and sweet and as a result clocks in at a relatively high (for salsa) 50 calories and 13g carbs per 2tbsp serving. It's great with chips and even better cooked into some eggs and sausage.All that said, it's great to receive as a gift but I'm not sure I could ever convince myself to spend over ten bucks on a jar of salsa for myself.

Perfect blend of spices with just a bit of oil to keep them firm yet dry. Perfect for salads, salsa, even a Martini. Too bad they never made it to a dish, so good just eat em right out of the pouch :)A side note, these olives would be great served on airplanes, they keep and they have a good design. They would also be great to take along hiking.Best  Wishes,  E.A.C

These things are delicious. The packaging in single-serve size is great. Especially since if it were one big package, I'd be tempted to eat all the olives in one sitting. They're a great way to eat olives on the go without all the mess. I took a pack along in my lunch the other day. The olives are pitted, super flavorful, just the right crunch/firmness. I could eat them all day. I'll definitely have to order again.

I first encountered this product in an airline snack box and fell in love with it. Flavor is great and it makes a wonderfully portable snack. These may not be as firm as olives packaged in jars but because of the portability and the wonderful flavor I don't miss having a really firm olive. I enjoy these enough that I have subscribed to them.

I bought the garlic and the thyme with chili. I love them! I have them at work. They are the perfect after lunch snack when I have to work a late but I don't want to eat a full on meal.  They came quickly and with no problems at all! I will be buying again.

Olives are GOOD for you and I was very intrigued by the packaging.  I would like to find some that NOT herbed or flavored... just nice, plain green olives... I wasn't a huge fan of the flavoring.. but the olives themselves were good.  A few were extra soft, but I don't mind that.  Super convenient!

column9: Wish they would send them Overseas!!!
column10: I'm a US Soldier currently deployed to Afghanistan.  I experienced these in a series of care packages from a group called Operation Gratitude.  They're the most tasty things I have ever received in a care package!  I ran around the whole camp, asking anybody else who received these if they didn't want them, so I could have them.  Now I'm trying to buy them on my own, but sadly, no business's seem to ship them to APO address's on their own.  I'm having to have my family buy them and send them to me.

These were really GOOD! Did not last long at my house!  Would give more than 5 stars if I could. The flavor is fantastic. Olives flavored with garlic & thyme. Three of my favorites. All together. If you like these flavors you are going to like these olives.
I really like olives, and these are OK.  VERY salty, even for olives.  The marinade is nice, but not sure I'll order again. I like this brand of olives, so may look for other options :)

Let me start off saying that i LOVE olives, especially green ones.  I will put away a jar of Mario's in one sitting.These olives, since they are packed without the juice (just some oil on them in the pouch) just seem kinda dry, and they are really soft.  Almost mushy.  The flavor is good for sure, but i am not exactly won over by the firmness (or lack thereof)/texture, and actually i miss the juice.

I was a little hesitant to order these.  I was afraid of how they might taste.  But, I really wanted flower candy for a party.  So, I decided to give these a shot.  The pieces are a nice size, larger than a gummy bear.  And, the flavor is great.  They are rather addictive.  We used them in a dozen goody bags and still had half of the bag left.  This really is quality candy!
I ordered these for my daughters birthday party and they were a hit., it was nice to have something different in a gummy candy
I go through 5lbs of these a month. Very addicting and yummy! Fresh, soft, flavorful! Great value at 8 bucks for 5lbs!

I have a candy dish at work, which I stock with a revolving supply of gummy candy.  I tried these out a few months back.  Bright colors, consistent shapes, and large size make these great theme candy I think.  they also have 5 different, distinct flavors, all of which are pretty tasty.The only real complaints I have about them are that all the flavors seem highly unnatural, which may not appeal to some people, and that the candy initially smelled strongly of chemicals, like some kind of industrial solvent maybe.  It didn't seem to affect the flavor of the individual candies significantly, but it was highly unnerving.

column4: J. Shaw "If momma ain't happy, ain't nobody h...
column10: These are amazing! The best gummy candy we have tried. They are sooo soft, but let me note that these were too soft and chewy for my 4 year old, he choked a bit. So we saved these for adults and that was just fine by me. I can't distiguish all of the flavors, but my favorite is the light pink which is grapefruit. The candies are about the size of a quarter. Yum! The bag will be gone before you know it. If you are debating between these of the butterflies, these are the better choice.

These candies--all five pounds of them--are out of this world.  They are extremely soft, very easy to chew.  They are also the most translucent--the closest in appearance to plain water--of any gummy candy I've seen.  So the colors of these translucent candies are pale, pale aqua; pale, pale yellow; pale, faint red.  Beautiful and different from a traditional bunch of, say, gummy bears.  Another departure from the standard gummy bear, is that each of these pieces is roughly 1.5 to 2 times the size of a gummy bear--so they're nice and large, chunky, easy to pick up and hold.  The flavors are extremely pleasant, and very subtle.If you're ready for a change from your current gummy candy, give these a try.  I think you'll be delighted with their flavor, taste, and pretty forms.

I am a gummy bear addict and these Albanese Gummi Awesome Blossoms were so good.  I ordered these to try a different gummy bear. They were awesome!  Just a couple after dinner satisfy my sweet tooth.For a more chewy gummie, you won't be disappointed.

I just wanted to say a few words about the Good Sense Natural Vanilla Yogurt Pretzels.  They are the best pretzels that I have ever eaten and the good news is they are much cheaper than the ones you can find in the natural food stores.  The order arrived very quickly and I was extremely pleased.  I will look no further in the future.  I have found the supplier for my incredible addiction for yogurt pretzels.  Thanks,

Have always purchased this item from WalMart. WalMart has decided to discontinue this item.  For what reason, who knows. We contacted Good Sense and they recommended various suppliers.  Amazon was one of them.  After receiving our order, we found the coating on pretzels was very light and a lot of pieces instead of full like we had been used to receiving when we bought from WalMart.  The taste was dull and not enjoyable to eat.  Either Amazon is buying seconds and not letting us know or Good Sense is sending seconds to Amazon and not letting them know.  We won't be buying these in the future from Amazon.  We'll try to find them in grocery stores or speciality stores.

These are very very good -- comparable to the ones sold in my local upscale supermarket, and less expensive per pound, too.  I have to be careful and "parcel" these out into individual snack bags or I'll eat way too many!  They have a nice vanilla yogurt flavor, with just enough crunch and salt from the pretzel.The expiration date is far enough out (I purchased these in mid-August 2010; the expiration date is the end of June 2011) that I'll be able to finish these off before they expire, sometimes a concern when I purchase in quantity like this.I'm very pleased with these, and I'll likely purchase them again.

My bride likes caviar (and my home made blini) for her birthday.  Bemka's Ossetra is too expensive to eat often, but that speaks well of its quality.  But at under a hundred bucks an ounce, you can buy two ounces and eat it in big, greedy bites.I prepared it simply, on ice with all the usual accoutrements -- blini, crème fraîche, red onions, egg -- but went light on the accoutrements and heavy on the fish eggs.  And my bride's birthday-dinner-for-two was a huge success.  Ossetra has just the right combination of bite, saltiness and squishiness for a romantic dinner for two.Just don't forget the champagne.

I was based in England and every time I went food shopping, Ming imperial lotus lead tea was always my priority buy. So I am glad to see that I can finally purchase it in the U.S. it is a great tasting tea, I mainly use it for the purpose to cleanse my whole  System and maintain my weight.
I use this tea as part of my supplements in gymming. It Worked perfectly in cleansing my system, and helping me maintain my weight.
The product is good and as described, though a bit expensive. Hope can help lose weight as described in the product title.

The breathe of my three year old cat wasn't very nice and I was reluctant to have his teeth cleaned by our Vet because a dear friend of mine lost a pet due to anesthesia for teeth cleaning. I ordered beef and salmon flavored greenies and he loves both flavors.  It's been less than a month so I'm not ready to say how much his breathe has improved but would recommend them to others and plan to order more.

I can't believe how good this is.  Sure beats manwich sauce.  My husband doesn't even like sloppy joe sandwiches and he loved this.  I would highly recommend this to anyone who needs to make a quick meal.  It is on the sweet side - just like the sloppy joes I used to eat when I was growing up.

These are absolutely exquisite cookies, with the richness of pure English shortbread plus the haunting spiciness of minced crystallized ginger.  The tartness of the ginger and the sweetness of the shortbread blend tantalizingly, leaving a light, captivating taste that lingers in your mouth after the last bite is gone.  Great with tea, with coffee, with an after-dinner drink, with a fruit dessert, or with your best ice cream.  I love them with milk, with a small dish of fresh berries, with after-dinner coffee and a small snifter of brandy, or alone just before bed. column9: Excellent Food for Hard to Please Dogs
column10: We went through at least a dozen samples of better quality dog food before we found one that our new dog would eat.  This lamb formula must be very palatable to dogs and the ingredient list is about as good as you can get.  The food is made in a family owned single plant in MN from US and New Zealand sources.  Note that Nutrisource revised their feeding guidelines and that many bags out there have the old, higher quantities.  For example, the old feeding guideline for a 50lb dog is about 3 cups, whereas the new one is 2 cups.  This further makes the food a good value, so keep that in mind when evaluating price against other brands.  The food is very nutrient-dense. Best of all, our dog loves it.

column9: Caribou Pulls a Fast One on Loyal Customers
column10: I've been drinking Caribou Blend for years and it is just right for my taste... or at least it was.  Got a new shipment in and I noticed a color change on the K-cup, orange to light green.  Uh-oh, wrong product?  I compared the box to my old one and found the same SKU number but the roast level has been dropped from medium to very light along with the color change.  My taste test revealed exactly that... a mild, relatively tasteless coffee more like their dishwater Daybreak than the old Caribou blend.  Caribou (I got this second hand) claims that their flagship blend is more of a light roast than a medium roast and they made the change accordingly. Yeah, sure. Nice try but we all know that the wholesale price of coffee has skyrocketed.  Sounds to me, the skeptic, that perhaps they have been forced to switch to a cheaper coffee with less gusto and more bitterness to maintain their competitive price points.  How sad.  I would have gladly paid more for my favorite.  The new blend is far inferior.  If you're a regular, have someone  brew both and I bet you'll have no problem distinguishing the difference. Time for a new favorite with a company that doesn't play sleazy tricks on its loyal customers.  If and when prices return to normal, watch the return to the old orange based on "we listen to our customers" and more corporate-speak BS.

column9: Truly disappoiting. Product Changed. Not for the better!
column10: We have been buying Caribou Blend K-cups for a couple of years. It is a fine medium blend that we, and everyone that we have served it to, loves. We usually order it in larger quantities to try and save some money since we go through it fairly quickly. The last order we placed for 2 x 80 boxes was fulfilled with the K-cups with green color labels (the older labels were orange around the edges). The taste of this new k-cup can only be described as vile and has nothing to do with the former product. It is not drinkable. We have written to Caribou and have been waiting for a response, but nothing yet (I will update if I hear anything). DO NOT BUY this product if you have used the older product with he orange color on the label and liked it. You will not get the same thing and this coffee is truly terrible!Deserves 0 Stars...Update - a note from Caribou Corporate:Thank you for taking the time to contact us.We certainly apologize for any confusion. Recently the packaging for Caribou Blend K Cups did change. Previously the regular blend had an orange band and the decaf had a green band. The new labels the regular is a green band and the decaf is an orange band.The coffee itself has not changed, simply the label. There are two factors that might be involved in the change you taste. The change in taste is affected by the time that has lapsed between roasting the coffee beans and brewing them...freshness.  Also, coffee is an agricultural crop that varies with weather and other environmental factors.  Our Roastmasters put in a lot of time and attention to provide a consistency when roasting the coffee beans.We do apologize for any confusion and please let us know if there is anything else we can do for you.Sincerely,LindaCaribou Coffee Customer RelationsThe coffee is Dramatically different, but they will not admit to the change. Oh, well. Goodbye Caribou Coffee.

Almost a year ago now I suffered from 4-5 debilitating cluster migraines a week that were killing me.  Then I read some article online that lead me to believe the migraines might have been triggered by caffein.  So I completely stopped drinking caffein about a year ago.  It was very hard to stop drinking caffeinated coffee (and soda) but it was worth it because it successfully reduced my migraines from several a week to about ten in a year (and two of those migraines were caused by drinking unlabeled Amish root beer which must have caffeine in it).  But, I still missed the comfort and taste of morning coffee and holding a warm mug in my hand while sitting on the porch wrapped in a blanket and the smell or going to coffee shops.  After no coffee for several months, I tired decaf for the first time and experienced no headaches, but the taste was so bland that it wasn't worth the calories.  I experimented with many different decaf brands, including Starbucks.  This past weekend, I visited my cousin who insisted I try this brand.  And, hellooooo!  This is what I remember coffee tasting like!!!  It's smooth, bold, strong without making you spit it out, it has flavor!  It doesn't leave a gross taste in your mouth!  I didn't believer her that it was decaf, but I did not get a migraine! column9: one month of use made a nonbeliever out of me
column10: In reading all the reviews of different decaf k-cups, the opinion I came away with was that Tully's was where I should go to get a really bold, dark roasted flavor similar to Starbucks' coffee. It does get closer to Starbucks than any of the other decaf k-cups I have tried. But in a way it goes too far and results in a somewhat strange and overpowering taste.I had tried Timothy's decaf and Newman's Own decaf, with the latter vastly superior to the former. I would say Tully's beats Timothy's (which is just brown water), but probably not Newman's. I also tried Donut Shop decaf simultaneously with Tully's (I had Donut Shop at work and Tully's at home). For the first few days, I thought Donut Shop was a little weak and I liked Tully's better for its bolder flavor. But after a couple of weeks I grew tired and a little sick of Tully's strong taste - it's not just strong like a normal cup of Starbucks, it's strong almost like they added some kind of artificial chemical to it to make it taste darker or more burned than it really is. After one month I was long done with the Donut Shop and was just slowly getting through the Tully's (diluted with lots of milk).When I reordered, I only considered Newman's or Donut Shop. I couldn't bring myself to drink another cup of Tully's. It's a shame because they definitely took a step in the right direction with their stronger flavor, but it was a misstep that makes the coffee a poor choice for long-term consumption.Perhaps a good strategy for a newcomer would be to order Tully's AND another brand or two like Newman's and Donut Shop, and trade off which one they drink. That might make Tully's flavor less grating over time

I love Tully's coffee, and I love the convenience and consistency of making coffee by the cup using the K-Cup product. However, when I ordered the Tully's Decaf French Roast, what I received was the Tully's Decaf French Roast BOLD product instead. I didn't really notice it until I made the first cup.Next time, I'd appreciate getting the precise product that I order. The Decaf French Roast BOLD is good, it's Tully's, but it is not what I ordered!DanHill

column9: never order from this company again
column10: priceed to hight compare other companys that sell tullys decalf french k-cups. i got bad coffee liquid nation would not exchange or refund price payed,was not packed up from the a-to-z  , never buy from ln again. ted
its great for making bread, my mom loves to bake with it! She says she would buy it again. I am not a baker/cook so that is only my moms opinion. But shes happy, so i'm happy.
I'm not sure what else to say, but it is a very tasty syrup.  It comes in a pretty standard bottle, but it was packet very well and arrived in fine shape.

First of all, let me say that I only use this to make bagels. However, it does a bang up job and I love the fact that it's organic. However, like most sticky cooking/baking ingredients, the screw on lid gets really stuck on unless you clean it after each use or put plastic wrap over the opening before screwing the lid on. This is a great malt exract for replacing 1 can of mr beers unhopped malts. or add your own malt grain & hopsi did both on a 2 gallon test.the mr beer came out close to the same & Edens malt with a cup of Karo's dark corn syrup,a cup of brown sugar,1 oz hops came out exellent.i cant wait to taste the rice beer that i made with 1 jar of Edens & 1.5lb jar of Lundberg's sweet dreams brown rice syrup with 1.lb peal barley &1.lb wheat grain + honey & ginger. Brew On.

This product is not always available locally, but is worth ordering the several boxes from Amazon.  Not too sweet or salty, and as near huskless as popcorn can be, it is a treat that does not need to wait for autumn evenings.

This is the best micro popcorn ever. I was looking for the sweetend kettle corn and when this arrived and I saw it was similar to, what I would compare to hot air corn, I was skeptical. I thought it would be dry and flat. I plan to buy this again and never another brand.

Much better than other microwave popcorns.  Doesn't leave that waxy feel in your mouth and has a more authentic sweet taste.  Also you can actually taste the corn flavor.  Very good.  I will be buying this from now on.

Unlike air popped corn it is not at all dry and even somehow manages, for me anyway, a light butter flavor. It is lightly salted which is perfect for me. My husband adds salt to his.As others have noted with all flavors of this popcorn, microwave timing can be a bit tricky. -Keep it in there long enough and nearly every kernel pops but you might wind up with a few on the extra crispy side.My reason for mentioning the natural flavor first is that it will always be my all time biggie favorite and is the basis for this product. Right now however, I am loving the "Sweet & Salty". It has the same attributes of the natural flavor with just a hint of sweetness that is very pleasant and satisfying.Man do I love this stuff - I think the family is planning an intervention based on stash I keep in pantry to ensure there is always some on hand.

I'm a sucker for good kettle corn and usually buy Orville Redenbacher.  However, they are moving towards that bag-into-a-bowl version which isn't as good and gives you less product, so I decided to give Black Jewell a try. I buy this popcorn for a DAV at the Indiana Veteran's Home.  He really enjoys it and I am unable to find it in any stores in our area.  Thank you Amazon for making our Veterans happy!
Has a very nice light Kettle Corn taste...we were used to the pop-secret kettle corn, but, is no longer available.this compares or exceeds very nicely..it all pops up well, very few old maids
Did not pop completely.  Left 30% of the kernels unpopped and what did pop was hully and tough.  Would not buy again.

My husband bought two cases of this popcorn based on all the 5-stars reviews.  We waited over 2 weeks for delivery.  What a disappointment!!!  Tiny pieces of popcorn.  Lacks kettle corn flavor.  Then, he contacts Amazon.com about returning it.  Nope, they won't take it back.  BAD experience all the way around!

My pooch has just been initiated to the world of Milk Bone treats. He seemed puzzled, licked them, took them and hid them for later consumption - a new and strange behavior. He consumes them like a fine cigar after dinner. No matter what time of day I give these to him, he stores them to be savored later.Only problem is he hides them under the covers at the foot of my bed. This is a perfect item to use as a dog treat.  My dog loves them. The good thing with Milk Bone is they can be purchad in small size up to normal size dependenent on your dog size.

im in Afghanistan and i missed this drink so much i looked it up on Amazon. i was so happy to find out that they shipped out here and the shipping was quick! it wasnt spoiled and the taste was amazing. nothing like a cold glass of chocolate milk on a hot day!

I was instructed to increase my amount of protein daily and I am not a real meat eater.  I tried different protein drinks and was not satisfied because they made me feel full and I was not trying to suppress my appetite, plus many of them had ingredients that didn't appear natural or had added flavoring and sugar and I am trying to stick with natural products.  I was already eating egg white straight from the egg but was getting tired of that and decided to give this product a try.  I now use this everyday, I put it in my freshly juiced vegetable juices, I add it to my freshly juiced smoothies and it is great.  I even put it in my oatmeal and bake it for a real treat adding agave nectar as a sweetner. I am very satisfied with this product and would highly recommend it to anyone trying to increase their protein intake and not trying to suppress their appetite.  I would also recommend it for anyone just looking for a cleaner way to crack an egg and use just the egg whites.

This product is far more expensive than just buying fresh eggs and throwing away the yolk. Do you measure it packed or loose? I bought this product to use in Royal Icing. It worked great and taste sooooo much better than using "meringue powder" as some recipes call for. I'm going to use it in a buttercream frosting recipe tomorrow. Package arrived fast and well packed. Thank you!
Came in the time estimated. Strangely via USPS. Cans look big on page small in real life.

I use this for my muffins that call for two egg whites.  I could just separate eggs and it would actually be a little cheaper, but I hate to waste the yolks or force myself to make something that calls for the yolks, like flan, which I don't eat as often.  The only thing you really need to know is that you do have to wisk them well so that you don't have lumps which bake up as small white rubbery blobs that is not pretty and feels like trying to chew a rubber band. I use 1 tablespoon in a blender along with skim milk, fruit such as banana, 1 scoop of a dry greens product, and 1 tablespoon of a nut butter.  I may also add a few drops of stevia along with 1 tablespoon of cocoa powder.  This makes a great liquid lunch and keeps me full of energy, since it is high protein.  The egg whites can also be mixed with skim milk and plain yoghurt and frozen fruit such as peaches for a special treat.  I am so glad to have found this product.

I love this product.I use it every morning in a protein shake and before I found it on amazon I was getting it at my market.When they discontinued it I was miserable but thanks to Amazon I found this wonderful product.
Great product. Very versatile and useful especially for low carb eating. This product is pasteurized for safety, too. The price is best for the case on Amazon.
Hey, it beats throwing out egg yolks to get rid of the fat, and they're very handy to use.  They whip up great and last a long time in the cupboard, so nothing bad about 'em!Diane

I love the Deb-El Just Whites.  They allow me to always have a little extra egg white on hand when I need it without the worry of refrigeration space or going bad before I can use them. I ordered the powdered egg whites for my baking and they arrived in about three days.  Great service and well described product.
Very good! Arrived on time and it is delicious. Very easy to prepare, it takes only a few minutes. Everyone can now taste one of the favorites Brazilian receipts.
Great product.  Added a cup and a half of sharp grated cheese and you are ready to go.  Thanks.

column9: Tastes as good as traditional roobios
column10: I've bought roobios from the expensive madison avenue tea shop in New York and this tastes just as good. I don't often need to make a pot at a time and the convenience of having the tea in this form is a little lost on me, but you know, it does work, it does taste nice and I might save it for company, when my little teapot and strainer just isn't enough.

Those who are tea lovers will undoubtedly find this product quite delightful. Unlike most decaffeinated teas, the flavour is rich and aromatic. It does not taste at all like espresso coffee (which I'll admit I found initially disappointing), but is an exceptionally flavourful tea.I prepared the tea in three ways - in a stove top espresso pot, then in a French press, then with an infuser in a teapot. Though the last manner isn't recommended by the instructions, it worked very well, and flavour with the brewed espresso pot was very fine as well. The only drawback was in using the French press, though the flavour remained excellent. The grind of the tea is too fine for the press, and I found that it made using the plunger very difficult - I was fortunate that the pot was of stainless steel, because a glass press may have been damaged in the process.

column9: Not quite sure what the point is.
column10: When I first saw this product I thought it was an awesome idea.  Rooibos tea mixed with espresso beans... YAY! But, unfortunately, this was my mistake and I read the package wrong.  This is simply rooibos tea blended in an espresso "fashion".  That is, finely.  Nothing else.  It is a very clever product, but I see no point to it.  If you want to try a great Rooibos tea try Tick Tock.  This product isn't even organic... it's natural.  I just don't see the point.
I bought this tea at a coffee shop and it was so good I had to go out and my it myself.  It is delicious and I think so good for you.  You must try this and you will keep drinking it for along time.

I'm very, VERY pleased to have the opportunity to help bring this product to the attention of American consumers because I've been enjoying it for the past two years (a friend brings it from South Africa when he goes home between semesters). My review will try to supply some background on both rooibos and the product itself, after which I'll provide what I hope are some helpful tips for enjoying and appreciating red espresso.Rooibos (literally "red bush" in Afrikaans, pronounced more or less "ROY'-bawss") is a shrub that grows in South Africa which tea-deprived Afrikaaners discovered made a not-too-shabby substitute for tea when dried and oxidized. It turned out to have been a fortuitous discovery because research seems to support claims indicating that rooibos contains lots of healthful elements and provides a high level of antioxidants without caffeine. It  has a pleasant, sweetish taste (nothing to which I can compare it--sorry) and though most folks prefer it sweetened (a spot of agave nectar is the perfect complement), with or without a splash of milk, it's quite nice straight up as well. It also blends beautifully with spices and makes a fabulous chai (check out Rishi--they have excellent rooibos-based chai blends).Interestingly enough, red espresso also came into being as the result of desperation. It seems the founder of the company was jonesing for an espresso and, finding the cupboard bare, it occurred to him that perhaps substituting the rooibos he DID have on hand would provide a temporary fix. Lo and behold, his espresso maker produced a deep brew that actually had a crema! Seeds sewn, he began to experiment with different grades of rooibos and then with different cuts in an attempt to develop the best-tasting, most robust rooibos possible--one that would hold up to espresso brewing. Red espresso was born!Red espresso is a much heavier brew than other rooibosses I've tried, even when prepared by drip method (you can use a Chemex or other some such for this). You can also, I imagine, use a French press. However, the best way to prepare it is in a stovetop espresso maker such as a Bialetti Brikka. The last time I checked, red espresso wasn't completely approved for espresso makers but that might have changed by now--it's been two years since I read that. Simply use the same routine used for coffee: fill the tray with red espresso, fill the pot to the correct water level, and heat until you hear the "pop." You're now ready to have fun with your red espresso shot (I've read on coffee sites that the two-cup stovetop makers produce better results than the four-cup models that are most often available here in the States--shop around).The company's Web site has some wonderful recipes and suggestions for red espresso; have a look: http://redespresso.com/ (hit the link for "red drinks"). It's delicious  (and beautiful) in shakes and smoothies, and there's a really nice recipe that floats red espresso on apple juice, although it tastes better with a natural, "cloudy" apple juice than with a clear one. Get creative!I e-mailed the red espresso team two years ago after first trying it (I'd stumbled onto the Web site and asked my friend to bring me some) and they actually called me to chat! When they e-mailed me a few months ago to announce that Amazon would be carrying it, I replied that I suspected it would turn up in Vine, in which case I'd be able to review it and they wrote back that it was indeed slated for Vine and that they were eager for my review. I've been holding my breath ever since, especially since it didn't show up last month. I've been hoping ever since that not only would red espresso take off in a big way internationally (it's apparently very popular in South Africa), but that I'd have easier access to it. With any luck and Amazon's help, fulfillment on both counts is looking good!  :)If you have any interest in brewed beverages and want to experience something that's healthful, delicious, and novel (stovetop espresso makers are fun to use), by all means, give red espresso a "shot," especially if you already have an espresso maker of some sort that doesn't involve pods (feh). You can always try it with the drip method to see if you want to make the small investment required for a stovetop pot.

column9: Stong Red Tea -- Not a coffee substitute
column10: I don't drink coffee but drink several high-end varieties of teas.  In other words, I gave up Lipton years ago.  My normal teas are Oolong, Organic gold bud, Genmai Cha, jasmine and white.  Redespresso does not taste like any other tea I drink but it is very tasty.  I used to make my tea stronger but over time have become used to milder tea flavors.  This tea calls for 12 grams/double shot or about 1/2 an ounce in imperial measurements.  That's about 10 times as much as I'm used to.  If I use what I consider to be a normal amount - say 1 teaspoon to 2 cups of water, I get an excellent cup of tea.  I think the manufacturer is trying to pass good tea off as coffee.  No amout of tea will make a coffee substitute.  So be what you are and call yourself red tea.  Yes, I would imagine at the overdose amounts of tea the instuctions call fot that it would be higher in anti-oxidants.  I also belive I could achieve the same results with just about any other tea -- particularly Oolong.

column9: Wish I could review this, but some parts not included...
column10: I'll have to pass this on to someone to try out, as I have no access to an espresso machine (who actually has one of those???).  The package looks nice...

The first impression on opening the bag is that it smells very strongly of moist hay.  It is very dusty, reddish-brown in color, and the texture is very fine.  The leaves do not curl like tea leaves.I made the rooibos in both a stovetop espresso maker and in a regular drip coffee maker but I don't have a french press or an electric espresso machine.  I also did not try it brewed loose in a pot because that is not suggested.Compared to normal steeped rooibos, it is a bit stronger and has more body, presumably due to the finer grind.  The stovetop method makes a stronger brew than the drip maker and this presumably has to do with the filter in the drip maker and the higher water temperature and pressure from conversion to steam in the espresso method.  The strength of the prepared beverage is also determined by how much rooibos you use.After each method of preparation, i tasted it plain, with raw sugar, and then with both raw sugar and milk.  I did not try to froth the milk or add anything else because I don't take coffee or tea that way, drinking them plain most of the time, occasionally with milk and sugar, and very rarely with sugar only.  I didn't try it with honey because I did not think the honey flavor would go well with it although I frequently use honey in tea, more often than sugar.  I prefer the stovetop espresso method taken with sugar only.The prepared beverage certainly has a beautiful, rich color, quite remarkable, like old cherry or mahogany.  The flavor is similar to the smell, a bit like green tea with a strong moist or even musty hay- or grass-like flavor that lingers on the tongue for a very long time, over an hour.  It is a quite complex flavor, definitely not one-note.  I don't particularly care for the taste, I must confess, but I am rating it on quality, not on my personal preferences in hot beverages.  I wouldn't hesitate to offer it to guests, especially if they had never had rooibos.I am not impressed with it as a substitute for coffee or tea as a way to avoid caffeine because decaffeinated versions of both coffee and tea are readily available.  The health appeal doesn't seduce me, either, because I know of no reliable independent research clearly demonstrating favorable health outcomes in humans from drinking rooibos.  Because of the price, I would experiment with regular loose-leaf rooibos and run it through a coffee grinder or food processor or even a blender if I decided that this were something I wanted to drink on a regular basis and that achieving a fine grind was important to the final product.The novelty of preparing rooibos with coffee equipment and the stronger than average brew that lends itself to fancy methods of presentation should appeal to many and from that viewpoint I can give it a favorable rating.UPDATE:What a mess!  I just made another pot with an electric drip machine and this time the filter completely clogged up and the brew overflowed all over the counter and clean floor (mopped it yesterday) and even got into the heating element of the Mr. Coffee.  Make sure if you use an electric drip machine that you don't leave it alone while brewing.  Better yet, use a different method of brewing.It is interesting that I actually used less of the rooibos this morning than I did during the original test.  I use standard paper filters.

I am a coffee drinker who usually uses Keurig machines and pod coffeemakers as I really don't like coffee that's been sitting in a pot for a while.  I got this product to try as I had read good things about the antioxidants and wanted to see how I liked it.  I don't like green tea at all and have been struggling to force myself to drink it now and again for health reasons.When I first got the product, I was like, now what??  I don't have an espresso machine although I do have a French Press.  I took it to work with me and after a few cups of coffee decided it was time to try it out.  We have a Melitta One pod machine there and one of the guys bought some Melitta FilterPads so we could make our own pods.  I filled a pod with the Red Espresso, tossed it into the One machine, and fired it up.  A few minutes later I had a cup of dark red liquid.  After adding creamer, the beverage was an interesting dark brownish red color.  It smelled good and the first sip was very pleasant.  The flavor is very mild with very subtle flavors.  It didn't taste like tea or coffee, and while the flavor is very mild, it doesn't taste watery either.  I liked it very much and can't really say why.  I felt good after drinking it.  I had a few more cups that day and liked it better each time.I stopped on the way home and bought a mini stovetop espresso maker. This made an even stronger, redder drink.  I also tried it in my Keurig reusable filter.  I got good results with this too, but actually liked the drink I got from the pod coffeemaker the best.I have begun adding a touch of cinnamon which is very nice, and will try adding some chai spices when I make it in the french press.  I think that will be outstanding.

column9: Flavorful Tea Uniquely Strong But Not Bitter
column10: Espresso tea is quite obviously strong tea. I do not particularly like strong tea because it is almost always bitter. The redespresso tea is smooth and richly nuanced -- yes, I said nuanced. There are layers of flavor and all are pleasant -- no cloying fruity flavors -- it is decidely tea, and absolutely delicious. I drank it hot, but it will make wonderful ice tea -- and a little fresh mint would be perfect in the glass. As soon as I tasted it, I knew it would be great as an ingredient in jelly, cookies, sorbet and even chili (where I would normally add a little cocoa for depth.)So why four stars instead of five? I made the mistake of brewing the tea in my automatic coffee maker. The package indicated this was an acceptable method (or you can use an espresso maker or coffee press.) And, although I followed the instructions on the package to the letter, the tea swelled up and impeded the water from passing through to the pot. I ended up with 2/3 of a pot of delicious espresso tea and the rest of the water and tea were splattered all over the coffee maker and counter. Next time I'll just use my coffee press.

column9: Something new to brew in your espresso machine
column10: This review is only based on the espresso brewing method. I used a Racillio Silvia espresso machine. I've tried making both hot (Red Lattes, Red Cappuccinos, Red Americano) and cold (Iced Red, Red Fresh) drinks with good results. My favourite so far is the Iced Red.Pros:- Tastes great.- Naturally caffeine free.- Health benefits.- Vibrant red/orange colour.Cons:- Can be pricey.Tips:- Do not tamp. Just level.- Pre-infuse by wetting the grounds and wait ~15 seconds before brewing.
This tea has a storng medicinal flavor. I can not drink it without adding a LOT of lime. I will never buy it again and could not recommend it to anyone else.

This has a fragrance and a taste that is offputting to me, I've tried it several times - hot, iced, sweetened, not, additions of cream, lemon - and I just can't get past that "whang" it has.  I'm sure others probably love it but I won't be buying it again.

Be prepared with the right equipment to make this tea, it can be as simple as a low cost french press or a suitable coffee maker. Suitable meaning something like a espresso machine or pod system where you won't cross contamination with coffee flavors.Once made the curiously strong tea has a nice aroma and flavor. Suitable for milk, cream, spice, or other additions.If you are not looking for a caffeine drink, I highly recommend giving this unique beverage a try.

I brewed it in the coffee maker as instructed and drank it with sweetened milk as the Thai do. It gives a strong, deeper flavor and dark red color which is good. However, it didn't impress me given the extra trouble of having to brew. I'm a green tea lover, so not sure how often I'd be drinking this version despite the health benefits.

This was delicious. I used a regular tea maker to make this, and followed the instructions on the bag. It was delicious. I drank it on ice. I also tried it mixed with coconut water, sweetened with agave nectar. I did try to make this like a regular pot of tea and it clogged up my tea maker, even though it has the capability of making loose teas. So don't try it even if tempted.

This espresso tea is wonderfully aromatic, reminds me of cherry tobacco, but does not transfer well to the palate, or at least mine.  The scent is very strong as you are sipping the tea, and it overwhelms me, but I have a keen sense of smell so that may not be a problem for others.  It is hard to differentiate the actual taste from the scent.  I don't think I will try it again.

The description of the tea on the package made me think there would be something espresso-like in the tea, when there really wasn't.  It's a strong red (black) tea in what is allegedly an espresso grind, but tea doesn't really grind the way coffee beans do and so it just makes a lot of very small, hard to filter bits.This grind of tea needs to be in an espresso machine or else you will get floaties.  I tried this tea three ways: espresso, regular drip coffee, and loose in boiling water and strained later.  It had to be strained 3 times to get most of the floaters out of it, and while I'm okay with some actual tea leaves in other brands occasionally making it into the cup, this fine grain floaty stuff really put me off for some reason.  When you make it as you do espresso coffee, however, you really concentrate the taste and it becomes nearly undrinkable.The taste was the same every time, very strong, bitter to the point of smelling a bit dirty, with an acidic sweetness that lingered on the tongue for ages.  My husband grabbed the grounds the first time and literally ran them outside, and immediately cleaned the coffee pot to make sure the taste did not affect the machine later.  He adamantly refused to even be in the house when I attempted the tea twice more.For people like us who like nothing in our tea except maybe a little lemon, a tea like this that must be doctored heavily isn't really our thing anyway.  But one of the reviews here recommended the tea for Thai Iced Teas, which I tried.  That was the best result of the 3 attempts at using the tea, but I still like the kinds of teas you can get in restaurants or international food stores much better than this tea.We're big tea drinkers in this house, and at any given time have at least 7 types of tea in the house.  I really don't believe our dislike of the tea was a case of unfamiliarity.  The price is also quite a lot, considering we often buy our tea online at gourmet shops for $7-$10 per 4 oz.

column9: Good Rooibos (but I'm not diggin' the espresso strength thing)
column10: I am a Rooibos junkie. I have been drinking it for a few years and adore it. I can only tolerate limited caffeine, early in my day or I'll be up and cranky and not ready to face the world the following day.  Rooibos, in a regular tea strength, with milk is a caffeine free and still tasty (tastes like black tea, when brewed properly, with a little less of the note of bitterness)...I also love espresso drinks and worked for a long time as a barista in a cafe. So I figured this would be the perfect blend for me...I followed the bag directions but as I am sans espresso machine I prepared an entire pot in my trusty Bodum french press.I guess a person who enjoys a straight espresso might enjoy this, but without sweetener and milk it really did taste like superconcentrated, over-brewed regular tea.  I added milk and that dry, bitterness was still clear as a bell and not enjoyable.So I dumped the RedEspresso and started fresh. I prepared my usual cup of afternoon Rooibos, using my usual amounts (much less than that suggested for espresso prep on the package) and yum. Perfection.So would I buy this tea again?Sure. It is packaged well and secure, it seems to be high quality rooibos, and I can get it from Amazon.com so I probably will order this again, for use as a regular rooibos.

I made the Red Espresso Rooiboos Tea Espresso in a slow drip coffee maker.  I was not fond of the stand-alone flavor.  I am use to drinking white teas and green teas without adding any flavors.  This tea had a pleasant taste when we added raw honey or flavored creamer.  It left a rust colored powder residue in my coffee maker - which did not disappear after several pots of coffee preparation.  The filter holder had to be removed and washed to remove the residue.  If you are interested in the anti-oxidant benefits - go for it.  It does not suit my taste buds.

Let me first start off by saying it doesn't, NOT ONE OUNCE, taste like espresso, coffee, or anything similar. It tastes like tea, PERIOD.Now with that out of the way on to the rest of the review.When you first open the package you are hit with this odd, earthy smell... not something that most people would find pleasant. I've had a lot of teas, but this one takes the prize for the oddest smelling.After trying to figure out whether or not I wanted to drink something that smelled that odd I went ahead and added a fair amount (three tablespoons) to my four cup Mr. Coffee. The last thing I wanted to do was make a large pot of the stuff and end up throwing it out. A few minutes (about eight) pass and I hear the distinct "slurping" noise indicating that the coffee maker was at the end of its cycle and go to get me a cup of Red Espresso. Odd thing was the coffee carafe was only half filled up... odd, right? So I carefully pull out the coffee basket and to my surprise it still had two cups of water/tea in it literally 1/8" away from spilling out everywhere. So be VERY careful when using this in an drip coffee machine as the tea seems to clog the filters more then coffee ever would.As for taste, it's not great, but it isn't awful. The taste I get out of it is very similar to a good black tea without the bitterness. And that is one thing this tea has over some of the others, doesn't matter how strong you make it, it doesn't get bitter.Personally, I wouldn't buy it. The taste is nowhere near espresso, thus you are left with nothing more then expensive loose tea that smells odd.Pros:Comes in a resealable pouch.Doesn't get bitter.Cons:Doesn't taste like espresso.Very odd smell, before, during, and after the steeping process.Kinda spendy, I would hope that it would at least taste like mediocre coffee for this price.Seems to backup drip coffee makers really easily, so be careful!

This is fine. It's just not all that.Perhaps if I had special equipment that would make it without getting little floaties in my cup, I would have given it more stars. (I used a fine mesh strainer and poured the boiling water through twice). And perhaps if I didn't get an unimaginable headache a half hour or so after drinking it...I might have gone for three stars. (Unsure whether this caused the headache--I have to try it one more time). But, the end result tasted like tea...nothing special and at 11.70 per bag--uh, I'd rather go for Celestial Seasonings if I want some caffeine-free tea-beverage-drink.SO if you have an espresso machine and want to branch out into tea, this might be for you--otherwise go for some loose-leaf and steep the hell out of it.

As one of the previous reviewer, I'm a tea drinker, always straight without anything else. At first I thought this was coffee mixed with tea and not being a coffee fan that did not resonate well.But then realized that this is just ground tea. However it's not even tea. I had not heard about this South African plant before, but it's not tea even though the smell and taste remind me of a very dark, steeped for too long and too bitter black tea.I did try with the recommended serving size, 4 spoons, and then reduced as this is really dark. They only show it on the packaging drunk with milk or cream or fruit juice. I only tried it like I like tea, so without anything and it's too strong/bold/powerful... it's not a complex taste, just quite ... raw.I find the idea attractive for people who want to quit drinking coffee (hence the not just 1 star) but this is not for me :)

column9: Not A Good Espresso Substitute but OK for Rooibos Chai
column10: I am an avid tea drinker who turned to the drink after realizing my body can't really tolerate coffee. I enjoy Rooibos on occasion and use it for chai when serving to people who are sensative to caffine.One important point about Rooibos is that it isn't technically tea it doesn't come from the Camellia Sinensis fmaily and therefore is considered an herbal.  It's a common mistake to label things which aren't true tea as teas, but a bigger mistake would be to label this "espresso".The only thing Red Espresso has in common with Espresso (aside from how you may chose to prepare it) is how it is ground.  When dealing with herbals and teas the more surface area that the water has contact with when you brew it, the more bitter the resulting beverage. With Red Espresso, rather than getting a sweet and clean tasting beverage, that you'd get from traditionally prepared rooibos, you get one which is much more bitter and sharp.I tried preparing this tea a number of different ways and found it took a lot to get the water to grounds ratio right. With only one exception I was never quite pleased with the resulting beverage.  The best luck I had with Red Espresso was to put it on the stovetop in water and then add chai spices to the mix, drain through a strainer and then adding milk and sweetner.I recognize people will turn to products like this for the health benefits, but I think they'll be disappointed with the experience of drinking this like coffee. For a much better coffee substitute I recommend Choffy which approximates the taste of coffee much closer.But if you're looking to give up your regular cup-o-joe for tea, this isn't the way to go. You'd be much better served picking up some Yunnan Gold or an Assam black tea, brewing it strong and adding milk and sweetener (if desired). If you're set on rooibos then look for the full unground needles to use to brew a much more pleasant cup.

column9: Love Teas, Just Not This One
column10: To give you a bit of background, I drink tea every single day, several times a day.  Not your typical American bag tea, but loose tea.  I like the variety of flavors available in loose teas.  I enjoy Rooibos and other herbal teas, White teas, Green teas, and Black teas.  Basically, I should own stock in Teavana since I drink so much of their tea.  I also found a phenomenal tea from Stockholm.  These teas are much better than your standard Orange Pekoe and Black or bagged teas in Starbucks or my local grocer.  That said, this product intrigued me and I figured I would give it a chance.  We only brewed it straight in our drip coffee maker.  No foam and such that was shown on the package...Here are the pros and cons we found:Pros:*health benefits - but I get that with the teas I already drink*seems easier to get more concentrated flavor (if you want that)*Cappuccino or other methods could be good if you're trying to replace coffee with healthier alternative (I still would just opt for loose tea since the deep, rich flavor of coffee isn't "there" with this product.)Cons:*flavor was ok, a bit heavy, not spectacular (on the other hand, the teas I drink each day are complex, varied in taste, and refreshing)*texture was off - usually I don't think of teas as having much of a texture but there was a definite difference due to the ground nature of this product - felt "off"*It reminded me of how creamed corn is the leftovers.  I wonder if the leaves used to make this were so small they were ground up in hopes of still making a profit.  I could be wrong or pessimistic...

column9: Not my cup of tea...or expresso
column10: I love coffee...and I love tea, but this really left me wondering what I was drinking and why.  It isn't either one really, and didn't catch my interest as something novel and new either.Unfortunately, none of my taste test victims were thrilled with it either, whether they were coffee or tea fans.  I can't recommend it.  It just didn't please our palates.

This review comes from drinking it out of a coffee maker.- Earthy (red/dark brown) color- Distinct smell (a bit like hay)- the doubleshot suggestion seems to be quite strong. I would say stronger than most teas I've had.A friend who drinks a lot of tea said it reminds him of Postum tea.Most people who tried it (I shared it in the office) said something along the lines of: "Hmmm... Interesting". It wasn't the most positive response, but nobody seemed to dislike it. I felt similarly. It is interesting, but didn't sweep me off my feet. Co-workers did go for seconds when I made another pot.Obviously, this is tea, so don't expect it to taste like regular coffee espresso.note: I may edit this later if I try it prepared in a different way.

I used a real espresso machine (not a steam toy) and it made an excellent rooibos espresso.  A very good substitute for coffee espresso if you are trying to cut caffeine.  No need to tamp (pack) the rooibos.  I use a 1/8 cup measure, run the machine until drips come out, turn the machine off for 30 seconds, and then fill to 3 ounces in the brew cup.  At a little agave, and 5 ounce of steamed soy milk ( or milk).  An excellent cup better than Starbucks.

column9: Ignore the packaging....its a  great product  !
column10: I don't believe that the packaging on this item really does it justice.From the packaging I couldn't figure out if this product was for  an expresso machine or a coffee machine or what.A lot of my confusion was from the pictures and service suggestions featuring what to me looks like sugar and cream.The title didn't help either "expresso " ! I didn't know what this was going to be a coffee or a tea.Well , what it turned out to be ---is the finest cut tea leaf in bulk form that I have ever seen in my life.Rooibos ia a red tea that is very  highly sought after. It has one of the biggest amounts of healthful antioxidants , minerals and other  just plain good stuff known to man.It is mostly seen in tea bag form.This tea does wonders for your overall well being and gives you a helping hand to health. There is nothing  else like it--not green nor white nor black. Its special...very special.Now with this large sized  bag---you DO NOT have to fool around with the small and hard to find tea bags anymore. This loose tea can be brewed  in a machine ,put into any loose tea holder be it  ball or spoon style or used in the pots that have that special  filter compartment for loose tea built for it.Add honey or other sweetners if you want or milk I suppose...but I only drink my "au naturale " . I am thinking HEALTH when I drink this tea not Coffee light and sweet.I am filled with wonder over what I ultimately found inside this awfully designed bag.I cannot believe that people use cream and sugar with this.........as the pictures show on the designs of this bag.But again its from South Africa and maybe thats how the English , Dutch people there take their Tea.But let me tell you again..that it is the finest , fine cut Rooboos tea you can find in a wonderfully made pouch........that has a  horrible design job and bad serving suggestions.This ones a WINNER !!!!!!!!!!!!!!

I really want to share what an amazing food product this is, in my opinion. It tastes absolutely delicious, can be prepared and drunk like coffee, and has tonnes of health benefits! (See their website.)I should note that I was already a fan of rooibos tea and drink it regularly. The preparation method I am having most success with is using a stovetop espresso maker. These little coffee makers are super easy (and kind of fun) to use and very easy to clean up. The extraction is deep red and quite strong, which makes it feel to me a lot like coffee.I decided to try this out because I am not drinking coffee right now for health reasons, but love my morning ritual of making coffee and drinking a hot, strong, energizing brew. This has fit the bill perfectly, and my body has adjusted well to being caffeine-free for the most part.I drink mine with a fair amount of vanilla almond milk and a bit of sweetener - I'm sure milk and honey would be delicious too!Highly, highly recommended!
This caffeine free red tea was pleasant but rather bland to my taste though with very mild fruity notes. It simply doesn't catch my fancy or excite my taste buds.

Although this is a little pricey it is well worth it for it does help me to relax and sleep and it is a healthy alternative instead of sleeping pills. It claims to help your immune and digestive system. I like it with a little honey, milk, cinnamon and nutmeg.

Made this in a espresso pot on the stove.  Very good if you are a tea drinker.  Does not taste or resemble coffee or real espresso.  However, very tasty if made like a latte.  Much cheaper than Starbucks everyday, and so so good for your health.

I couldn't get used to this.  Rooibos tea has a distinctive, flowery/herbal flavor which some people love.  To me it never seems like a drink for grown-ups.  If you like it, this is a great brand and an easy way to fix your tea.

I was initially unsure what to make of this ..  I have always equated decaffeinated coffee with non-alcoholic beer.  what's the point?  However while this particular item may not appeal to me in some ways, I was drawn in by the taste and texture.  While it is a bit difficult to make, it has a very unusual but likeable taste, and the texture is almost creamy.  It tastes nothing like "real" coffee.  The actual product inside the bag looks like sawdust, and is so finely ground that pieces will inevitably make their way into your final brew.  Beyond this minor annoyance, I would have no qualms with drinking this again.  The taste takes some getting used to, but if you happen to be pregnant, or caffeine sensitive, this coffee is for you.  I like mine with a bit of milk.  Recommended if you're into this sort of thing, or just want to try something new.

I gave up caffeine 6 months ago and it was only possible because of traditional rooibos;  however, I really missed the luxury of a good espresso or cappuccino.  Red Espresso is almost that product.You really can use a Bialletti to get a good strong base; but the thick, red liquid with its lovely creme is no espresso.  It has a very strong tea taste, almost over brewed and a lot of the tannin flavours that are normally so delicate in rooibos are suddenly the most prevalent aspect of the beverage.It is not without merit:  red con leche; red latte, and red cappuccino are all wonderfully comforting and tasty drinks that are in many ways superior to their decaffeinated coffee alternatives, but without milk the flavour was not as enjoyable as a nice cup of brewed rooibos.

column9: Tea in the automatic espresso maker
column10: I'll start this by stating that I've never been much of a tea drinker.  When I do have tea, I find myself consciously criticizing it as being too weak.  I've always left tea bags or loose tea to steep far longer than most, and for tea bags, I've always used a spoon to squeeze any remaining "concentrate" from the bag in my attempt to make it as strong as possible.  Seeing the Red Espresso peaked my interest, particularly because I recently splurged on a semi-automatic espresso maker, which does everything automatically except for steaming the milk.I was certainly surprised by the smell upon opening the bag; it was a strong smell, not pleasant, but was similar to an odor of laundry that's been forgotten for days in the washer.  Fortunately, this isn't highly apparent in the finished product.  My automatic espresso maker requires the use of an override function when using pre-ground coffee, or in this case, tea.  One limitation to using the override feature is the somewhat limited quantity of powder that can be used - about 2 tablespoons full.  I've found my machine doesn't make good espresso with this little coffee, so was curious how the tea would come out.Following the instructions, I brewed several shots, using the water quantity as the variable.  The first shots were weak and tepid, similar to the few coffee shots I've tried to product from pre-ground coffee.  When pulling back on the water to about half, I was able to get quite strong and flavorful shots of tea, which has a nice rich taste to it.  Everyone's preference varies, and I'm sure my taste in tea would probably be too strong for a usual tea drinker, but the ability to vary the water is the key to success for not brewing weak tea.  I tried Red Espresso without milk, with milk, without Equal, and with Equal.  I think my favorite was one of the shots pulled with minimal water (strong), with a little milk and about 1/2 of an equal packet.After trying this tea I can't say I'm one of the new consumers, and I believe the limitations of my espresso maker may have caused some of the poor results I experienced.  The machine I have is designed with the principle of fresh grinding beans, a good tamp, and plenty of extraction.  Despite my efforts, I wasn't able to get full extraction from this tea, and being my first experience with espresso tea, I'm not sure if there is something I could have done to extract more.  I give it 3 stars.
I enjoyed this, for something different.  The taste is nice and it makes good lattes and espresso.  I use it in my Keurig brewer and it works well.

column9: Distinctive color, passable flavor, but not a coffee substitute
column10: Red Espresso Rooibos Tea is marketed as a coffee substitute, and it isn't.  The flavor is a passable tea flavor, but lacks the body to make it coffee-ish.Taken on its own merits, it isn't bad.  The flavor is very similar to a black tea, but the color is a deep red.  Prepared like a brewed coffee (drip or french press) the flavor was mild compared to coffee, but strong compared to tea.  Prepared in an espresso maker, the flavor gained so character, but was very thin compared to espresso.Meh.  If you're trying to get caffine out of your life, it might have something to offer you.  It was interesting to try, but I won't order it again.E. M. Van Court

column9: Works with the Keurig machine too!
column10: Red Espresso® Rooibos Tea Espresso, 8.8-Ounce Pouches:When I ordered this tea, I hadn't realized it required an actual espresso machine. So it sat going unused. I wanted to bring it over to my friend who has a really fancy (read expen$ive) espresso machine, but as is normal, it needs repairs. So the tea sat.Today I was in the mood for a cup of tea, so was going to do what I usually do. Take a teabag and use my Keurig coffee machine to pump hot water in to the cup and brew it.  A lightning bolt hit! I have an unused "My K-Cup" cartridge for the Keurig that has sat unused. I gave up grinding when I got it and the My K-Cup came in the Costco kit. What if I put the redespresso tea in the My K-Cup. Worst that would happen is I get out my teabag and do it the old way. I measured in about 1 1/8 tablespoons in to the basket. Sealed it and popped it into the machine.  I chose the 8oz. size and pumped a mug of tea. By gosh it worked! I got a really beautiful dark red mug of tea. The filter held the leaves perfectly and it tasted GREAT! Really rich and bold. I'm not a tea efficianato so I can't give all the flowery details BUT I can say it was tasty and it worked. So I can recommend this if you have a Keurig and want to try this with your My K-Cup cartridge. Thumbs up!

column9: Tastes good but definitely not like espresso
column10: My husband and I tried this red espresso tea and have had mixed reviews.  Initially he thought it was great and I thought it was not-so-great, and now we he would give it a three while I would give it a five, so I split the difference for the four stars.Initially I expected this drink to have a taste in the vicinity of espresso.  It does not taste like espresso at all and it did not taste like tea either.  We prepared the tea per the package directions of using a cappucino machine and adding steamed, frothed milk and some honey.  All subsequent times we flavored by using plain sugar instead of honey and I thought that was better.  The taste of this drink grew on me over time.While it was a nice drink, the product is pricey and I probably wouldn't buy it again.

column9: Different and Pleasant Tasting Tea Beverage
column10: I have been a tea connoisseur for a number of years so I was pretty excited about trying this Red espresso Rooibos tea.  It is definitely pleasant tasting and can easily become a substitute for coffee and tea drinkers who wish to cut down their caffeine intake.  Personally I think that caffeine is part of the magic of tea and coffee and drinking these beverages without the stimulant effect of caffeine is like eating chocolate that is not sweet.Though this tea definitely has a unique appearance and taste, it would be great to have a regular caffeinated version that can be consumed for its taste and stimulant effect.*** Positive Points: ***+ Unique taste for a tea+ claims to have the same antioxidants as normal tea*** Negative Points: ***- No caffeinated version for people who like the stimulant effects of tea and coffee- Somewhat pricey- A bit difficult to prepare for the uninitatedOverall:A unique and different type of tea that most coffee and tea lovers should try at least once.

column9: Neither tea, nor espresso, and meh in flavor
column10: Let me start by saying I love tea, and have cupboards full of it, which I drink regularly.  I also love my coffee, and drink espresso regularly (though mostly for the caffeine, rather than the flavor) -- all of which may of course leave something to be said for my neurons.I was intrigued by the premise of this new sounding substance, so I tried it happily.  I was unimpressed by the flavor, however -- it wasn't quite bitter, but it was everything approaching bitter that I could think of.  I just didn't want to finish it.  It was thin, like water, but felt thick on my tongue (weird to type, weird to read, but even weirder to feel, I assure you).  And I love rooibos teas, normally.I made this in a French press style pot, but I doubt it would be much better in an espresso machine.While only a semantic distinction, note that this is neither a true "tea" nor an espresso.  And the flavor, well, the flavor left me unimpressed.  I hate throwing things away, but I honestly can't imagine going back to this when I have so many other delicious teas to turn to, and real coffee with the reward of caffeine if I dare to have something slightly bitter-like on my tongue.

column9: This drink doesn't fit in either category.
column10: I am both an avid tea drinker and sort of a manic coffee person.  I have definite likes and dislikes when it comes to both tea and coffee.  This beverage sort of fits into a "no man's land" when it comes to either.  I tried it as espresso (as the name suggests) and ended up with a murky,thick, sludge like drink that was anything "but" espresso.  Next, I tried it as a tea in the finest mesh strainer that I have, same results... terrible.  I tried it hot, I tried it cold.  It was like trying to make a beverage with the fine grit left at the bottom of my vacuum cleaner bag and had about the same appeal.I gave it two stars because rooibos is chocked full of health benefits and it is 'supposed' to be good for you.  That presupposes that you can stand to drink it.  I can't.
