Rooibos tea is available in blends from major tea outlets such as TEVANA and I have tried it from other sources with no difficulty in preparation or loss of flavor.  It is not the rooibos that I object to, it is the way this manufacturer chooses to process it and way you will have to scramble to find a way to fix it that you can at least drink it.There are too many enjoyable flavors of tea and coffee for me to sample without all the irritation and drama that this product causes me to go through.I was not in any way happy that they chose to call it "espresso" as it is far from it.  It is as a matter of fact far from anything that I want to experience again.  Go buy some rooibos tea or espresso and enjoy them.  This is a failed experiment and a terribly misleading product in my opinion.

column9: convenient rooibos with a rich flavor
column10: I like rooibos tea but don't drink it often because it is a little troublesome to prepare. You have to steep it for a few minutes, and since Rooibos tea leaves are small (even a fine mesh tea ball can't always strain them) you often get leaves in your drink and a mess in your teapot.I used a manual coffee maker to prepare the Red Espresso. It was great!The special espresso grind gives you rich, strong rooibos flavor in a very short time, without risk of over-steeping or the mess of leaves.Making a latte out of the resulting liquid yields a rich, luxurious drink. It also makes a delicious iced tea.The packaging says caffeine-free, but for me, the tea seemed a little stimulating anyhow. I felt pretty energized after drinking it. So for me it's a good choice for caffeine-free energy.Only one thing to note: once or twice, I noticed that the ground rooibos clogged my coffee filter.

Red Espresso is a great idea for health minded persons who love brewed drinks such as lattes. This is high-quality rooibos ground fine to be used in an espresso machine.Rooibos is an herb traditionally used for tea in Africa. It has many health benefits, is very mild and non-acidic. It is also completely caffeine free! Rooibos is good for the stomach and there are promising studies showing it helps with insomnia and headaches.Rooibos has a mild, earthy flavor that is very pleasant with milk or cream. The flavor is not to be compared with espresso or tea. It has no bitterness or bite, tannins or acidity.

column9: Sorry, no cafe revolution for us.  Marketing letdown.
column10: My husband was thrilled when this arrived-- he'd been intending to buy some to try.  However, we were both less than impressed.My husband's an obsessive master of the espresso machine, and despite several attempts, his shots of Red Espresso included almost none of the rich crema pictured in its advertising.We're both espresso and tea drinkers, but this hybrid of the two left us pretty cold.  It's novel to make tea with the espresso machine, I guess, but grassy strong muddy tea isn't my idea of a good drink.  Adding milk and sweetener helps, but it's still not ringing my bells-- or my husband's.  The taste lingers in your mouth, and since we didn't much care for the taste, that's pretty unpleasant.It's pretty expensive, too, at over twenty dollars a pound and about a dollar a serving.  The claims on antioxidants are interesting (5x more than green tea?  really?  according to who?), but there are plenty of foods we actually like with antioxidants in them-- I think we'll pass on this one.  I'd rather drink five glasses of the Republic of Tea's orange spice green tea than choke down a shot (or sweetened latte) of this stuff.Bleugh.

column9: just don't drink it straight; as a mix it's quite refreshing
column10: The idea for making tea in a coffeepot doesn't occur to an average person, and for that Red Espresso is to be commended. However, for a tea drinker like myself, finding a coffeepot to make tea isn't always the easiest solution.And yet, you can ignore all the reviewers who say that they were unable to try this drink without having a cappuccino machine. Although one needs a coffeemaker to make the tea - any coffeemaker from an expansive espresso to a simple drip machine will do.When I was making this rooibos tea, I had to go to work to make it and coworkers drifted in from their workspace to find out from where the luscious, rich smell of tea was emanating. a few were turned off by the idea of drinking tea from a coffeepot, but most were willing to entertain the idea.For them, just like for myself, the taste seemed interesting. By itself Red Espresso drink is too strong and too demanding. When mixed with apple juice though, the tea absolves all the acidic properties of the juice and the juice highlights the flavor of the tea. The tea becomes subtle and refreshing and spontaneous at the same time.I have yet to try other variations of this drink (the website has quite a few suggestions), but I found that drinking it as an iced tea is sufficient to keep me pleased ad to make me want to buy more of it (and to grab a coffeemaker while I'm at it).

column9: Solid product - Maybe not for everyone
column10: I drink a fair amount of coffee, and have for many years.  I drink some tea (mostly green and Earl Grey or Darjeeling) and have had Roobois tea before.True to its name, this stuff produces a super-concentrated Roobois flavored beverage.  I don't own an espresso maker and brewed it in French presses without much problem. The tea itself is very fine and you need to make sure your press screen has no holes in it and fits snugly or you'll be sipping red sand. I drank it in the evening and had no jitters or caffeine-type sleeplessness.When mixed with honey and milk, it reminds me of Thai tea (which is often black tea colored with tamarind and ends up with a similar color to this tea).  I hit their website and checked out the recipes, but preferred to add a bit of vanilla sugar, half and half, and cinnamon.  When I drank it straight, the flavor was kind of earthy and I found the flavor much better hot than after it sat in the press for about 10 minutes.Notes: this beverage is orange-red and will probably stain clothing. Be careful.

This tea has an excellent rooibos flavor that I really enjoy. I made this tea three ways so here are the three short reviews of each method:Drip Coffee Pot: The package says you can do it, but the tea swells up and backed up my coffee maker something fierce. Taste was full flavored but not too heavy, despite missing a good portion of water that was supposed to drip through and never did. After this incident I decided I would try a different way and just tossed a coffee filter tied with tea in the bottom and tied off at at the top with some cotton thread into the bottom of the pot and ran plain hot water through the maker and it turned out much better. Would achieve the same results from the stove and boiling water, too.French Press: This was the best way of making the tea so far. Since the tea tended to swell up when I added water to it, using the press was the best method because it's pretty difficult to clog a french press.Espresso Machine: I enjoy drinking hot tea for maybe a half hour at a time so there was no real benefit in making a small amount. I still had difficulties with it brewing properly and the whole process just wasn't worth it.

This product brings rooibos tea out of the boring closet into the bright light of day. When made using enough tea, the flavor is deep and intense, and fabulous when mixed with foaming hot soy milk in a latte. Most rooibos tea is, to my taste, either wimpy or slightly bitter - this is neither. It is full-bodied and delicious, so full-bodied that it belies its status as a caffeine-free beverage. The jolt comes from the intensity of the flavor, not from caffeine. My only  quibble is that the directions on the bag are entirely imprecise -- we really had to experiment to get the correct proportions. But, the effort was worth it for the delicious result.

This is called Tea Espresso but it has no caffeine.  I don't know what I was expecting when I got this in the mail, but I don't like it.  I was hoping for something with an interesting flavor but it just tastes like run of the mill tea.  I probably will not use the remain product I have and wouldn't recommend this to people unless they specifically wanted something that has a high antioxidant content or is caffeine free.

if you like honeybush or red, rooibos tea, this is really good.  i like it with milk and honey, or whipped milk like a latte.  it does take alot of the tea to make a good strong brew.  definetly a nice treat for the tea or coffee lover.  it is decaf also, which is good if you like a coffee treat too close to bed time.

This has a very rich and robust taste. I have enjoyed the Bush Teas and I enjoy this just as much. This makes a great ice tea drink or hot tea. This also makes a great Lattie. You will enjoy this anyway you try it. The drinks are very simple to make. I recommend this product to everyone.

Ever since reading Alexander McCall Smith's The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency (Book 1) and learning about bush tea, another name for Rooibos Tea, as I understand it, I've been a fan. I've noticed some coffee house chains offering Rooibos drinks and the ones that I have tried are quite tasty. I used my regular low end espresso maker to make a pot of Red Espresso® Rooibos Tea Espresso and it turned out great. It has a pleasant smell, I think, and a beautiful color. I just mixed it with milk. It tastes a lot better sweet, but even without adding anything has a slight natural sweetness. This is a convenient way to enjoy "Red Espresso". I'm really enjoying this tea.

This drink had an odd smell and flavor. Hard to describe,kind of woody.I never drink my tea with milk or sugar. So for comparisons sake did not want to jazz this up with it. I do not see myself purchasing this or adding it to my wonderful assortments of teas that I have on my counter. I love and have various rooibos tea in my kitchen. I am not a daily tea drinker. I actually prepare it for special alone times. This brand of rooibos tea was too sweet and not a flavor that I would want to turn to again.

I made a pot of this up in a percolator, no worries. Good, dense flavor and interesting color. It's actually a very dark walnutty type of red. The taste is somewhere between herbal, gently spicy and dense. Not quite coffee but definitely not weak. I'd say this is about as dense in flavor as a good British Black Tea, like PG tips.I added cream and sugar and found it to be quite lovely. It may do as an alternative for caffeinated coffee because it is so very strong. I went back to the percolator to make up a second batch and discovered that the groans had plugged up the filter basket.It's a bit thicker after it's hydrated than I expected. Definitely something you could get used to, though. I find myself wondering how this would be served up like an ice coffee - twice as strong with loads of ice.
I like to drink tea a lot and try different types of tea this one has a different flavor strong and a little bit fermented but I liked, is a good tea alternative and a healthy one.

I really enjoyed drinking this tea. In fact, I'm nearing the end of the pouch and ready to order more. It is very mild and not bitter at all due to the low tannin content. The flavor is mildly sweet and very smooth. Mixed with orange or apple juice, it's great served cold over ice as well.Considering the fact that this tea has very high antioxidant levels, I'll be continuing to drink this a couple of times a day. I did find the tea made me hungry though, so if weight loss is your goal, this tea will probably stimulate your appetite so it would be best to drink it before a meal.

column9: good tea - not for coffee drinkers
column10: I happen to be a coffee and a tea drinker so I liked Red Espresso Rooibus Tea but I was disappointed.  For some reason, I expected this tea to taste more like coffee.  Instead, I had a very tasty cup of tea with steamed milk and sugar.My espresso machine has been loaned to one of my college kids so I chose to use my Keurig B70 Gourmet Single-Cup Home Brewing System with the Keurig My K-Cup Reusable Coffee Filter.  The tea is a very fine grind, what you would expect for espresso machines, and I carefully measured it into the filter and attempted to tamp it down.  I didn't have much luck as dried tea doesn't compress like finely ground coffee.  I set my Keurig to the smallest cup setting and the temperature to the highest and pressed the brew button.The tea came out with a lovely red color and I added steamed milk and sugar to my taste and took a sip of this red concoction.  Good tea - I was expecting something a little stronger with a little of the bitterness of coffee.  Still, good tea and it's decaf!The bag the tea comes it strongly recommends you use an espresso machine and suggests you log on to their website to see if your machine is compatible with their tea.  Because the tea packs differently than coffee, check out their website.  You wouldn't want to have something go terribly wrong during the brew process.  I knew I'd be able to use my Keurig to at least taste this product because you can buy tea in k-cups but I suspect the tea will be more flavorful brewed for espresso or in a french press.

column9: a very good alternative to diet soda works great iced as well.
column10: I like this one reason is cause it can be used in  various coffee/tea appliances and is quiet versatile. I even tried it in my Mr.Coffee iced tea maker Mr. Coffee TM3-2 3-Quart Ice Tea Maker .Minute I saw this  I thought I would simply give it a try as a iced tea, as I am currently in the process of giving up diet soda after reading countless articles on the net and news that is just isn't as good for us as say juices, teas,etc. I find this 'red' tea to be very mild and mellow as compared to say whites and greens which can be a bit bitter. It's also excellent as hot too. I still have one diet soda a day but in between I like drinking iced teas and crystal lite ,diet kool-aids etc. so in the summer I love to dig out my iced tea maker and have it around and found this tea in particular to be very delicious. I will definitly order some more so I can have it around the house during the summer for company for those who don't do coffee or diet sodas that much.

column9: Great idea, but a bit pulpy
column10: I though this was a great idea; I love tea and coffee!  I like strong beverages.  This combines all together.  The only thing is it is very pulpy coming from a regular drip coffeemaker, so I am thinking there is a better way to make this?  The taste is not bad, it is just that it is quite dense.  I am not sure I find the smell very enticing, either.  So, I am going to give it another try.  I had it with sweetener and coffeemate powder, so maybe I will try the honey that is suggested.  and the milk.

column9: An interesting alternative to morning joe.
column10: Red espresso is made in the espresso machine just like coffee. It even has crema like espresso but tastes like a rich tea. With cream and splenda, it is a nice hot beverage. This product is good if you want to try something different, but it tastes nothing like coffee. I would drink it occassionally for health benefits since it is rich in anti-oxidents but not a beverage I would crave.

I love tea. I drink all kinds, but mostly strong, black teas. I drink my tea plane. No sugar, honey, milk or cream.This tea however was not for me.Upon opening the bag, I lowered my nose in a little to take a sniff and if burned my sinuses. That was a new one for me. I believe it was because it is so finely ground that the first smell went right up my nose. So I don't recommend taking a whiff right after you open the bag.After I go my since of smell back, I carefully smelled it again and found it had a 2 aromas to it. One was a similar smell of a Red Bush/Cranberry/Orange tea from Harney teas called African Autumn. That part was nice. The second smell was a bit of a hay smell to it. It reminded me of the alfalfa we feed our guinea pigs.The resealable bag was nice, since tea has a shelf life when it comes to flavor. No complaints there.The taste was the same as the smell. Half good (the Red Bush flavor like the African Autumn tea), and half not so good (the part that has an flavor/aroma of Alfalfa).If you like a tea with a earthy taste to it, this may be the one for you. However, it wasn't to my liking.

column9: Interesting Taste, Needs to be Prepared Right
column10: I'm not quite sure what I expected from this product, and after sampling it I'm not quite sure what it is.This is actually not a "tea" at all, but rather Roobios (Aspalathus Linearis), ground up into what the manufacturer calls "Espresso ground". In actuality, the ground is a bit more course than espresso.First of all, I must describe my espresso setup. I am using a Briel Lido espresso machine, which is a manual machine that makes coffee at about 180 degrees and has a 15 milibar pump.The instructions say to use 4 rounded teaspoons for a shot of espresso. I found that to be about two standard scoops. However, when I tried that, my machine had problems - unlike coffee, the "tea" doesn't provide a seal, and the first time I tried it, I had to hold the handle to keep the "tea" from going all over the place and ejecting the stuff all over. I discovered that using ONE scoop would work OK, although on some cups I still had to hold the handle closed.As to the flavor, well, it has it's own distinctive flavor, that is different from any "natural" tea. I did find out that you need to have boiling water for this tea to extract correctly. My machine allows me to heat the water either to about 180 degrees, or to make it steaming hot (to be diverted to the froth mechanism, but it will go out through the coffee filter is you turn on the pump). When one uses boiling water, the tea tastes good. However, if your coffee maker does not allow you to divert the boiling water to your coffee, this tea will not taste right. Actually, although I abhor them, this tea would make well with a steam powered espresso maker (which boils the water to force water through the coffee). It might also do very well with the traditional stove top Italian espresso maker, where the water is forced up from the bottom, or even an old fashioned perculator. I don't think it would taste good in a standard coffee maker, because in my opinion the water needs to be forced through the "tea".I can't really describe the flavor. It is not very bitter (I drink it straight), and is is somewhat "earthy". OK, some people might say it tastes like what one would think tree bark might taste like, but then it is a natural "Tea"; it isn't going to taste like any normal tea or coffee drink. When prepared with boiling water, I actually liked the flavor - but it isn't my favorite hot drink.The packaging suggests making cappucino and latte, but there is no way that this was strong enough (in my opinion) to be able to make those two drinks. I didn't try it iced.Recommended? Well, I don't know. I gave it four stars for it's unique flavor, the very cool red color, and it's supposed health benefits. I'm not a natural foods person, so I don't know if any product health claims are correct. If you are into these kinds of natural "teas", then this one is worth a shot (pardon the pun).

I am a big tea drinker, with only the occasional coffee, but this product was just too malty for me. By "malty", I would also describe the flavor as having a "fermented" flavor to it which could not be made "tasty" by the addition of milk and sugar. The only way I have found to make this product tasty is by disregarding the directions and brewing it much weaker (or by mixing it with other tea blends). I was not able to enjoy this product as an "espresso", but brewing it as normal rooibos tea in my Zarafina tea maker produces a lovely cup of tea.Is this review helpful? Let me know. Please vote. :-)

column9: Break your espresso addiction with this healthy alternative
column10: Let's get this straight up front: Rooibos tea espresso is tea, not coffee. Personally, I'm a coffee drinker by day and a tea drinker by night. Rooibos red tea reminded me of hot, brewed Chinese Oolong tea or Asian varieties other than green tea. It is earthy and slightly sweet without the bitter aftertaste I equate with decaffeinated coffee.Packed with antioxidants (the company claims five times more than green tea) this drink will appeal to the health-conscious; naturally caffeine-free makes this a suitable beverage to enjoy in the late afternoon, evening and just before bedtime.I drank mine straight, as I do my coffee. My wife enjoyed her cup with Miller's Honey. We're going to try the fresh red recipe next - a double shot of red espresso Rooibos mixed with chilled fruit juice (they recommend apple juice) and served over the rocks.In summary, while I can't attest to the health claims - relieving insomnia, easing digestive disorders and calming the central nervous system - I can tell you this is an enjoyable beverage for a person who enjoys Asian teas. If you are looking for a coffee-flavored substitute you'll be disappointed. Rating: Five stars.

My cup of tea was delicious and very tasty.  Of course, I did add cream and sugar and it's hard for anything to taste bad with cream and sugar...When I opened the bag, it had a very nice earthy smell.  I used a stove top espresso machine Bialetti Moka Express 3-Cup Stovetop Percolator, a spare that we don't use for our coffee, and the tea smelled marvelous while it was 'perking'.  I couldn't wait to try it!The color of the tea was an amazing, deep red.  The aroma as I poured the tea in my cup was wonderful.  The fragrance hinted at the rich flavor of the tea.After I added my cream and sugar and had a sip, I was very pleased.  The tea was delectable and full of flavor.  It had a nice feel in my mouth, with a slightly creamy texture.Some folks have a likened it to chai tea and I would agree there are some similarities.  Although this tea does not have the multitude of spices that a chai tea has.My mom was not interested in this tea AT ALL.  In fact, she thought it was terrible.  But, I enjoyed it!

I am not a regular coffee drinker, but I do like a cup now and then. I am a tea drinker, and I enjoy most teas. The ones I don't like get extra sugar and I will finish it off not to waste it. I will not be finishing this bag. This is one of those things that look good on paper. I'm sure some might like it, but I did not, nor did my wife. I was disappointed to find that it does not taste like espresso or any kind of coffee. It's flavor is sharp, and not to my liking. Had it not been marketed as it was, I still do not think I would like the flavor. It's not that I do not like strong teas, it's just that this particular tea had a gritty, dirt-like taste that I could not get past. I wonder how it would be if it were pressed (I do not have one, and I don't know if it will just bring out more of the sharpness). The cost of this tea is another issue. For the price, I think you can create a wonderful blend, and still have money left over for a real espresso...or two. The only thing I can think of is trying to combine this with another tea to try to mask it, however, if you have to do that, something is wrong. I do not see this enhancing the flavor of a blend...though I suspect if you try hard enough you might find a combination that suits you. This certainly was not for us (my wife and I). Top that off with the smell and I was almost ready for another star reduction. It did not bother me as much as it bothered my wife. She had to , "air out," the kitchen. I din't think it was THAT bad, just very different and not very pleasant. I do like the resealable pouch. We resealed it quickly! By no means is this a coffee alternative. It's almost like thinking a vegi-burger (very few of which I actually like) will replace a hamburger. It will not, and neither will this.

First, the technical:  It comes in attractive packaging with a good Ziploc seal that actually works.  I really had high hopes for this and give them an A+ for effort.When you open it, however, you clearly realize this has nothing to do with espresso.  There is a super-fine, orange-red dust that comes out almost like smoke and gets all over things.  Next, the texture of the tea is not small flat-like crushed leaves like normal tea, but smallish woody/grassy splinter-shaped material.  It definitely does not tamp like espresso.  Also, being a tea, it does not brew like espresso.  It seems to take about 1-1/2 shots of water to extract the tea.  For a double-shot, this is 3 ounces or more (in 2 passes).  Next, the tea expands into a relatively hard puck more like particle board.  You will have to do some real banging to dislodge it from the portafilter.  I wound up using a fork which furthers the mess.  The fines also got stuck (a bit) in the screen.  Thus, I found the whole "espresso" brewing process a bit of a farce.Next, the taste.  It does create a nice crema which is sort of surprising.  The aroma and taste remind me distinctly of Thai tea.  The taste is about 1/2 Thai tea and half wood/sawdust.  I personally did not like it and could only finish about 2/3 of a mug (with steamed milk).  I personally would rather just buy Thai tea which is available from a local Asian store for $2 or $3 a pound and brew it in a standard drip coffee pot.  I think this tastes better, is less mess, and is vastly cheaper.  If you've every used Thai tea, you'll recognize the orange-red spice/dust that tends to get all over.I would have given it 1 star, but my wife absolutely loved it.  Maybe it was the novelty or maybe it was that it was like Thai tea, but she really liked it.  Given the price, though, it might not be an every-day type of tea.  I would recommend that if you are familiar with Thai tea and like the taste, then stick with it.  If not, give this a try.  It's worth a shot just for the experience.

I brewed this in my coffee maker and mixed it w/ condensed milk.The result was a taste similar to Thai Tea. I absolutely loved it. It was more like tea as opposed to coffee though. There's a hint of the expresso scent, but overall, it tasted and felt more like Thai Tea.The brew was a nice reddish brown concoction.Actually, I'd highly recommend this product, and plan on buying this product myself for personal and party usage. The only thing I would have preferred would for it to have been a caffeeine beverage as opposed to caffeine free.

I think the name and description is a bit misleading. There is really nothing espresso-like about tea. It simply does not have the depth of flavor that coffee does.However, that being said, this is a very good flavored tea. It is very robust. It is also absolutely delicious as an iced tea with a touch of honey. Sugar just does not bring out the flavor like honey will.If you prefer mild or weak teas then this probably isn't for you. Red tea does have a somewhat unusual flavor if you've never had it but it is worth getting used to!I have had a couple of small problems brewing it in the coffeemaker. The tea tends to float and make a mess in the filter area.

column9: A fancy name for Chinese Red ( black) tea.
column10: At first I thought this was more like instant espresso taste made with a something completely new, similar to tea.  When I got it, it is tea.  It's what Chinese call "red" tea aka black tea.  There's nothing wrong with it, it's just instead of something completely new, it's the same red tea I've had every since.Now, this does teach me a new way to brew tea.  Never thought of using a coffee or espresso machine on tea, and it actually came out pretty good.  We made a drink using this tea with coffee machine, added heavy dose of creamer and sugar - came out like Thai Tea, which you can find in most Chinese Cafe's.  It's a fairly popular drink, good taste.Then tried this with espresso machine, added condensed milk, this came out tasting like royal milk tea, which is a real bonus.  This drink is really expensive, in restaurants, it's about $3-$4 each, and if you buy instant mix it's about $0.50 each and it mixes about 4oz, so with this tea, it's a good deal.Although the item itself isn't something new, but it does bring new ways to enjoy the food.  Use some creativity and this product is fun and tasty!

I am drinking this Red Espresso Rooibos Tea as I write this.  It has a unique flavor....strong but not bitter though it does have a bit of an after taste.  I had to stain the tea because, despite the package instructions, I found it to be too gritty and twiggy when just mixed into water.  Even after staining, just looking into the drink shows lots of bits and pieces but NOW I do not taste or feel them as I drink it. It's like drinking a really dark roast or real expresso cup of coffee but it's really tea.  I've never had this type of tea before but I find it rather interesting and tasty.  Since it has no caffeine, I will be able to drink this after dinner without worries of being kept awake.  I love the fact that it is loaded with antioxidants!  I wish I could find the words to describe the flavor but if you like really strong dark tea, you'll like this one.  I recommend this strong flavored tea!

I was interested in the product as it seemed a good and healthy alternative to my normal choice of decaf expresso. First point to know - this is tea.  From the description and even the packaging it is sometimes easy to confuse with some kind of coffee. According to the packaging, it is quite good for you, with heavy antioxidents, and it also claims to relieve insomnia, help with digestive disorders, and calm your central nervous system.  They offer several recipes for ways to use the product which I did not try.  Unlike most teas, you use coffee preparation techniques to make Redespresso.Per the directions, I did prepare the tea in a french press.  It was a dark red color, and because the tea is finer than coffee, loose tea does get into the liquid.  The flavor was pleasant, but not overly distinctive for a tea.Overall, it was not as tasty as some of my other favorite teas.  It is an interesting idea and preparation, and if the health claims are true it makes for an interesting product when compared to coffee.  However, I suspect I will stick to some of my more flavorful tea alternatives.

column9: It isn't coffee and it isn't tea... so, what is it?
column10: When I first saw this product, I thought that what the company had done was to take tea leaves and market them as a coffee alternative.  I was partially correct: they are marketing this product as a coffee alternative, but it isn't tea.  What we have here are finely-ground rooibos leaves.  Rooibos isn't tea, but when brewed in hot water, it produces a very pleasant tea-like infusion.The directions on the package state that this product can be prepared in an espresso machine (hence the name "red espresso"), as well as in a French press or even an automatic drip coffeemaker.  I don't own an espresso machine and I no longer have a French press, but I do have a very good quality coffeemaker, which I use to make cafe au lait every morning.  (For those not familiar, cafe au lait is similar to a latte, except there's no foam, and you don't necessarily have to use an espresso machine. I use a coffeemaker and I use about 2x or 3x as much ground coffee as one would use for a regular cup of coffee, while using less water; this produces a very concentrated brew that tastes similar to espresso, and I add it to hot milk.)I prepared this product in the same way that I prepare my cafe au lait every day: 4 heaping teaspoons of Red Espresso added to the filter basket, and 8 ounces of water (the "2 cups" mark on the carafe) to the reservoir.Within a few minutes, I had about 4 or 5 ounces of brewed "red espresso" in my carafe.  Where did the other 3 or 4 ounces of water go?  I looked in the filter basket, and that's where it was.  The dust from the finely-ground rooibos must have clogged the filter.  Fortunately it didn't overflow, but beware that it might overflow if you try to make several servings at once.I added the steaming red brew to my cup of hot milk and added some sugar, just like I do with my cafe au lait.  The aroma was pleasant: it smelled similar to Thai iced tea.  (A good sign, since I LOVE Thai iced tea!)  I took a sip, and sure enough, the similarity was still there.  It wasn't quite as strong or flavorful as Thai tea, and it didn't have the wonderful smokey undertones that Thai tea has, but it was enjoyable.  I'm sipping a cup right now as I write this, and I think it's the type of drink that I could see myself enjoying in the evening, when the lack of caffeine would be of particular benefit.In the future, I think I would like to try brewing it in a French press, as that would allow the leaves to steep longer, which would add much more flavor to the infusion.  In a drip coffeemaker, the leaves simply don't have enough time to steep.  An espresso machine, which uses high pressure to force water through the leaves, would probably do a better job as well.There is nothing coffee-like about this product, and including the words "espresso" and "tea" in the name is a bit misleading... but if you take it for what it is -- a tea-like herbal infusion that lends itself nicely to a variety of preparations -- this could be a very unique and satisfying product.  I certainly wouldn't hesitate to recommend it to anyone who is looking for something new and different to try.  And unlike products which have had the caffeine removed from them, this product is naturally caffeine free.  Enjoy!

This was a bit of a disappointment, it offered so much promise but the packaging is a bit vague on how to make the best use of it. I tried to make it up in two different ways but it did not seem to have any taste. One serving suggestion on the package suggests making it with Apple Juice, but, to be honest the Apple Juice tasted better on it's own.If anyone can offer a better serving suggestion I will be willing to try it again and update my review.

I got this bought because my husband and I love tea. Last night I made some Red Espresso and it tasted like really cheap strong tea. It had a weird after taste and texture. I drank a 1/2 cup to give it a chance - but I got a terrible headache from this product.  If you are a fan of Red Expresso this might be a great product - but if you are true tea fan I would pass.

column9: I did not care for this product
column10: I am a tea drinker but I did not care for this tea.  I found it to have an overwhelming taste, smell and aftertaste.  I do not have an espresso maker so I brewed it in my coffee maker.  My wife's comment was, "I hope that smell doesn't stay in the coffee maker."  I've never had Rooibos tea before so I may not be used to it but I like most teas.  I tend to prefer black teas like Earl Grey (my favorite) and English Breakfast Tea.I gave this 3 stars because I didn't want to downrate a product just because it wasn't to my taste preference.  It may be a very good Rooibos but having never tried one before, I have nothing to compare to.  I just didn't care for it myself.

Let me preface this review by saying that I don't have an espresso maker. So I didn't really make this the way it's intended, and I didn't know what the water to tea ratio should be. I used the 4 teaspoons tea, put it in my gold mesh coffee filter and brewed it with 2 cups water (as measured by my coffee carafe) in my coffee maker. It turned out a very tasty, very strong reddish colored tea. I added cream the way I would coffee, but would never mistake it for coffee or espresso in any way. It tasted like very strong tea, and although I was quite aware of the tannin, it seemed surprisingly smooth for how strong I made it. An interesting, tasty product and I will enjoy this bag, but I don't think I'd purchase it - it's quite expensive and certainly can't replace my coffee!

I was excited to try this, since I like both espresso and various types of tea. Don't expect this to taste at all like coffee just because it says "espresso" on the bag--it doesn't. But it does taste good, a uniquely sweet, smooth blend of tea. It tastes great with anything you would put in coffee or tea, I particularly enjoyed it with cream and just a pinch of vanilla. I really liked the smooth texture and even flavor. I may be hooked!

I've had red (Rooibos) tea before and liked the nutty flavor, but I was still dubious about something called Red Espresso.  This is Rooibos tea sourced from the Cedarberg Mountains of South Africa that has been treated to an espresso-grind texture.  You then treat it as you would regular espresso, using it in an espresso maker or French coffee press, for example.The first sign that this is going to be something you've never experienced, is the striking red/orange/brown color.  But it's the unique, rich, pleasing taste that hits it home.  It actually reminded us a bit of Thai iced tea, but served hot--we turned it into a cappuccino, adding steamed milk, a bit of foam and sweetened it with Stevia--it's something completely unique.It also lends itself to lattes, and the package recommends turning it into an ice tea, mixing a double shot with fruit juice.  Haven't tried that one yet, because we're still enjoying the cappuccino.Red Espresso is 100% naturally caffeine free and has more than five times the antioxidants of green tea.We still like our cappuccinos the traditional way, too, but this is a nice way to wind down in the evening--and it smells great, too.

I've loved rooibos tea since I first tried Celestial Seasonings Madagascar Vanilla Red not so long ago. This is a loose tea for use in your espresso machine, stovetop espresso maker, French press or coffee maker, so it takes a little more commitment (and time) than a bagged tea, but the results were well worth the effort. For my first batch, I used a French press and the results were strong (literally and figuratively). I added some milk and sugar and enjoyed 8 ounces of red tea bliss. Although it's smooth and creamy, this is not a tea I would drink straight, but then I prefer tea and coffee loaded with milk and sugar. Next time I think I'll try making a Thai tea-type iced beverage.  If I have one complaint, it's that rooibos tea contains no caffeine, because this would be the perfect caffeine delivery system.

I have ordered all types of rooibos tea for years and have never thought of making an espresso from it until I saw the ad for Red Espresso.  This makes a very smooth rich drink.  I made a Red Cappuccino with it, and a few packets of Splenda, and it was delicious. The fine grind of Red Espresso makes for a very rich drink.

column9: My new anti-oxidant fix! I love this tea.
column10: Length:: 0:46 MinsAlthough I didn't enjoy my previous experience previously with red tea, I found this product to be a wonderful beverage.Rather than using a tea bag, the espresso grind rooibos tea is made in a an espresso machine, a french press, or a drip coffee maker. I personally tried all three methods and really enjoyed the Red Espresso when made with the Senseo using the Ecopad Refillable Coffee Filter for the Senseo. It produced a beautiful crema and the flavor was mild and indulgent. When I added a little sweetener, it didn't taste too much unlike Thai iced tea, one of my favorite beverages.I also tried it with a bit of fruit juice and/or milk, but really, this tea is wonderful on it's own, especially over ice.I can see espresso fans enjoying this for a change of pace, the richness of this tea makes a nice replacement beverage for coffee. Some people might prefer this beverage in the afternoons and evenings because of the fact it has no caffeine. Rooibos is also touted as aiding in digestion.The anti-oxidant levels per ml in this beverage far exceed most other beverages, according to their ORAC measurement (Oxygen Radical Absorbance Capacity). The ORAC levels are indicated on the back of the package as:59 red espresso11 green tea10 beetroot juice8  black tea3  carrot juiceAlso, in addition to being high in anti-oxidants, this tea has no caffeine, making it ideal for very health conscious people.

This is a premium Rooibos herbal tea (with no caffeine) marketed as red espresso. The manufacturer recommends preparing this using an espresso machine but I prepared this as regular tea and it works great. It is good quality herbal tea that is rich in antioxidants that are known to scavenge tissue damaging free radicals. The health benefits of these compounds should persuade a health conscious person to try this product. Priced at $[...] for a pack of 2 (8.8 OZ each), I would say it is pricey for two bags of herbal tea. Other websites marketing herbal tea sell similar product at a much lower price.

This tea has a tart and woody flavor which is not at all unpleasant. When experimenting in brewing it I found it difficult to adjust the strength by either varying the amount of water or the tea. It is foolproof to brew and a great caffeine free warm drink substitute.

I received this drink from the Amazon prime program and I decided to try this drink out of sheer curiosity after passing it a couple of times when I was looking for something to review.  I never give much thought to coffee in any of its many forms such as cappuccino, espresso, lattes, half-cafs, and so on.  I would have to say that I drink more Tea than I do coffee so when I saw the tea espresso combo I became curious.So I get the package in my kitchen.  My first thought was what  am I going to do with this.  Do I make it like an espresso or put it in my tea maker.  So I decided to do both at the same time.  The visual aspect of the resulting brew is it appears as a cup of espresso dyed a powerful red.  Too red for my taste but let's see if it tastes good.Here, at the point of tasting the drink, 1st is the espresso;  It carries the red rooibos flavor via the consistency of a thick, punching espresso.  The red rooibos has a very distinctive, sugary flavor that is not exactly the same as coffee. While this is NOT delicious, healthy, robust and bold drink that is a great alternative to coffee but some die-hard coffee drinkers may find the flavor to be different and unusual at first.Up next is the tea.... According to the folks at Red Espresso, Red Espresso may also be brewed as a tea, but due to it's very fine grind it will make a much stronger cup of rooibos than what you would brew with normal rooibos leaves.  It can also be brewed in a regular style coffee maker or even in a french press!  I didn't like the texture of the tea.  Very hot, strong tea, in which the bag's been left for hours.  Not my type of tea.  If you like the taste and having a tea bag in your tea for hours then you should give this a try.My thoughts:  I wasn't expecting it to taste like espresso.  I also wasn't expecting that it would taste like tea. The problem with the arrangement, which I half-feared prior to consuming, is that the two don't blend all that well. It isn't bad, but it doesn't feel proper on either end. The texture for a rooibos drink is key to its amiability, and this just doesn't flow well.  Indeed this would be *an exceptionally healthy* alternative to regular espresso.  If you are a chronic espresso or coffee fiend, and your habit is causing you health related issues such as caffeine jitters, withdrawal symptoms, headache, insomnia, and so on, you switch from coffee to Red Espresso.  It is so much healthier for you than coffee that the health benefits are literally endless.  I think that where this product really shines is as an espresso substitute, and every espresso drinker should give it a try as a healthy alternative to coffee.

column9: Hard to compare to tea or coffee.
column10: First, I prepared this product like you would cappuccino, I ran it through my espresso machine and served it with steamed milk and cinnamon.  It didn't taste like tea or coffee to me, and took a little getting used to, but it wasn't bad.  It's a strong, concentrated taste which reminds me of the smell of sweet, freshly baled hay.Next, I decided to brew it like coffee, which I didn't care for.  I don't like to add milk or sugar to my drinks and I would have preferred to have been able to drink it "black".I'm not going to give up though, I see they have many recipes posted on their website, so I'm going to visit it and see if I can come up with something I like, and then update my review.

I prepared the Red Espresso Rooibos Tea Espresso in a regular coffee machine. You can prepare it the same way you do coffee. It has a rich dark color that's so dark it barely has a hint of red.Rooibos is OK with me but has never been my favorite, (My favorite is Lipton's Bavarian Wild Berry) but it was a favorite of my husband's. He couldn't finish his and said that this has put him off Rooibos for a bit. I finished mine, but felt that it had a bit of an aftertaste. It also smells slightly burnt. It looks unpleasant and muddy when you have to go back and clean it out of the coffee maker.I gave it 3 stars since taste is subjective and I could see how someone else could love this tea.

I have been making this tea for the last two days and I have to say yumm overall.  I tried it with milk and sugar and it was okay but wasn't impressed.  I then made it up and decided to try it as Iced Tea and I really like this.  I put a shot of vanilla coffee flavoring in it with sugar and yumm, yumm.  Tomorrow I plan on trying it with the raspberry coffee flavoring and I'm sure it will be a hit.  I have company coming so it will be a nice treat since our main dish is going to be fish.  This is a very strong tea so it is best diluted unless you really like a punch.  I will try it as a latte over this weekend as that looks like it might be yummy.  It is well worth trying if you like red tea which I do.  I also like the fact that it is healthy for you.  Take a chance and be wild.  It's really pretty good.  You do need a french press or espresso machine so don't say I didn't tell yah.

this tea has a wonderful flavor and you make it like you would coffee. I made it in my drip coffee maker and it is a very good tasting tea. I drank mine with cream, honey and just a hint of cinamom and I thought the taste was wonderful. I don't drink tea plain so I didn't try this, as some had done, plain.Pros-I like the tasteIt is full of anti-oxidantsIt is easy to make in the coffee potit can be made strong, weak or anything in betweenno caffeine (good for me any way)cons-this is nothing like espresso so coffee drinkers don't expect this to replace your espressoI feel the price is a little high for this

This is an interesting brew, but I have to admit it tastes a bit different and has that "health" drink tang to it, I love black tea and good coffee so this is something I would drink to have instead of those two but never as a substitute. The flavor and scent is bit grassy, and makes me feel a bit like a farm animal when I drink it lol, for health benefits I prefer my green tea and mesh bags of Rooibos tea with nice flavors such as almond or coconut , I wouldn't buy this again even though its was free from Amazon...Other than the acidic flavor it's hard to make, prepare to have your coffee pot clogged up...not fun and not fast/easy for sure

column9: An excellent beverage for a former caf-fiend pregnant lady!
column10: When I saw this product I was a little skeptical- after all, how can an herbal tea be used as a substitute for coffee or used to make shots like a latte? However, when my husband came home and we found a Vine promotional package of the stuff waiting for us, he made me a latte of the stuff using our Barista espresso machine. The shot of rooibos was a rather eerie red color that initially put me off, and made me wonder if it would turn my teeth red. However, after the initial sip, when I came to grips with the inevitable difference between a rooibos and espresso shot, I found that I actually enjoyed the tea-like flavor. Because I am pregnant, I was a little worried that it might not be healthy for me (even though it is caffeine-free) but after searching online I found that this herbal tea does not interfere with iron absorption like the tea plant, and is actually recommended during pregnancy. It may even have all kinds of health benefits, if you believe the health sites. I probably wouldn't have bought this if it hadn't been a promotional sample- but now that I have it, I'm quite happy about it and might even buy more once I run out....

It's definitely bold and richly flavored, but in no way does it have the intensity that a good, strong cup of coffee has.If you like a dark tea that's slightly sweet, you'll probably like this.

column9: My Very Particular Cat Loves This Food
column10: I don't know if its the fact that Stella and Chewy's Freeze Dried Salmon and Chicken Dinner is hot when served to my cat or if its the extremely potent fishy taste that appeals to her.  Whatever it is, she anticipates eating this as soon as she senses that I am putting the kettle on to heat the water that will hydrate this food.Yes, this food does require some preparation, but it is minimal and not really worth mentioning as it takes more time to open up a can of soft cat food without cutting yourself.  I heat some water add it to the portion of food I have already placed aside in a container, swirl it around a bit and then drain the remaining water.  The idea is just to reconstitute the food.My only complaint about this offering is the fact that it needs to be protected by bubble wrap or styrofoam peanuts in order to insure that it arrives in one piece.  I have had it delivered to my home and upon opening the bag found that most of the food had been crushed to powder rather than the nuggets that my cat prefers to eat.Its a little tricky to determine just how much your cat will eat per sitting (standing:)  I find that if my cat does not finish her food, I must clean this out as it does harden and if left too long out will begin to emit a less than pleasant odor.The food is definitely nutritious no matter what else you feed your cat.  My cat eats kibble and I do serve this on top of the kibble so that any moisture emitted will also flavor the dry food.  I have found my cat to be much more alert and healthier since she has been eating this food.  Its expensive, but well worth the price for anyone who loves their pet.  My cat had been ailing for over a year and since I added this to her diet in addition to Organix Adult Indoor Feline Dry Cat Food, 5.25 Pounds and Wellness Canned Cat Food, Sliced Turkey & Salmon Dinner, 24-Pack of 3 oz. Cans in a variety of flavors, I have seen a marked difference for the better.Bottom line? Buy it, your cat will love you. Highly Recommended.Diana Faillace Von Behren"reneofc"

column9: Convenient way to give raw food

column9: Great stuff! My 13 favorite uses for white vinegar described
column10: I use vinegar in many different ways at home, not just for cooking.  It is a great cleaner - cheap and totally green, no harsh chemicals.My favorite use for it is to clean suede shoes and boots.  Once suede is stained, there is about 24-48 hour window before the stain sets in.  I mix 40% white vinegar and 60% water solution, and blot the stain with a wet paper towel.  When the cleaning is over I stuff the shoe/boot with newspapers to make sure the shape is retained and let it dry.  Note that it should dry naturally, not next to a heat source like a radiator, as it the heat will damage the skin.Vinegar's magic ingredient is acetic acid. All vinegars are produced by oxidization of alcohol into acetic acid.  Since people have been making wine for ever, vinegar was an accidental by-product a long time ago.Here are some of my additional uses for vinegar:1. I add a few tablespoons of white vinegar to water when poaching eggs.  It helps whites stay firm, so if you get an accidental crack in the shell the white will not leak out.2. Adding vinegar to wilted veggies will make them perk up.3. After cooking I don't like to keep the smell of onions on my hands, a quick wipe with vinegar removes the odor.4. When I had a garbage disposal i would mix vinegar with baking soda and put it down the drain. After the mixture fizzed for a few minutes I would flush it along with the smell.5. After washing stemware in some dishwashing linquids they become cloudy.  Cleaning them with vinegar removes the white cloudiness.6. Vinegar works well cleaning grout. I dip an old toothbrush into vinegar and can get stains and dirt out quite easily.7. Vinegar and vegetable oil (50/50) work well removing water stains from wood.8. If I have stains on clothing (food or sweat stains) I wet them with vinegar before putting in the washer. It helps to get out stubborn stains.9. My mom always added a cupful of vinegar to the rinse cycle. Acetic acid is not harmful to clothing, but it dissolves soap residue and dark clothing comes out brighter.  It also has a side effect of working like a fabric softener.10. In the winter I use vinegar/water solution (3-to-1) to wipe down my windows and it keeps them frost free.11. I have a few cracks in my drive way, rather than pouring chemicals on the weeds that grow from these cracks I use 50-50 solution of vinegar and water to keep them under control.12. I like to keep cut flowers on my dining room table, and to prolong their life I add a tablespoon of vinegar to the water along with a teaspoon of sugar.Vinegar is a very useful thing to have at home, I recommend it!Ali Julia review

I'm a huge fan of Colombian food, and I eat or cook it whenever I can, tapioca flour goes into one of my favorite items from this wonderful cuisine, I make Yucca Buns with a simple recipe that tastes better with this silky and organic flour than with the other tapioca flours I have found so far. Not to mention it's organic, something very important as this crusty old planet ages under our rule. This recipe that I now love, annoyed me to extreme lengths because I didn't understand the way the dough must feel and change into until I made it the second time, adding too much liquid made it too sticky once the cheese melted into the flour so I had to add even more flour to balance it out... not pretty in baking haha.  Tapioca starch can be used as a thickener or substitute for allergen causing flour, but I recommend checking the conversions for each online, also don't use it as a batter on a cutlet ( dip in flour then milk the bread crumbs then fry) it will come off in a gooey skin, even of a non stick pan. It's amazing for baking though and I love the boxes, I was quite surprised how tiny they looked, each box hold 2 cups of tapioca flour, and it takes me one box to make a double batch of Yucca Buns. I have adapted the below recipe from Ingrid Hoffman's Yucca Buns recipe from the FoodNetwork.com2 cups tapioca flour4 egg yolks ( or 3 for less cakey bread)2 teaspoons baking powder .... ( make sure its fresh and not expired¼ tsp salt .........( my favorite is freshly ground in a mortar and pestle grey sea salt) also salt depends on how salty the cheese it. Ingrid's recipe didn't have any, I find it much better tasting with salt as the cheese melts and mends with the dough, so add a little more each time you make this until it tastes right, but don't over do it because it can go from great to over bearing, a small amount is good starting point).4 cups grated cheese.... ( Oaxaca is the original one from the main recipe, but also nice dry mozzarella works, use your favorite but it cant be the fresh one kept in water, has to be the hard kind you can all ready find shredded but I recommend getting your own and grating it, usually one large block of Sargento or Polly-O is more than 4 cups)*Extra bit I add - little pieces of cheese from leftover shredding, I put a tiny piece into each bun and wrap the dough around it, great when it melts and cooks. *To make, put the flour, salt and baking powder into a large bowl and mix, add the egg yolks, mix in as well, then add all the cheese. The dough will feel very dry and funny, keep squishing everything between your hands, it will take some hand muscle and a few minutes of kneading inside the bowl, once it starts coming together you can mix it on a large cutting board. I add a teaspoon or milk or cream if it's really dry, but wait till the last minute, this is a very dry dough to work with at first, once the cheese starts to melt it will come together quickly and be little sticky. Roll into oblong ellipses, line 8 per sheet ( non stick pan or a plain one rubbed w/ butter) and bake for 17-20 min under a preheated 350degree oven.  Sometimes I sprinkle extra cheese on top and broil it at the end. When they are warm and ready to pull out they will be pale golden, there will not be a brown outside. And these are quite flat, they don't rise into a ball or anything but that's ok.  As I mentioned before, sometimes when I roll the raw dough up I put a tiny bit of cheese I used fir shredding inside and seal it in, that creates this crusty lovely cavern as it makes a bubble on the inside, it's a crunchy cheesy salty bite at the end, yum!These are best fresh but also good reheated later, or toasted and smeared with butter. This recipe takes some practice to make but it's so worth it! I cant believe that I just wrote this, but its one of my favorites and I'm happy to share it, this flour works so well in this that I will be reordering as I'm about to run out, highly recommended for delicious home baking. I even taught my boyfriends grandmother (the are both Colombian) how to make these and she loved them which shocked me, I was confident in my baking but still to get a compliment from her on something she eats all the time is great, so I gave her a box of this flour to take with her in the end, it was a good day!- Kasia S.
