column9: Too much of a bite for me.
column10: I love a good cup of strong coffee, but this has way too much of a bite for me.  Even my husband, who does like it a little bolder than I do, thought the same.  If you are looking for a smooth, full bodied coffee, this is NOT it.  If, on the other hand, you want something that is bound to curl your toes in an attempt to wake you up, this will do it.  Not what I look for in coffee though.  I like to be awakened with ease, not a jolt.

NOTE: This is a review of this coffee in the K-cup format, not of Amazon's packaging.  However, I have never had trouble with the Frustration-free packaging; I simply cannot comment in this case.Reviewer's preferences: Strong, medium-dark roast coffees, mid-to-heavily sweetened with whole milk (4:1 ratio or a little heavier toward the coffee side).  I occasionally add a hint of vanilla syrup and cream or half-and-half if a coffee is overly bitter.I picked up this coffee in a large sampler box of Coffee People "Extra Bold" K-cups, which I have just finished off.  The collection contained the following blends/coffees: Wake-up Call, Jet Fuel, Black Tiger, and Organic.  I have had each coffee multiple times.  From the four, I give the Organic blend the top spot with a slight edge over Black Tiger (we're talking 9.1/10 over 9.0/10 here).  Both the Black Tiger and Organic were strong and bold in flavor but not too bitter, while the Wake-up Call tended to be a little more harsh on the palate.  The Jet Fuel blend was appropriately named, as it almost always required a little vanilla and more milk or even heavy cream to make it palatable.Qualities of Coffee People Jet Fuel:Dark, almost burned coffee flavor (think bad Sumatran roast).  Heavy bitterness that overwhelms the flavor, harsh on the back of the tongue and a fully bitter aftertaste, but probably drinkable if you are a fan of Sumatran or French Roast coffees.  Medium acidity, a little tangy but not really sour, with an earthy flavor that tends toward muddy.  Flavor envelops the entire mouth, but generally overwhelms the palate.  Heavy body, but not sludgy, though your mouth may be convinced otherwise from the flavor.  While I can and sometimes do drink other coffees black (mostly full-bodied medium roasts), I can't imagine anyone drinking this black even if they take their espresso that way.  Requires sweetener and cream/half-and-half or a heavy addition of milk.  Personally, I had to use a small splash of vanilla syrup to hide the bitterness.  Drinkable, but just barely with better choices available. Hard to find the good qualities in the disappointing profile.  Certainly not the WORST dark roast I have had, however.I give this 2 stars for one reason.  If you were using this coffee as an ingredient where you wanted the coffee and perhaps the bitterness to not be hidden too much, then this would be an excellent choice over many harsh Sumatran and French Roast coffees.

This is my first shipment for this coffee.  I'm on a subscription basis.  Each K-Cup is flushed with nitrogen and then sealed in an air-tight, moisture-tight cup.  This lid is adhered to the top of the cartridge as soon as it is filled with fresh coffee or tea grounds, and the K-Cup remains air-tight and moisture-free until the needle of your Keurig brewer punctures the foil.  However in this shipment 35 of the 50 k-cups were deflated and lost there seal.  Not sure how fresh this coffee is since the seal was broken prior to shipment.  If the next shipment returns the same result I'll go back to paying more for a fresher product.

First of all, I like this coffee. It is smooth, aromatic and doesn't bite going down.Having said that, I expected it to be a strong, aggresive coffe that stripped the skin off the roof of my mouth. It didn't.I would likely buy this again, but only if I was looking for a milder coffee, which I don't do very often.

column9: Love Coffee People, but Not Jet Fuel

I was deeply disappointed to see their stores absorbed by Starbuck's (nothing against Starbuck's, they make a good cup of coffee and are a very responsible company). column10: ASIN B0029XLH4Y - All right, I'm going to start by saying something negative about the Keurig coffee makers, which I will later explain better in my review of IT. Here goes: this coffee maker makes the weakest dang coffee in the history of the free world. You get a choice when brewing: itty bitty cup of semi-strong brew or sort-of-big cup of brown caffeinated water. This displeases me. I bought the thing because I love coffee and would like to mainline it but cannot. Now, I've learned to live with and even get around some of the deficiencies of the maker, but finding the coffee that makes the maker look good... tough job, but someone's got to do it.Jet Fuel is fantastic. It makes Keurig look like the geniuses they ought to be. This stuff is strong enough to overcome the wimpy options of the maker and then some. It's not bitter, but it might taste bitter to folks who aren't hardcore coffee drinkers. To me, that "bitter" taste is sharp, crisp and maybe a little chocolate-like. This is the stuff to wake up to, the perfect morning jolt.If there's a true negative for me, it's the individual cup issue, from the ecological point of view. You get a plastic cup with a foil lid and, inside, a small paper filter filled with grounds. It is, generally, thrown away as one piece. This means that the (unnumbered) cups, which may be recyclable, cannot be put with the plastics; the foil cannot be put with the rest of the foil; the biodegradable filter and grounds not only don't go into the composter, but they'll biodegrade very slowly, deprived of air, sun and water in their little foil and plastic casing. It's possible to take the thing apart and deal with the individual pieces appropriately, but that defeats the convenience factor of the maker. Someone's got to design a better k-cup, but I can't take points away from Jet Fuel for a flaw that all k-cups share.  On the up side of the packaging, Amazon's packaging is awesome - not just frustration free, but 100% recyclable!- AnnaLovesBooks

column9: Yogi's NEW, and, very ambitious blend!
column10: Yogi, 'Perfect Energy Vanilla Spice Tea,' is an ambitious grouping of Green Tea, and Black Assam Tea, with several herbs and spices making recent news, for promoting health benefits.  The added bonus resides in one of the Yogi Principles: "We work with what nature already offers rather than trying to concoct it.  We don't have laboratories.  We have kitchens."  That said, it's no wonder the, all natural Yogi brand, has a dedicated following.I personally really like this blend.  The fragrance is enticing, and there is just enough spice to mask some of the underlying earthiness detected, likely from the herbs.  It IS a very mild tea. I've resorted to two bags per cup for full flavor, which is why I took off one star for this review.  Once brewed, I add a little Rosemary and Lavender honey, and it's yummy.  With two tea bags providing approximately 160 mg of caffeine, I would normally expect to feel jittery.  The fact is, I'm quite the opposite. I don't feel particularly more energized, but I do feel somewhat more focused to task.Here's a list of ingredients: Green Tea, Black Assam Tea, Cinnamon Bark, Rooibos Leaf, Honeybush, Ginger Root, Licorice Root, Stevia Leaf, GotuKola Leaf, Ashwagandha Root, Shatavari Root, Shankpushpi, and lastly 15 mg of L-Theanine.Interestingly, L-Theanine Suntheanine, has had several clinical trials with some evidence that it assists in managing stress, anxiety and PMS, while enhancing the immune system.  The problem is, that the recommended dose is 50 to 200 mg/day.  With only 15 mg per tea bag, you'd have to drink four cups for the minimum therapeutic effect.  Perhaps when coupled with Shatavari, and Shankpushpi, which both provide some nervous system support, too, less is required to offset the caffeine jitters. Surprisingly, it does seem to work.I've noticed a little more diuretic effect than with simple teas. Perhaps this is a result of the Shatavari Root, which is 'Indian Asparagus,' but I'm not sure.  You will want to avoid this tea, if you are allergic to asparagus, or any of the other ingredients.  And, as with many other herbal tea blends, it is not to be used by pregnant, or breastfeeding women, infants, or children. It's a good idea to familiarize yourself with ALL the listed ingredients.  Yes, there are benefits, but also potential side effects. For example, Ashwagandha Root is not recommended for those with thyroid disorders, or liver ailments, without consulting your physician. Enjoy, the bounty of nature, but always be informed.Will I purchase in the future?  Yes, I think I will.

column9: Tastes great and provides a nice energy boost.
column10: A few times a week at work, I'll drink diet soda in the afternoon as a pick-me-up.  I know soda isn't very healthy for you, so I've also tried a few different flavors of hot tea.  Unfortunately for me, a lot of teas are caffeine free.  And those that do have caffeine are typically of a low dose.Therefore, I was eager to try Yogi Perfect Energy Vanilla Spice tea.  The Oregon-based company advertises the product as a natural energizer, without the jitters.  Each tea bag contains 80 mg of caffeine, which is about the same as an 8 ounce cup of coffee.  One of the first things I noticed is that each tea bag has a large amount of ingredients.  There are 14 different herbs listed, including Organic Cinnamon Bark, Green Tea Leaf Extract, and Stevia leaf.  It also contains natural vanilla flavor, Organic Chai Spice Flavor, and Vanilla Bean.You are instructed to use 8 oz of water and steep the bag for 4-6 minutes (longer than a typical tea bag).  Simply put, this is a great tasting tea.  I especially think it's good for people who are not used to drinking normal tea, since the Stevia leaf adds natural sweet flavor.  You don't need to waste calories by adding in your own sugar.  So in terms of taste, I would give it 5 stars.  In terms of energy boost, I would give it 4 stars.  It did not give me as much of an alertness boost as coffee does, but there was definitely a noticeable pick-me-up.Overall, I think this is a great product for those that like mildly sweet vanilla flavor, or for those that need more caffeine from their tea bag.  I will definitely be ordering these for my office.

I'll get back to you in thirty or forty years with an update  on the long term  health benefits. As for the more immediate claims, I give it five stars!It has a wonderful taste, it's worth the price for that alone.The vanilla is just right, delicate, but not overpowering.As for being energizing,  after three cups I found it to be subtle. There was no noticeable, jumpy effect, but I didn't get a case of the mid-afternoon drowsies, either.It made my work day go more smoothly, without calling attention to the fact that it was doing so.This is a good tea to take to the office, for afternoon breaks, and it's much cheaper than the expensive cafeteria teas at work.

I love Yogi teas in general. I happened to have just ordered twelve varieties of it, including this one, when I was offered a free box to try out. I simply adore their Tahitian Vanilla Hazelnut, and figured that anything else with vanilla in it would be as good.I drank three cups of this tea, steeped at 4, 6, and 8 minutes. I found it had practically no flavor steeped at four minutes, and had a bitter taste, somewhat dirty tasting, at eight. Unfortunately, even at six minutes, I found the tea to be too weak for my liking. The vanilla flavor was almost undetectable to me. I added a bit of cream, for this often will bring out the flavor of weak tea, but I just did not find this tea tasty. Whether it gave me a "lift", I can not say, for I don't respond to coffee either.Yogi's Vanilla Hazelnut tea has a strong vanilla taste, and I was probably expecting something like that, but it is an herbal tea and can be steeped for a long time without becoming bitter. I figured I was merely disappointed, as I love Yogi's herbal teas so much. In the interest of being fair (and also because I had almost two full boxes), I gave one box of the Perfect Energy to a friend who drinks tea and had not sampled any of the Yogi brand.Here's the email I got two days later:  "I like it because it was smooth, flavorful, not too sweet and gave me the energy it promised! I would really love that other box!" Obviously, she really liked it a lot!Tea is a matter of taste, especially teas that are blends, such as this one. If you're looking for a lot of vanilla flavor and no caffeine, I'd recommend their Vanilla Hazelnut. If you like a more subtle taste, and do want caffeine, you might want to give this a try.

Having two jobs requires a lot of energy. Face it life as we know it takes a lot of energy, but I need my espresso in the morning, and I drink coffee until the early afternoon.I love to savor caffeine products, and the ones that taste the best win me over.  Life is too short to drink anything that isn't close to perfect.What I really enjoy about Yogi Vanilla Spice Perfect Energy Tea is that it lives up to its name.  I start to unwind with tea and lower the caffeine content late in the afternoon, but I'm a connoisseur of both coffee and tea beverages.This tea is especially smooth and good tasting.  I've drunk all kinds of Green and Chai teas, and I've had all kinds of flavored teas, both black and herbal.  To me Vanilla Spice is smooth and tasty enough. I do not like teas that are too spicy--too much black pepper, too much ginger, etc.Add to this the herbs that calm, the caffeine that boosts so gently, and the antioxidants that purify and cleanse, and this tea is just about perfect.  At least it's a perfect fit for me.  (At $3.51 per 16-count box in a group of six, it is a bit more expensive than what you find elsewhere, but I think it's a fair deal.)Taste *****Health ****Cost  ****Feel  *****

I am a huge tea drinker, usually going through 4-6 cups of various flavors a day. I've never seen Yogi brand tea's before, and Vanilla Spice sounded pretty tasty, so I was pleased to be offered this. It's pretty good! I needed to add a few cubes of sugar to it to sweeten it up a bit, but the vanilla spice flavor is good...very subtle. You can definitely taste it, but it's not at all overpowering. As for the energy, I couldn't really tell any difference. I'm usually pretty energized in the mornings just from a good nights sleep and a nice breakfast, so I can't recommend purchasing this if you're looking specifically for an energy tea. As far as teas go though, it's definitely a tasty one, and I'll have to look into other Yogi brands to what else they have to offer!

column9: Just as good quality as the others I've been purch for years
column10: Have enjoyed the Yogi Bedtime & Fasting "flavors" for years.  Occasionally order the Peach too.  Intrigued by the "vanilla" and was not disappointed.  Was not sweet; as long as one lets the tea brew it has a nice flavor.  Energy part, well, not sure if it's the tea or re-starting commitment to exercising 20-30 minutes couple days per week or more likely a combination of both.  Will be re-ordering again.  Can't beat Amazon for Yogi 6pk price as compared to food stores!

I was excited to try this tea, because my husband and I collect teas and love to sample them. I was also excited because this claimed to pack a punch of energy, something that I am sometimes lacking because I am a chef. However, I thought that while it was good, it was not GREAT. I was not in a huge hurry for another cup of it. There was something slightly off about the after taste. However, that could have just been me, so I encourage everyone to try it for themselves. It also did not give me a huge energy burst, but I love coffee and drink a lot, so perhaps someone who is more use to herbal teas would find it more stimulating.

As far as flavored teas go this is a rather nice blend with smooth yet bold vanilla spice taste.  It has a good bit of caffeine in it as a pick me up and can be a nice change for an afternoon cup of coffee.  Beyond the caffeine it also purports to be a healthier choice than many other energy drinks.  While I was not overwhelmed by this tea, as I tend to like heartier blends, I would give it a qualified thumbs up.

column9: good combination of (nonherbal) Tea and other flavors
column10: This "Vanilla Spice" energy tea is based on a combination of Green and Black Tea with a variety of organic root and leaf flavors to round it out. Both my husband and I like the taste of this tea. The vanilla flavor is mild and I also taste the Rooibos, and some hints of the other flavors. I normally don't care for plain rooibus tea, but it works well in this combination. The tea is slightly sweet, probably because of the addition of Stevia Leaf and the Licorice Root. I am not a coffee or energy drink consumer, so the 80 mg of caffeine is rather much for me, but I did not feel jittery, and I also did feel a bit of a lift. I think any caffiene (most of which is "naturally occurring" anyway) could make you feel jittery, though. The Yogi people have also added a "naturally occurring amino acid found in green tea, [which, (they say)] promotes relaxation by calming the mind."I am definitely going to drink some more of this tea in the a.m.s and check out how it makes me feel.

I don't like a lot of herbal teas.  Lots of them taste the way health food stores smell--like herbs and vitamins--or else they go way off the flowery end.Yogi Vanilla Spice Perfect Energy Tea is hearty without being overpowering, the herbs are evident without being weird, and it provides a real afternoon pick me up.  I was a little worried about the caffeine.  Afternoon sodas, regular tea and coffee disturb my sleep at night, but this seems to have no ill effects.  It smells wonderful, the vanilla is the predominant flavor and aroma but it's not all vanilla.  There's enough spice to make it interesting without being a chai.  It's definitely tea and is a true "beverage that cheers and does not intoxicate".  It's a very nice afternoon break and does seem to provide a little energy, though that may just be the power of suggestion.There's lots of stuff in this tea.  Green tea and black tea, and a lot of other things that sound like they came from the ashram in Eat Pray Love.  I haven't had the urge to start meditating since I've been drinking this, so it's safe if you want to stay mainstream, and it really is delicious.Just as an aside, it would also make an excellent base for a hot adult beverage if one felt inclined to add a shot of something to a cup after a long freezing afternoon spent shoveling the mountains of snow we've had this winter. Not that I've tried that or anything.

I am a big fan of teas, including herbal.  During a normal day, I drink some PG Tips black tea for energy and herbal teas for the flavor.  This Yogi tea is essentially a combination of both.  It contains black tea, green tea, and a variety of herbs that create a vanilla chai flavor.  The flavor is really good, albeit similar to other things I've had.  The green and black teas provide an energy boost from caffeine (80 mg), while the organic Gotu Kola leaf and Ashwagandah provide the more hippy resolution to low energy.  I really don't know if the latter ingredients help, but I can say that I don't get jittery.The one qualm I have is that by mixing herbal, black, and green teas, you are not going to get proper steeping on all.  For example, black and herbal are best steeped in freshly boiled water, while green can become bitter if you don't let the water cool a bit.  All types are generally steeped for different times as well.  Regardless, I still enjoy this tea enough to drink it regularly and if you enjoy flavors such as cinnamon and ginger, I would recommend giving it a try.
Every morning for my ride to work I make myself a cup of Yogi Vanilla Spice Energy Tea. It makes walking into work a whole lot better. The taste is just right.

I simply LOVE this tea! It is yummy, full of flavor and the best part is the caffeine! I really love Yogi brand tea, but it could get a big expensive at retail or grocery stores, so the bulk prices on Amazon are perfect for customers like me that drink tea daily! Shipping was a breeze, as always!

I don't know if it gave me any energy but it was a fine tasting, smooth tea. The vanilla and spice is a nice combination. I'm not sure about it being labeled "perfect energy." It doesn't contain near as much caffeine as a cup of coffee but that could be a good thing for a lot of people. Overall an enjoyable tea.

column9: Love the taste- but not energizing
column10: I think this tea tastes great. It is sweet with a hint of spice, and is very mild (not like a chai tea). BUT, this tea makes me tired. It is supposed to be an energy tea, so I'm not sure what exactly is happening, but within 30-60 minutes after drinking a glass I feel like I want to lay down and take a nap. I'm going to try some of their other energy teas and see if they work any better for me.

This is a soft and delicately flavored tea with a heavenly aroma. I'm a big coffee fan, but I like tea too and for a few days decided to try substituting this for my usual coffee. While I did enjoy it, I think it's better as a middle of the afternoon treat than a substitute for morning coffee. I think that could change if I got used to substituting the mildness of tea for the robustness of coffee, but I think I'll just keep it around for an occasional treat. For those who prefer tea, this one would be a wonderful way to start the day.

column9: Better than coffee, energy lasts for hours
column10: This tea is absolutely delicious and gives me energy throughout the day. No more yawning, feeling tired, etc. I wanted to try a powerful tea because coffee wasn't doing the job for me anymore in the morning. One tea bag has almost as much caffeine as one cup of coffee, but it energizes you much more, and it's very healthy too. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND TRYING IT.

I love caffeine but hate coffee, and it's probably not good to have an energy drink every day. I've found this to be a great substitute. For awhile I was drinking Teavana's Samarui Chai, which has a pretty similar taste, but is far more expensive. Very mild tasting and smells wonderful, "like Christmas," as my husband said. I find I feel more energized without feeling jittery. The price is also great on Amazon.

I have tried many flavours of Yogi brand tea. I think they all taste good and do what it says.Since its hard to tell the pick up in energy I tried this tea for 1 month 2-3 times a day at work. I was always energised and feeling good. Then I stopped having the tea and went back to Coffee and other cafenieated drinks couple times a day. Feeling was not so great and I was sometimes sleepy afetr coffee in the middle of day.Now, I am back to having this tea and back to my high performance, feel and look good days :-).There is a very apparent and stable energy boost to my body with this. And it comes with many other health benfits of tea. I have it with no sugar or milk added.Cheers
I really love the flavor of this tea, and it does make a much healthier choice than a can of soda for your afternoon break.But overall didn't really notice any extra energy after drinking it.

Let's start with the positive - this is a very tasty tea.  The spicy aroma and the perfect amount of vanilla flavor makes for a cup of tea that is worth savoring.  It has caffeine, for those of us that need our tea to provide a boost in our energy levels.  It is also a relatively mild (or weak, if you prefer) tea, which is the way I prefer my tea (this might be a negative for those that prefer a stronger cup of tea).While being 100% Natural is a good thing, I have to balance that against my budget, and this tea, while having a great flavor, simply doesn't provide sufficient value to me to justify the price.  There are a lot of other tea options out there, and it is really hard for me to pass over other, more affordable, options for this.  For people with different budget priorities, this may well be worth it.

I have tasted other teas that are similar but the boost that goes with this tea is a pleasant boost.  Caffeine jolts aren't for everyone and this tea uses a variety of stimulating herbs that I found pleasant. I didn't sweeten this tea but for those who prefer to sweeten their tea this seemed like a tea that would be enhanced by sweetener. This is an enjoyable addition to the Yogi collection. For those who enjoy Celestial Seasonings Bengal Spice Tea, this would be an excellent alternative for a change of pace. The two aren't identical but have enough similarities that they can both be used and enjoyed as I do. I don't buy one or the other but drink both depending on my mood.

The Yogi Vanilla Spice energy tea has a light sweet flavor to it.  I'm not a huge tea drinker but do go though phases.  For a quick cup of something good and warm this does the trick.  I'm not too affected by caffine but obviously there is some and the expected pick me up is there.  With tea with me it's really rather simple.  Does it taste good?  The answer is yes.

The flavor just wasn't for me... I tried it hot, iced, sweetened, unsweetened, and luke warm.  I just couldn't get past the flavor of it.  It tasted super strong with some type of herb or something that just didn't agree with me.  Now, why am I giving it two stars instead of one?  My husband thought it was okay... He didn't hate it, so I figure there might be others out there who don't take offense to the one overwhelming flavor that I just couldn't get past.

column9: Good taste.. energy depends on your caffiene tolerance.
column10: This is a good tasting tea but needs to be steeped for awhile or it's a bit weak. I think the "perfect energy" is a bit of a stretch since there are so many variables to whether or not this will help your energy level. It does have caffiene so if caffiene does anything for you it might boost your energy. I rarely ever have caffiene so for me it did give me an energy boost but also insominia so it wasn't a good trade off.  Overall, I liked the flavor and if I was going to stay up late or needed an extra burst for a specific reason I would have a cup. However, it's not something I would incorporate into my routine because of the caffiene and my low tolerance for it.

column9: WONDERFUL AND FULL BODIED HERBAL TEA
column10: This was a great choice for me as I love herbal teas .  My only complaint is that I only received one box and not the 6 box count.The melange of flavors and a perfectly blended amount of vanilla make this a smooth and delicious drink both hot and cold.  Iced that is.I am adding this one to my list of favs

column9: Good taste, Energy? Not so sure
column10: This tea has a great taste for those of you who love vanilla. It's not over powering but a nice hint of it. I'm not sure how to write this review, because it is tea. If you enjoy tea, you'd enjoy this... if you're looking for energy, go drink coffee or an energy drink. That's my 2 cents on this tea.

column9: Great flavor, helps me focus, but still leaves me with jitters
column10: This tea claims to naturally energize without the jitters. I wish it did that. Although "all natural", it's important to note that each cup of tea contains about 80 mg of caffeine. That's enough to give me jitters in the middle of the afternoon, which is when I've been drinking this tea for about a month. I don't use any sugar, so the effect is completely a result of the tea.That aside, the tea does somehow relax my brain. My mind wanders constantly, and usually by 1:00 or 2:00 in the afternoon, I need something to keep me focused and keep me from getting cranky. The only way I can describe the effect this tea has on me is "calming". It's easier for me to focus, even though I still feel "jittery". One cup of this tea keeps me going through the late afternoon hours, and the "jitters" usually subside within one to two hours, while I remain focused for at least three or four.The tea has an excellent aroma. I love opening the package and just smelling the tea-bag -- the scent alone is quite calming. You can definitely smell and taste the vanilla. The spices aren't too overpowering, and I find this tea to have an excellent taste overall. It's not bitter compared to other "all natural" herbal teas I've had.Ultimately it depends how sensitive you are to caffeine, but I would recommend this tea for ocassional use.

column9: Great Tea and a good Value
column10: I love tea. I drink 4-6 cups a day. I've been a tea snob and usually only make tea from loose leaves.When offered this tea I was worried that the vanilla would be over powering but it wasn't it was a very good blend.I also found the extra energy kick this tea has very refreshing. It didn't give me the jitters.I would definitely use this again.

With a 2 hour commute, I enjoy a good cup of tea/coffee on my drives home from work.  This tea is one of my favorites.  I drank this tea without sweeteners and I really do enjoy the taste and the smell is nice too.  The only (sort of) negative I would have is that it doesn't keep me quite as alert as coffee does.  With this in mind, I would choose this tea over coffee on any day that I don't need the max amount of caffeine.  I also like the fact that it is 100% natural.  Now I have to try the other flavors of Yogi teas.

When I get a product or even look at something in the store first thing I do is look to see what's in it.  Unfortunately it didn't list all the ingredients online so I took a chance anyway.  First off let me say that this smells like heaven and tastes great too but if you have a heart condition you won't be able to drink it.  I was only able to take a few sips so that I could try it for the flavor.  DH said it did indeed make him get a little pick me up after drinking it so I will go with it does help energize you.  The flavor is perfectly balanced and not overwhelming so as long as you don't have a health issue give this a try.  It really is good and I do hope at some point the company can come out with this particular flavor in a decaf.

Can you call a tea smooth?  I don't know if a tea can be labeled as smooth, but every time I take a sip, I can't help but think how smooth this tea is.  And it smells so good...a gentle, light, spicy aroma with a hint of vanilla.As for flavor, this tea has a mild spicy flavor & is not bitter. I can smell the vanilla more than I can taste it. I don't need to add sweetener.The product claims ".... this delicious tea is sure to energize the body while calming and focusing the mind with every cup."  I don't notice an energy increase after drinking this tea, but I drink, on average, 3 cups of drip coffee during the day. So it's understandable to me why I wouldn't feel an energy lift.  I do feel more calmed and focused when I drink Yogi Vanilla Spice Perfect Energy Tea. So for me, the 2nd part of their claim is correct.Ingredients as listed on the label:Proprietary Blend of Herbs:  1660mg per tea bagOrganic Green Tea Leaf  "  Assam Black Tea Leaf  "  Cinnamon Bark  "  Rooibos Leaf  "  Honeybush  "  Green Tea Leaf Extract  "  Ginger RootOreganic Licorice RootStevia LeafOrganic Gotu Kola Leaf  "  Ashwagandha Root  "  Shatavari Root  "  Shank PushpiL-Theanine Suntheanine®  15mgOther Ingredients:Natural Vanilla Flavor, Organic Chai Spice Flavor, Vanilla Bean.Each tea bag contains 80mg of caffeine, as compared to approx. 90mg in 8oz of coffee.Warning:Not for use by pregnant or breastfeeding women, infants or children. If you are taking MAO inhibitors or other prescription drugs, consult your healthcare professional before use.I like this tea and am having my 2nd cup as I finish this review.

I handed this tea over to my husband to drink, because he likes/consumes energy drinks a lot, and I figured he would have the best opinion on how well this tea lives up to it's name. To begin with, he was mildly impressed with the flavor. He generally likes vanilla flavor but did not seem to find this flavor to be anything remarkable. I thought it smelled pretty good when he brewed it. Reminded me of those glade plug-ins air fresheners. (Seriously!) As for the energy aspect of this tea, he said it did not affect him one bit. He drank it over several days and said he felt no difference in his energy level as a result of this tea. I was stunned by that, considering it packs 80mg of caffeine per cup! And he did not drink it watered down either! On the upside, though, he said it naturally tasted slightly sweet which he liked (no need to add sugar!), and the long list of the herbs in the tea are actually good for you, so that's a nice plus. Overall it's a good product but if you are looking for a marked energy boost, I believe this tea will not offer that. He never felt any side effects from it either, which is good. That being - no headaches, no stomach upset, no jitters, etc. It seems to be a high quality product. Maybe for people who do not regularly consume caffeine or energy drink products, this might work differently or better as an energy beverage. :)

column9: A Good Way to Start Your Day
column10: I am a tea drinker, drink lots of it and I like the spicy taste of this vanilla tea. A couple cups in the morning I'm ready to tackle my day. Much better than coffee. And there's no let down later. So two thumbs up for Yogi Teas Vanilla Spice from me.

I've been enjoying this tea. It has a very mild, pleasant flavor and you can really taste the vanilla. Everyone that has tried it has liked it.We also feel like it does give you an energy boost. On days when everyone is coming home in the evening very tired, drinking this tea seems to perk everyone up a bit. I'm careful about drinking caffeine too close to bedtime, but this tea doesn't seem to have enough caffeine to aversely affect my sleep.Overall I would recommend it. I've had Yogi teas before and some I like more than others, but this one is definitely one of the better varieties.

column9: Won't Kill My Coffee Habit But It's Alright
column10: I've been an herbal tea drinker since I was a toddler. I blame my new-agey grandmother. ;)When it comes to caffiene though, I tend to gravitate toward a steaming cup of black coffee. I like the taste and texture of coffee over tea if I want a jolt of perkiness. That said, lately I find myself shaky after my third cup. That awful jittery feeling is not fun and tends to make me so nauseous I regret my last cup of coffee. I'm not a big fan of tea as my post lunch pick-me-up, white and green teas tend to leave an awful after taste. But I am always open to trying something new when it comes to teas, again I blame my grandmother.I'm very familiar with Yogi's products. Last year I was an Amazon Subscribe & Save customer for their Yogi Woman's Nursing Support, Herbal Tea Supplement, 16-Count Tea Bags (Pack of 6) which is a great product. Their teas are well blended for whatever health benefit they are made for and for the most part they taste pretty good. I expected I would like the Vanilla Spice flavor of this one much more since I enjoy Chai.For the past week I have replaced one of my three daily cups of coffee with this to see how it would do in curing that midday jitteryfest I've had going on. It works like a charm! My problem? I don't like the taste. *head/desk* If you like a very mild, weak tea this one has a very mellow and Chai-like quality. But no matter how strong I've steeped it I just haven't cared for the flavor.If you're someone who likes the flavor of Chai and are looking for a mild caffienated beverage to give you some perk without the shakes I DO highly recommend this one. I would, however, suggest trying the Yogi Refreshing Mint Revitalize Tea, 16-Count Tea Bags (Pack of 6) as an alternative if you prefer green tea or mint over black teas, I loved it and will be reviewing it soon.

I am a big fan of herbal teas including the Yogi brand.  This tea has a very delicate vanilla aroma and a little spice but not too much.  A good afternoon pick-me-up at the office or at home on a rainy afternoon.  A good gift for a sick friend along with those homemade cookies you were planning to take.

column9: The taste is very mild - and it was only so so on the energizing
column10: I thought this would be a perfect tea to try as I am trying to cut down to one cup of coffee in the AM. So I made this about 9:30AM (I am usually at work by 8am at the latest and am usually having coffee #2 about this time). I liked the flavor but it's not very strong. Definitely can smell and taste spice but not so much the vanilla. I really like vanilla so I would have preferred that be stronger. It is smooth, not bitter, and slightly sweet - it did not need much sweetening to me.So the flavor is o.k. I like it just fine. The energizing part though - I'm not sure it gave me any energy. I did not expect it to give me anything like I would get with coffee but a very small bit would be nice. I didn't feel it delivered that. I did feel more focused - perhaps that's another benefit they didn't mention?Regardless this is a nice tea - it would be fine for a late afernoon or mid morning for those who enjoy tea's like chai with the traditional spices. I wouldn't go out of my way to pick this up but if I saw it in the store I'd likely buy it. I think it would be a nice tea to have around the house. Some tea's have odd flavors (or so the looks on my visitor's face tells me lol). This one seems solid - I think many would enjoy it.

I like this tea.  It works at least as well as coffee for me.  Actually, even better in that the energy it supplies seems to last longer than your typical cup of coffee.  As the advertising states, no jitters show up after drinking it.  I'm usually a calm type person, so it's hard to tell about the claimed mentally calming effect of this tea, but for sure it produced no anxiousness.  I remained quite calm.  The taste is good, naturally sweet.  When I first tried it I threw in some natural sweetener but soon learned it was unnecessary.  Seems to me to be a good herbal energy tea, especially if you would like to try something instead of coffee.  It does contain caffeine but also a lot of healthy herbal ingredients.Recommended.

Don't ya just hate it when the afternoon just drags on, and it's not quitin'-time for several hours?Yogi Vanilla Spice Perfect Energy Tea is a wonderful, simple, take anywhere, pick-me-up!Yogi Vanilla Spice Perfect Energy Tea has a pleasing aroma, smooth, pleasant flavor with no bitter aftertaste.  I like a little Splenda in my tea -- 'just saying. :)  Highly Recommended!  --Katharena Eiermann, 2011

I do like Yogi teas, and have tried several kinds over the years.I prepared this tea as per their instructions, letting the tea steep for 4-6 minutes.  I actually let my tea steep even longer then that.  It looked dark enough in the cup, but I found the tea too weak to only use one tea bag for an 8 ounce cup, which is what I used, and what they said to use.To me, it tasted like very weak chai tea, which I do enjoy chai tea.  The vanilla flavor was very faint, at least to me.  I was hoping for a stronger vanilla flavor to this tea.It didn't do anything for me energy wise.  Next time I use this tea, I will be using two tea bags instead of one.  It wasn't bitter to me, so I just drank it straight, using no sweetener, which I normally use honey, but that is more for if Iam drinking tea because I have a sore throat, or if the tea is bitter, which was not the case this time.Some medicinal teas do a very good job at helping with whatever ailment you have, but to me this tea will just be enjoyed as another cup of tea, without thinking it will actually go anything specific, like giving me added energy.What's funny, they compare this tea to having almost as much caffeince as a cup of coffee,80 mg for an 8 ounce cup of this tea, versus 90 mg for an 8 ounce cup of coffee, but to me, even tho I don't like my coffee very strong, one cup of coffee I would feel a difference, it would perk me up sooner, but with this tea I didn't notice any change at all.I agree, this tea does not make you jittery, because it really doesn't have any effect of that kind at all, at least not on me!

I've always liked Yogi tea, and this new blend is no exception. The vanilla flavor is subtle and refreshing, so it's not at all overpowering. As far as it delivering a boost of energy, I'm not too sure about that, but this definitely doesn't make me sleepy like some of the chamomile or licorice tea blends. Overall, this is good tea. Try it!

I have been drinking tea for over thirty years, and tea in America has improved! Vine offered me a chance to try another basic tea, and its a good entry level, AM drinking tea.I found the vanilla just a little strong for my taste, so I mixed it with black tea and it makes a large pot, perfect with stevia and a touch of milk.I do not think this would taste well without milk, but then I like the english school of tea, and do not understand why Americans try to drink black tea black, like its coffee?Not impressed my the less caffeine argument on the side of the box, the only way to get no /less caffeine in teas is to drink steeped herbs, this has tea in it, so it has cafffeine, duh.So enjoy, its good flavorful choice when tired of the basic teas.

Vanilla Energy Tea has a light, sweet scent and a sweet vanilla flavor.  There is also a hint of spices, not overpowering--just right.  I felt somewhat energized after drinking the tea, but the effect was also subtle.  I enjoyed the tea and recommend it for anyone looking for a pleasant-tasting tea without any jittery effects.

This definitely will appeal to those who enjoy a vanilla spice flavor to their tea.  I tried not to steep mine for too long (the package says 4-6 minutes), but the flavors were still there and pleasant enough.  The tea itself is not the greatest, but it is a mixed blend of a few types of tea so you are not going to get the best of all worlds just something from each type of tea (as pointed out the steeping time(s) are different for each type of tea, so when you mix them you're going to be missing out on at least one of them).  Otherwise, it's an enjoyable tea, I definitely wasn't jittery and the tea did wake me up, so recommended for that.

column9: The perfect energy might be coming from the caffeine boost, instead of the herbs!  It also doesn't have much flavor.
column10: I tried this one and Yogi Refreshing Mint Revitalize Tea, 16-Count Tea Bags (Pack of 6) at the same time.  Well, not in the same cup at the same time, but within the same week.  This one can't compare to the mint one.  Maybe since my palate likes black tea over green.  I can smell the great scent of vanilla and ginger, but something is lost in the taste.  It could be that too many flavors are coming to this party.  There are two types of red tea, then green tea and also Assam black tea in this. There are some herbs that make me laugh, like Shank Pushpi and then oddly trademarked ingredients like L-Theanine Suntheanine.  I have to watch this one when it brews. The other one I tried, the mint, doesn't get bitter if you let it brew too long, this one almost has to be brewed at the minimum time stated on the package, which is four minutes, in order for it to taste the best.  I don't like the flavor of this without sugar.  It's a bit too astringent.  Again, that might be the weird mix of green and red teas, along with herbs and ingredients I haven't ran across before now.  It packs even more caffeine than the mint tea, 80mg when a cup of coffee has 90mg.  It's strong stuff.Overall, I got this box to review and will drink it merrily with a bit of sugar in it, watching closely to make sure I don't overbrew it.  I can't use the bags over again, it's way too  bitter.  I don't think I'd buy a box of this because the flavor isn't that interesting to me, even though it has a lot of the spices and herbs I enjoy in teas -- cinnamon, licorice, natural vanilla flavor, vanilla bean, chai spice, ginger -- I don't get why I don't like this as much as I feel I should.  Perhaps there is too much of everything in this tea, making none of the herbs or teas stick out so it is has a lackluster taste.  It isn't horrible, but it's all the memorable either.  It does energize me, but I am not sure if it is because I just drank the tea version of coffee or if I am getting any benefit from the weird mix of herbs, spices and other ingredients.
My wife is the tea drinker and she says this tea is flavorful and the blend of vanilla and spice tastes and smells wonderful

I don't know, maybe I expect too much."Perfect Energy"? "Vanilla Spice"? Those phrases evoke something pretty awesome in my mind, while this tea is just... fine. Nothing objectionable, but nothing fabulous either.I didn't notice the energy lift being any more perfect than any other mildly-caffeineated tea. About equivalent to an Oolong, maybe. The flavors of vanilla and spice were both very gentle, not strong enough to add milk and make chai. Fine with a bit of sweetener and no milk, though.Maybe the fact that the other Yogi Tea flavor I like is ginger has set me up to expect something with a bit more punch.

I'm not sure what I enjoy the most about this Yogi tea flavor.  The tea smells so delicious as it is steeping. The taste is also wonderful.  It tastes like vanilla chai.  The tea is sweet and no additional sweetener is necessary. As far as the energy aspect, I do believe it.  I have been drinking a cup every morning after my workout and have had an high energy and focus level for the rest of the day.  It seems to be a long lasting effect with no sudden energy burst or drop.  Perfect.  I'm planning on ordering more before my supply runs out!  Highly recommended.NOTE: I have purchased this item since my review.

I was expecting vanilla flavor with maybe a true spicy flavor, something like a lingering taste of cinnamon maybe. But there was nothing. Barely could I taste the vanilla. I was really bummed, usually I use energizing teas as a pick me up. I make some, freeze it, and when I'm running around with my kids in the early hours, I have something refreshing and light to drink. But this tea was very flat tasting. And didn't give a boost of energy.

This is quite an enjoyable tea. There's a bit of a mixed message that comes across when it talks about giving you energy without the jitters, since it is a caffeinated product. I drink it for the flavor, which I enjoy. I didn't find that it energized me, but neither does coffee, so that doesn't mean that it wouldn't energize others. Caffeine doesn't impact me at all so I am not a good benchmark for that.I didn't like having yoga promoted on the box because of the religious connections, but that wouldn't prevent me from purchasing it again. It has been a nice cup of tea on a cold winter day. I've also enjoyed the clever proverbs on the teabag tags. That's a nice addition.

column9: tasty with almost as much caffeine as coffee
column10: Although it advertises energy without the jitters, this is not a caffeine free product.  The nutrition label states that it contains 80mg of caffeine compared to an 8 oz cup of coffee which contains 90mg.  If you don't don caffeine, this is not the tea for you.As for flavor, it is a mild tea with a hint of vanilla and spice.  It is not sweet even though it has stevia in it and I recommend using your favorite sweetener.  I use splenda or agave nectar.  Without the sweetness, the flavor is a little on the light side so don't cheat yourself by a short steep time.  If steeped long enough, and sweetened, it is very tasty and a great substitute for that cup of coffee.

column9: Not a plesant combination of flavors
column10: I am not a tea drinker, so I let my wife try this product since she enjoys tea and has several varieties on hand at any given time.  She was eager to try this vanilla spice tea, since she had never had tea flavored in such a way.She had the tea as a mid-afternoon "pick me up," intrigued by its package claim, "energizes the body and focuses the mind."  Her initial reaction was not enthusiastic.  In fact, she wasn't thrilled with the combination of vanilla and tea.  She looked at the package information and found that an 8-ounce cup of this tea contains only 10 mg. less caffeine than an equivalent cup of coffee, so the "Naturally energizes without the jitters" package claim is misleading.  The tea contains quite a bit of caffeine.She tried a second cup the next day, wanting to be sure to give it a fair evaluation.  The second cup confirmed her opinion.  Yogi's Vanilla Spice Perfect Energy tea is far less satisfying than peppermint tea, green tea, or orange spice tea, three of her favorites.  She would not be inclined to try this product again.

column9: Okay taste, just not for me.
column10: It's a great taste, but it's not for me. Others may like it, but for me, it's not bad but just in-between. This tea is calming and relaxing. Maybe drink it before you go to sleep.

column9: Thanks for providing a hard to find item.
column10: I can no longer find these cough drops in local stores.  They are strong, and work great on helping to keep my sinuses and throat clear.  Thanks again.

Halls soothes my throat like no other reasonably priced cough drop! I tried some of the more expensive ones in the drug stores, compared them and saw that they all have the same basic ingredients. Gave me no other choice but to find the best deal online if possible. Amazon rocks!

Halls "Plus" cough drops are the best and only cough drop that really stops a cough. After weeks of extremely bad coughs and bronchitis, we found Halls Plus was the only cough drop that would control our coughs. In fact it was even better than a prescription cough syrup. The difficulty we had was the drug stores and grocery stores very seldom carried the "Plus" product. Finally we checked Amazon and were able to order it and received it within 2 days. The Halls non plus and brand name cough drops did not work. The Halls "Plus" was always successful.

Tried just about most and these are just okay. I do not use them myself, but a lovely lady I die for is an expert and you can tell when she is seriously pleased, or just satisfied. This product warrants a 3 Star and the comments were that they did not have the punch that. let's say Honey's, have. In our situation the stronger the mix the more satisfied she is. Fisherman's have a very strong one, Riccola are pretty decent, and I guess that what drives her to consumption is that she claims they help her to breathe well and since my job is to find the best for the moola I asked her about Halls Plus Drops, Honey Lemon, 25-Count Drops (Pack of 12) and she said for me to get her the, Honeys?, next time. I suppose people have different tastes and I am not criticizing or putting down the fine reviewers that gave this product many stars. Everyone is perfectly entitled to their own opinion, where one person might like a particular product, another might not. So I guess is all about the average from the number of reviews that I look for. 3 Stars.

I lived in Germany for 6 years, the last 3 years was in Baumholder, I have not had a Ferrero Hanuta Chocolate Hazelnut Candy Wafer in 27 years and thought I would never ever be able to have them again unless I jumped on a plane and went back to Germany, thanks to Amazon, they brought a taste of Germany here to me in the states, I received mine today and I have to say it was like stepping back in time, exactly as I remembered them, these things are so good you will hurt your self on them, ABSOLUTLY!!!!! now for me its more than just how good they are, its the emotions that flooded me and all the memories of a very good time in my life long ago, if you have never been out of the states , you have no idea what you are missing in the world, give these a try, you wont go wrong,, they have a lot of other good things also,  PS,, Don't get me wrong I love America and would never trade her for anything

column9: what to expect from the product
column10: i had an issue at first with the order. i ordered the 36 count times three boxes and they only send me the 3 small boxes containing 12 pieces. i contacted the distributor via e-mail and within a week i received the remaining of the items. at first i was upset and confused why they only sent me the small boxes and i thought i would just going to be charged for something that does not exist (36 count boxes). but the business owner was very curteous and fixed their problem. the hanuta was great and appears that it taste better than the small pack hanuta maybe because they are sealed better. but either way, at first i said i will not order anything from them, but i changed my mind once they fixed the problem. hanuta is greta better than anything Ferrerro ever came up with. buy some, you'll enjoy them too and you will ask for more, they are very addictive.

column9: If you love Nutella, you'll love Hanuta!
column10: Tried these when my mother brought some back from Germany.  The best way to describe them is that they are like Nutella filled wafer biscuits, just delicious (if you enjoy Nutella.)  I also like that they are individually wrapped, so you don't have to eat the entire package within a few days to keep them from going stale.  Great for packed lunches too. A+ product.
Why are all German products so expensive on Amazon ??I would buy more German candy if it wouldn't be so high !These taste so good I used to eat them all the time but I can't find these in US stores.

I was about to order these but saw that the second ingredient is hydrogenated oil. Since this oil is so harmful it's banned for use in restaurants  in some cities I'm amazed to see it here. No thanks.
My Uncle used to bring these home when he would come back from Germany.  They are seriously the most amazing thing ever made!

Got this for a gift.  Pricey because of the fact that it is a real import from Germany.  Product reportedly arrived promptly and well packed.  Taste was fresh and as expected.  Would prefer the single packs if they were available.

column9: W A R N I N IN G
column10: T H I S  C H O C O L A T E  I S  A D D I C T I O N  I  C A N 'T  S T O P  E A T I N G  I T T T T T
Good taste, just like the regular onesñ. Specially made for kids. The wrapping was awful, though.

column9: taste great but hard on the intestine...
column10: i love peach o's and so i was thrilled to find a sugar free option when i was on atkins.  i had about 10 and paid dearly for the next 4-5 hours with extreme gas, and i am not a gassy person at all!  they taste amazing, so if you can stick to just having 1 or 2 in a sitting, they are wonderful.

I really like these, and have used them to make my own trail mix.  However, I have recently had a hard time finding them *anywhere*.  Russell Stover, please don't stop making these, for those of us who are not supposed to be eating regular chocolate.  Take pity on us, please.

column9: seriously, 18 lb bag for a 100 lb dog?
column10: 18 lb bags are perfect for dogs you can fit in your purse. However for large breed dogs as the product states, this bag will last all of 4 days. AMAZON: please list a subscribe and save for 50 lb bags.

First of all, Amazon, if you read this, PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE make pet food available for Subscribe & Save!!! :)I buy this at my local Walmart. I live in a small bedroom community to a larger town, and I really try to stick to foods I can get easily without having to make a special commute into town to go to a pet store. It's about $30 a bag at Walmart - so close to what Amazon charges. I was looking for something slightly cheaper than Iams that my dog would like better. He would often let his breakfast sit until dinner time because I don't think he cared for the Iams.My dog is a 104 lb German Shepherd, so he is a big boy who definitely benefits from a large breed formula. He seems to really like this Purina, he wolfs it down in the mornings now. I like that it's $10 cheaper than Iams, but still a high quality food that has good ingredients. I think the first one is a meat. There are no fillers or soy in it either, which will save on vet bills in the long run.HOWEVER... and this is a dealbreaker... this gives my dog the WORST GAS. Like.... room-clearing gas. It's utterly disgusting. He has it consistently for an hour or two after he eats... and the only word for it is NASTY. It took a couple of weeks of this food before it set in (and nothing else has changed in his diet or habits)... I think I had already bought the second bag of it before I made the connection.We will be switching to a different food. I picked up plain old Pedigree at the grocery store last time I stocked up. It is a much cheaper food, that requires I feed him 50% more by volume for the same weight (6 cups a day versus 4 cups) so that negates any savings. I think the Pedigree was $20 a bag, and the main ingredient is a filler. =/ I didn't know these things when I bought it, I just wanted something, ANYTHING, other than the Purina and it's stink bombs.We will probably be switching back to Iams, alas.

This is a great Chai to go along with the many other spectacular Chai's made by Celestial Seasonings. It is light, and a good drink before bed due to it being decaffeinated. I found this blend to be best with half and half with some light brown sugar to make it nice and creamy. This is a great tea!

A co-worker introduced me to this wonderful tea and I am hooked.  Let me see if I can describe it.  I like Chai Tea, but sometimes the "smokiness" of the chai can be overwhelming to me.  This tea combines the lovely sweetness of coconut with the dark rich quality of the chai.  The aroma is a treat as well.  Everyone I have made this for LOVES this tea.  When I brew this tea, I am able to use one tea bag for 2-3 cups of hot water and it still is flavorable.  I drink it with a small amount of cream and one artificial sweetner, but many of my friends like it without any sweetner at all.  I highly recommend this tea.

This is my all time favorite decaf chai.  The coconut undertone is subtle, but definitely present.  This is a very smooth chai, with a full, but not strong taste, which I prefer at bedtime.  As with all CS chais, I wish they would use a bit more cardamom.

I am a big fan of the high quality of Celestial Seasonings products and their usually good tea blends.  This particular blend does not make the cut. I want to like it but somehow the coconut does not really work in this tea.  The aroma is artificial coconut, and the flavor is a strange somewhat musty coconut flavor without noticable chai spice.  Drinkable but an eccentric blend--perhaps a diehard coconut lover would find this appealing.Celestial Seasonings gets extra points for their packaging: they utilize 100% natural recycled paperboard in their boxes and they don't package each tea bag individually. Instead they use a system of a waxed paper bag inside the box that stays shut when you fold it. It keeps the bags fresh and utilizes less packaging than individually wrapping each bag. The art they use on each box is beautiful as are the quotes and information they put on every surface.Quote from the box:"Love the moment and the energy of that moment will spread beyond all boundaries." Corita Kent.

column9: Got me on the tea bandwagon
column10: When in Boulder this summer I took a tour of the Celestial Seasonings factory.  Kind of boring.  Except for the enclosed room where they keep the various mint herbs.  It will clear your sinuses!  But I digress.  You do get to sample any tea they have and that is worth the trip.In any case, I love this tea.  I have always enjoyed the iced tea they serve at Thai restaurants.  Not the full version with the sweetened cream.  Just straight.  To me, this is very close.  I kind of wish it was caffeinated, but its nice to have something to drink at night.Coconut flavor?  If I had drank it not knowing what it was, I'm not sure I'd be able to identify such a flavor.  But something about this tea does have a very unique flavor, which I like.  And it is also absent vanilla, a flavor I dislike in teas.I drink it iced.  I have gone thru 6 boxes in a couple of months and re-ordered early via Amazon's subscription service and am pleased.
I love having this tea in the evening with milk and honey.  It's not overly coconutty, but there are hints of it and overall it's just a lovely tea with a nice slightly spicy sweetness to it.

column9: Outstanding Decaf Tea  - Spiced Coconut Thai
column10: The freshness of the product was outstanding.  The product is shipped neatly, in containers that you would find in the store(not bulk) and excellent for giving a way to friends to try as well as sipping on this unique, robust flavored tea.I highly recommend this product.  It is truly outstanding!

When it comes to Chai tea, this Celestial Seasonings Chai Decaf Tea, Sweet Coconut Thai is my favorite. I really love the Indian and Thai fusion of flavors in this tea. A perfect combination I must say. I like the coconut taste in this tea, and when it comes to Thai-inspired at-home teas, this Celestial Seasonings Sweet Coconut Chai definitely tastes better than Yogi Tea's Sweet Thai Delight tea. It's also a bonus that this tea is decaffeinated, and as the other Amazon reviewers have said, this tea is definitely perfect for relaxation and before going to bed. If you like Thai-inspired teas such as this, I also suggest trying Harney and Sons' Bangkok Green Tea with Thai Flavors. It's an excellent, delicious fine tea with coconut, vanilla, ginger, and lemongrass. I also highly recommend The Coffee Bean and Tea Leaf's Thai-picked Lemon Chamomile, Blueberry Peach Green Tea, and Spring Peach Oolong Teas. Another tea with some Thai influence is the Fairmont Hotels and Resorts' Organic Berry Berry Caffeine-Free tea. For cold Thai teas, I highly recommend Taste Nirvana's Real Thai Tea Latte and Real Green Tea Latte. My parents were born and raised in Thailand, and thus I'm Thai American. If you actually visit Thailand, which I have multiple times since the majority of my relatives live there, then I highly recommend trying Thai Chrysanthemum tea. I had the best tea I've ever had in my entire life in Thailand. And that's saying something because I've actually traveled up (sometimes my small traveling party and I had to walk a long and grueling hike for intervals of 30 minutes to a whole hour. Even actor Blair Underwood made a comment how he was amazed that even elderly Chinese women could climb up these mountains for long periods of time, and claimed they were in better shape than him! That's how I felt as well. If you visit China, you will see that a lot of Chinese are very physically fit - they walk, hike, bike a lot and do all sorts of exercises such as swimming and Tai Chi and fan exercises in their parks) the tea-growing terraced mountains in and around the Guilin region of China and tasted tea from those Chinese regions and also tasted some tea when I traveled to Japan, but those Asian teas don't compare to the Chrysanthemum tea I had many years back in northern Thailand. (I haven't traveled to England and India yet, but would love to. I bet the teas there are amazing. But like I said, from all the countries I've traveled to so far - Thailand has the best teas, cold and hot.) When I think about it, I was very young then, and I should have asked the Thai waitress where they got their tea from. All I know is that I drank that tea at a restaurant at a Thai hotel resort many years back in Northern Thailand not far from Chiang Rai and the Golden Triangle region. Anyways, I have given boxes of this Celestial Seasonings Sweet Coconut Thai Chai Decaf Tea as small gifts to friends in the past few years. The fact that you can order this in packs of six at an affordable price is great, and allows you the luxury to share some of this tea with friends and family. My verdict is that this is a nice aromatic, delicious tea to unwind for the day.

I received this tea as a gift and it sat in the pantry for 6 months. When I finally tried it I was in love! I drink it all the time now! I use a little cream and honey and its fabulous! I am a huge coconut fan, but I didn't really notice much of the coconut.This is wonderful if you are a chai tea fan!

column9: Terrific but a bit pricey compared to buying it in stores
column10: I love this tea. Its terrific for night-time when caffeine would be a bad idea. It satisfies the sweet tooth without all the calories. But Amazon has its price about 30% above what can be found in the stores. If one buys a big carton of 6 boxes, it would seem that the price should be lower.

I'm really fond of this chai.  I like a lot of chais, but this one is unique with the blend of red and decaf black tea, sweetened with coconut.  It forgives a long steep or a wide range of temperatures (though hotter temps bring out better flavor), and I find the blend of flavors quite nice, particularly for such an inexpensive brand of tea.As with most chais, this tea is not at all bitter.

I am a fan of many different teas, with my taste spanning from herbal, black, white, green, and roobios. I appreciate the kick of some caffeine, but when evening arrives, that "kick" will keep me up all night. Enter this wonderful Thai coconut chai, and I have a wonderful evening beverage. Add a smidge of milk and sugar and it is honestly perfection. The flavors are well-balanced, and perfectly-suited to any time of the day. My kids (age 7 and 9) are hooked as well. It's their favorite tea, hands down.
This is my favorite tea. It's perfect for quelling a sweet tooth in the late afternoon and evening. And it's caffeine-free to boot.
A great decaffeinated tea!! Perfect before bedtime or anytime! I add a little cream and sweetener and it turns into a delicious light creamy drink! So flavorful!

I love this tea! It's a greta product. One bag is strong enough for a very large cup and I can taste all the good flavors. I like the fact it's a decaf so I can drink it any time of day and night. I'm having it now :-)  My order came in bulk but it's O.K. because it made a nice little gift to my friend who's an avid chai sipper.

I love this tea. After I brew it I add just a dash of milk, not too much, and some sugar. Nice smell and aroma. Very relaxing. The coconut is there but not overwhelming. I just tried the Chai from Tazo and I think I will go back to the Coconut Celestial Seasonings.

column9: Not so sweet or tasty, in my opinion
column10: Everyone has their own taste.  I'm a huge fan of the Good Earth caffeine-free original tea, but my local stores stopped carrying it, so I tried this one from a big box store as a substitute.  The price was right, but it doesn't taste sweet or spicy, compared to the Good Earth.

Celestial Seasonings Chai Decaf Tea, Sweet Coconut is my favorite decaf tea. I drink it all day. Until I found this tea, I thought I would never find a decaf Chai that was full of flavor. If you love Chai, this is a winner!
Rooibos has a lot of health benefits so I'm really glad I found this tea. It's very sweet and wonderful before bed.

My favorite tea, and my only tea. Two tea bags easily makes a full quart. To this I add a heaping teaspoon of xylitol, which is a healthy and alkalizing sweetener.I especially like that this tea is caffeine free and features rooibos tea. Rooibos tea is as healthy as green tea, I've read, and it's far more palatable when combined with these delicious spices.I see one reader didn't like the coconut flavoring. Fair enough, but I recommend you try buying one box locally and deciding for yourself. I like everything about the flavor, as do many others who rated the tea. And the prices offered here can't be beat.

column9: Perfect way to end the day
column10: I have been drinking this pretty much every evening for the past year.  I had a hard time finding this flavor in my local stores, and I was delighted to find it at Amazon.  Yes, it might be a bit more expensive this way, but it's worth it to me to have 6 shiny boxes lined up on my shelves, all ready for me to brew a cup.  In a way it reminds me of an old flavor from Celestial Seasonings--Pelican Punch.  I agree with the person who loves chai spice flavor but sometimes finds that to be a bit too dark.  This decaf coconut thai is excellent!  And in the daytime I love PG Tips, another black caffeinated tea that is available through Amazon.
This is my favorite chai flavor of all the different brands I've tried.  It doesn't really taste like coconut, but....  it's good nonetheless.
I just found this tea and it is my favorite drink at the time. I love it with half and half and splenda. Great for the Fall and Winter. I recommend you try it.
I love this tea it is really good if you add a little milk or creamvery fast shipping

column9: Do not like the taste.  Amazon packaging is great.
column10: I read all the nice reviews here before i made the purchase.  But it is really not my 'cup of tea'.  All the nice descriptions could not help.  It tastes like medicine.  On top of that, of course it is not returnable.I am going to see whether my colleague would enjoy them.  I am happy as long as I do not have to drink it myself.
This tea tastes more like spiced tea rather than coconut.  Try CS vanilla maple if you crave an excellent tea.

Thank you for the fast delivery of my product.  My only compliant was that when I received my package it was in a box twice the size of the original package.  This in turn had cost me an extra $30 (because of the size of the box) to be delivered to me as I reside in Bermuda and have a US mail address for ordering items on the web.  For future my I ask that the package be shipped in the original box.Thanks kindly

column9: Excellent, but PRICE is way off!
column10: This is an excellent product, but for the same quantity it is $5.34 at Costco.I use this for cleaning and getting rid of stubborn odors everywhere, and it just works.  I seriously don't know why it is so overpriced from this merchant though.
I found this at Costco today for 6.59. Seriously irritated. I payed 3 times that...pfft.I guess I need to start checking around a bit more.
It is an industry standard for a reason, exceptional in and for everything I use with it.

Started using this instead of bubbles in sons' bath, and its helped alleviate his eczema & itching.We had a big bag like this for years before figuring out how to use it up.Turns out it is fun to play with in the bath as well, so double the benefit at a good price.

I am rating for the product not the price. I have found it much cheaper in Costco & BJ's. I use this product for my almost 3 yr old son's bath along with Epsom Salt. He has sensitive skin & allergies. The baking soda & Epsom salt bath helps to detox him. The size is very convenient. Now I don't have to buy a million little boxes.
I sprinkle a layer of baking soda at the bottom of cat litter box and it absorbs the urine and odor, it works wonderfully!!

For those who like to do two or more things at once, this is the product for you. It freshens laundry, removes stains from dishware AND best of all, whitens teeth. I love products that have more than one function. Arm & Hammer put natural products on the map. I love it. A++

There are few things today that have stood the test of time, and still have as much value as this product.  Couldn't believe all of the uses they have on the website. column9: Great Buy and the Price is Right!
column10: we've been devout Folgers coffee drinkers for over 35 years and never thought we'd switch brands. after my husband had a bout of heart problems, he was told to go to decaf coffee or stop drinking it, which wasn't an option. we started buying the Folgers half caff and he cut back to 2 cups a day. when i bought the keurig coffee maker Keurig B70 Platinum Brewing System i switched to the Green Mountain Breakfast Blend Green Mountain Coffee Breakfast Blend, 24-Count K-Cup for Keurig Brewers (love it) and bought the ekobrew refillable k-cup Ekobrew Cup,Refillable K-Cup For Keurig K-Cup Brewers 2-Pack - BROWN $ GREEN for him and his Folgers half-caff.on a whim, i decided to buy a small box of the Green Mountain half-caff k cups for him to try. i was very nervous about it because he's such a die-hard Folgers kind of guy. since i don't care for decaff coffee i didn't want to have to drink it if he didn't like it. he took a couple big drinks of the coffee and i finally asked him how he liked it. he said he liked it a lot, and thought it was much better than the Folgers half-caff, it seemed to have a lot more flavor. phew!in fairness to Folgers half-caff ground coffee, the reason he may think the Green Mountain half-caff has more flavor could be because of how much of the Folgers he used to make a cup. with these refillable k-cups it doesn't seem to be an exact science, so one cup could be a bit stronger or weaker than the next. i think this is what he was saying. because the Green Mountain k-cups are accurately pre-measured, you get the same taste in every cup.the bottom line is, he loves the Green Mountain half-caff coffee, and we will definitely be buying more of it. i asked him if he wanted to try the Folgers half-caff keurig coffee and he said, "ummm, i don't know". for a hard-core coffee drinker to be ok with that kind of change says a lot about the GM half-caff coffee. as least it speaks to me of how great this coffee is.

Hazelnuts were one of the foundational foods of paleolithic and neolithic communities in western Eurasia, from the British isles to Turkey and the Caucasus. There are hazelnut shell mounds, comparable to the sea-shell mounds of Mayan and other New World cultures, still being discovered in Europe and Turkey and being excavated. Their bulk testifies to the nutritional importance of hazelnuts in prehistoric cultures. One such mound on the Isle of Man has been dated as 9000 years old; other mounds are mentioned in the wikipedia article devoted to hazelnuts.Hazelnuts and filberts are not precisely synonymous, though most of the nuts grown in Oregon and Washington are hybrids or cultivars of the two. Genuine hazelnuts from Turkey and Italy are far more flavorful than the Oregon 'filbazelnuts', but the time-lag between the nut grove in Anatolia and the supermarket in your neighborhood may impact the quality and freshness of imported hazels. The Bergin Company, with headquarters in Minnesota, packages Turkish hazelnuts but labels them filberts. Go figure!There seems to be a surge in popularity of hazelnuts in the USA and Canada these days, with Italian gelato/ice cream becoming a standard flavor. Hazelnuts blend well with chocolate, both in ice cream and in candy. The whole nuts can be eaten raw or roasted, and their nutritional value is high. Hazelnut-milk is a very tasty substitute for cow's milk, with a far more agreeable flavor than soya-milk. On the other hand, hazelnut-flavored coffee is (to my tastebuds) an abomination. Hazelnut oil is wonderful in salad dressings, but expensive; it should never be used for cooking, especially not for frying.No, I don't own a hazelnut grove, nor am I connected in any way to hazelnut marketing. I just like the things a lot, and hope to see high-quality hazels more widely available in markets everywhere.
