This is an outstanding kit, there IS everything you need to makecheese exept the pot and the milk.I'm going through the book as the author suggests, starting atpage 1 and understanding the concepts and the chemistry involved.Nothing is too difficult to understand, unless you skip around,(like my hubby does), then you can get a little confused.but all in all I'm very pleased with the product.
What can you say about sardines, in oil, good size and flavorful.  Well packaged, I love the little bone-in and skin-on.  Good for anytime snack(s).  from China, best price I could find.

column9: Ordered 25-count,got 2 pieces.Seller explained it was a spam listing.
column10: Petco.com explained it was a spam listing.But just wondering why amazon.com allowed the spam listing on their website to collect money? Anyway, seller has refund money.The two pieces Snozzles have very bad oil smell.Have droped it to trash can.

I am writing this to inform you, and save you the headache. Like the others, I saw this 25-pack of snozzles at a price too good to be true, and naively purchased them immediately for my dogs. They were listed and sold by PetCo. When they came, I got one huge box, containing a lot of stuffing paper, and a single tiny snozzle....joke was on me it seems.After this, PetCo emailed me a generic message saying there was a discrepancy with the item listing, and they sent me the wrong amount. I emailed PetCo and never received a response. I checked their seller profile, and found a gigantic archive of negative seller ratings, many of them specifically related to the same issue I was experiencing. I then emailed them a few more times. I'm not surprised they never answered a single one of them. Probably too backed up with hundreds of other emails like mine.I never did get my other 24 snozzles, although they refunded me, probably because I kept emailing them. I gave my dog the single snozzle we got, and they did not even want it. I examined it, and it has a chemical smell to it, and looks old. It is quite unfair how someone does this, and can just get away with it, and one does not even get a personal apology.I have decided to join a few others in going to the Better Business Bureau about this. Hope you decide to join in too.
Received exactly ONE item - not the multi-pack as described. Petco blamed Amazon, Amazon blamed Petco. Payment was refunded, but trust in Amazon and Petco lost.

It is unfortunate that ratings from 2010 still dominate the ratings for this item.  The listing now specifically says 25 count and that is exactly what I received the first time I ordered these.  I had no fear ordering these regardless of the negative postings, as Amazon is an amazing site and stands by its products.By the way, my Belgian Shepard, Cooper, loves these things and they are a welcome change from pig ears.  Giving him these to chew following his regular, weight-watching meal keeps his teeth clean and extends his 'eating' experience.

We initially purchased some Merrick Snozzles at our local pet superstore at the recommendation of one of their personnel who said they were better for puppies than the rawhide chews. Rawhide used to really tear up our last dog's stomach, so we didn't feed them to him for long. Our Airedale Terrier loves them. Now that he's a year old, one will only last him about 20 minutes vs. lasting a couple of days when he was younger, but they have never upset his stomach. Buying them in bulk on Amazon is also a lot cheaper than buying them individually at the pet store.

however the dogs went crazy for these. I'll probably order more in the future if I can find a good deal. Fyi, they are pig snouts, so if you are squeemish...*Petco did refund my money, so all is good.

column9: Good product but bad math skills
column10: Dog loved the treat, but I ordered 3 packages of 25 each for a total of 75 pieces. I recieved 3 pieces. I did get a refund after complaining, but think they need a calculator.

This was a COMPLETE RIPOFF.  There were supposed to be 25 count in the package and there was only 1. This was the fault of the company not Amazon.It didn't take long to get credit but I thought it was BS they didn't honor their advertising.I will NEVER buy from them again.

column9: Bad business.  Order cancelled by the supplier.  Never received them.
column10: I was notified that there was a mistake in price so my order was cancelled right away by the supplier.  I never received my item.
My dog realy loved them, too bad I only recieved 2-5 count, not the 25 count as stated in the ad.I think there was a mix-up, my money was refunded.

Ordered 2 lots of 25 each. Reciever one single item. They refunded my $$$ but they should have honored the original order ammount. Even the invoice I recied said 2 orders of 25. Typical bait and switch! But the dog luved the Snozzle!

column9: Bad Business Practice byPetco and Amazon.com
column10: I decided to try these because they had a very nice offer for a 25 count.I purchased and paid for the Snozzles and awaited my package to arrive.A few days later, instead of my package arriving I received an email stating this they do not carry the Merrick Snozzles Pork Chew Dog Treat in a 25 pack.Well if you don't carry it then why is it still listed on Amazon.com's website.In my opinion either Petco or Amazon.com should have honored this sale.They did not and shame on them.

column9: After I ordered I was told that the ad was a mistake & the price was not honored!
column10: Placed order then got an email stating that the ad on Amazon.com was in error and that they unfortunately cannot fill my order.  What ever happened with customer service that if the price is wrong its YOUR problem not mine. Neither Petco nor Amazon.com stepped up to the plate!  As my grandfather taught me, measure twice and cut once.  Obviously someone didn't read before they pressed the listing button and the customers paid the price.

column9: Good Product but on the expensive side.
column10: Our two small dogs really enjoyed the snozzles.  Since the dogs are only about 6 pounds each, I cut a snozzles in half to make them go a little further.  These are rather expensive treats for dogs.

column9: Lower protein than the pork flavor
column10: I have been using this flavor as well as the pork flavor for my feral queen whose kidneys are failing.  Like the Hill's k/D and Purina N/F, this does not have meat as the first or second ingredient.  It's lower protein than the Royal Canin pork flavor, too.  But, unlike the k/d and n/f, my cat will eat this stuff.  And it doesn't seem to make her sick.  At least so far.Word to the wise:  if you're feeding dry food to a CRF kitty, make sure she has lots and lots and lots of fresh clean water available.

column9: Renal failure cat likes it over all others
column10: I guess my cat is the judge here and she likes it over all the other dry renal foods. She's a picky eater too since she got renal failure. She also likes the Royal Canin canned morsels, the 2.5 oz can.

Bought this to replace Prescription Diet Feline K/D that my one of my cats had to eat after a renal dysfunction diagnosis. He  ate it  but din't particularly loved it. He clearly prefers Royal Canin over PD. Maybe it's the softer texture (not much teeth left, bad dentition case). Even the other cats prefer this food to theirs (so I guess the taste is better too). I have to supervise the meal times now. And about the efficiency of the food (mixed with K/D caned food and renal powder): my 14 year old big lazy cat is like almost a kitty again. He runs all around, he regain his personality, he plays and purrs all the time.

column9: like many similiar foods, poor quality ingredients, but may need anyway
column10: like many similiar foods, poor quality ingredients.  I only bought it as emergency food for when my cat refuses all wet food.  at least I know the levels of phosphorous etc are safe for him.

I tried this BBQ sauce over the summer on ribs and chicken and it has a nice, bold sweet taste.It's a good brand. I like the other products by this company. It make cost a few cents more and it's worth it. Try it.

column9: Better than other brands I've tried
column10: This seems much less chemically, and is fresher tasting, than other canned or foil-pouch packed poultry products I've tried.I'm old enough to remember when cans were packed full of the actual product on the label, so it's really annoying that most cans I buy now are about half full of product, with the rest of the can being filled with liquid.However, these cans are much fuller than other brands I've tried.  The liquid is broth, and it seems to keep the chicken meat flavorful and in good condition.  The chunks are of a generally nice, useful size.  The meat doesn't tend to disintegrate or mush, like other canned chicken brands I've tried.  The meat also was not stringy, dry or of a bad texture.  It really was a very noticeable improvement over the other brands.I will keep this product on hand as a staple in my pantry.

This is good quality canned chicken breast. Nice big chunks and a delicious broth that you can also use. Obviously, as with any canned meat, it is not comparable to freshly cooked chicken but it's a great go-to meat when you don't have time to thaw something out.This would work well for soups or chicken salad or just on it's own as a low-carb snack.

Great gift, delicious treats, individually wrapped, ready to enjoy!  Nice hostess gifts as well as convenient to pull out for drop in guests.  We try to keep a canister available at all times.  Very nice candy which appeals to nearly everyone.
I bought this candy for a relative for Xmas and got totally hosed on the price. I should have held out and bought it for a third of the price when it went on sale at Walgreen's. Stupid me.
This seasoning never lasts long in our cupboard.And, it's time to order more.That pretty much says it all, doesn't it?

Our daughter loves to cook so we sent the Tuscan & Mediteranean versions to our her for Christmas.  She called us Christmas morning to tell us how much she absolutely loved them.  She said (and I quote) "When I opened them and smelled them it brought tears to my eyes.  They smell so good it makes me want to cry.  I didn't think food could make me feel this way.  These are the only spices I want to use from now on!"  Of course I ordered some for myself right away and will post an update as soon as I try them for myself.

We enjoy this salt mixture on roasted vegetables, grilled meats, and whatever I think to put it on.  We originally got it in Oregon and when it was used up... I went looking and found it here.  What a relief... we are happily using it again and our food has perked up!
We love this salt product, it's great on everything including popcorn.I also like to give it in gift bags.

Tiny Footprint Light Roast coffee is the almost the mildest of all the coffees I have tried. I also like high caffeine coffee. Remember: Light roast = high caffeine. Most people think the opposite.Anyway, I like this, and the price is very reasonable, especially in the three pound bag. Note: It is NOT for people who like the taste of dark roast coffee.Another note: This company markets the product as "ecologically very sound", which is good. I have asked, and they also are proud that they compensate their coffee growers at fair prices, even though they are not certified as Fair Trade.

I thought I would give this a try.  Compared to other light roasts I've purchased (Gevalia) it's dark and it has a bitter taste. Not smooth.  It's more like a burned ash taste.  Some may like this taste. I don't.  I can't stand Starbucks for example, but if you do, you may enjoy these beans.  I'll try a courser grind next and update if the grind makes any difference.

I use Diabetisweet for cooking and baking (both the white and brown sugar versions).  With no glycemic response, it lets me make "friendly" sauces, toppings, and baked goods - with absolutely no taste difference or any other perceptible difference from sugar.  You can caramelize with it (yumm... cinnamon buns!), bake with it, and substitute it one-for-one for sugar in your coffee or tea.  The brown sugar version is great for topping oatmeal, too!
Can't use this as 100% replacement for sugar for baking or cooking. Gave me the worst stomach cramps followed by diahrea and gas. Small amount is OK. It may just be my side effects.

column9: A good sweetener for many things
column10: I like Diabetisweet for many reasons.First of all, it's not the same as the others, it's not aspartame, or saccharine or sucrolose, so I can have additional options for sweetening.Another thing I discovered by mistake is that Diabetisweet browns better than other sweeteners. Because it has some calories/sugar it can actually turn brown and become crunchy.  I baked a cheesecake and while we  prefer they not brown I was surprised to see it did.  I use it to make faux cinnabuns by melting butter in a skillet, then sprinkling a Tablespoon of Diabetisweet and a layer of cinnamon powder, and waiting till it bubbles then I place some bread down in the pan and swirl it about wiping up the syrup onto the surface and let it cool. it tastes like the top of cinnamon buns.It has a nice "sugar granule" texture to it for when you want that. I use it as part of a sweetener blend of 1/3 splenda, and 2T each Diabetisweet, Xylitol and Erythritol to equal one cup of sugar.Lastly, the price for this product beats the walmart price to death with a big stick. I was paying almost $10 per box and often had to special order it cause it is not a regular shelf item.  Now I have found a great price and with the subscription service I will never run out again unless I want to.ETA March 10, 2011I've found It also makes a good faux caramel for caramel popcorn.  if you take a quarter cup of it and a couple capfuls of caramel Sugar Free syrup for flavor, and heat it in a small non-stick skillet/sauce pan, till it bubbles and turns tan, then add a tablespoon of butter and stir it in, then drizzle it over a serving (one personal sized bag) of cooked popcorn, it's lighter in flavor but makes a great lower sugar caramel corn treat.  It could be a great treat for someone who doesn't want to diet but still wants less sugar and it's fun and easy.ETA January 16, 2012While my previous review still stand, I have noted that the price of this subscribe and ship item has been climbing rapidly. Fairly soon it will not be a good of a deal as other sellers except for the free shipping.  Right now it is only 30-40 cheaper per box than buying it singly.

No aftertaste, mixes perfectly, just a little less sweet than real sugar but easy to compensate for.  I made Crème Brulee with this and it even caramelized like sugar, not a deep rich brown color but still excellent.  I will buy lots more for baking.Ingredients:8 large Egg yolks1/3 cup Diabetisweet sugar2 cups Heavy creamscrape the seeds of 1/2 vanilla bean1/2 teaspoon of Almond Extract (optional)1/4 cup Diabetisweet sugar (for the caramelized tops)Preparation:Preheat oven to 300F. In a large bowl, whisk together egg yolks and sugar until the sugar has dissolved and the mixture is thick and pale yellow. Add cream and vanilla, Almond Extract and continue to whisk until well blended. Strain into a large bowl, skimming off any foam or bubbles.Divide mixture among 6 ramekins or custard cups. Place in a water bath and bake until set around the edges, but still loose in the center, about 50 to 60 minutes. Remove from oven and leave in the water bath until cooled. Remove cups from water bath and chill for at least 2 hours, or up to 2 days. When ready to serve, sprinkle about 2 teaspoons of sugar over each custard. For best results, use a small, hand-held torch to melt sugar. If you don't have a torch, place under the broiler until sugar melts. Re-chill custards for a few minutes before serving.

column9: It actually does what it claims to do!
column10: It claims to be great for baking and it is--and it is the only sugar substitute that I have found that absolutely performs as well as sugar.  I like to bake various breads and  sugar imparts a quality essential to those loaves that call for it and so does this.  Hallelujah!  And a Huzzah too!  Oh, and as to cooking--same great results.

This procuct is great, besides it not having any other ingredients as calories, sugars, or names you can`t spell much less pronounce you also use the same amount as for regular sugar. I will continue to buy this product as long as they make it. It is good for baking, cooking and diabetics which I am one.

column9: Not good for cooking at all
column10: Prepared 2 cookie recipes - one with DiabetiSweet and one with Splenda.  DiabetiSweet basically melted all over the cookie sheet while the cookies made with Splenda kept their shape.  Not good.Next I actually ate the cookies.  The DiabetiSweet cause severe cramps and multiple bathroom trips.  Splenda had no effect.What's alarming is there is no warning on the package.  If you purchase items made with malitol you get a warning.  Isomalt must be malitol.  I'd look it up, but why bother.  I'm done with DiabetiSweet and if I can warn someone else away from this horrid product then so much the better.

My husband was diagnosed with diabetes more than 5 years ago.  I have used this ever since.  It does not have bad ingredients that other artificial sweeteners have.  His doctor was also pleased with the write up on it.  You can even bakae with this with no bitter taste.  Use in same equal measure and regular sugar.

When my brother was diagnosed with diabetes, my wife asked me to cut back on my sugar intake.  I agreed as long as she could find something that tasted like sugar.  After trying about a dozen substitutes that I couldn't stand, she found DiabetiSweet.  It's expensive compared to most, but it's so worth it!  I can enjoy it in coffee or tea, and I've used it in every recipe where I would use sugar.  It tastes more like sugar than any other sub I've tried.  And my wife is happy from the health standpoint.

I get this sugar for my husband who has diabetes.  He loves it in his coffee.  If you take two teaspoons of sugar in your coffee, you only need one teaspoon of this stuff.  I heard that the other artificial sweeteners mess with your kidney eventually, and this product does not.  There is no aftertaste and it improves the taste of coffee.  I drink it also, and prefer it to sugar.

This is the best sweetener that I've ever used.No after taste.  It's just like sugar!I'm a diabetic but this has been terrific.No effect on my insulin levels..The only thing better is their Brown Sugar on Oatmeal!It's all I use now.Thank You Diabeti........

column9: Very woody with little lemon flavor.
column10: A disappointment.  I will not order this again.  The product is not grated or granulated lemon rind I have used in the past.

column9: Love this brand and this flavor is great
column10: Myself and pretty much my entire family love coffee. But for the most part the flavors we enjoy most differ. This can be a hassel when we all get together.Last year I decided to find a brand of syrups that had enough flavor options and the quality I belive my family deserves.Amoretti Delivers. My family used this seasoning in chicken nuggets when I was a child, and now I use it. Delicious! Whenever I make it for friends, they ask for the recipe. It's simple:-4-6 chicken breasts (thaw if frozen)-2 cups flour-4 tablespoons Nature's Seasons, or to taste (my mom uses 1 T per cup of flour)-oil to fill your fryer appropriately-milk (4 cups?)Cut up the chicken breasts to make nuggets. An inch wide and two inches long is about right, but you don't need to be exact. Put the chicken in a bowl and fill it with milk (until just covering the chicken). Let it sit in the refrigerator until you're ready to cook it. In another bowl, mix the flour and seasoning together. Heat the oil to 340 degrees. Coat each piece of chicken in the flour mixture and fry two minutes and forty-five seconds or until light golden in color. They will darken a bit after they are out of the oil.Mmmm. It's good with Paula Deen's corn casserole.

column9: A young vigorous Islay with a huge flavor profile but also a sweet and wooded side.
column10: Jim McEwan has really shaken up the whiskey world in his decade or so at Bruichladdich.  Rocks is one of his new products, along with Peat, and Waves.  Peat is smokey peat monster.  Waves is buttery fat and sweet.  Rocks strides between and manages to be something unique and something, in my opinion, very true to the original aspect of Bruichladdich:  a sweeter, fruitier, more harmonious take on briny iodiny smokey Islay malt.In the glass, Rocks is golden with a lovely peachy rosy glow.  Rocks is aged for several months in French red wine casks which McEwan says accounts for the color.  Aroma is delicate and dry with iodine, pork rind, dry oats, maritime brine, and a mineral tang.  It smells like rocks on the sea shore.  First sip shows a huge and unexpected (from the nose) explosion of honeyed cereal sugars with a midpalate expansion of oak vanilla, blackberry, and red fruits.  The finish is long with smoky notes and anthracite char joining the honeyed cereal sugar red fruit medley with some oak resin tannins unfolding at the very end.  It's a beguiling flavor profile, reminiscent of the Port Charlotte PC6-8 monsters, but less intense (and minus the peat), less proof, and far less expensive.  It captures a measure of their intensity of flavor and maritime brine meets honeyed malt splendor.  There's no age on Rocks' label.  McEwan says its a blend of young single malts ranging from 6-9 years old.  That's another way it's like the Port Charlotte offerings.Rocks quickly became a favorite for me and the first bottle went quickly.  Shopper's Vineyard recently dropped the price and quickly got more.  This is very reasonably priced for the quality.  This is the everyday drinking version of the big Port Charlotte salty-sweet Islays from Bruichladdich.

column9: Mrs. Leeper's Pasta Organic Gluten Free Corn Spaghetti
column10: These are amazing and unable to consistently find in the Atlanta area . . . so rather than continue driving around looking for them, I found them at Amazon.com. Only other tip to offer, let water boil VERY HOT with a smidge of oil before dropping pasta in and there will be no sticking.  Also, other brands may break down while leftover in the fridge if mixed with other ingredients.  Mrs. Leeper's won't!

A year ago I was diagnosed with allergies to wheat and gluten, among other things.  After trying brown rice pasta and a few other kinds, I went back to eating the regular stuff.  I bought a package of Mrs. Leeper's and had it in my cupboard for quite a while.  But whenever I'd make my husband's favorite pasta, with white clam sauce, I'd be afraid to "ruin" the dish by using gluten free pasta... and it was just too much work to make two different kinds, so I'd just eat the regular stuff and deal with the allergy symptoms.My husband went out of town so I decided to try the Mrs. Leeper's while he was gone.  I was VERY pleasantly surprised at how delicious it is!!  I am confident that I could use it in my hubby's favorite dish, not tell him that it's GF, and he would never even know the difference.I had to cook it slightly longer than the package directions... it was still a bit too hard.  I like my pasta al dente but not raw.  I think I cooked it a minute or two longer than the directions called for.  I also didn't rinse it... just drained it and threw it in with the sauce I had going in a different pan.  It held up very well to being added to sauce, and the extra minute of heating and tossing (unlike all the other GF pastas I've tried, which turned into 1/2" pieces of gloop when I did that).  The pasta retained its form and texture throughout the eating phase as well.  There would be nothing to indicate that it was not "regular" pasta.One thing... I did have a SLIGHT allergic reaction to it... a histamine kind of thing.  The ingredients say "100% organic corn flour" and that is all.  But what do they use to bind it together?  The word "flour" implies to me that it is ground corn mixed with a blend of other things that make it "flour."  Hopefully they use corn starch, to keep it 100% corn.  But I'm not so sure that corn is the only thing it contains... because I have these types of histamine reactions whenever I "accidentally" consume soy or tapioca.  So I've got a call into World Finer Foods to determine whether there is any other ingredient other than corn.  Of course whenever I call any manufacturer to find out what "hidden ingredients" are in their products, you can never get a true answer.  Especially because this product is from Italy, and you have no way of contacting Mrs. Leeper's directly... every contact link redirects back to World Finer Foods.Let me just say that as a person who suffers from numerous food allergies, our FDA does a very poor job in enforcing disclosure on labels.  I have a potentially deadly allergy to red pepper, and companies don't have to disclose that ingredient.  As long as the ingredient is considered "natural," they can just put "spices" on the ingredients and leave it at that.  This should really be addressed by our legislators.  There are MANY people out here in the good ol' US of A who are allergic to hot pepper flakes, chili powder, paprika, cayenne pepper, garlic, black pepper, and many other "spices."  It's time that we know what's in something when we eat it.  Food manufacturers need to have better disclosure, and be accountable for what they put in their products.  I know that this isn't specifically about this pasta... but it is about the difficulty I'm having in finding out what the "binding" agent is in the corn flour.

column9: If you have never had bean threads, try these
column10: I bought these on a whim and then cooked them up with a chicken stir-fry when I realized that I was out of the brown rice I usually use.  Let's set the record straight first, though.  These are NOT good for you, as another poster claimed.  I bought them without looking at the ingredients and thought, hmm... noodles made from beans.  Healthy!  Then I realized that they are made from bean starch, potato starch, and water.  I don't know where I fall on the whole "starch is bad for you" issue (I'd have to do more research) but if you religiously avoid starch, you won't want to use these.  From my point of view, though, the worst I can say regarding their nutrition is that they are pretty much devoid of nutritional value.But now for the good stuff... I know these are common in certain cuisines, but I had never before had them.  They are very interesting - glossy and translucent, with a distinct gelatinous quality.  They basically look like clear gelatin extruded into noodle shape, but they hold together.  This texture can take some getting used to, as gelatinous texture is one texture, in particular, which Westerners are not used to and don't like (except for Jello, of course.)  But, they absorb pretty much any flavor and I have found that if I make a stir-fry one day and refrigerate the leftovers and eat them the next day, these have become very flavorful.  I will definitely keep using them.  If you are looking for a way to change your basic stir-fry, you might try adding your meat and veggies to a base of these bean threads.

column9: makes a mean pad woon sen
column10: My favorite Thai restaurant is about an hours' drive away and gas prices being what they are I decided to try and figure out how to make my favorite entree from there, Pad Woon Sen. A couple of youtube videos later I had seen a demonstration of exactly how to make the recipe which includes my favorite element of the dish - the mung bean noodles.I found these Dynasty noodles here on Amazon, gathered the remaining ingredients locally and it was pretty easy from start to finish. The recipe I used comes really close to the dish I've always enjoyed at the restaurant. I've posted the link in the comments section so you can see if you'd like to try this easy, tasty dish too.As per other reviewer's comments, I'd have to agree these noodles are somewhat gelatinous in texture which I happen to like. They also firm, not unlike ordinary al dente pasta. I've had thinner versions of this kind of noodle but I think this is a nice size. Very mild flavor like rice that readily absorbs the taste of the seasoning or sauce it is paired with.This pack of twelve is a really good value; I always check and compare prices first but at the time of my purchase this is a much better deal than I could find locally. One pack has three bundles of noodles and after soaking/cooking, one bundle tends to be more than enough for one person per meal.Prior to ordering I had a small concern that because the noodles fine they may suffer breakage during shipping but as it turns out they shipped very well - double boxed, and all arrived in excellent condition.Very pleased with this purchase and highly recommended.
They were hard and dry and I threw them away.  I had had them before and they were soft and fresh so this was quite a dissappointment.

This is quite a bargain when you compare the price to the small cannisters of Accent in the stores. It seems perfectly comparable with Accent. I use it, however, on my dogs' food. It keeps them from eating each other's droppings by making them untasty (as if those weren't untasty to begin with, but not to a dog). Since I sprinkle MSG on their food daily, this product is quite a savings for me (and the vet is the one who endorses use of MSG for this purpose).
Sale said 97% off. sells in the stores for 1.69  I just ordered it and paid $3.77 a round not such a good deal should of been 250% offf

column9: Forget salt, for my money it's MSG...SPICY WORLD MSG!
column10: I have replaced all the salt in my recipes with MSG, and boy does everyone love my cuisine.  Sure we all get debilitating headaches from it, but when you taste it you know it's worth it! But it is a pain washing dishes with the spins.Overall I recommend this to any chef!
These taste wonderful...so very much like the originals.Our local stores sell these for about 1.99 a bag, so if you can't get them in your area, this is a decent deal.

My husband is gluten sensitive, dairy sensitive, and diabetic.  He also has a sweet tooth.  This candy gives him a good option of candy he really likes that doesn't make him sick.  It tastes good, espcially for sugar free candy.  As long as you eat it in moderation, it can be a tool in enjoying food in a good way.

I like the product.However, it took quite a while before we got them.As a result the Peter buttercups themselves were melted.They are still edible, and good.They are hard to open though because they melted. The school

There was only one in stock--tea bags with strings.  The others were round bags without strings apparently the new style.  The bags were discolored and the tea apparently old, judging from the taste.  Probably my fault for ordering the last one one of a discontinued item.  I have used the tea in round bags and found it excellent.
Ordered 2 5 lbs bags, packaged well and shipped really fast from this company.  Works great in my restored candy machine.  Having the ad card to insert inside machine is nice as well.

I am just so glad that I finally found this product.  It is not distributed anywhere in Michigan.  I use to make annual trips to Florida and pack my trunk full while I was there.  One year I even had it shipped and the price was astronomical.  This is the only Puffed Rice product that is the real thing.  Those knock off brands in bags don't hold a candle to the Quaker product.  I will purchase this again and again through Amazon.

I was thrilled to find out that the Quaker company still made Puffed Rice cereal, and also had an online store to purchase from. It was quick and easy to order what I wanted, and made an 85 yr old woman very happy to be able to have her favorite cereal for breakfast again. She has diabetes, a bad heart, and is a fussy eater. Not only is Puffed Rice good for her, but she also loves it and wants it everyday!
Really HEALTHY breakfast choice that has  bulk & fiber and can be used with fruit!!GREAT price!!!

it is hard to beat the original puffed rice.  all the generic cereals just do not compare.  i wish i knew why stores do not carry this product.  they carry the puffed wheat but no puffed rice.  the price was right and i have no problem eating the entire case in a reasonable time.  this is the second time i have ordered this product.  never have been disappointed.

column9: Wish our grocery store still sold this
column10: Service was good.  We can't get this in the grocery stores around here, so we have to order "by the case".  Thanks for carrying it!

I have no idea why you can't find Quaker Puffed Rice in the U.S. anymore, or, at least, not anywhere in the U.S. except at Amazon. This is the real stuff, and it looks, feels and tastes just like it always did, which is great! The info on the side of the box says it's made in Canada, and there's an 800 number, in case anyone wants to call Quaker and ask them what they're thinking by removing their product from American markets. Anyhow, you can buy this with confidence-it's the real Quaker Puffed Rice you remember from your childhood. Thank goodness for Amazon-they always have everything!

One day we were having a discussion about how so much breakfast cereal is pre- sweetened.  My daughter-in-law mentioned she use to eat Puffed Rice.  I hadn't thought about that cereal for years.  It sounded so good that I went on line to Amazon and found ten boxes for $30.00 with free shipping.  It arrived shortly thereafter and I took a few boxes to my daughter-in-law and she was thrilled.  Best of all it still tasted exactly like it did years ago.  Excellent transaction

Puff Rice is sodium free , sugar free and fat free , Ideal for those with diet restrictionsI love this product , always have since childhood .  It is even better than popcornas a snack.  It is great with milk too.  Quaker Essential Puffed Rice Cereal, 6.4-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 10)

Thank you so much!  Great price, product and super fast shipping.  Ordered it on Tuesday arrived Thursday.  You made a 86 year old man very happy!  My father in-law ate this cereal for 30 years and was so excited when it arrived!

Since I live alone and am going to order Puffed Wheat also, I would outlive 20 boxes of cereal! If you go directly to the Quaker web site, you can order as few as one box. Of course the shipping is steep because it's based on distance, but it's the same for one box as it is for more.

What you really have here is, too much money and a need to, throw some of it away to pay this price... Give me a break - $25.00 for 1 lbs. of Wis. Cheddar cheese.? I am not saying anything at all against Wisconsin Cheese, it's great stuff! Just not worth $25.00 a pound no matter where it's made or comes from...

Everything I have ordered from Amazon has been on time or someone follows up to let you the know the status..NO GUESSING games.  Very reliable, very professional, very easy!!  Thanks for taking the stress out of my Christmas shopping this year.

column9: Best olive oil I've ever had
column10: I tried some of this olive oil and the vinegar at a greek festival in Nor Cal and it was great. I will be buying it here from now on.

Bee Raw Buckwheat Honey.  Excellent honey!  Dark, rich, not overly sweet.  It's perfect for baking with when you just want rich flavor, or spread on fresh baked bread.Plus I love the fact that it's locally produced.

I ordered this honey along with many others and have to say it is unique. No other honey comes close to this strangely dark goo. My first thought when I opened the jar that contained this semi-solid honey was that I had been duped and was sent something rotten. It honestly smelled like something you would not willingly eat. But I went ahead and tried it anyway. It tasted like dirt at first and was not sweet at all. After a second or so the flavor changed to a heavy sweet like dark honeys usually taste like.I now realize that when the product description mentions "an earthy peat moss flavor with a bright finish", all it means is that it will taste like dirt with a slight bitterness and then turn sweeter. Unless you like odd flavors or are going to mix this with other products to create a complex flavor, I wouldn't recommend this honey to just drizzle or to eat alone.

I have had many types of Jerky through the years, but I think this is one of my favorites. Very easy to chew and the flavor is very long lasting. We have gone through 2 cases at work so far and all of the guys loved it.

I agree with the first poster---this was complete waste of money. No one in my family could eat it. It was beyond hard and tough, and I have eaten many, many brands of jerky in my lifetime. I simply cannot believe that this product got through quality assurance testing. I wish I had asked for my money back for this because it was totally justified. At any rate, I was lucky that I had tried other Trail's Best products that were excellent beforehand. If I had to judge their other products based on the quality of their ham jerky, I would never have ordered from this company again.
I was looking forward to giving this to my husband who loves anything Jerky but this was a big dissappointment. Very Hard! I would not recommend this particular Jerky. It was a waste of money

i think this is quite tasty cereal.  the kamut flakes were just like wheaties or any other standard wheat flakes. they didn't get too mushy or soggy but they felt much softer & gentler than those rock hard kashi flakes i've been eating. this cereal seemed much more like "normal" cereal i am used to. it's a nice option to have for days when kashi seems to hard to handle. Also i love that there is whole grain amaranth & whole grain quinoa flour in it too.  i will buy more when it runs out.

too many breakfast cereals are laden with sugar, but the arrowhead brands leave room for honey and blueberries.  i rotate between the various flakes, and i like them all.  they're all light and crunchy, organic, nutritious, plus they taste great...that's a sweet way to start the day!
I've been eating this cereal for many years, after first finding it in a health food grocery store. To be that healthy and yet taste that good is amazing!

I'm a big fan to Arrowhead Mills' shredded wheat cereal, but I thought I might try this other kind, just for variety. It's okay, but it's not very substantial. I put a lot in my cereal bowl--including yogurt, chopped fruit, raisins and chocolate chips, and this cereal just seems to disappear in there. Maybe if you just add a little milk and some raisins or so, it might be more impressive. However, I don't think I'd order it again. I'm going back to the shredded wheat. Pricier, but you get what you pay for, I guess.

This cereal kicks a* and takes names. It isn't offered anymore in our local co-op catalog, so it is great to find it here for about the same price if free shipping is available. I like the cereal because it uses fruit juice for sweetener and is also great for people on wheat and gluten free diets. Texture is also just right for flakes.
My husband and my son love this cereal. We used to buy them from Whole Foods. It is a bit pricey. Now we order from Amazon.
My grocer stopped carrying this product, but was gald to find it here.  It is heaper than grocery too.  Really like this product.
I have purchased several Sam Mills corn pasta items, and they are excellent.  They are every bit as good as the ones that cost 2 to 4 times as much.

this is the best brand of gluten-free pasta i've had. it's hard to detect the difference between this and regular pasta.  i've made it with light, veggie-based dishes and it is still delicious.  i've paid up to $6.00 for 1 lb so buying here is a huge bargain and well worth ordering in bulk.  manga!

*****St. Dalfour's Certified Organic Vanilla Tea is made from hand-picked, organic Ceylon tea. It is enhanced by "the natural flavor of vanilla", a very, very subtle, and in my opinion, very enjoyable addition. If you like strong artificial flavors you probably will be disappointed in this tea. If you enjoy authenticity in a tea, and your palate can discern subtle taste distinctions, you'll really enjoy this tea---I did! As with other St. Dalfour teas, I left the tea bag in as I drank the tea (the whole time, much longer than recommended), which turns most teas bitter, but not this one.St. Dalfour is a French firm that makes natural teas, including this organic tea. There is not a lot of information about them on their web site beyond the basics, but what is there looks good.St. Dalfour's Certified Organic Vanilla Tea is different and fun, great to serve to guests. They'll ask---"Wow, this tastes different...what is that flavor?" I drink my teas black but I imagine it would taste wonderful with cream and/or sugar too. Note that black tea does contain caffeine.Highly recommended.*****

Clear American has harnessed the flavor that CC contained but bottled it in a standard plastic bottle. The flavors are rich and pure, without that heavy syrupy taste.Nutritional Facts(1/30/2012)Calories  0Total Fat 0Sodium  0Sugars  0Protein  0Check out these other flavors as well.Clear Choice Sparkling Water 12 Pack - Black Cherry, 1 quartClear Choice Key Lime Sparkling Water - 12 PackClear Choice Kiwi Strawberry Sparkling Water 4 ct - 6 PackClear Choice White Grape Sparkling Water 4 ct - 6 PackClear Choice Tropical Fruit Sparkling Water 4 ct - 6 PackClear Choice Golden Peach Sparkling Water - 12 PackHighly recommended.

I was delighted to find Theo chocolate on amazon.com. I can no longer have chocolate with soy in it (which all common brands of chocolate have); Theo is soy-free. I had found Theo chocolate at a store 2 hours from my home but dreaded asking my husband to take me back there (the store doesn't do mail order). Oddly, the Theo website didn't mention that their chocolate is available through Amazon. It's less expensive at Amazon, as well, plus it qualifies for free shipping. The 45% cacao milk chocolate bar comes in a flat, 3-oz bar, similar to a regular Hershey bar. It's scored into 6 horizontal sections. The candy itself has a slightly "waxier" mouth feel than Hershey's but tastes richer. I'm happy with it, and will buy it again when my supply runs out.

A bold and "authentic" tasting milk chocolate. It has some intriguing flavor notes that I would describe as being almost, every so slightly, "spicy". Very satisfying when I'm after a milk chocolate with more to it than sweetness alone.

I lived in Seattle for 7 years and have a business / chocolate crush on Theo. So, I still buy their chocolate online, justifying the expense on the premise that I will only use it for baking, thus making my baked goods that much better, winning the admiration of all my friends, etc.  However, my husband has taken to breaking open a bar on normal weeknights, and then inviting me to join him in snacking on a hunk or two.  Neither of us can resist eating the chocolate plain, despite my intentions to ration it.  It is simply delicious.
This is one of the few chocolate bars around that doesn't use soy lecithin. So if you want soy-free, munch on this.(It's also very addictive.)
I love this chocolate and it doesn't have soy. I don't usually like milk chocolate and I think it's quite yummy.
I buy Theo because it is the only chocolate I've come across that doesn't contain any soy. Fortunately it's delicious too so I'm happy.

Tinkyada Brown Rice Penne Pasta with Rice Bran, 16-Ounce Bags (Pack of 12)Tinkyada makes pasta that actually tastes like pasta. I have tried many different brands and nobody comes close to Tinkyada. If you are allegeric to wheat you can have great tasting pasta again.

This is by far the best pasta you can get. If you suffer from wheat allergies. Then I urge  you to try this. You'll never be disappointed from anything for this company. Italian food is still on the menu. Try the lasagna, It's great!!!

This pasta is not bad at all!  Some of my friends who tried bites of other rice pasta, all agreed they could eat this brand anytime - even in place of regular pasta.  As for me, I will only buy this kind.  No more from the grocery stores again.There was one thing I did not like about the penne, and that was the size.  It's smaller than regular pasta and was a 'little' bothersome trying to pick up with the fork at first.

column9: Best gluten free pasta I can find
column10: I have been on a gluten free diet for one year plus due to having DH.  This is by far the best pasta for gluten free needs.  Other pastas get soft and slimey when cooked.  This pasta holds together and has good flavor.  I acutally discovered it at a natural food store but the expense drove me to look for a better deal.  I found it on Amazon.com
This pasta tastes like regular pasta. I eat along with my husbad who has to eat gluten free.

column9: Great texture for a GF Pasta
column10: Since i live a gluten free lifestyle, I try all the gf pastas.  This is by far the best in my book with the consistency of wheat flour pastas.It's a large bag of pasta, which will make enough for at least 8 people (with heeping plates full).  But once bag is opened, you have to store in plastic or glass container to keep fresh - so not convenient unless you're using entire bag at once.I've cooked it traditionally, boiling and then cooling - and also the way it suggests on bag, boil quickly and cool longer.  Both work fine.Again, my favorite thing about this pasta is the texture.  When I add a small amount of olive oil it melts in my mouth.  The flavor is bland (which it's supposed to be - it's pasta!) and it goes well with an assortment of cheeses.They're a little more expensive than other brands, but worth it to me for taste.Love to mix it with vegetables.  Enjoy!

The best gluten free pasta brand I have ever tried.  The texture is just like "regular" pasta.  Don't overcook!  I cook it for 10 minutes.It tends to get a dry texture when stored in the fridge.  But add some sauce and microwave it and it gets nice and soft again. For cold salads,  if I make a tuna pasta salad, I try to make just enough, because of the dryness factor.

I love this product. It tastes great and doesn't have any wheat or gluten to which I am allergic to. My husband who doesn't have the allergies notes decreased bloating and thinks it tastes better than regular pasta. I also love the energy saving cooking directions. You boil the water, throw the pasta in, bring it to a boil, then take it off the heat. In 20 minutes, you are done! Fabulous!
Simply put this is the best GF pasta I have ever tasted.  I is virtually the same texture and taste of normal pasta.  Thanks Tinkyada you are the best.

I have tried just about all their products and they are all excellent. You really can't tell the difference from regular pasta. If you're gluten free try Namaste stuff too, the pizza dough (only one I tried so far) is superb. I liked it better when I made the pizza crust thin and then cooked for about 10 min before adding toppings then cooking for the remainder, makes a better texture this way, imo.

column9: By far the best GF pasta!
column10: I'm giving Tinkyada Brown Rice Pasta (in all its shapes and sizes) my highest recommendation--it surpasses every other brand I've tried of gluten-free pastas--and being a pasta lover, I have tried many brands. No weird texture/taste with Tinkyada and it cooks up as creamy or al dente as you want with a simple addition/reduction of cooking time. Sauces cling to it exceptionally well. Had a gloppy problem with Japanese yam-based noodles, and the other brands of rice/corn noodles had strange textures and tastes. Tinkyada, I love you for the wonderful pasta dishes I thought were gone forever. Thank you so much!

After trying several g-f pastas, and having awful results, I tried Tinkyada after reading consumer reviews.This is , far and away, the absolute best!I truly doubt  whether anyone could detect the difference between the taste and texture of this rice pasta and regular wheat pasta.You will not be disappointed!

column9: I can't think of a single negative thing to say. . .
column10: I've had no success with other gluten-free pastas. I tried one that turned the water bright yellow and then tasted like a cross between a corn kernel and styrofoam, and I tried one that tasted just fine as long as what I wanted was a tasty blob on my plate. Yuk.  When I read Bill Henderson's book on healing cancer (I'm a stage III ovarian cancer survivor) and discovered that gluten can work against all the other things I'm doing by possibly feeding my cancer cells, I imagined never having pasta again. When I found other pastas that purported to be tasty and easy to cook, I snapped them up and brought them home to create my fave pasta dishes. Disaster! The aforementioned corn-y yuk-extravaganza and the gelatinous (but, hey, TASTY) glob made me think it was sayonara, pasta. Then, just two weeks ago, I saw this pasta at a local market, and I bought it up thinking that it would also be a disappointment. Imagine my surprise today when I cooked it up and found it not only holds its shape but tastes good and handles sauce beautifully. Wowsa! I'm in pasta love! I cooked mine by boiling it up for approximately 12 minutes, and it didn't glob up, fall apart, or otherwise cause me any grief. I drained it, rinsed it, and then tossed with hot sauce. It kept its shape throughout and did a good job of doing the same as I forked it up. I'm so impressed. I will now order a case of the stuff and have it ready for pasta salads and tosses (tapenade with some extra garlic, anyone?). I love to take pasta and simply toss it with extra virgin olive oil, garlic, fresh basil, and a bit of salt and pepper. Very simple and quite excellent. Also, I'm looking forward to combining this with my fave sauce, which is simply fresh organic tomatoes processed to crushed consistency, olive oil, fresh basil, lots of garlic, and a wee bit of pink salt. So very delicious! Next, I will take this pasta and turn it into pasta salad for a weekend gathering. I shall let you know how it goes. :-)

This pasta is the best of the best.While I'm not very picky in my eating habits, even I got annoyed when every gluten free pasta I tried ended up more like a gluten free paste from getting so mushy and disfigured once cooked. This stuff is perfect. It legitimately does NOT get mushy. I have no idea how that strange little bunny on the package did it, but he has. And I thank him.This stuff is EASILY swapped in for regular pasta. They seriously won't know the difference.Hallelujah!

This is by far the best gluten free pasta I've tried. It's great to buy it in bulk and save over health food store prices. I love it for Mac and Cheese. It requires less cooking than traditional wheat but withstands a little over cooking unlike other gf pastas.
This is the best gluten free pasta I've eaten.  Best of all my kids love it.

If you can't eat wheat pasta, Tinkyada is the brand to buy.  The white rice pasta I bought at the store was mushy and didn't hold its shape.  It was a pale imitation of the "real thing."  But Tinkyada's pasta I can enjoy eating.  As long as you cook according to the directions, you can't tell it's not "normal" pasta. I usually add a bit of oil to the water with the pasta to discourage sticking, because I don't do a very good job remembering to stir it!  It's also brown rice-based, so it's healthier for you.  One warning, if you put plain pasta in the fridge, it will be hardened when you pull it out.  But, heat it with some sauce, or reheat it in a pan of water on the stove, and it's nice and soft again.I like the penne shape.  It holds its shape well when cooked and doesn't fall apart.  It's great for a casserole to be made ahead of time, as the pasta won't fall apart with reheating and lots of stirring.  This shape is good with a smooth sauce, but I especially like it when there's something chunky mixed with it, such as diced tomato or meat chunks.  Definitely recommend this brand, as well as this particular shape.

This is the absolute best gluten-free pasta out there.  There is no way to tell the difference between this and regular wheat pasta.  We have tried most of the other brands and nothing compares to this.
This pasta tastes good and has a great texture. Almost as good as "real" pasta.

column9: Hands down, the best GF pasta!
column10: All the Tinkyada pasta products are awesome.  One recommendation, don't overcook.  I bring the pasta to a boil then turn it off and let it sit for about 9-10 minutes.  The texture is very similar to wheat pastas.

You will never know the difference from the wheat pasta.  Great pasta and good for you to boot. I always cook it a little less than the recommended time and I always rinse off the starch.  A staple in our house!!
This pasta is the best I have tried!  Not soggy or mushy.  No one would know that they are eating gluten-free.  Try it... you'll like it.
Tinkyada is consistently one of the best pasta products for gluten-free foods that I have found. Excellent!
I thought I loved DeBoles pasta until I tried this. Holy cow!!! Used it in pizza casserole and couldn't tell the difference from regular pasta at all. Will be buying lots and lots of this.

I ordered 12 bags of this Tinkyada brown rice penne noodle. It arrived quickly and I am satisfied that I'll have pasta on hand for awhile.It cooks up nicely at home. I have also brought it to restaurants and the chef will cook it for me and top it with their special sauces! My family also eats this pasta and they do not have to be gluten-free. My husband said it doesn't taste any different from the wheat pasta!

Our child with celiac loves this pasta, so I buy it by the case. All Tinkyada pastas hold up well, even if slightly overcooked, and have a great texture. Some other GF pastas fall apart in the cooking water and taste awful, but not Tinkyada. Our whole family loves it.
This is a very good product.  I enjoy it very much.  However, this is not really penne, it is ziti.

I have Celiac and cannot eat any Gluten or Wheat products. Pasta is a favorite of mine. It took me some time and trying of different pasta products. By far 'Tinkyada Brown Rice Penne' is the best and closest to regular wheat pasta in texture & taste (mostly the texture) Once you put gravy or sauce over it, there is hardly to near none of a taste difference. If you like 'al'dente', only cook for 8 to 8 1/2 minutes after it comes to a boil. The package suggests 15 to 16 minutes. Don't do it. If you don not have a health food store near you to buy this product, you can get it shipped to you from amazon.com.

column9: Tinkyada Brown Rice Penne Pasta Review
column10: Excellent tasting pasta that has a wonderful texture when cooked, much better than any of the store brands of rice pasta.

I only use pasta products made by Tinkyada. The pasta always comes out perfectly and non-celiac people can't tell the difference. I've used the spiral pastas for my veggie pasta salads and they turn out great. I eat Tinkyada pasta every week!

column9: A sensible way to control my intake.
column10: I love potato chips and was eating way too many of that sort of thing.  I have lost 102lbs in the last year and can still enjoy a controlled amount of what I intake.  If I open a big bag, bar the door as they will mostly all somehow disappear.  A great way not to over eat.

I've been eating Lays Potato chips every sence I was kid. The BBQ chips are my favorite. When I was in school I use to crush them in the bag and pour them straight out of the bag into my mouth. They are still Delicious. The bag looks good too.

This is the closest it gets to a perfect BBQ potato chip. Not too sweet and not too spicy. Great balance of crisp and tasty for a BBQ chip. Matches my all time childhood favorite, Laura Scudders BBQ chip which is not made any more.

These looked great online, but I was disappointed that I couldn't find a product label ... even when I found "Emily's" website. Since they were listed as "gourmet," I was hoping for premium ingredients. While not as bad as some, they do include natural flavors and corn syrup, for instance.Having said that, the Dark Chocolate Strawberries TASTE very good, and the taste alone might warrant 5 stars (considering that they're packaged fruit).For the prospective buyer hoping for an ingredient list, here you go:INGREDIENTS: Dark Chocolate (sugar, chocolate liquor, cocoa butter, milk fat, soy lecithin added as an emulsifier, and vanilla). Dried Strawberries (strawberries, sugar, rice flour, natural flavor, citric acid). Corn Syrup, Tapioca Dextrin, Confectioner's Glaze (refined lac.).

I bought a bag of these and the chocolate covered blueberries and both are great. The stawberries are about the size of a marble and covered in thick dark chocolate. You can still taste the berry though. Its the perfect mix of sweet and  dark chocolate. The chocolate and berries contain no artificial colors or flavors. The taste is addictive and for the price you cant go wrong. If I knew they were this good I wouldve got 2 bags. Enjoy.

I thought the price was good until I saw how much it was to ship the item. I tried to cancel the order twice (maybe I was too late?) but the seller NEVER responded at all. The product was as disappointing as the seller. Bag is about 1/2 full, can't really taste the fruit, although chocolate tasted good. This was not worth the time or money.

column9: chocolate covered dried strawberries to die for!
column10: The chocolate covered dried strawberries tasted so amazing and were addictive! I didn't buy any more because I would have no self control and would start to become a little fat piggie LOL!

column9: I could eat these all the time
column10: Dark chocolate and strawberries, how can you go wrong?  These are my favorite candies.  Very impressive thank you gift for a chocolate loving friend.
AWESOME~AWESOME~AWESOME!!! You must buy these!! Wonderful seller as well. FAST shipping.  Would purchase again!!!

I think it is a tasty and healthy replacement for fries when eaten as a side to any sandwich.  I am diabetic and have to count carbs.I have ordered this twice through Amazon.  Delivery both times has been prompt.
This bean salad does not  have the typical flavor of 3-bean salad, but it works good for using in minestrone soup!

I bought this gift basket as a fun little "stuffer" for each of our 4 boys. I have cooked with these products for years and knew that my boys would like them, too. And the Christmas sale was a great time to get them started!

Have tried a number of this kind of dry packaged raviolis. This isn't the worst, it's passable (and there are a couple I like a lot). Filling is marginally tasty, if you can taste it. It's just a chunky pasta dish -- buy some elbow macaroni instead.

column9: Nice Variety, Tasteful Presentation, Great Idea!
column10: Got these for my sister for her housewarming... for individuals with small households these are ideal - spices are so expensive and to make most recipes you need a reasonable selection but they go bad so quickly (relative to how much is left) that it can be very discouraging.The presentation is beautiful... my sister couldn't decide whether to put them away or display the tins on the counter!The selection in this collection is fairly wide ranging and useful... she was very excited to get the more fragrant spices that you need to be fresher for them to do their job.This is not really "cheaper" or more economical than buying jars of the included spices... but the difference is that in six months or two years when you need ginger again you won't be forced to choose between old ginger with little flavor left or springing for a new jar... the next packet will be as fragrant and intense as the first packet was.  So while not a lower cost in the short run, in the longer run it's more convenient and flavorful and, ultimately, a reasonable balance between flavor and cost.

This is such a clever idea- Tsp sells spices in tins that contain individualy sealed teaspoon sized packets of spice.  Only the spice you are using gets opened and the rest stays fresh and flavorful!  The spices are beautifully packaged, organic, and so delicious.  I fully reccomend this product.

I just found PB2 and PB2 with chocolate and I am thrilled.  I love sugary goodies but I'm not a fan of calories and I don't like chocolate.  I thought I'd try PB2 with chocolate anyway and I'm so glad I did!  Eating a serving or two of PB2 with chocolate satisfies my sweet craving without breaking my calorie bank!  Sometimes, when I want to splurge, I spread some PB2 with chocolate on a graham cracker, spread some marshmallow fluff on another and sandwich them together! YUM!

In trying to cut calories from my daily routine, I examined what foods I ate most often. Peanut butter was at the very top of the list.  While I can't just scoop out a spoonful and eat it like regular peanut butter, this still tastes awesome mixed with some almond milk and oatmeal for a delicious and satisfying breakfast or afternoon snack.

This came in quickly.  It was just what I was wanting and I have almost eaten it all already!!  I had tried this product before and bought it at HEB but either they don't carry it or everyone else is onto the secret.  It is better than regular peanut butter and MUCH healthier.  You gotta try it and the price on Amazon is wonderful.  Thank you!
It took me a few times to figure out the consistency I like but after that it was all golden. I will keep buying this product. I highly recommend this product and the non-chocolate version too.
This stuff is really good/great as peanut bitter or in a smoothie!  Especially if you want it low cal and low carb.
Delicious and well packaged! It came right when it was supposed to. I love using this for baking and snacks!
great PB flavor with out the calories or fat. I use it in my Shakeology for extra flavor. love love. great product
This product is awesome. Tastes amazing. Great to mix up, or if you want to add a little something interesting to smoothies and milkshakes!!

I tried someone's recipe with the frozen banana, no dairy milk (eek used dairy!), and pb2. First of all, major froth - I assume because of the actual milk. Second of all, NOT enough PB2! column9: This makes enjoying peanut butter while on WW so much easier!

We just moved out of the country and we were looking for an easy way to transport peanut butter with us.  This is a much healthier alternative to add to my morning protein shake. The flavor is great and it traveled well.  We just ordered more to take back with us!
I bought this to put into smoothies.  I do weight watchers and the serving size is 1-2 points. You can taste the PB but not have to worry about the extra fat and calories. I really like this product.

column9: I can eat it with a spoon
column10: This is fantastic. If it's really 85% less calorie and fat, I will eat it with a spoon with no reservations. Being constantly on some type of diet, it is a real find. It tastes a lot like peanut butter with chocolate mixed together. I used it first with Yonanas mixer and it worked out rather well with bananas and berries (very little berries, or otherwise the taste clashes)I've bought Peanut butter powder too so I can't figure out which one I like better, they are kind of similar, but both yummy. One little critics I have is the packaging. I had trouble opening it, so in the end I had to cut it. Now it sits open and I would rather have it tight closed. Any ideas? (except zip lock bag)? Next time I think I will buy it in a jar. And I will buy it again.

Love PB2 in my smoothies. Great peanut butter flavor without the calories! I use unsweetened almond milk, one scoop of protein powder, a frozen banana and 2T of pb2 and it makes a great low cal shake!

If youre on a low cal diet (or any diet!) and you crave chocolate, GET THIS!! You mix 2 tbsp of the powder with 1 tbsp of water.. You can add a little more water if you want a drizzle like consistency for drizzling on desserts or waffles. But otherwise, its super creamy and absolutely delicious! If it isn't sweet enough for you, try to add one packet of splenda or sweet n low! Will buy again and again! Absolutely LOVED it!
PB2 is a wonderful product that I frequently add to protein shakes without fear of adding extra fat. Great taste and satisfying. Highly recommend!!!

this is great!  cant tell the difference from original peanut better.  I have it with my fruit or on toast. Compared to the origanal calories of 45 vs 190 per serving..can't beat it.  Love this and will keep buying it.

This is a pretty solid alternative to peanut butter. If the instructions on the label are followed, the peanut butter ends up a little more liquid-y than one might expect, but that is easily remedied by adjusting the amount of water. This works well for sandwiches, and is an awful lot less messy than trying to add proper peanut butter to a smoothie. I've not yet tried using it in baking, but it seems like it would be satisfactory, so long as the amount of water is reduced when making the paste.

column9: PB2 makes you forget about PB1
column10: This product has changed the way I view peanut butter.  Once afraid to use it and only sparingly, I now get the beautiful flavor of peanut butter in my morning protein shakes, With none of the guilt.  I recommend to anyone who loves peanut utter but doesn't like the fat.
The chocolate PB2 is just as amazing as the regular PB2 - plus a healthy indulgence. I love to use it as a dip for animal crackers! Also great on apple wedges.

I make smoothies, Lots of smoothies. Both this, and PB2 straight-up ... are my favorite additions.  Chocolate shakes with chocolate PB2 are like eating a very chocolaty peanut butter cup ...through a straw ... with the fat removed  ...  Sinful without the guilt!!!  Add a few extra ice cubes and it turns thick as soft ice cream. OMG!  If you're on a diet (or not), this my friend, is your new guilty pleasure. I know it's mine! Try it.  You will be hooked.

This product is a dream come true!  Peanut butter flavor without all the fat and calories.  Both kinds, regular and with chocolate are delicious.  Great added to shakes, or I even eat it right from a spoon as a snack.  I mix up the chocolate and dip fresh strawberries in it!  Great product and it is helping me lose weight.

Love this low fat alternative product!  I use it in savory and sweet recipies!  It is a bit salty so I reduce any additional salt required.The only drawback is the shipping cost.  Because of the high cost of shipping this product remains a luxury purchase for me.
I did not experience any of the negatives but perhaps because I used Almond Milk Great both with unsweetned vanilla And dark chocolate milk add a banana whey powder and you are good to go!
Love PB2 Chocolate Powdered peanut butter. Tastes great, not a lot of calories, easy to store, and combined chocolate and peanut butter! What's not to love? Well worth the price.

I really love peanut butter, but one sandwich worth of peanut butter uses up most of your daily intake of saturated fats generally. This powdered stuff doesnt come close. It is as easy to use as simply stirring with a spoon and comes out just fine by my estimation. There isnt really a noticeable drop off for me personally, but i dont really eat really sugary peanut butter anyway (i would normally buy Justin's or somesuch). The chocolate is just right in this as well. Although i wanted to be able to eat PB&J's without taking up all of my fat intake, i also wanted to have something for my daily smoothies. I play around with variations, but my go to drink is kale, banana, apple, mango, and mint with flaxseed meal. This makes a great addition to that blend.Anyway, i have seen mention of cheaper prices elsewhere, but for me, with Prime membership and a $5.50 price point currently, i feel the price is more than adequate, especially when factoring in no shipping and two day delivery.I recommend trying this product. No transfats, high fructose corn syrup, or any added carp. Just a good, simple product.Enjoy!

This stuff is good, and once you wrap your mind around the possible ways to use it,  you will need to be buying more!  The powder is very fine, much like Nesquick. Baking with it is easy, as well most things.  The flavor is spot on, though eating it plain is not recommended. I love this mixed in with my cereal or breakfast shakes.

This product tastes great. I use it in my protien shakes to help mask the tastes of some of the flavors I have tried and do not like. With the PB2 I now like the taste of the shakes and use this every day. I prefer the PB2 with coco powder but both products taste great.

I'm about to place my third order of the Chocolate PB2.  YUM.  I use this product in my Medifast Soft Bake Chocolate Chip Cookie.  I mix in about 2 Tbsp into the dry cookie mix, add enough water to get to the right consistency and then microwave for about 5 seconds less than directed.  The end product is a warm, chewy, moist peanutbuttery chocolate chip cookie!

column9: WOW LOSING POUNDS DREAM !! TASTES GREAT !!
column10: When I have a peanut butter/chocolate need this is great about 75% less calories & fat.Easy to make 2tbs powder to 1tbs water. I like the taste better then jar peanut butter + somuch healthier. Weight watchers + Nutrition action healthletter RAVE !! about this & theyshould. Enjoy.

I just received my order of this and the regular PB2 today. column9: Feeding my sweet-tooth AND shrinking my waistline!
column10: I'm not worried about my fat intake at all, but I love peanut butter and would easily eat 400 peanut butter calories daily.  I'll eat a spoonful by itself, put a couple in a smoothie... column9: Not Peanut Butter, Peanut Flavored Peanut Butter
column10: I ordered this at the asking of my wife because she is dieting. I was against it from the start, but I will make my review fair.The product is not peanut butter, if you expect peanut butter than you will be disappointed. It tastes like peanut butter. If I could compare it to something it is like eating a regular Oreo and a reduced fat Oreo. The reduced Oreo tastes like and Oreo, but really just leaves you wanting the real thing. This product is no different. If you mask it will jelly and bread, the off taste becomes less noticeable, but there in lies the problem. You have to add more calories back in to make this product taste better. There by negating the fact that you have cut calories. As I explained to my wife after we both decided this product was not for us. The problem with any peanut butter food is normally everything but the peanut butter. The fat is the healthiest part. You wouldn't eat omega free fish because it's lower in fat, why would you do the same to peanut butter?The only way I could recommend this is if you are doing a starvation sort of diet (i.e. you eating this with celery and water). If you are doing a healthy diet don't cut out the peanut butter of your PB&J, cut out the jelly first and then the grain. I eat again "regular" non-hydrogenated peanut butter will celery, now there is a healthy food.Pros+lower calorie+great price here on amazon+does taste similar to peanut butterCons-less nutritional value-doesn't taste like real peanut butterI will give it four stars if you are doing a starvation sort of diet, which I don't recommend, but it does taste alright for a lot less calories. For everyone else I give it one star as you should not be eating products like this and the product itself is not that good. Overall 2 stars, weighted towards everyone else.
Go to Bell Plantation's web site and get a 4 pack for the same price.  I made the mistake of not shopping around...  You can get this for a much better price.

column9: Love this product but the price is rediculous

Two tablespoons of chocolate peanut butter for just 45 calories! It's a real treat! Creamy with good peanut and chocolate flavors. I like the chocolate PB2 better than the plain PB2.

With all the top heavy happy reviews I expected more.  This barely lasted us through 10 peanut butter sandwhiches and it was just "eh."  It is not over the moon mouthwatering flavor.  And for how long it lasted, not worth the price.IF you are only doing ONE TEASPOON at a time, than this will last you longer.  But the directions state for 2 tbsp at a time and that is about right for one serving.

I did not like this.  I think if you're going to have peanut butter you might as well have the real thing.  I thought I would try this because I just joined Weight Watchers and other members recommended it.  I ended up turning the cookies that I made into treats for my dog.  He loves them!

Oh my goodness... If all I ever used this in was smoothies, I'd still get my money's worth. In order to get this much peanut butter flavor you'd have to add a ton of peanut butter to even perceive it in there.
